title: specs/04 feedback: delete-from-browse, deleted-note surfaces, save-and-new
description:
Tracks the feedback items in specs/04-tui-features.md, filed after evaluating each against the shipped E0-E11 core. Two feature areas: (1) delete/undelete a note from the browse TUI + surface deleted notes in the CLI; (2) a save-and-new keybinding so you never have to leave the TUI to start a fresh note.

Substrate already exists: versions.delete() appends an op='delete' tombstone (CAS-guarded) and versions.recover() repoints the head back past it (src/lode/versions.py:302,337). list_notes / 'lode notes' already filter op != 'delete' (notes_read.py:112). So these children are mostly wiring the existing primitives to keybindings and CLI flags, not new storage.

DISAMBIGUATION (resolved with user, 2026-07-08):
- 'CLI option to show deleted notes' => BOTH: a --deleted/--all flag on 'lode notes' to LIST tombstoned notes (the counterpart to browse, which shows only live), AND a [deleted] marker on 'lode show <id>' so a tombstoned note isn't rendered as if live (it already prints its carried-forward body today, just unlabeled).
- Recover IS in scope: add 'lode recover <id>' wired to versions.recover(), so delete is a complete reversible loop rather than a one-way trip to 'lode purge'. A TUI deleted-notes view + in-TUI recover key was NOT requested and is out of scope (recover reachable via CLI for now).
design: Delete-from-browse defaults (chosen, not asked — reversible + low-risk): key = 'd' on BrowseScreen (free; current bindings are escape/e), guarded by a Save/Discard-style confirm because there is no in-TUI recover surface yet, then reload the table via the existing on_screen_resume path. Save-and-new: key = Ctrl+N on CaptureScreen — the exact screen the complaint names (Ctrl+S there calls app.exit(), capture.py:259). Ctrl+N saves via save_capture then RESETS the buffer (clear text area + related panel, keep focus) instead of exiting; empty buffer is a no-op notify; a CAS conflict still routes to ReconcileScreen.
acceptance_criteria: All child tickets closed: a note can be tombstone-deleted from the browse TUI (with confirm) and recovered from the CLI; deleted notes are listable via 'lode notes --deleted' and flagged when shown via 'lode show <id>'; and Ctrl+N on capture saves-and-opens-a-fresh-note without leaving the TUI.
notes:
CRITICISM (/debate, 2026-07-08) — the epic's premise "wiring the existing primitives" names the WRONG primitives.

1. Repository.delete() and Repository.recover() ALREADY EXIST (repository.py:249, :261). All four children point at raw versions.delete()/versions.recover() instead. This is a seam violation with teeth: Repository.recover() is the ONLY thing that applies redact_before_index() before re-indexing the recovered head (lode-ibv, repository.py:270-283). Calling versions.recover() directly makes a recovered secret-bearing note keyword-findable again via FTS — a documented invariant, silently broken. Repository.delete() also owns the cache.evict(); versions.delete() does not. FIX: route all three children through Repository.

2. NO DEPENDENCY EDGES between the children. /code fans out across the ready frontier, so all four build in parallel and land in arbitrary order. Consequences:
   (a) d32.1 alone on trunk = a destructive 'd' key with no recovery surface. This epic's own DESIGN justifies the confirm dialog "because there is no in-TUI recover surface yet" — that reasoning only holds if the CLI one exists. d32.1 should depend on d32.3.
   (b) Merge collisions: d32.2 + d32.3 both edit cli.py; d32.1 + d32.4 both touch capture.py (d32.1 must generalize DiscardConfirmScreen, which lives there). /land will bounce one of each pair on conflict.
   (c) Hidden dep d32.3 -> d32.2 (see d32.3 note 1): recover is unusable until 'notes --deleted' can surface a full id.

VERIFIED SOUND (no action): versions.delete() is CAS-guarded and carries the body forward; versions.recover() repoints the head; list_notes filters op != 'delete'. A soft-deleted note is ALREADY invisible to Q&A — retrieval.py:83,89,491 scope every leg to v.op != 'delete'; reconcile.py and enrich.py gate on it too.

OPEN DESIGN DECISION (blocks d32.3, escalated to human): resolve_note_prefix is LIVE-ONLY by design. recover only ever operates on tombstoned notes. See d32.3 note 1.

title: Harden the unattended 3-loop autonomy story (sweep + debate gaps)
description:
Make running the loop family (`/code` + `/land` + `/epic-audit`) safe UNATTENDED by
adding the one missing leg — an exception surfacer — and closing the real gaps a
`/debate` pass surfaced. Today `/code -> /land` runs reliably, but two pipeline
outputs have NO downstream consumer: `land-escalated` branches and `human`-labeled
decision tickets. Nothing pings a human when work parks on a decision; you only find
it by manually running `bd`.

## Where this came from
Design pass captured in scratchpad `sweep-spec.md` (the `/sweep` skill, v2) and
`debate-agenda.md` (companion changes), then stress-tested by `/debate`. The debate
REVERSED several of the original agenda items — this epic encodes the debate's honest
build list, not the original wishlist.

## Debate verdict (what actually holds)
- The unattended story HOLDS. Its real load-bearing assumption is that concurrent
  `bd dolt push` from the existing N-producer fan-out is safe — NOT any new lock.
  ("single-lander lock" guards `trunk`, not Dolt; the system is already many-writer
  to Dolt by design.)
- The ONE genuine upstream gap: `land-escalated` has no defined resolution transition
  — the queue never drains.
- Epic auto-close and the bounce/rebase caps are OVER-ENGINEERING or YAGNI — DEFER
  them (see this epic's Design field). The surfacer IS the detector.

## Build list (children)
1. `/sweep` skill — surface-only human-decision surfacer, cross-machine-safe dedup.
2. Define the `land-escalated` resolution transition in `/land` (the real gap).
3. Validate concurrent `bd dolt push` under the `/code` N-producer fan-out.
4. Record the debate decisions in `docs/` (per CLAUDE.md, design facts live in docs/,
   not tickets/memory).
design:
SETTLED BY DEBATE (these are decisions, to be mirrored into docs/ by child #4):

DECIDED — DO:
- Build `/sweep` surface-only. Scope = surface the human-decision queue
  (`bd list --label land-escalated` ∪ `bd human list`) + epics that are
  `epic-audited` + open + all-children-closed ("ready for a human to close").
  NO audit dispatch (that is already `/loop /epic-audit`). NO decisions made.
- Dedup store = the digest issue ITSELF (Dolt-durable, travels cross-machine).
  A scratchpad state file re-notifies the whole queue from a second machine — rejected.
- Fix the real gap: define how a human clears a `land-escalated` (child #2).

DECIDED — DEFER (captured, NOT to be built until evidence appears; do NOT file as
ready children — that would contradict the debate and let `/code` build them):
- `/land` bounce-lineage cap (bounce_depth counter → escalate after N). Mechanism is
  sound (`--set-metadata bounce_depth`, survives supersede), but no bounce-chain has
  been OBSERVED. The `/sweep` digest IS the detector; add the cap when a real chain
  shows up. See debate-agenda.md §A.
- `/code` rebase-attempt cap. Churn-only failure; a real rebase conflict already
  escapes to `land-escalated`. YAGNI. See debate-agenda.md §B.
- Epic AUTO-CLOSE + confirming re-audit. REJECTED, not merely deferred: epic closure
  is a human capability-judgment; auto-close trades a high-cost false "done" to save
  one rare click. Each gap child already passes code-review + land-review + land gate,
  so a re-audit only re-does judgment a human should own. Manual `/epic-audit <id>`
  already re-verifies on demand. See debate-agenda.md §C.

DECIDED — REFRAME:
- The "bd-write concurrency / shared lock" agenda item is a category error (guards
  trunk, not Dolt). The only real question is whether concurrent `bd dolt push` under
  the existing N-producer fan-out is safe — a PRE-EXISTING property, filed as child #3,
  not a `/sweep` blocker. `/sweep` writes one self-owned digest row → cannot contend.
acceptance_criteria: /sweep exists and surfaces the human-decision queue (land-escalated + bd human list) plus close-ready epics, with cross-machine-safe dedup; land-escalated has a defined resolution transition so the queue drains; concurrent bd dolt push under /code fan-out is validated (or a follow-up bug filed); all debate decisions recorded in docs/.
notes:
EMBEDDED DEBATE AGENDA (verbatim, source of record — replaces scratchpad/debate-agenda.md; covers the deferred/rejected caps + the concurrency reframing):

# Debate agenda — the 3-loop autonomy story

Companion to [`sweep-spec.md`](./sweep-spec.md). Package for `/debate`: one
concrete change (the `/land` bounce cap) plus the cross-cutting questions that
surfaced while reading the `land` / `epic-audit` skills. Nothing here is built.

The framing to debate: **`/sweep` makes livelocks *visible*; caps make them
*impossible*.** Do we ship surface-only (v1) or surface + prevent (bigger)?

---

## A. COMPANION CHANGE (drafted) — `/land` bounce-lineage cap

**The problem it closes.** A bounce supersedes the ticket and opens a rebuild
ticket (`/land` SKILL.md §"Bounce", lines 324-364). If `land-review` bounces the
rebuild for the same reason, you get an **unbounded supersede chain** — a real
internal livelock, needing no external churn. There is no cap today; the only
escape is a rebuild finally passing or a human noticing.

**The change.** Carry a `bounce_depth` on the lineage. On the Nth bounce, stop
rebuilding and **escalate** instead — routing the stuck lineage into the same
`land-escalated` queue `/sweep` surfaces. Local to `/land`'s Bounce section:

```bash
BOUNCE_CAP=${BOUNCE_CAP:-3}                       # tunable; 3 rebuild attempts then hand to a human
DEPTH=$(rtk bd show <id> --json | jq -r '.[0].metadata.bounce_depth // 0')

if [ "$DEPTH" -ge "$BOUNCE_CAP" ]; then
  # Lineage has failed land-review $DEPTH times — this is no longer a "rebuild",
  # it's a genuine "a human must break this loop". Escalate, keep the branch+findings.
  rtk bd update <id> --add-label land-escalated --remove-label ready-for-land \
    --append-notes "BOUNCE CAP ($DEPTH ≥ $BOUNCE_CAP): lineage bounced repeatedly without landing.
Latest land-review findings: <findings>. A human must decide: is the acceptance
achievable as written, is land-review wrong, or should this epic child be dropped?"
  rtk bd dolt push
  # NOTE: branch KEPT (like any escalate) so the human has the artifact.
else
  # ... existing bounce flow (create NEW, re-parent, re-point deps, supersede) ...
  NEW=$(rtk bd create ... --json | jq -r '.id')
  rtk bd update "$NEW" --set-metadata bounce_depth=$((DEPTH+1))   # repo convention (coding.md uses --set-metadata for land_head etc.); value stored as a string, bash -ge reads it numerically
  # ... rest of existing bounce flow ...
fi
```

**Debate targets for this change:**
1. **Counter vs. chain-walk.** A `bounce_depth` metadata counter is simplest and
   self-contained, but is manual state. Alternative: walk the `supersede` chain
   (`bd` links `<id> -> NEW`) and count depth from the graph — no counter, but
   depends on the chain being cleanly walkable. Which is more robust?
2. **Cap value.** 3? 2? Too low = premature human interrupts on legitimately
   iterative work; too high = tokens burned on a doomed lineage.
3. **Keep or drop the branch on cap-escalate?** Escalate normally keeps the
   branch. Here the branch is judged bad-as-is — but the human still wants the
   artifact + findings. Draft keeps it; is that right?
4. **Does the cap belong in `/land` or `land-review`?** `land-review` produces
   the bounce verdict; `/land` executes it. The depth is a landing-loop concern,
   so the draft puts it in `/land` — agree?
5. **Sequencing:** ship this WITH `/sweep`, or ship `/sweep` first (surface-only)
   and add the cap once a real bounce-chain is observed?

---

## B. SMALLER SIBLING (sketch) — `/code` rebase-attempt cap

Same pattern, lower priority. `needs-rebase` starvation is **theoretical** —
only under perpetual trunk churn; a finite backlog quiesces, and a real rebase
*conflict* already escapes to `land-escalated` (`/land` line 322). A
`rebase_attempts` counter in `/code`'s needs-rebase sweep, escalating after N,
would bound even the perpetual-churn case. **Question for debate: is this worth
building at all, or is the churn-only failure mode too rare to guard?**

---

## C. POLICY QUESTION — epic close + re-audit of filed gaps

`/epic-audit` **never closes an epic** (line 156) and, after filing gap children,
does **not** re-arm — re-auditing is a manual `/epic-audit <epic>` (line 155). So
after an audit's gaps are built and landed:

- nothing **re-audits** to confirm the gaps actually filled the holes, and
- nothing **closes** the epic — it sits `epic-audited` + open forever until a
  human closes it (`/sweep` will now *surface* this, but not resolve it).

**Debate:**
1. Is "a human closes every epic" the right permanent policy, or should there be
   an **auto-close** when `epic-audited` + all children closed + a *clean*
   confirming re-audit?
2. If gaps were filed, should landing the last gap child **re-arm exactly one**
   confirming audit — and how do we do that *without* reopening the regeneration
   loop the `epic-audited` terminal label currently prevents? (e.g. a distinct
   `epic-reaudit-pending` label that grants exactly one more pass.)
3. Or is manual re-audit the correct, deliberate human checkpoint — keep it?

---

## D. CROSS-CUTTING — running three loops unattended

1. **Quiescence / poll cost.** `/code`, `/land`, `/epic-audit`(, `/sweep`) poll
   forever; a no-op tick still spends a model turn. Do we want adaptive backoff
   or a quiescence stop ("N passes, all queues empty, no new tickets → stop") for
   the loop family, or is fixed-interval polling an acceptable cost?
2. **bd-write concurrency.** `/land` guards itself with a *land-specific*
   lockfile; `/epic-audit` and `/sweep` have none. On one machine that's three
   `bd dolt push` writers (plus parallel subagents). Do they need a **shared
   bd-write lock**, or is one-machine turn-interleaving + Dolt's own conflict
   handling enough? This is the operational risk of adding a third writer.
3. **One machine, three loops — is that the intended topology?** `/land`'s
   single-writer guarantee is a one-machine convention. `/code` fans out
   producers (possibly cross-machine). Does adding `/sweep` + `/epic-audit`
   pressure the "everything landing-side on one machine" assumption?

---

## Suggested debate order

1. **C** and **D** are the biggest-leverage — they're about whether the
   *unattended* story actually holds, independent of `/sweep`'s shape.
2. **A** — is the bounce cap worth building now (surface + prevent) vs. later.
3. `sweep-spec.md` open questions — only after the above settle its scope.
4. **B** — smallest; may be a "won't build".
CRITICISM (/debate 2026-07-08) — EPIC-LEVEL COMPLETENESS GAP:
1. TWO OF THE DEBATE'S OWN 'BIGGEST-LEVERAGE' QUESTIONS DROPPED WITHOUT DISPOSITION. The embedded agenda calls C and D the biggest-leverage items. The epic records dispositions for A (defer), B (defer), C (reject), D.2 (reframe -> child .3). But D.1 (poll/quiescence cost — do the loops back off or stop when all queues empty, or is fixed-interval polling accepted?) and D.3 (is 'all three loops on one machine' the intended topology, given /land's single-writer guarantee is a one-machine convention while /code may fan out cross-machine?) have NO recorded disposition — not in the epic Design, not in child .4's record list. Adding /sweep as a THIRD forever-polling loop directly implicates both. This is exactly the 'forks the record' failure the project warns against. RESOLVE: give D.1 and D.3 an explicit disposition (decide/defer-with-rationale/reject) and add them to .4's record list, or state in the epic why they're out of scope. [DECISION PENDING x2 - surfaced to human]
DECISIONS (human, 2026-07-08) — epic completeness gap RESOLVED:
- D.1 (poll/quiescence cost): DEFER (deferred-but-not-forgotten). Fixed-interval polling stands; adaptive backoff / quiescence-stop ('N empty passes -> stop') is revisited only if no-op poll cost is OBSERVED to matter. Record in docs/decisions.md.
- D.3 (topology): DECIDED. INVARIANT — the landing-side loops (/land + /epic-audit + /sweep) run on ONE machine; /code producers MAY fan out cross-machine (they write disjoint Dolt rows + push branches only). This makes /land's single-writer guarantee an explicit stated invariant, not an implicit convention. Record in docs/decisions.md. (Distributed refs/locks/land stays deferred — NOT un-deferred.)

title: E-TUI feedback — expose ids, introspect enrichment, work-to-completion, quieter logs, readable dates
description: Tracks the five feedback items in specs/03-tui-features.md (current-work feedback after E11 TUI + async queue landed): (1) expose note id for purge via TUI Browse + a CLI list command; (2) make enrichment outcomes visible to the end user; (3) a 'work to completion' option that polls/blocks until submitted jobs are processed; (4) stop mirroring httpx 200-OK lines to stdout/stderr from work/ask — errors only; (5) shorter, human-readable dates in Browse. Children filed per item after disambiguation.
design:
## Success Criteria

- purge is usable end-to-end: a user can find a note's id (CLI list + TUI Browse) and hard-delete it, ideally by a short prefix.
- Enrichment outcomes are visible: after `work`, and on demand per-note, the user can see what tags/entities/summary/edges/embeds a note got.
- `lode work` has an opt-in mode that blocks until submitted jobs are fully processed (bounded by a timeout).
- `work` and `ask` no longer mirror httpx 200-OK lines to stderr; only actionable errors surface.
- Browse dates are short and human-readable (adaptive absolute), not full ISO-8601 timestamps.

## Design notes (post-disambiguation, specs/03-tui-features.md)

- Item 2: build the in-flow `work` summary + a `lode show <id>` CLI. NOT the TUI note-view panel and NOT enrich-counts-in-jobs.
- Item 5: adaptive absolute format (time today / weekday+time this week / mon+day this year / ISO year older).
- Item 1: 8-char id column in Browse + full id on NoteViewScreen + purge-by-unambiguous-prefix.
close_reason: Epic complete: all 8 children landed on trunk; /epic-audit clean bill (5/5 success criteria satisfied, no gaps). Closed by human direction.

title: E15 — 02-feedback: logging telemetry cleanup, --debug flag, save-on-exit popup
description:
Tracks the four feedback items in specs/02-feedback.md (trunk snapshot 3c2f365; current trunk 59b5018): two logging items (undocumented LODE_LOG_LEVEL; debug logs corrupting the TUI console), a new top-level --debug CLI flag to enable diagnostic instrumentation, and a UX fix so the save-on-exit confirm is a popup over the editor instead of a full blank screen.

## Design decisions (confirmed with user 2026-07-04; refined after /debate)
- Item 3 (lode-1i8.2) = TUI-ONLY file logging. Suppress console/stderr log output only while the TUI runs, keeping the file handler (and guaranteeing one is attached so Python's lastResort can't fire). Plain CLI commands (ask/add) KEEP stderr — 'lode ask' deliberately mirrors an AuthError's cause to stderr; that path is preserved. (Re-scoped from an earlier 'drop stderr globally' after debate flagged the CLI regression.)
- Item 2 (lode-1i8.3) = TOP-LEVEL 'lode --debug' flag on the root Typer callback: sets DEBUG log level + enables diagnostic instrumentation (event-loop-lag probe, etc.) for every subcommand. Accepted coupling: --debug == DEBUG log level (verbosity == feature-enablement); split later if needed.
- Item 4 (lode-1i8.4) = external Textual .tcss stylesheet (repo's first), wired via CSS_PATH and shipped via pyproject package-data.

## Sequencing
- .2 blocks .3 (shared logconfig/cli files).
- .1 blocks .3 (both edit docs/configuration.md — avoid merge collision; .3 appends to the logging section .1 creates).
- .4 is independent.

Related prior epic lode-0wj (E14) delivered the exit-safety confirm guard (lode-0wj.1 Escape, lode-0wj.8 Ctrl+Q) and the lag-diagnosis spike (lode-0wj.2) whose probe is gated on DEBUG; item 4 here refines that confirm UX.

## Success Criteria
- LODE_LOG_LEVEL (and ANTHROPIC_LOG) documented in docs/configuration.md.
- A top-level 'lode --debug' flag raises log level to DEBUG and enables diagnostic instrumentation across all subcommands.
- Running 'lode tui' writes ZERO log output to the terminal (console suppressed for the TUI session, file handler retained), so latency telemetry is collectible via the log file without corrupting the TUI; plain CLI stderr logging is unchanged.
- Pressing Escape (or Ctrl+Q) over a dirty capture buffer shows a centered popup dialog (external .tcss, shipped in the wheel) over the still-visible editor; Cancel dismisses it and returns to the editor unchanged.
close_reason: E15 complete: all 5 children landed; epic-audit (manual re-audit) confirmed all four Success Criteria delivered on trunk (LODE_LOG_LEVEL/ANTHROPIC_LOG docs, lode --debug flag, TUI console suppression, save-on-exit popup); deferred --debug↔DEBUG coupling decision recorded in docs/decisions.md.

title: Instrument the capture screen: reveal what runs during input (lag diagnosis spike)
description: Feedback: typing feels laggy/blocked and it's unclear what the app does behind the scenes. Add lightweight, toggleable instrumentation (timing/logging around the event loop, keystroke->render latency, and the passive related-notes worker: how often it fires, how long find_related_notes / the ONNX embedder / LanceDB take, whether passes overlap). Prime suspect: on_text_area_changed debounces a pass that runs the embedder+LanceDB via asyncio.to_thread on every idle pause. Goal is DATA, not a fix: identify what actually blocks input. Blocks the optimisation follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: REPRO PRECONDITION: reproduce the felt lag against a realistic seeded corpus (reuse the deterministic seed-corpus fixture from lode-5y8.4), NOT an empty DB — an empty/small DB makes the related-notes pass return instantly and hides the lag. Define a target keystroke->render latency (e.g. p95 threshold) so the spike has a pass/fail, not just 'notes'. MUST-ANSWER: does the passive related-notes worker actually yield the event loop? i.e. does the fastembed/ONNX embed release the GIL during inference — asyncio.to_thread only relieves input if it does; if ONNX holds the GIL the 'background' pass stalls typing anyway. Deliverable: findings on this ticket (what runs on the input path, measured cost, and the GIL/event-loop-yield verdict). No behaviour change beyond instrumentation.
notes:
Debate (lode-0wj): the prime suspect (related-notes pass) is ALREADY off the UI thread via asyncio.to_thread + @work(exclusive=True) in src/lode/tui/screens/capture.py, so on paper it should not block input. The one mechanism that WOULD make it block: to_thread does not help if the offloaded C code holds the GIL — fastembed/ONNX inference may not release it. Verifying that is the load-bearing question for whether lode-0wj.3 (disable related-notes) is the right fix or a red herring.
FINDINGS (spike, git 96e2c19, tests/test_capture_lag_diagnosis.py, opt-in LODE_DIAGNOSE_LAG=1):

Reproduced against the REAL lode-5y8.4 seed corpus (10 notes) with the REAL
fastembed/ONNX embedder (not the eval scorer's offline hash stub) -- an empty
DB was avoided per the acceptance precondition.

PASS/FAIL TARGET: p95 event-loop tick lag < 100ms during the pass (the
standard "feels instant" interactive-response threshold), measured as how much
longer a 10ms asyncio.sleep heartbeat comes back late by -- a direct proxy for
keystroke->render latency since Textual's key handling/repaint run on the same
event loop.

MUST-ANSWER, DIRECT RESULT: YES, fastembed/ONNX DOES release the GIL during
inference, and asyncio.to_thread IS relieving input as designed.
  - find_related_notes cost against the seeded corpus: min=52-63ms
    mean=64-68ms p95=70-76ms max=70-76ms (5 realistic mid-typing drafts).
  - Event-loop lag, full find_related_notes pass (FTS5+ONNX+LanceDB) via
    asyncio.to_thread, sustained over 10 repeated passes: idle baseline
    p95=0.3-0.4ms; DURING the pass p95=5.2-7.7ms, max=5.8-9.6ms. Comfortably
    under the 100ms target -- PASS.
  - Isolated to embedder.embed_query alone (no DB/LanceDB, ONNX only): idle
    p95=0.4-0.5ms; during embed p95=1.2-1.5ms, max=2.2-2.4ms. PASS, and
    confirms the (small) lag above is not concentrated in ONNX specifically.

INTERPRETATION: the passive related-notes worker is NOT the mechanism behind
the felt lag. It already runs off the UI thread via asyncio.to_thread +
@work(exclusive=True) (structurally can't overlap -- a new pass cancels/
supersedes any still-running one), and the offloaded call (FTS5 + fastembed/
ONNX + LanceDB combined) yields the event loop well within the pass/fail
target. This is evidence AGAINST the prime suspect the lode-0wj debate raised:
lode-0wj.3 (disable/opt-in the passive pass) is likely a red herring as
currently scoped and should be re-evaluated against other candidates (Textual
render cost, TextArea internals, terminal I/O, something outside this pass)
before being treated as the fix -- lode-0wj.4 (optimise based on findings)
should look elsewhere first.

Caveat: this spike measured a *single* related-notes pass's cost per call, not
compounding effects from many other things happening concurrently in a real
long TUI session (job queue worker, reconciliation scan, etc.) -- if the felt
lag persists after lode-0wj.4 investigates other candidates, re-run this
spike's heartbeat instrumentation (now permanent, DEBUG-gated, in
lode.tui.latency_probe + lode.tui.screens.capture) against a live session to
see if some other component holds the GIL longer.

INSTRUMENTATION (permanent, toggleable, no behaviour change): DEBUG-level
logging in lode.tui.screens.capture around debounce restart/fire and each
related-notes pass (sequence number, duration, result count, whether it was
cancelled by a newer pass), plus lode.tui.latency_probe.probe_event_loop_lag,
an event-loop-lag heartbeat only started while
log.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG). All gated behind LODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG
(existing lode.logconfig convention) -- zero log calls and zero extra worker
at the default INFO level.

Reproduction: LODE_DIAGNOSE_LAG=1 pytest -s tests/test_capture_lag_diagnosis.py

metadata.land_summary: Lag-diagnosis spike (lode-0wj.2): DEBUG-gated event-loop-lag instrumentation (lode.tui.latency_probe + capture screen) + opt-in seeded-corpus repro; verdict: fastembed/ONNX releases the GIL, related-notes pass is not the felt-lag cause. No behaviour change at INFO.

title: Confirm-on-unsaved guard for the capture screen's Escape (stop Escape silently discarding)
description: ASSUMED DECISION (proceeding without user confirm — revisit if wrong): scope to ESCAPE ONLY — fully screen-local, directly solves the vi-muscle-memory footgun. Escape on a dirty (non-empty/non-whitespace) capture buffer pops a Save/Discard/Cancel confirm; an empty buffer exits immediately so get-in/dump/get-out stays fast. Ctrl+S keeps its direct save+exit. title: code-reviewer runs /code-review + /simplify against an EMPTY diff: its cwd is a clean launch worktree, not the builder's branch
description:
Phase 2 of /code (.claude/skills/code/SKILL.md) mandates that the code-reviewer subagent 'runs /code-review --fix + /simplify' on the built branch. As written this cannot happen, and it fails SILENTLY as a false green.

ROOT CAUSE. The built-in /code-review reviews 'the current diff' and --fix applies 'to the working tree'; /simplify likewise reviews 'the changed code'. Both are cwd-relative and neither accepts a path/base argument. But a code-reviewer is dispatched with isolation:'worktree', so its cwd is its OWN launch worktree, created off trunk HEAD with no changes. The builder's branch lives in a DIFFERENT worktree (metadata.review_worktree), driven via 'git -C $WT'. So the two skills analyze a tree with an empty diff.

EVIDENCE (2026-07-09). Live launch worktree agent-a610601c24feac4de sits at 86b62ba == trunk HEAD, 0 uncommitted, 0 diff vs trunk. Conclusion is robust to the implementation: whether the skill diffs the working tree or diffs branch-vs-trunk, a launch worktree at trunk HEAD yields empty either way.

WHY IT IS DANGEROUS. 'No issues found' on an empty diff is indistinguishable from 'no issues found on a clean branch'. A reviewer that trusts the tool rubber-stamps. The producer flow's whole premise is that neither review of a branch is done by its author -- this silently removes one of the two.

OBSERVED. Across a 6-branch fan-out today (vcb/c5l/0as/x7f/at8/pzr) only the lode-c5l reviewer noticed and said so, substituting an equivalent hand review. The other five did not mention it. Three reported 'nothing to change'. Those verdicts happen to look sound (the Opus reviewers read the diff by hand via 'git -C $WT diff' and found real defects in vcb/pzr/at8, and 0as even found a pre-existing IPv6 bug -> lode-lt1), but we cannot distinguish 'reviewed and found nothing' from 'reviewed nothing'.

DOC GAP. .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md lines 124-132 document only the APPLY half -- Edit/Write are guard-pinned to the launch worktree, so fixes go through bash. It never states that the ANALYSIS half is pointed at the wrong tree. Step 4 (line 144) still instructs 'Run /code-review --fix ... on the branch', which is not achievable as written. Line 272's summary table repeats the apply-half framing only.

NOTE: a marketplace plugin at ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/claude-plugins-official/plugins/code-review also defines a /code-review command, but it reviews a GitHub PULL REQUEST via gh and comments on it -- a different command that shares the name. Worth confirming which one actually resolves when a subagent types /code-review, since the plugin one would be even more wrong (no PR exists for a land/<id> branch).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Dispatch a `code-reviewer` subagent with `isolation: "worktree"` at any ticket carrying `ready-for-code-review` (per .claude/skills/code/SKILL.md Phase 2).
2. Inside that subagent, note its cwd is `.claude/worktrees/agent-<hash>`, a worktree freshly created off `trunk` HEAD.
3. Run `git status --short` and `git diff trunk --stat` in that cwd — both empty. The builder's branch lives in a different worktree entirely (`metadata.review_worktree`).
4. Run `/code-review --fix` (or `/simplify`) as Phase 2 mandates. It analyzes the cwd's diff, which is empty, and reports no findings.
5. Observe that the reviewer cannot tell that result apart from a genuinely clean branch.

Verified 2026-07-09: live launch worktree agent-a610601c24feac4de sat at 86b62ba == trunk HEAD, 0 uncommitted, 0 diff vs trunk.
design:
DECISION (human, 2026-07-09): adopt the 'review in the reviewer's OWN launch worktree' architecture.

The probe (see prior note) FALSIFIED the EnterWorktree premise: EnterWorktree(path=...) reports success, but a separate isolation guard still hard-pins Bash/Write to the agent's original launch worktree. So 'git -C' was never a workaround for a nonexistent constraint — the constraint is real.

But the constraint does not require driving the BUILDER's worktree. Verified 2026-07-09: no land/<id> branch is checked out in any worktree — builders work on 'worktree-agent-<hash>' branches and merely PUSH to land/<id> as a remote ref. Therefore the reviewer can fetch origin/land/<id> and check it out INTO ITS OWN launch worktree, where Bash/Edit/Write/nox all work natively and cwd's HEAD *is* the branch. /code-review --fix and /simplify then analyze the real diff and write the correct tree.

This resolves lode-k5e (empty-diff review) AND lode-8k3 (rebase pickup cannot write a conflict resolution) with one architecture, and retires the 'git -C $WT' contortion plus the bash single-match workaround.

Shape:
  git fetch origin land/<id> trunk
  git checkout -B land/<id> FETCH_HEAD     # or --detach if it is checked out elsewhere
  /code-review high --fix trunk...HEAD ; /simplify
  ./scripts/python-init.sh && nox -t fix && nox -s tests
  git commit -a && git push origin HEAD:land/<id>

Known costs, accepted: (1) the launch worktree has no venv, so python-init.sh rebuilds it per review; (2) metadata.review_worktree becomes vestigial — /code SKILL.md step-1's stranded-review guard must key on review_head instead; (3) uncommitted work in the builder's worktree is invisible, which is fine because the builder's hand-off contract already requires a clean tree.

Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this fix (file a follow-up): changing whether builders keep their worktrees, and /land's worktree GC.
acceptance_criteria: Determined empirically whether /code-review and /simplify can be aimed at a directory other than cwd. Phase 2 of .claude/skills/code/SKILL.md and step 4 + the summary table of .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md no longer instruct an action that silently no-ops. If the skills remain unreachable, the docs say so explicitly and mandate a concrete alternative, so a reviewer cannot mistake an empty-diff 'no issues found' for a clean branch. Confirmed which /code-review resolves inside a subagent (built-in vs the marketplace PR-review plugin).
notes:
Filed 2026-07-09 from the /code fan-out that built vcb/c5l/0as/x7f/at8/pzr. Discovered because the lode-c5l code-reviewer disclosed it in its hand-off rather than quietly working around it. Related: lode-tpt (clean-tree assertions), lode-pzr (concurrent /code topology). Do NOT fix by loosening the isolation guard -- the guard is what keeps reviewers off trunk.
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-07-09 (docs, not speculation). The EnterWorktree tool description states: 'Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched...) and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session.'

This DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md:98 ('I do not call EnterWorktree with path = $WT') and .claude/skills/code/SKILL.md ('the isolation guard refuses EnterWorktree for commands resolved into a path-entered worktree'). The builder worktree IS under .claude/worktrees/ of the same repo, so a code-reviewer launched with isolation:'worktree' MAY EnterWorktree(path=$WT).

Consequence: cwd becomes $WT, so (1) Edit/Write work normally — the bash single-match workaround becomes unnecessary; (2) /code-review and /simplify analyze the REAL branch diff instead of an empty one — this bug's root cause; (3) nox/gates run in cwd with no -f flag. This is option (c), and it resolves lode-k5e and lode-8k3 with a single change.

Constraint from the same doc: 'After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with path to return to one.' So only one worktree is active at a time; that is fine for a reviewer that only ever touches $WT.

Secondary finding (from the shipped skill's own prompt text): /code-review DOES accept a target argument — 'If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument, review that target instead' — and its arg spec is [low|medium|high|max|ultra] [--fix] [--comment] [<target>]. This is a FALLBACK if EnterWorktree(path) turns out not to work: aiming it at 'trunk...land/<id>' would at least give the finders the right diff. But note --fix applies to the CWD working tree, so --fix would still write the wrong tree; the fallback requires dropping --fix and applying by hand.

CONFIDENCE: [Likely], not [Certain]. Our agent docs may encode a real failure observed on an older CLI (current: 2.1.205). VERIFY EMPIRICALLY BEFORE REWRITING THE DOCS.
ESCALATION: empirical probe FALSIFIES this ticket's 'ROOT CAUSE FOUND' theory (option (c) / (a), the EnterWorktree(path=$WT) approach). Do NOT rewrite the docs to use EnterWorktree(path=$WT) as originally proposed — the current git -C architecture in code-reviewer.md / coding.md / code/SKILL.md is CORRECT and must stay.

PROBE PERFORMED 2026-07-09 (as directed by the dispatching task, before any doc edit):
1. `git -C <repo-root> worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/probe-k5e trunk` — created a throwaway worktree (had to use --detach since `trunk` was already checked out at the main repo checkout).
2. Called `EnterWorktree(path=.../probe-k5e)` from this producer (launched with isolation:'worktree', cwd pinned at .../agent-a80ef25cb56ab4339). The call returned SUCCESS: 'Entered worktree at .../probe-k5e. This agent's working directory and write access now point at the worktree...'
3. Ran `Bash: pwd && git rev-parse --show-toplevel && git status --short`. RESULT: REFUSED. Exact error: 'This agent is isolated in the worktree .../agent-a80ef25cb56ab4339, but this command's working directory resolved to the shared checkout (.../probe-k5e). Refusing to run it there — commands from a worktree-isolated agent must run inside its worktree. Re-run the command from .../agent-a80ef25cb56ab4339.'
4. Tried `Write` to a new file inside probe-k5e. RESULT: REFUSED. Exact error: 'This agent is isolated in the worktree .../agent-a80ef25cb56ab4339. Edit the worktree copy of this file instead of the shared-checkout path.'
5. Returned via `EnterWorktree(path=<original launch worktree>)` — succeeded, cwd/writes back to normal. Removed the probe worktree with `git worktree remove --force`.

INTERPRETATION: EnterWorktree's own success message is technically true in a narrow sense (it does shift the tool layer's *default resolved cwd* — the Bash error explicitly names probe-k5e as 'this command's working directory'), but a SEPARATE isolation guard sits underneath and still refuses to execute Bash or Write against anything but the agent's original launch worktree. The EnterWorktree tool description's claim that 'the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session' does NOT mean writes actually reach the target path for a subagent pinned at launch with isolation:'worktree' — that pinning appears to be enforced at a layer EnterWorktree cannot override. Confidence: [Certain] on the observed behavior (two direct, reproducible refusals with explicit error text); [Likely] on why (the guard is probably keyed to the agent's original isolation-worktree assignment, not to whatever EnterWorktree last pointed at).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS TICKET AND lode-8k3: option (c)/(a) (dispatch/EnterWorktree into $WT so cwd-relative skills + Edit/Write 'just work') is NOT AVAILABLE to a code-reviewer or coding producer launched with isolation:'worktree'. The existing git -C <path> / nox -f <path>/noxfile.py architecture in .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md and .claude/agents/coding.md remains the only mechanism that actually reaches a different worktree's files — CONFIRMED correct, not superseded. lode-k5e's real fix is option (b): stop instructing /code-review + /simplify to run mandate-as-if-cwd-relative-works; make code/SKILL.md Phase 2 and code-reviewer.md step 4 mandate an explicit hand review (or the documented /code-review <target> arg WITHOUT --fix, applying fixes via the existing bash single-match workaround) instead. lode-8k3 similarly loses its option (c) escape hatch and must resolve via its own (a) or (b) (permit bash single-match writes into $WT for mechanical rebase conflicts only, or make coding.md's escalate-on-conflict an explicit policy choice + fix SKILL.md's 'no manual nudge needed' claim).

DECISION NEEDED FROM A HUMAN: which of (b)'s two ticket-specific resolutions to take (lode-k5e: hand-review-checklist vs /code-review <target>-without---fix; lode-8k3: permit-mechanical-bash-fix vs escalate-always-and-fix-the-frontmatter-claim). Both are legitimate design calls, not further-investigable facts — I did not implement either because the dispatching task explicitly scoped this session to 'STOP; escalate' on a failed probe, not to freelance-pick between the remaining options.

Branch land/lode-k5e was pushed for continuity but carries NO changes (HEAD 86b62ba55664586ff76c5d74223270afbf6750 == trunk HEAD at claim time) — there was nothing to revert to since the probe was run before any doc edit.
close_reason: Landed on trunk via /land (merge bad00ea). Semantic review: accept. Doc corrections filed as lode-en9.

metadata.land_summary: Retire the git -C builder-worktree review architecture: code-reviewer + coding rebase-pickup now fetch land/<id> and check it out into their OWN launch worktree (Edit/Write/nox native); mechanical rebase conflicts auto-resolve, genuine ones still escalate; step-1 guard re-keyed to review_head. Docs-only.

title: /land Section 3: bd calls inside the merge loop re-dirty .beads/issues.jsonl and fake a merge conflict (would mis-kick-back clean branches to needs-rebase)
description:
Observed live during the /land pass that landed lode-6fc/t83/ay5.3/nps.4/28d/bpl/alv on trunk (merge 01d3c6a), 2026-07-09.

land/SKILL.md Section 3 does the 'git restore --staged --worktree .beads/issues.jsonl' ONCE, immediately before the merge loop. But the loop body itself is written to call bd:

    for id in $ACCEPTED; do
      rtk git merge --no-ff "origin/land/$id" -m "Merge land/$id: <summary> ($id)"
    done

and the <summary> in practice comes from a per-iteration 'bd show <id> --json' (that is where land_summary/title live). Any bd read regenerates the passive .beads/issues.jsonl export and leaves it STAGED. So the restore protects only the FIRST merge; from the second iteration on, the tree is dirty again.

Observed failure: merges 1-3 (lode-6fc, lode-t83, lode-ay5.3) succeeded, then merges 4-7 ALL failed with

    error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:
      .beads/issues.jsonl
    Merge with strategy ort failed.

This is NOT a textual conflict. But Section 3's own instructions say a merge failure inside the loop means the branch 'conflicts with an earlier survivor merged this pass' -> 'git merge --abort and handle it as a needs-rebase kick-back'. Followed literally, this pass would have kicked FOUR clean, accept-verdicted branches back to needs-rebase (lode-nps.4, lode-28d, lode-bpl, lode-alv), each triggering a pointless /code rebase cycle. lode-28d is a ONE-LINE deletion in src/lode/retrieval.py that cannot conflict with anything merged this pass — that implausibility is what exposed it.

Verified by re-running the four merges after (a) pre-computing all titles into files BEFORE the loop and (b) restoring the jsonl: all four merged clean, no conflicts, combined re-gate green (887 passed, 6 skipped).

The bug is a seam between two rules the skill already states separately: 'never let the passive export block or enter a merge' (bd-sync discipline) and 'a merge failure in the Section 3 loop = needs-rebase'. The second silently assumes the first still holds mid-loop. It does not.
design:
Two independent fixes; do BOTH (they fail differently).

(1) Keep bd OUT of the merge loop. Section 3 should pre-compute every merge message BEFORE the first merge — one bd read pass over the accepted set, cached (assoc array or tmp file), then a merge loop that touches only git. This is the root cause: no bd call inside the loop, no re-dirtying. Same rule already applies to the Section 4 GC loop, which calls 'bd show <id> --json' per iteration to read review_worktree between 'git push --delete' calls.

(2) Make the conflict classifier honest rather than positional. A failed 'git merge' must not be assumed to be a textual conflict. Distinguish on the actual failure:
      - stderr matches 'would be overwritten by merge' -> NOT a conflict. Restore the jsonl and RETRY the same merge once; only escalate if it fails again.
      - 'git ls-files -u' non-empty (unmerged index entries) -> a real textual conflict -> abort -> needs-rebase kick-back.
    A needs-rebase kick-back must be justified by real conflicting paths, never by 'the merge command exited non-zero'.

Optionally (3): assert a clean tree at the top of each loop iteration ('git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet'), so the invariant is checked rather than assumed — note plain 'git diff --quiet' is insufficient (a STAGED jsonl reads clean), which is the exact trap Section 3's own comment documents.
acceptance_criteria: land/SKILL.md Section 3 pre-computes all merge messages before the merge loop, so no bd command runs between merges; the Section 4 GC loop likewise reads its bd metadata up front. A non-zero 'git merge' is classified by inspecting the failure ('would be overwritten by merge' -> restore-and-retry; unmerged index entries -> real conflict -> needs-rebase), never by exit status alone, and a needs-rebase kick-back names the conflicting paths. Verified by a /land pass merging >=2 branches where a bd read occurs between them: all clean branches land, none is kicked back.
notes:
Surfaced by the /land pass of 2026-07-09 (merge 01d3c6a). The pass recovered by hand: titles were cached to files up front, jsonl restored, and the four false-conflict branches merged clean.

Blast radius: every multi-branch /land pass. Single-branch passes are immune (the pre-loop restore is enough), which is likely why this survived until a 7-branch queue. Severity is high because the failure mode is SILENT and INVERTED: it does not lose work, it manufactures busywork and corrupts the needs-rebase signal, and the branch it accuses is arbitrary (whichever came after the first bd read).

Related: lode-6ra (import.auto: false; jsonl is export-only), and the Section 3 comment that already warns 'a STAGED jsonl aborts git merge even though git diff reads clean' — the warning exists, but only guards the pre-loop restore.
PARKED 2026-07-09 pending lode-k5e. This branch's Phase 2 technical review ran /code-review + /simplify from the reviewer's own launch worktree, which sits at trunk HEAD with an empty diff — so the mandated review tooling analyzed nothing and its 'no issues found' is not evidence of a clean branch (lode-k5e). The Opus reviewer's hand review still happened and its findings stand; what is missing is the skill's independent 5-agent coverage (CLAUDE.md adherence, shallow bug scan, git-history context, prior-PR comments, code-comment compliance). Label ready-for-land was REMOVED so /land cannot land it. Deliberately NOT set to ready-for-code-review: that would let /code's step-1 sweep re-review it with the same broken tooling. Once lode-k5e is fixed, swap needs-rereview -> ready-for-code-review to re-enter Phase 2 for a real review.
RE-REVIEW 2026-07-09: promoted needs-rereview -> ready-for-code-review after lode-k5e landed (merge bad00ea) fixing the empty-diff review bug. metadata.review_head refreshed to the branch's CURRENT origin tip, which includes the FIRST technical review's refinement commits — those are legitimately part of the branch and are what must now be re-reviewed. This is not builder drift. The prior Phase 2 ran /code-review + /simplify against an empty diff, so its 'no issues found' carried no information; the reviewer's hand findings from that pass stand, but the skill's independent coverage never ran. Re-review from scratch under the new architecture (fetch land/<id>, check out into own launch worktree, /code-review high --fix trunk...HEAD).
