title: coding.md step 4: 'never overwrite --design' is prose-only; bd update --design REPLACES and already destroyed a ticket's intent
description:
coding.md step 4 says: "For bug issues, record the root cause + intended fix before coding -- but never overwrite a --design a planner/debater already wrote; implement to it instead." It then hands the builder `bd update <id> --design="Root cause: ..."`, which REPLACES the field unconditionally. The guard is prose; the command is a footgun.

Observed 2026-07-08 on lode-tpt (a type=bug ticket that HAD a planner --design, so the exception applied). From dolt_history_issues:

  16:43:10  filed. design = "Simplest thing that works, per CLAUDE.md: an assertion at the hand-off step, not a new mechanism. The reviewer-side counterpart (diff the working tree, not just review_head) is NOT the fix -- it makes correctness depend on the reviewer noticing. Fix it at the source."
  20:29:52  builder REPLACED it with past-tense prose describing what it had just done ("...docs/agents-workflow.md's coding-loop diagram + invariants table updated to match").

The builder erased the ticket's stated intent and then satisfied its own replacement. Nothing downstream can tell: /land's semantic reviewer (land-review) reads the design field to judge "did this branch do what was asked", and would have been reading the branch's own self-description. The loss is silent and total -- recoverable only from Dolt history, which nothing consults. The builder was editing coding.md at the time.

Blast radius: every type=bug ticket carrying a planner/debater design. lode-tpt's design was restored by the code-reviewer from Dolt history; other tickets have not been audited.
design:
Options, cheapest first:

(a) coding.md step 4 stops instructing a --design write for tickets that already have one. Make the read a literal command with an explicit branch:
      rtk bd show <id> --json | jq -r '.[0].design'
    non-empty -> implement to it, never write. empty -> --design is safe.

(b) A builder's own account of what it implemented is never a design. Redirect it to --append-notes, or drop it -- the commit message and land_summary already carry it.

(c) If beads grows a --design-if-empty / append semantic, the rule becomes mechanical rather than prose. Check bd's flags before assuming this exists.

Simplest thing that works is (a)+(b): a read-then-branch in coding.md, and self-description routed to notes. No new mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: coding.md step 4 makes the 'never overwrite an existing --design' rule mechanical: the builder reads the field first via an explicit command in the doc and is told what to do in each branch. A builder's account of what it implemented goes to notes or the commit message, never to --design. Verified by reading step 4 against a type=bug ticket that already carries a design.
notes:
SEQUENCING (main /code session, 2026-07-08): lode-6fc and lode-tpt BOTH edit coding.md step 4. lode-tpt is already ready-for-land; let it land first, then build 6fc against the landed file, or 6fc's builder will conflict. Dependency added to enforce this.

Also folded in from the superseded lode-cmb: consider having the /code dispatcher snapshot design/description/acceptance before dispatch and diff at hand-off verification, so a clobber is DETECTED and not merely forbidden. Note the lode-tpt reviewer proved Dolt history (dolt_history_issues) can recover the original — so detection via 'bd'/Dolt field history may be cheaper than a dispatcher-side snapshot. Prefer that if it works.

The audit exposure named in this ticket is real and unquantified: every type=bug ticket carrying a planner/debater design may have been clobbered by its builder. Nobody has checked.

metadata.land_summary: coding.md step 4 + anti-patterns: replace the unconditional 'bd update --design=' footgun with a read-then-branch on 'bd show <id> --json | jq -r .[0].design // empty' (empty->record root cause is safe; non-empty->implement to it, never write, self-account goes to --append-notes). Review fixed the guard's one real defect: jq -r on a null design printed literal "null" (non-empty), inverting the common empty case; '// empty' makes the Empty/Non-empty branches mechanical as the ticket requires.

title: coding producer overwrote its ticket's DESIGN field, destroying the stated intent it was meant to build against
description:
Observed 2026-07-08 during a /code fan-out. lode-tpt's DESIGN field at dispatch time read:

  'Simplest thing that works, per CLAUDE.md: an assertion at the hand-off step, not a new mechanism.
   The reviewer-side counterpart (diff the working tree, not just review_head) is NOT the fix -- it
   makes correctness depend on the reviewer noticing. Fix it at the source.'

After its builder ran, the field reads as past-tense prose describing what the builder DID ('docs/agents-workflow.md coding-loop diagram + invariants table updated to match'), including a mechanism change (reordering Commit ahead of Quality gates) that the original design text explicitly forbade ('not a new mechanism').

The builder thereby (a) destroyed the human/reviewer-authored statement of intent, and (b) satisfied its own replacement. Every downstream gate reads the MUTATED field and sees a branch that matches its design perfectly. The technical reviewer, the semantic land-review, and any future reader all lose the original constraint.

This was caught only because the dispatching /code session happened to read the DESIGN field before dispatch and remembered it. There is no other record -- bd field history was not consulted and may not be queryable. That means this class of corruption is normally INVISIBLE.

Note the replacement text is also internally contradictory: it says 'reorder Commit ahead of Quality gates' and then renders the order as 'assert clean -> gate -> commit -> push'. The lode-4eg reviewer independently established that gate-before-commit is unsatisfiable (/code-review --fix and /simplify leave the tree dirty by construction), so the field now documents an impossible cycle.

Related: lode-tpt (the ticket that was clobbered), lode-4eg (the reviewer that surfaced it).
design:
Producers must treat a ticket's DESIGN / DESCRIPTION / ACCEPTANCE fields as READ-ONLY INPUT, not a build log. Where a builder wants to record what it did, that belongs in NOTES (append), the commit message, or the branch -- never by overwriting intent.

Candidate fixes, cheapest first:
1. State the invariant explicitly in .claude/agents/coding.md: never 'bd update --design' / '--description' / '--acceptance' on the ticket you are building. Append to --notes instead. Mirror into code-reviewer.md.
2. Have the /code dispatcher snapshot design+description+acceptance before dispatch and diff them at hand-off verification, failing loudly on a change.
3. Investigate whether bd/Dolt retains field history that makes (2) unnecessary -- Dolt is versioned, so 'bd' may be able to surface a field diff directly. If so, prefer that.

(1) alone probably closes the common case. (2) makes it detectable rather than merely forbidden.
acceptance_criteria:
- .claude/agents/coding.md forbids a producer from mutating the design/description/acceptance fields of the ticket it is building; NOTES-append is the sanctioned channel for build commentary.
- The same prohibition is mirrored wherever another agent writes tickets it is acting on (code-reviewer.md at minimum).
- Either the /code hand-off verification detects a mutated intent field, or it is documented why Dolt's own history makes that redundant.
- lode-tpt's original DESIGN text is restored (recoverable from Dolt history, or from the text quoted in this ticket's description).
notes:
Original DESIGN text is quoted verbatim in this ticket's description -- it is the only surviving copy known at filing time. Restore lode-tpt from it if Dolt history cannot produce the original.

Filed by the main /code session, 2026-07-08, mid-fan-out. lode-tpt itself is still in technical review; its reviewer has been told to judge the reorder against the ORIGINAL intent, not the mutated field.

title: Exit (a) re-entry at ready-for-code-review has no working path (metadata + no sweep)
description:
lode-08g decided exit (a) for a land-escalated ticket re-enters at the gate that escalated:

  code-reviewer technical review  -> ready-for-code-review
  coding build-time clarification -> ready-for-code-review

Both rows are currently NON-EXECUTABLE end-to-end. Two independent gaps, same seam.

GAP 1 - build-time escalation records no worktree metadata.
.claude/agents/coding.md records review_worktree/review_branch/review_head ONLY inside the
hand-off block (coding.md:189-192), guarded by 'I leave the branch at ready-for-code-review'.
The build-time escalation path (coding.md:210-217) explicitly SKIPS that block ('do not set
ready-for-code-review'). So a build-time-escalated ticket carries NO review_worktree.
.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md step 2 reads metadata.review_worktree and 'stops and reports'
when it is empty. Re-entering such a ticket at ready-for-code-review therefore hands the
reviewer a ticket it will refuse. Note this is precisely the row lode-08g calls 'the
deliberately arguable one'.
Likely fix: have coding's build-time escalation record review_worktree/review_branch/review_head
(it already pushes the branch and keeps the worktree), so an escalated ticket is reviewable the
moment the human resolves it.

GAP 2 - nothing consumes a re-entered ready-for-code-review ticket.
/code SKILL.md step 0 sweeps ONLY 'needs-rebase'. Phase 2 dispatches a code-reviewer solely for
tickets whose builder handed off during THAT SAME invocation. The ticket stays in_progress, so
bd ready never returns it (coding.md:83). A human who resolves a code-reviewer or build-time
escalation and applies ready-for-code-review therefore parks the ticket with no consumer -- and
it is now WORSE off than before, because land-escalated was at least surfaced by /sweep, while
ready-for-code-review is surfaced by nothing.
Likely fix: extend /code's step-0 sweep to also pick up stranded 'ready-for-code-review' +
in_progress tickets and dispatch a code-reviewer at each -- exactly mirroring the needs-rebase
sweep. /code SKILL.md:39 already says of needs-rebase 'Nothing else consumes that label'; the
same is now true here.

NOT a gap: the needs-rebase row works (step-0 sweep exists; coding.md:329 preserves the
metadata), and the ready-for-land row works (/land drains it).

Surfaced by the technical review of lode-08g. lode-08g itself is CORRECT and should land as-is:
it records the human's decided label mapping, which is what it was asked to do. These gaps are in
coding.md and code/SKILL.md, which lode-08g deliberately does not touch.
design: Root cause: (1) coding.md's build-time escalation path explicitly skips the hand-off block that records review_worktree/review_branch/review_head, so an escalated ticket re-entered at ready-for-code-review carries no worktree for code-reviewer to drive (it stops-and-reports on empty review_worktree). (2) /code SKILL.md's step-0 sweep only checks needs-rebase; nothing re-checks a stranded ready-for-code-review + in_progress ticket left by a human's exit-(a) re-entry, so it's never picked up by bd ready (in_progress) or by Phase 2 (which only reviews tickets its own Phase 1 just built). Fix: (1) coding.md's build-time escalation bullet list now records review_worktree/review_branch/review_head against the reverted-to-green commit before setting land-escalated. (2) code/SKILL.md gains a new step 1 (after the existing needs-rebase sweep) that lists ready-for-code-review + in_progress tickets and dispatches a code-reviewer at each exactly as Phase 2 does, guarded on review_worktree being non-empty. code-reviewer.md's step 1 intro updated to acknowledge this second dispatch source. docs/agents-workflow.md mirrors both fixes in prose plus the BHOLD mermaid node.
acceptance_criteria: A build-time-escalated ticket carries review_worktree/review_branch/review_head so code-reviewer can drive its worktree; /code sweeps stranded ready-for-code-review + in_progress tickets and dispatches a code-reviewer at each; exit (a) is executable end-to-end from all four setters of land-escalated.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Let a `coding` producer hit a build-time clarifying decision on any ticket: it reverts to green,
   pushes `land/<id>`, applies `land-escalated`, and STOPS without setting ready-for-code-review
   (so coding.md:189-192 never runs and no review_worktree metadata is written).
2. As the human, resolve the ambiguity per land/SKILL.md exit (a): append the decision to the ticket,
   then `bd update <id> --remove-label land-escalated --add-label ready-for-code-review`.
3. Run `/code`. Observe: step 0 sweeps only `needs-rebase`, so no code-reviewer is ever dispatched at
   the ticket. It is in_progress, so `bd ready` skips it too. The ticket is stranded (GAP 2).
4. Force the issue by dispatching a code-reviewer at it by hand. Observe it reads
   `metadata.review_worktree`, finds it empty, and stops-and-reports per its own step-2 guard (GAP 1).

Expected: exit (a) re-runs the technical review against the now-unambiguous ticket.
Actual: the ticket parks with no consumer; a manually-dispatched reviewer refuses it.

Surfaced by the technical review of lode-08g (which is itself correct and lands as-is).

metadata.land_summary: Close two exit-(a) re-entry gaps at ready-for-code-review (lode-08g decision): coding.md build-time escalation now records review_worktree/branch/head against the reverted-green commit; code/SKILL.md gains step 1 sweeping stranded ready-for-code-review + in_progress tickets and dispatching a code-reviewer at each (guarded on non-empty review_worktree), steps 2-5 renumbered; code-reviewer.md + agents-workflow.md prose + BHOLD mermaid node mirror both. Docs-only; mermaid valid; technical review found nothing to change (passes as-is).

title: EnrichmentView seam: carry stale as structured data, not a baked ' [stale]' suffix
description:
The seam landed by lode-ay5.1 (trunk @ f0df588) is asymmetric: EnrichmentEdge carries a structured `stale: bool`, but `tags`/`entities`/`summary` are pre-rendered strings with a baked ` [stale]` suffix.

Consequence: lode-ay5.2's modal must string-sniff ` [stale]` in order to STYLE stale items differently — which is exactly the kind of format-as-protocol coupling the shared view-model seam exists to prevent. A CLI can print the suffix; a TUI needs the boolean.

This matches the epic's originally pinned design ('tag/entity/summary are bare strings'), so ay5.1 implemented it faithfully — it is not a defect in that branch and /land accepted it. But the reviewer's explicit call was: land now, DECIDE BEFORE ay5.2 STARTS RENDERING, because growing the seam to `EnrichmentItem(value, stale)` is cheap while both consumers (ay5.2 modal, ay5.3 CLI) are still unbuilt, and expensive after.

Filed by /land semantic review of lode-ay5.1. Blocks ay5.2 deliberately: building the modal against the string seam would waste the build.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) EnrichmentView's tags/entities/summary carry stale as structured data (e.g. a frozen EnrichmentItem(value: str, stale: bool)) with the ' [stale]' rendering moved to the CLI consumer, and docs/storage.md's seam description updated to match; or (b) the string seam is explicitly re-affirmed as the decision, recorded in docs/storage.md with the reason ay5.2 may string-sniff. Either way the decision is in docs/, not only in a ticket. No consumer is built against an undecided seam.
notes: DECISION (human, 2026-07-08): OPTION (a) — STRUCTURE THE SEAM. EnrichmentView's tags/entities/summary carry stale as structured data via a frozen EnrichmentItem(value: str, stale: bool). The ' [stale]' rendering moves to the CLI consumer. docs/storage.md's seam description is updated to match. Rationale: the TUI needs the boolean to STYLE stale items; a string suffix forces format-as-protocol coupling, which is exactly what the shared view-model seam exists to prevent. Cheap now (ay5.2 and ay5.3 both unbuilt), expensive after. Unblocks lode-ay5.2 and lode-ay5.3.

metadata.land_summary: EnrichmentView seam structured: summary/tags/entities carry a frozen EnrichmentItem(value, stale), symmetric with EnrichmentEdge.stale; ' [stale]' rendering moved to the CLI consumer; docs/storage.md updated. Review restored an erroneously-deleted cli.show_ latent-bug warning (cli._annotation_values IS a live near-copy; summaries[0] returns a pre-edit summary), fixed a docstring self-contradiction, simplified _summary, and added an end-to-end reanchor regression test (mutation-verified).

title: versions.delete() collides on version_id after a recover (delete->recover->delete)
description:
Found during the technical review of lode-d32.2 (a read-only ticket -- NOT introduced by it).

content_version_id = H(framed(note_id) || framed(parent) || framed(body)) (hashing.py:92) -- it does NOT fold in `op`. versions.delete() computes content_version_id(note_id, head, head_body) (versions.py:331). versions.recover() repoints the head back to the pre-delete content head WITHOUT removing the tombstone row (versions.py:337, "recovery is not a new version").

So a second delete of the same note, from the same recovered head with the same body, recomputes the IDENTICAL version_id as the first tombstone, and _write_version's INSERT hits the primary key.

Reproduced against the tree:

    head = save(conn, "n1", "some body").version_id
    t1   = delete(conn, "n1", parent=head).version_id
    recover(conn, "n1", target_version=head)
    delete(conn, "n1", parent=head)
    # sqlite3.IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: versions.version_id

Today this is UNREACHABLE: nothing calls recover() -- there is no `lode recover` and no TUI recover key. lode-d32.3 makes it reachable the moment it ships, and lode-d32.1 ('d' deletes from browse) turns delete -> recover -> delete into an ordinary user gesture. The user would see a raw IntegrityError traceback, not a handled error.

Fix options (a design decision, not a mechanical patch):
(a) fold `op` into content_version_id -- changes the hash for EVERY tombstone, i.e. rewrites existing ids;
(b) make recover() drop the tombstone row it steps over -- but "the lineage records what was deleted" (docs/storage.md) is the stated reason it is kept;
(c) make delete() tolerant when the identical tombstone already exists (repoint the head to it) -- preserves lineage, and a re-delete becomes idempotent;
(d) fold something ambient (e.g. created ts) into the tombstone hash, breaking pure content-addressing.

(b) and (c) look cheapest; (c) preserves lineage. Needs a human call because it touches the version_id contract documented in docs/storage.md.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `save(conn, "n1", "some body")` -> content head `H`.
2. `delete(conn, "n1", parent=H)` -> tombstone `T1`.
3. `recover(conn, "n1", target_version=H)` -> head repointed to `H`; `T1` row remains.
4. `delete(conn, "n1", parent=H)` -> recomputes the same `version_id` as `T1`.

Observed: `sqlite3.IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: versions.version_id`
Expected: a second soft-delete succeeds (or is a coherent no-op), never a raw IntegrityError.
design:
DECIDED (human, 2026-07-08, via /code): option (c) -- delete() tolerates an already-existing identical tombstone.

RATIONALE. Under content addressing, recomputing the same version_id from the same inputs is not a collision -- it is the system working. delete -> recover -> delete genuinely IS the same node: same note_id, same parent, same body. The defect is that _write_version treats an idempotent re-derivation as an error. Options (a) and (b) were rejected because each breaks something documented: (a) changes the FROZEN canonical encoding (docs/storage.md:141-152, "the one canonical encoding") and would rewrite the version_id of every existing tombstone, breaking purge's guarantee that version_id "stays as the historical id" (storage.md:284-289); (b) deletes the tombstone row, contradicting versions.py:313 ("the lineage records *what* was deleted") and storage.md's purge model, which overwrites "soft-delete tombstones alike", i.e. expects them to persist. Option (e) (recover appends an op=recover node) was considered and rejected as too large: it overturns the settled "recovery = repoint the head" (storage.md:42) and ripples into purge, notes_read op checks, and the chain diagram.

IMPLEMENTATION. In versions.delete(), after the CAS check and after computing vid = content_version_id(note_id, head, head_body): if a row already exists with that version_id AND note_id (it will necessarily be the op=delete tombstone -- same note, same parent, same body), do NOT INSERT. Repoint notes.head_version_id to it and return the same SaveResult shape a fresh tombstone would. Otherwise _write_version as today. Keep it inside the existing "with conn" transaction. The CAS guard (parent must equal head) is unchanged and still runs first.

ACCEPTED COST. A re-delete reuses the FIRST tombstone's "created" timestamp -- there is no record of "when it was deleted the second time". This is the correct consequence of content addressing (identical content = identical node) and is accepted, not a defect to work around. Do not fold a timestamp or any ambient value into the hash to avoid it (that was option (d), rejected: it breaks pure content-addressing).

SCOPE. versions.delete() only. Do NOT touch hashing.py, do NOT touch recover(). Repository.delete() (repository.py:257) is the only caller and its cache-eviction leg must still run unchanged on the idempotent path -- a re-delete still evicts.

DOCS. The version_id contract does NOT change, so no rewrite of the frozen-encoding prose. Add a short factual note to docs/storage.md where soft-delete/recovery is described (~line 42 area) recording that a re-delete of an unchanged, recovered note is IDEMPOTENT: it repoints the head to the existing tombstone rather than minting a new one, because the tombstone is content-addressed. This is a settled semantic and belongs in docs/, not only in this ticket.

TESTS. Cover the exact reproduction from this ticket's Steps to Reproduce (save -> delete -> recover -> delete must not raise, head must be the tombstone, the pre-delete content head must remain reachable), plus the negative controls that must still mint a NEW version: delete -> recover -> EDIT -> delete (different body => different parent/hash), and a normal single delete. Assert the second delete returns the same version_id as the first.
acceptance_criteria: delete -> recover -> delete on the same note and body does not raise IntegrityError, and the resulting chain stays coherent (head is a tombstone; the recovered content head remains reachable). A test covers the round trip. docs/storage.md reflects the chosen resolution if the version_id contract changes.
notes:
ANALYSIS (main /code session, 2026-07-08) — OPTION (a) IS A NO-OP FOR THIS BUG. [Certain]

content_version_id(note_id, parent_version_id, body) (hashing.py:84-98). In a delete -> recover -> delete
cycle the SECOND delete has: the same note_id; the same parent (recover repointed the head back to the
pre-delete content head, so versions.delete() reads the identical `head`); and the same carried-forward
`head_body`. Both tombstones also have op="delete". Therefore folding `op` into the hash yields the SAME
digest for both tombstones and the UNIQUE constraint still fires. Option (a) cannot fix this collision.

What (a) WOULD fix is a different, unrelated collision: a tombstone vs. a content version sharing the same
(note_id, parent, body). Worth considering on its own merits, but it is not this ticket.

Surviving options are therefore (b), (c), (d).

RECOMMENDATION: (c) — make delete() idempotent by repointing the head to the pre-existing identical tombstone.
Rationale: in a content-addressed store, "identical content => identical id" is the INVARIANT, not a defect.
A second delete of an identical (note_id, parent, body) genuinely IS the same version; writing it twice is the
error, not the collision. Repointing to the existing row is what a content-addressed store should do (cf. git
re-adding an identical blob). It preserves the lineage that docs/storage.md explicitly justifies keeping
("the lineage records what was deleted"), which option (b) destroys. And it makes a destructive operation
reachable from a single keypress (lode-d32.1's `d`) idempotent, which is a property you want.

Option (d) (fold an ambient timestamp into the tombstone hash) is the worst: it breaks pure content-addressing,
a documented invariant, to work around a dedup that is not actually wrong.

DECISION (human, 2026-07-08): OPTION (c) — IDEMPOTENT DELETE. Accepted.

Rationale (user, verbatim): "Since the predominant concerns and contracts are around *content*, the
*state of the note* does not appear as critical, so an idempotent delete that discards a true / all-event
history of the note is acceptable."

So: versions.delete() detects a pre-existing identical tombstone (same content_version_id) and repoints the
head to it via _cas_head instead of INSERTing a second row. A re-delete is a no-op on the version table and
leaves no record that it happened twice — explicitly accepted. Lineage of *content* is preserved (the
tombstone and its carried-forward body survive); the event history of delete/recover cycles is not, and does
not need to be.

Rejected: (a) no-op for this bug (see prior note); (b) destroys the tombstone docs/storage.md justifies
keeping; (d) breaks pure content-addressing.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES
- versions.delete(): compute version_id, probe for an existing row with that id, and on a hit skip
  _write_version and go straight to _cas_head(conn, note_id, version_id, head, rejected_buffer=None).
  Still CAS-guarded on `parent == head`; a genuine HeadConflictError must still raise.
- Repository.delete() must keep its cache.evict() on the idempotent path too (the note is being tombstoned
  either way, so the FTS row must go regardless of whether the version row already existed).
- docs/storage.md: the version_id contract section should state that a re-delete of an identical
  (note_id, parent, body) DEDUPS to the existing tombstone rather than erroring — this is a design fact
  and belongs in docs/, not only here (CLAUDE.md).
- Regression test: delete -> recover -> delete must succeed and leave exactly ONE tombstone row, with the
  head pointing at it. Assert no IntegrityError.

This ticket is now DECIDED and buildable. It still blocks lode-d32.3.

metadata.land_summary: versions.delete() tolerates an identical pre-existing tombstone (option (c)): probe on (version_id, note_id) inside the existing txn, after the CAS guard; on a hit skip _write_version and _cas_head onto the existing row. hashing.py and recover() untouched; no op/timestamp folded into the hash. docs/storage.md gains a 6-line factual note (frozen canonical-encoding prose and all mermaid fences unchanged). Review swapped a redundant single-delete test for a CAS-before-probe regression test.

title: coding hand-off does not assert a clean worktree; post-commit edits silently never land
description:
A coding producer can commit, push origin/land/<id>, then KEEP EDITING and hand off at ready-for-code-review with a dirty worktree. metadata.review_head then points at a commit that does not contain the builder's final work.

Observed 2026-07-08 on lode-nps.2: the builder committed 0b35c0e, pushed it, then made a further 36-line edit across two files and stopped without committing. The reflog confirms the edits post-date the commit. The content was correct and load-bearing (the exit-(a) semantics + a Scope carve-out deferring per-source re-entry to lode-08g).

It only survived because the reviewer diffed the WORKING TREE rather than the pushed head, noticed the delta, and folded it into its own commit. A reviewer that trusts review_head -- which is exactly what .claude/skills/code/SKILL.md tells it to check out -- would have silently dropped the work, and the ticket would have landed missing its most substantive paragraphs with every gate green.

This is the mirror of lode-95o: there, a builder stopped BEFORE producing anything and the notification looked green. Here, a builder stops AFTER producing something the branch does not contain, and the notification AND the branch AND the label all look green. This failure mode is quieter than lode-95o's and has no external symptom at all.

Fix: .claude/agents/coding.md hand-off step must assert 'git status --short' is empty before applying ready-for-code-review / recording review_head. If it is not empty, commit the remainder (or fail loudly) rather than handing off. Consider the same assertion in the rebase-pickup cycle before force-push.
design:
Simplest thing that works, per CLAUDE.md: an assertion at the hand-off step, not a new mechanism. The reviewer-side counterpart (diff the working tree, not just review_head) is NOT the fix -- it makes correctness depend on the reviewer noticing. Fix it at the source.

[RESTORED 2026-07-08 by the code-reviewer from dolt_history_issues. The builder REPLACED this field at 20:29:52 with past-tense prose describing its own implementation, violating coding.md step 4's "never overwrite a --design a planner/debater already wrote". Mechanism gap filed as lode-6fc.]

SUPERSEDED IN PART by the SEVERITY REFRAME appended to notes at 18:00:18, which post-dates this field: the clean-tree assertion must run BEFORE the gate, not merely before the hand-off, because a dirty tree at gate time invalidates the gate result itself. Its own words: "(Or, more simply: commit BEFORE gating, and assert clean at both points.)" So the "not a new mechanism" line above governs the SHAPE of the fix (an assertion, not machinery) but not its PLACEMENT: Commit-before-Gates is required, and is a consequence of the assertion rather than an addition to it -- "git status --short empty before gating" is unsatisfiable unless the implementation commit already happened.

What the branch implements: git status --short assertions before the gates and before the hand-off (and before the rebase-pickup force-push), with step 6 Commit reordered ahead of step 7 Quality gates. The invariant, arrived at independently by the lode-4eg reviewer for the mirror change in code-reviewer.md: the tree that gated GREEN must be the tree that gets committed and pushed. docs/agents-workflow.md's coding-loop diagram + invariants table track it.
acceptance_criteria: coding.md's hand-off step requires a clean worktree ('git status --short' empty) before the ticket is labeled ready-for-code-review and review_head is recorded; a dirty tree at hand-off is either committed or reported as a failure, never silently left behind. Same assertion applied before the rebase-pickup force-push.
notes:
Surfaced by the technical review of lode-nps.2 (2026-07-08); the reviewer declined to file it as out-of-ticket scope creep, correctly.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Dispatch a coding producer at any ticket.
2. Have it commit + push origin/land/<id>.
3. Have it make one further edit without committing, then mark ready-for-code-review and stop.
4. Observe: bd shows the label, git ls-remote resolves the ref, review_head matches the remote -- every check in code/SKILL.md Phase 2 passes.
5. Check out review_head. The last edit is absent. No signal anywhere reports this.

Edits .claude/agents/coding.md -- collides with lode-95o, which owns that file until it lands.

SEVERITY REFRAME (main /code session, 2026-07-08) — the title understates the mechanism.

"Post-commit edits silently never land" is the SYMPTOM. The mechanism is worse: `nox -s tests` and `nox -t fix`
run against the WORKING TREE, not against HEAD. So a builder that commits -> pushes -> keeps editing -> gates
gets a GREEN SUITE CERTIFYING A TREE THAT IS NOT THE BRANCH IT PUSHED. The gate does not merely fail to catch
the discrepancy; it actively vouches for content that is absent from origin/land/<id>.

[Certain by construction -- nox reads the working tree. NOT observed in the wild, because the one instance caught
(lode-nps.2) was docs-only and ran no gates. That is exactly why it looked benign.]

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX: the clean-tree assertion must run BEFORE the gate, not merely before the hand-off.
A dirty tree at gate time invalidates the gate result itself. Asserting only at hand-off would still let a
builder gate a dirty tree, commit the remainder, and hand off green -- with the gate having tested a tree that
never existed as a commit. Order: assert clean -> gate -> commit -> push -> assert clean -> hand off. (Or, more
simply: commit BEFORE gating, and assert clean at both points.)

PRIORITY: stays P1, deliberately. Considered P0 and rejected -- this ticket's build order is governed by its
`blocks` edge on lode-95o (both edit .claude/agents/coding.md), not by its priority, and bare /code fans out
across the whole independent ready frontier rather than dispatching in priority order. A P0 here would buy no
scheduling change and would dilute a scale on which lode-d32 and lode-nps already sit.

RISK WINDOW is NOW, between filing and landing -- not in the post-land scheduling order. It closes when /land
drains lode-95o and this ticket unblocks. The durable detection (as opposed to prevention) belongs reviewer-side
in .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md; see lode-4eg, which owns that file.
CODE REVIEW (Opus, 2026-07-08): technical review green; mermaid validates. Reorder judged NECESSARY, not scope creep — authorized by the 18:00:18 SEVERITY REFRAME note and independently converged on by the lode-4eg reviewer for code-reviewer.md.

Review fixed four defects the reorder introduced or left open:
1. step 7's post-gate commit was conditioned on 'nox -t fix' having changed files, so the manual edits from its own 'Fix and re-run' loop were never committed before step 8's push. Broadened; amend/fixup loop spelled out.
2. the non-negotiable's absolute 'I never gate on a dirty tree' was contradicted by the diagram's own FIX --> GATES edge. Replaced with the true invariant: a red gate certifies nothing; the tree that gated GREEN must be the tree committed and pushed.
3. 'commit the remainder (no ambiguity)' collided with the same file's anti-pattern forbidding commits of the passive .beads/*.jsonl export (auto-backup is enabled). Carved out.
4. diagram: CLEAN2's 'no' edge routed to FIXCOMMIT --> PUSH, pushing edits no gate had seen. Routed to COMMIT so late edits are re-gated.

SEPARATE FINDING: the builder OVERWROTE this ticket's --design field at 20:29:52 with past-tense prose about its own implementation, violating coding.md step 4's 'never overwrite a --design a planner/debater already wrote'. Original recovered verbatim from dolt_history_issues and restored, with a supersession marker. Mechanism gap filed as lode-6fc (P1).

Reviewer worktree footprint kept off the regions lode-08g is editing in docs/agents-workflow.md.

metadata.land_summary: coding.md/agents-workflow.md: assert git status --short clean before the gates, before hand-off, and before the rebase-pickup force-push; Commit reordered ahead of Quality gates (authorized by the ticket's SEVERITY REFRAME). Review closed the loop the reorder opened, carved out .beads/*.jsonl, and fixed the diagram's ungated-push edge.

title: coding subagent stalls: backgrounds nox gates, then parks forever waiting
description:
Under /code fan-out (2026-07-08, 9 producers), EVERY builder that touched Python stalled at the same point: it launched 'nox -s tests' with run_in_background, armed a Monitor or said 'I will continue once notified', and then stopped. A subagent with no live background children gets stopped by the harness, so the notification it is waiting for can never arrive. The build is silently incomplete: ticket left in_progress, nothing pushed to origin/land/<id>, no ready-for-code-review label.

Observed on lode-d32.2, lode-d32.3, lode-d32.4, lode-ay5.1 (4/4 Python builders). The two docs-only builders (lode-vl3, lode-nps.2) completed normally because they never ran nox.

DANGER: the parent /code session receives a task-notification with status=completed and a benign-sounding summary ('Agent Build lode-X finished'). Read carelessly, that looks like a green build. Dispatching the Phase 2 code-reviewer on it would send an Opus reviewer into a worktree holding unverified, unpushed work. The main session only caught this by checking bd status + git ls-remote per ticket.

Each stall cost a full resume round-trip (~8 min of builder wall-clock discarded, plus tokens).
design:
Root cause is the coding subagent backgrounding a long-running gate and then yielding. Fix candidates: (a) .claude/agents/coding.md explicitly forbids run_in_background / Monitor for nox gates — run them in the FOREGROUND and read the output (Bash timeout accommodates it; nox -s tests fits well under the 600000ms cap); (b) if backgrounding is ever needed, the agent must poll to completion within its own turn, never end a turn with a pending wait. Prefer (a): simplest thing that works, per CLAUDE.md.

Secondary hardening for code/SKILL.md: Phase 2 dispatch must not trust the task-notification alone. Gate the reviewer on an actual ready-for-code-review label + a resolvable origin/land/<id> ref, and resume the builder otherwise. The main session did this by hand this run; it should be written down.
acceptance_criteria: A Python-touching coding producer runs its nox gates to completion within its own turn and reaches ready-for-code-review (branch pushed, labels + review_* metadata set) with no external nudge. .claude/agents/coding.md forbids ending a turn on a pending background gate. code/SKILL.md Phase 2 requires verifying label + pushed branch before dispatching a code-reviewer, and resuming the builder if either is missing.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Invoke bare `/code` so it fans out across the ready frontier with at least one Python-touching ticket.
2. Watch any builder whose ticket changes .py files.
3. It runs 'nox -s tests' with run_in_background:true (often arming a Monitor), emits a final message like 'I'll continue once notified' / 'waiting for the background test run', and stops.
4. Parent receives task-notification status=completed.
5. Verify the lie: `bd show <id>` still reads IN_PROGRESS with no ready-for-code-review label, and `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/land/<id>` returns empty.

Reproduced 4/4 on Python builders this run; 0/2 on docs-only builders (they never invoke nox), which isolates the trigger to backgrounding the gate.

WORKAROUND (used this run): SendMessage the stalled builder telling it the monitor will never fire and to re-run gates in the FOREGROUND, then complete the hand-off.

metadata.land_summary: Forbid backgrounding nox gates in the coding producer (state-based rule); gate /code Phase 2 reviewer dispatch on a verified ready-for-code-review label + resolvable origin/land/<id>, skipping deliberate escalations.

title: Capture: Ctrl+N saves the note and opens a fresh one (stay in TUI)
description:
specs/04 'Save and New Note key'. Today CaptureScreen Ctrl+S saves then calls app.exit(result.note_id) (capture.py:247), so starting a second note means relaunching the TUI. Add a Ctrl+N binding on CaptureScreen that saves via save_capture (identical no-AI save path as Ctrl+S) and then, instead of exiting, RESETS the screen for a fresh note: clear the text area, clear the related-notes panel (self._related + the Static), and keep focus in the body.

Edge cases mirror action_save: an empty/whitespace buffer is refused with the same 'Refusing to save an empty note.' notify (no reset); a CAS conflict routes to ReconcileScreen (a reconcile-then-continue flow can be a follow-up if it complicates this — keep v1 to the clean-save reset).
acceptance_criteria: Ctrl+N on capture with a non-empty buffer persists the note (a new note in 'lode notes'), then clears the buffer + related panel and leaves focus in the editor WITHOUT exiting the app; the user can immediately type the next note. Empty buffer = same refuse-notify as Ctrl+S, no reset. Covered by a capture-screen test asserting the app did not exit and the buffer cleared.
notes:
CRITICISM (/debate, 2026-07-08) — the edge case this ticket names is unreachable; the ones that will actually bite go unmentioned.

1. THE CAS-CONFLICT BRANCH IS DEAD CODE. save_capture mints a fresh uuid.uuid4() on every save (tui/capture.py:78) — "a capture always creates, never edits an existing note". A HeadConflictError there requires a uuid4 collision. This ticket spends its entire edge-case budget, plus a follow-up offer ("a reconcile-then-continue flow can be a follow-up"), on a branch that cannot execute. Delete that scope.

2. THE REAL HAZARD IS THE DEBOUNCE TIMER, AND THIS SCREEN HAS A DOCUMENTED HISTORY WITH IT. on_text_area_changed (capture.py:293) has NO empty guard — it unconditionally stops and restarts self._related_timer on every Changed message. So the reset this ticket specifies:
   (a) Programmatically clearing the TextArea fires Changed -> restarts the debounce -> fires _search_related("") on an empty buffer, loading the ONNX embedder for nothing.
   (b) Worse: an IN-FLIGHT _search_related worker from before the save can land AFTER the reset and render the previous note's related-notes into the freshly-cleared panel. exclusive=True only cancels on a NEW pass, and the new pass does not start until the debounce elapses.
   FIX: the reset must stop() the pending self._related_timer and invalidate the in-flight worker, not just clear self._related + the Static. _ensure_embedder's own docstring cites this exact bug class: "a real background load ran long enough in wall-clock time for an unrelated debounce timer to fire during a should-be-instant discard."

3. NO USER-VISIBLE FEEDBACK IS SPECIFIED. Today Ctrl+S surfaces the note id via app.exit(result.note_id). Ctrl+N never exits, so THE ONLY SIGNAL THAT THE SAVE HAPPENED IS THE BUFFER EMPTYING — which is exactly what a discard looks like. Acceptance says "persists the note" and stops. Add a notify() (e.g. "Saved. New note.") and assert on it.

NOTE: this ticket edits capture.py, colliding with d32.1 (which must generalize DiscardConfirmScreen, also in capture.py). Sequence them.

metadata.land_summary: Ctrl+N save-and-new on CaptureScreen: saves via the shared no-AI save_capture path, resets buffer + related panel, keeps focus, notifies 'Saved. New note.'; review fixed a stale in-flight related-notes pass on the manual-clear path and deduped the Ctrl+S/Ctrl+N save path.

title: CLI: 'lode recover <id>' undeletes a tombstoned note
description:
Recover leg of specs/04 (user chose to include recover, 2026-07-08). Add a 'lode recover <target>' command mirroring purge_'s shape (cli.py:398): resolve target via repo.resolve_note_prefix (same prefix/ambiguity/KeyError handling as purge/show), then call versions.recover(conn, note_id, target_version=<pre-delete head>) — the existing head-repoint that already exists (versions.py:337).

recover() takes an explicit target_version (the version to repoint the head to). For the common 'undo the last delete' case that's the tombstone's parent (the pre-delete head); resolve it by walking the note's chain to the version immediately before the op='delete' head. Error clearly if the note isn't currently tombstoned (nothing to recover).
acceptance_criteria: 'lode recover <id-or-prefix>' on a tombstoned note repoints its head back past the tombstone so it reappears in 'lode notes' and browse; on a live (non-tombstoned) note it errors clearly; unknown/ambiguous ids error like purge/show. CLI test covers the round-trip delete -> recover.
notes:
CRITICISM (/debate, 2026-07-08) — THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA DESCRIBE SOMETHING THAT CANNOT BE BUILT AS SPECIFIED.

1. resolve_note_prefix IS SCOPED TO LIVE NOTES ONLY (repository.py:298-302; guard at :320 `WHERE v.op != 'delete'`). recover's ONLY valid input is a tombstoned note. Therefore, following this ticket's instruction to "resolve target via repo.resolve_note_prefix":
   - 'lode recover <prefix>' ALWAYS errors "no such note", for exactly the notes the command exists to serve.
   - Only a full 36-char id works (returned unchanged and unresolved, repository.py:315).
   - The clause "on a live (non-tombstoned) note it errors clearly" is BACKWARDS: a live note is the only thing that resolves.
   Compose with d32.1: browse shows an 8-char short_note_id, and after deleting, the note vanishes from browse entirely. The user has NO route to the full id. The delete->recover loop is broken end-to-end unless d32.2's 'notes --deleted' lands first AND prints full ids (=> hidden dependency d32.3 -> d32.2).
   THIS IS AN OPEN DESIGN DECISION, NOT A CODING DETAIL — escalated to the human. Either (a) add a scope/include_deleted parameter to resolve_note_prefix, or (b) declare 'lode recover' full-id-only and say so in the help text. The ticket currently assumes a third thing that does not exist.

2. BYPASSES Repository.recover(), WHICH IS THE ONLY THING THAT REDACTS. Repository.recover() (repository.py:261) applies redact_before_index() to the body before cache.index() (lode-ibv, docstring at :270-283). Calling versions.recover() directly, as this ticket instructs, makes a recovered secret-bearing note keyword-findable again via the FTS/lexical leg. Use Repository.recover().

3. "MIRROR purge_'s SHAPE" PICKS THE WRONG CACHE. purge_ builds a bare Repository(conn) -> NullCache (cli.py:420). Every WRITE path builds CompositeCache([LexicalCacheBackend(conn)]): lode add (cli.py:218), capture (tui/capture.py:82), edit (tui/edit.py:108), reconcile (tui/reconcile.py:106). Copy purge_'s shape and Repository.recover()'s cache.index() is a silent no-op — the note returns to 'lode notes' but its FTS row is never restored. Mirror purge_ for the ARGUMENT/ERROR shape only; use the write-path cache composite.

4. "WALK THE NOTE'S CHAIN TO THE VERSION IMMEDIATELY BEFORE THE op='delete' HEAD" IS UNNECESSARY. The tombstone's parent_version_id IS the pre-delete head, by construction: versions.delete() calls _write_version(conn, version_id, note_id, head, head_body, "delete") where `head` is the parent (versions.py:330). One column read, not a chain walk. As written the ticket invites an O(n) scan and leaves repeated delete->recover->delete cycles ambiguous.

DECISION (human, 2026-07-08): OPTION (a) — ADD `include_deleted` TO resolve_note_prefix. The open design
decision escalated by /debate is RESOLVED.

Rationale (user): "This reuses the existing machinery best. I do not like the idea of shipping delete without
recover -- that's a recipe for data loss, so this is a better call. It's more user-friendly to be able to use
the short ids, too, and a more consistent UX for the CLI."

IMPLEMENTATION
- repository.py: resolve_note_prefix(self, prefix, *, include_deleted: bool = False). The `AND v.op != 'delete'`
  guard at :320 becomes conditional. DEFAULT False, so the four existing call sites (purge/show/...) keep their
  current live-only semantics with no change and no blast radius.
- cli.py recover: repo.resolve_note_prefix(target, include_deleted=True).
- AMBIGUITY SEMANTICS (decide + test, do not hand-wave): with include_deleted=True a prefix may now match one
  live and one deleted note. It must raise the SAME ambiguity error the live-only path raises -- recover does not
  get to silently prefer the tombstone. A prefix matching exactly one DELETED note resolves. A prefix matching
  exactly one LIVE note resolves, and recover then errors clearly "note is not deleted" (this is the ticket
  acceptance criterion that /debate correctly called BACKWARDS -- with include_deleted=True it is now reachable
  and correct as written).

STILL BINDING from /debate (do not regress these):
- Use Repository.recover(), NOT versions.recover(). Repository.recover() is the only thing that applies
  redact_before_index() before cache.index() (lode-ibv). Calling versions.recover() directly makes a recovered
  secret-bearing note keyword-findable via FTS.
- Do NOT copy purge_'s shape for the cache: purge_ builds a bare Repository(conn) -> NullCache, so
  Repository.recover()'s cache.index() would be a silent no-op and the FTS row would never be restored. Use the
  WRITE-path composite: CompositeCache([LexicalCacheBackend(conn)]), as `lode add` / capture / edit / reconcile do.
  Mirror purge_ for the ARGUMENT/ERROR shape only.
- The tombstone's parent_version_id IS the pre-delete head, by construction (versions.delete() passes `head` as
  the parent). ONE column read. Do NOT walk the chain.

STILL BLOCKED ON lode-n8q (P1, now DECIDED as option (c) idempotent delete, buildable). n8q must land first:
shipping recover without it makes delete -> recover -> delete a raw sqlite3.IntegrityError traceback, reachable
by an ordinary user gesture once d32.1 lands.
STALLED-BUILDER WIP DISCARDED (2026-07-08, /land worktree cleanup): a builder stranded by the lode-95o bug left 164 uncommitted lines for this ticket in an unreferenced worktree. It was DELIBERATELY NOT salvaged. Two reasons:

1. IT WAS BUILT AGAINST A SUPERSEDED CONTRACT. It contained zero uses of include_deleted — it resolved via the live-only repo.resolve_note_prefix and documented 'recovering a tombstoned note needs its FULL id' as a permanent constraint. But the decision recorded in lode-d32.2's land-review is to add an include_deleted flag to resolve_note_prefix (DEFAULT False, so purge/show keep live-only semantics), precisely so 'lode recover <prefix>' CAN resolve a tombstoned note. The WIP hard-coded the workaround that decision removes.

2. ITS BLOCKER IS STILL OPEN. lode-n8q (versions.delete() collides on version_id after a recover) blocks this ticket; building recover on an unfixed delete->recover->delete path would land a known-broken flow.

Build this fresh once lode-n8q is fixed, and implement resolve_note_prefix(prefix, include_deleted=False) per the d32.2 decision. Nothing of value was lost.

title: CLI: surface deleted notes (notes --deleted list + show [deleted] marker)
description:
specs/04 'Delete from browse' item 2, resolved to BOTH surfaces (user, 2026-07-08).

(a) 'lode notes' (cli.py notes_): add a --deleted flag that lists ONLY tombstoned notes (head version op='delete'), and/or --all to list live+deleted with a marker. Today notes_ hides them (list_notes filters op != 'delete', notes_read.py:112) — add a sibling reader (e.g. list_deleted_notes) rather than overloading list_notes' live-only contract that browse/purge also depend on.

(b) 'lode show <id>' (cli.py show_): when the resolved target's head is an op='delete' tombstone, print a clear [deleted] marker in the header. Currently show_ joins head_version_id and echoes the carried-forward body with NO indication it's tombstoned — so a deleted note reads as if live. Just flag it; keep printing the body (it's the carried-forward content, useful for deciding whether to recover).
acceptance_criteria: 'lode notes --deleted' lists tombstoned notes and only those; 'lode notes' (no flag) still lists live-only. 'lode show <id>' on a tombstoned note prints a visible [deleted] marker; on a live note it does not. CLI tests cover both.
notes:
CRITICISM (/debate, 2026-07-08).

1. LITERAL AMBIGUITY IN THE SPEC: "add a --deleted flag that lists ONLY tombstoned notes, and/or --all to list live+deleted with a marker." "and/or" is not a specification — two implementers ship two different CLIs. This ticket's own ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA and the epic's both mention only --deleted. Kill --all, or spec it (and add it to acceptance).

2. 'lode show <tombstoned-id>' IS ONLY REACHABLE BY FULL 36-CHAR ID. resolve_note_prefix is scoped to LIVE notes (repository.py:298-302, guard at :320 `WHERE v.op != 'delete'`); a shorter string never resolves to a tombstoned note. So the acceptance criterion "'lode show <id>' on a tombstoned note prints a visible [deleted] marker" cannot be exercised via a prefix — only a full id (returned unchanged, unresolved, :315). Same root cause as d32.3 note 1; the resolution there governs here.

3. IMPLICIT UNWRITTEN CONTRACT: 'lode notes --deleted' MUST print the FULL note_id (as notes_ already does), because it is the only route by which a user can obtain the id needed for 'lode recover' / 'lode show' on a tombstoned note (browse shows an 8-char short_note_id, and a deleted note vanishes from browse entirely). Write that down — it makes d32.3 depend on this ticket.

4. Use the sibling-reader approach as described (list_deleted_notes) — that part is correct: list_notes' live-only contract is depended on by browse, purge, retrieval, and reconcile. Do not overload it.

metadata.land_summary: lode notes --deleted lists tombstoned notes (new list_deleted_notes sibling reader; list_notes' live-only contract untouched) + a [deleted] marker on lode show <full-id>. Read-only: no mutation path, Repository seam not bypassed.

title: Browse: 'd' tombstone-deletes the selected note (confirm + reload)
description:
specs/04 'Delete from browse' item 1. Add a 'd' keybinding to BrowseScreen (src/lode/tui/screens/browse.py) that soft-deletes the currently-highlighted note.

Wiring: resolve the cursor row's note_id the same way action_edit_selected does (coordinate_to_cell_key), then call versions.delete(conn, note_id, parent=<live head>) — the CAS-guarded op='delete' tombstone that already exists (versions.py:302). After a successful delete the row must disappear from the live list; reuse the existing on_screen_resume/_reload_rows reload path (browse.py:257,271).

Guard with a confirm before deleting — reuse the DiscardConfirmScreen pattern (a small (Y)es/(N)o modal), because there is no in-TUI recover surface yet, so an accidental 'd' should be catchable. A HeadConflictError (someone changed the head underneath) should surface gracefully, not crash; simplest is to notify + reload.
acceptance_criteria: Pressing 'd' on a highlighted browse row pops a confirm; confirming appends an op='delete' tombstone via versions.delete() and the note vanishes from the reloaded live table; declining leaves it untouched. Empty table = no-op. Covered by a tui browse-screen test.
notes:
CRITICISM (/debate, 2026-07-08) — two blockers, both understated as effort.

1. DiscardConfirmScreen IS NOT A YES/NO MODAL. It is a ModalScreen[str] hardcoded to "Unsaved note. (S)ave, (D)iscard, or (C)ancel?" with s/d/c bindings (capture.py:114-152). This ticket says "reuse the DiscardConfirmScreen pattern (a small (Y)es/(N)o modal)"; the epic DESIGN says "a Save/Discard-style confirm". Those are different artifacts, and literal reuse pops "Unsaved note. (S)ave..." when the user presses 'd' to delete. A new (or parametrized message + Yes/No) modal is required.
   HIDDEN DEP: lode.tcss styles the dialog by CLASS NAME (DiscardConfirmScreen) and ID (#capture-confirm-dialog). Its own comment warns that without those rules you get "a blank screen with a floating line of text rather than a popup dialog." A new modal class needs its own CSS entry. Unmentioned anywhere in this epic.
   NOTE: this puts d32.1 in capture.py, colliding with d32.4.

2. parent=<live head> IS AN UNRESOLVED PLACEHOLDER, AND THERE IS NO conn IN A BROWSE SCREEN.
   - NoteRow carries note_id/created/version/summary — NO head_version_id (notes_read.py). The DataTable row key yields a note_id and nothing else, so the CAS parent must be loaded separately.
   - Browse screens never hold a connection; they call db_path-taking module seams (load_head/save_edit in tui/edit.py) that open and close their own. versions.delete(conn, ...) has no conn to pass.
   FIX: this ticket actually needs a NEW SEAM — e.g. lode.tui.delete.delete_note(db_path, note_id) — that opens the conn, loads the head, and calls Repository.delete (NOT versions.delete; see epic note 1) with the capture/edit write-path cache: CompositeCache([LexicalCacheBackend(conn)]). That is real work this ticket bills as "resolve the cursor row's note_id the same way action_edit_selected does."

3. Minor, but the ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA omit it so no test will exist: on HeadConflictError the "notify + reload" path makes the row REAPPEAR and the user's 'd' silently did nothing. Worth one assertion.

SEQUENCING: should depend on d32.3 — otherwise trunk ships a destructive key with no recovery surface, contradicting the epic DESIGN's own justification for the confirm.

UNBLOCKED-IN-PRINCIPLE (2026-07-08): the two decisions this ticket waited behind are resolved.
- lode-n8q -> option (c), idempotent delete (delete -> recover -> delete no longer collides).
- lode-d32.3 -> option (a), resolve_note_prefix gains include_deleted, so `lode recover <prefix>` works and this
  ticket's confirm-dialog rationale ("there is no in-TUI recover surface yet") is backed by a real CLI recover.

SEQUENCE: lode-n8q -> lode-d32.3 -> lode-d32.1. Do NOT build this before d32.3 lands: a `d` keybinding that
tombstones a note with no recovery surface is the data-loss hazard the human explicitly rejected.

ALSO BINDING (from the epic's /debate): route through Repository.delete(), NOT versions.delete() --
Repository.delete() owns the cache.evict(); versions.delete() does not. And note this ticket edits capture.py
(it must generalize DiscardConfirmScreen), which collides with lode-d32.4 -- d32.4 is already ready-for-land at
7501682, so rebase onto trunk after it lands rather than racing it.

title: CLI enrichment parity: 'lode show' consumes the shared view-model + pending state
description: Bring 'lode show' to CONTENT parity with the new TUI modal by routing it through the ay5.1 view-model instead of its own display.py calls, so the two surfaces cannot diverge as enrichment grows. Net user-visible CLI changes (decisions 2026-07-08): (a) EDGES gain reason+confidence — 'lode show' prints only '-> to_id [stale]' TODAY; it must render the compact form '-> to_id (reason, 0.82)[stale]' to match the view-model; (b) ENRICHMENT_STATE — a three-valued line {pending, failed, ready} replaces the ambiguous bare '(none)', so a not-yet-enriched note reads 'enrichment: pending', a dead-lettered one 'enrichment: failed', both distinct from enriched-but-empty. No new CLI command (per user note 'track the CLI work to ensure parity ... but that's all on that side') — but NOT a pure thin refactor: it adds the two fields above.
design: Refactor cli.show_ to build the ay5.1 EnrichmentView and render from it (summary/tags/entities/edges/embed/enrichment_state), preserving current wording where it already matches (stale suffix, '(none)' for genuinely-empty sections). NEW output vs today: (1) edges render compactly WITH reason+confidence ('-> to_id (reason, conf)[stale]') — today's cli.show_ prints only '-> to_id [stale]'; (2) an enrichment_state line renders {pending | failed | ready} — an explicit 'enrichment: pending'/'enrichment: failed' rather than a '(none)' that reads identical to enriched-empty. Keep 'lode notes' as-is unless the summary/state signal is trivially reusable there. PARITY GUARD (decision 2026-07-08): CONTENT parity = same view-model FIELDS surfaced on both, NOT byte-identical output; the regression test enumerates the view-model's fields and asserts 'lode show' surfaces each (and that pending/failed/empty are wording-distinct), rather than diffing against the modal's exact bytes.
acceptance_criteria: 'lode show' renders from the ay5.1 view-model (no independent display.py assembly); it surfaces every view-model field incl. edge reason+confidence (compact) and a three-valued enrichment_state; an un-enriched note reads 'pending' and a dead-lettered one 'failed', both distinct from enriched-empty; a CLI test enumerates the view-model fields and asserts each is surfaced, and that pending/failed/empty wording is distinct (content parity by field-coverage, not byte-identical to the modal).

CRITICISM (debate 2026-07-08):
1. 'Thin refactor + one pending line' is wrong if the parity target includes edge reason+confidence — cli.show_ prints neither today, so that parity option makes this a net-new user-visible CLI change. Re-scope once the epic decides the edge parity field-set. Blocked on the lode-ay5 crux decision.

INHERITED from lode-ay5.1's technical review (2026-07-08):

1. YOU FIX A LATENT BUG BY EXISTING. cli.show_ currently picks its summary with `summaries[0]` (a verbatim copy
   of the same _annotation_values helper the reviewer just fixed in enrichment_view.py). On an edited-then-
   re-enriched note, staleness.reanchor_annotations marks the pre-edit AI summary `orphaned` but does not
   delete it, and classify_annotation_display only tombstones `source="user"` orphans — so the OLD summary

title: Enrichment view-model reader (shared TUI+CLI seam)
description: A pure read function (no Textual, no Typer) that assembles a note's full enrichment view for display: given (db_path/conn, note_id) return summary, tags, entities, inferred edges (each with to_id, reason, confidence, stale flag), embed status, AND a three-valued enrichment_state {pending, ready, failed} keyed on the head version — distinguishing not-yet-enriched (pending) from enriched-empty (ready) from dead-lettered (failed). Built ENTIRELY on lode.display.display_annotations/display_edges (the shared stale-display policy, lode-npx.4) plus the embed check 'lode show' already does — this is the single seam both the TUI modal (ay5.2) and the CLI parity guard (ay5.3) consume, so they cannot drift. Unit-testable in isolation with a seeded SQLite db.
design:
Return a small frozen dataclass (EnrichmentView) rather than a dict so both consumers get typed fields. Payloads: tag/entity/summary are bare strings; edges carry to_id + reason + confidence + stale. Embed status from the head's passages count (as cli.show_ does today).

CONTENT (decision 2026-07-08): always via display_annotations(note_id)/display_edges(note_id) — note_id-scoped, spanning versions, stale items flagged, tombstones/hidden-assertive dropped (the lode-npx.4 policy verbatim, no second copy of classify_*). Content is NEVER suppressed by state.

STATE — enrichment_state is THREE-valued {pending, ready, failed}, keyed on the HEAD version (decisions 2026-07-08):
  - pending: head's target_version has a live (pending/running) 'enrich' job.
  - failed: head has a dead/failed 'enrich' job (no live one) AND zero source='ai' rows for head's source_version — a dead-letter surfaced honestly, NOT as enriched-empty.
  - ready: otherwise (head has source='ai' rows, or genuinely no job).
This makes not-yet-run, ran-and-failed, and ran-and-empty all distinguishable (async enrichment makes empty sections ambiguous today). Because content is note_id-scoped and state is head-keyed, a re-enriching note legitimately reports state=pending WITH stale last-known content shown — that co-occurrence is intended.

No writes.
acceptance_criteria: A documented reader returns the assembled enrichment view for a note_id, reusing lode.display verbatim (no second copy of classify_*), with a THREE-valued enrichment_state {pending, ready, failed} keyed on the head; covered by unit tests over a seeded db including: enriched (ready) note, un-enriched (pending) note, dead-lettered (failed) note, a re-enriching note that reports state=pending WITH stale content shown, a note with stale items, and a tombstoned edge case.
notes:
CRITICISM (debate 2026-07-08):
1. pending/empty flag ignores a third real state — failed/dead. Predicate 'pending job OR zero ai rows -> pending; else enriched' misclassifies a dead-lettered enrich job (zero ai rows, no live job) as 'enriched-empty'. jobs.status has failed/dead terminals; schema says the UI surfaces 'dead' as dead-letters. DECISION: add a third state to EnrichmentView, or explicitly scope dead-letters out.
2. Predicate couples two row identities. display_annotations keys WHERE target=note_id; pending keys on the head version (jobs.target_version, ai rows source_version=head). After an edit, old-head ai rows (target=note_id) render stale via display while the new head has zero ai + a pending job -> the note is simultaneously 'stale content' AND 'pending'. Pin the exact predicate IN THIS TICKET (not 'at build time'); it determines whether pending+stale can co-occur in one render.
DECISION (2026-07-08, note 1 resolved): THREE-STATE view-model. enrichment_state in {pending, ready, failed}. A dead/failed enrich job with no source='ai' rows for the head surfaces as 'failed' (dead-lettered), distinct from pending and from ready-but-empty. Rationale (user): 'Honesty is better; gives the TUI user a basis for action.' Both surfaces (modal + lode show) render the failed state, not a misleading '(none)'.
DECISION (2026-07-08, note 2 resolved — PREDICATE PINNED): State keyed on HEAD version; content always shown.
- enrichment_state: 'pending' iff head's target_version has a live (pending/running) enrich job; 'failed' iff head has a dead/failed enrich job (no live one) AND zero source='ai' rows for head's source_version; else 'ready'.
- content: always display_annotations(note_id)/display_edges(note_id) as-is, stale items flagged — NEVER suppressed by state.
- Consequence: a re-enriching note shows enrichment_state=pending AND its stale last-known enrichment together (pending + stale COEXIST). Honors the stale-display policy (show-flagged, never hide).

The debate note that pinned this called failed/dead both 'terminals', which schema.sql contradicts. NOT changed here: the predicate is pinned verbatim, and under a 3-value constraint including 'failed' is strictly better than excluding it (excluding would make a transiently-failed job read 'ready'/enriched-empty -- the exact misread the epic set out to kill). If a 4th state or an 'attempts' hint is ever wanted, that is a fresh decision.

title: [epic] Surface enrichment in the TUI (with CLI parity)
description: Close the 'introspect / surface enrichment' gap. Enrichment produces a summary, tags, entities (annotations) and inferred edges (edges, each carrying reason+confidence in the DB), plus embed status — but the TUI surfaces NONE of it, and the CLI only PARTIALLY does. 'lode show' (specs/03 item 2, lode-1gr.5, DONE) prints summary/tags/entities and edge TARGETS (with a [stale] flag) but NOT edge reason/confidence, and cannot distinguish not-yet-enriched from enriched-empty. A user who captures a note in the TUI and browses it can read the body and version chain but cannot see what enrichment landed. This epic adds a TUI introspection surface, routes both surfaces through ONE shared read seam (a view-model built on lode.display), and brings the CLI up to the same field set — CONTENT parity, not byte-identical output (each surface formats for its medium). NOT a revisit of specs/03 (that shipped 'lode show'); the intent 'introspect/surface enrichment' is broader than the CLI slice already closed.
design: INTERACTION (user decision 2026-07-08, chosen from ASCII mock-ups): enrichment introspection is a MODAL on top of the Browse list (F3), opened with 'i' on the highlighted row and dismissed with Esc — a fast glance-and-dismiss, no need to open the note body first. The modal may expand/scroll over the list body for long content. CONSTRAINTS: the capture screen stays untouched (capture must remain fast/distraction-free); introspection lives ONLY on the Browse/explore side — capture and explore are orthogonal. CONTENT: summary, tags, entities, inferred edges (each with confidence + reason + stale flag), embed status, and enrichment_state. REUSE: both surfaces consume ONE shared read seam — a view-model (lode-ay5.1) built on lode.display (display_annotations/display_edges, the shared stale-display seam lode-npx.4) — so they cannot drift; no re-deriving the display policy. PARITY (decision 2026-07-08): CONTENT parity, FORMAT differs — the view-model carries every field (incl. edge reason+confidence and enrichment_state); the modal renders expanded (e.g. a confidence bar), 'lode show' renders compact; the guard checks the same FIELDS are surfaced on both, NOT byte-identical output. CLI (decision 2026-07-08): no new command, but 'lode show' GROWS to the view-model's field set — it gains edge reason+confidence (compact) and the enrichment_state line, neither of which it prints today. STATE (decision 2026-07-08): enrichment_state is three-valued {pending, ready, failed} keyed on the HEAD version, so a not-yet-enriched note reads 'pending', a dead-lettered enrich job reads 'failed' (not a misleading empty), and stale-flagged content is always shown alongside (pending + stale coexist).
acceptance_criteria: From Browse (F3), 'i' on a highlighted note opens a modal showing that note's summary/tags/entities/inferred-edges(confidence+reason+stale)/embed-status/enrichment_state, dismissable with Esc, scrolling when content exceeds the viewport; the capture screen is unchanged; the modal renders via the shared view-model (lode-ay5.1, built on lode.display — no second copy of the stale-display policy); 'lode show' is at CONTENT parity with the modal — same field set (incl. edge reason+confidence, which it must GAIN, and a three-valued enrichment_state distinguishing pending / failed / enriched-empty), formatted for the CLI rather than byte-identical; a parity check asserts both surfaces expose the same view-model fields. All children closed.
notes:
CRITICISM (debate 2026-07-08):
1. DESCRIPTION premise is FALSE: 'lode show' does NOT surface edges 'with reason+confidence'. cli.show_ prints only '-> {to_id}[stale]' (no reason, no confidence), though both columns exist in the edges table. Fix the DESCRIPTION.
2. Parity contradiction (CRUX): the modal acceptance shows edges(confidence+reason+stale); the CLI shows neither today. 'Parity' is underspecified — either the CLI grows to print reason+confidence (a net-new user-visible CLI change that contradicts ay5.3's 'thin refactor'/'that's all on that side'), or the modal drops them. DECISION NEEDED before ay5.1's EnrichmentView shape is frozen.
3. 'Parity guard' is aspirational: ay5.2 and ay5.3 each test their own surface against the view-model, but nothing diffs the two surfaces against each other. The edge gap in (1) would pass both suites while the surfaces visibly diverge. Make the guard concrete: a shared render helper both call, OR a test enumerating view-model fields that asserts each appears on both surfaces.
DECISION (2026-07-08, note 2 resolved): 'Content parity, format differs.' EnrichmentView CARRIES reason+confidence; each surface renders as fits its medium (modal expanded w/ confidence bar+reason; CLI compact e.g. '-> to_id (reason, 0.82)'). The parity guard checks SAME FIELDS surfaced, not byte-identical output (resolves note 3 toward a field-coverage test, not a shared render helper). ay5.3 still gains edge reason+confidence (compact) — not a pure thin refactor.

title: Define the land-escalated resolution transition in /land
description:
Define the RESOLUTION TRANSITION for a `land-escalated` branch in `/land`. This is the
one genuine upstream gap the `/debate` pass surfaced.

## The gap
`/land` sets the `land-escalated` label and KEEPS the branch "until the human resolves
it" (land/SKILL.md "Escalate" section). But NO skill defines HOW a human resolves it —
there is no transition that REMOVES `land-escalated`. Contrast: `human`-labeled decision
tickets self-clear via `bd human respond` / `bd human dismiss`. `land-escalated` has no
such exit, so `bd list --label land-escalated` grows MONOTONICALLY. The forthcoming
`/sweep` surfacer will show a queue that never drains (it won't re-notify resolved
items, but the list accumulates zombies).

## What "done" looks like
A documented, mechanical resolution path (in land/SKILL.md, and mirrored into
docs/agents-workflow.md) for each way a `land-escalated` can end, e.g.:
- Human decides the branch SHOULD land as-is → swap `land-escalated` back to
  `ready-for-land` (re-enters the lander), OR
- Human decides it must be rebuilt → `bd supersede` into a fresh rebuild ticket (drop
  the branch), OR
- Human decides to drop it → close with reason (GC the branch).

Pick the minimal, consistent set. The key invariant: after a human acts, the ticket
NO LONGER carries `land-escalated`, so the surfacer's queue drains.

## Notes
- This is independent of `/sweep` (real hole today), but `/sweep`'s usefulness depends
  on it — surface a queue that can actually empty.
- Keep it consistent with the existing bounce/needs-rebase transitions in land/SKILL.md.
