title: Build /sweep — human-decision surfacer (surface-only)
description:
Build `/sweep` — the third `/loop` leg, a SURFACE-ONLY human-decision surfacer. It
scans `bd` for work that has stopped waiting on a human and nothing else consumes,
dedups it, and actively surfaces it (PushNotification + a running digest issue). It
writes no `trunk`, makes no decisions, dispatches no builders. It is the observability
layer that makes running `/code` + `/land` + `/epic-audit` unattended safe.

## Why (verified gap)
`/code` sweeps `needs-rebase`; `/land` bounces re-enter `bd ready`; `/epic-audit` runs
itself as `/loop /epic-audit`. The only pipeline outputs with NO downstream consumer
are the ones parked for a human:
- `land-escalated` label (set by `/land` escalate, incl. rebase-conflict) — queryable
  via `bd list --label land-escalated` — consumed by NOTHING.
- `human`-labeled `decision` ticket (set by `/epic-audit` escalate) — `bd human list`
  — only a human, manually.
- epic `epic-audited` + open + all children closed (`/epic-audit` never closes epics)
  — derived query — surfaced by NOTHING.

## Scope (in)
1. Surface the human-decision queue: `bd list --label land-escalated` ∪ `bd human list`.
   Notify on NEW items only; keep ONE running digest issue of the full current queue.
2. Surface epics ready for a human close-decision: type=epic ∧ status=open ∧
   labels ⊇ {epic-audited} ∧ every parent-child child closed.

## Non-goals (invariants — hold the line)
- Never writes `trunk` (that is `/land` alone).
- Never builds/lands/audits — not `/code`, `/land`, `/epic-audit`. NO audit dispatch
  (already `/loop /epic-audit`).
- Never makes/auto-defaults the human's decision — surface only (escalation-autonomy /
  wait-when-away norms).
- Does not own the livelock caps (deferred; see epic Design).
- Does not touch `.beads/issues.jsonl` (import.auto:false invariant, lode-6ra).

## Per-pass algorithm
```
1. bd dolt pull
2. queue = bd list --label land-escalated  ∪  bd human list
3. closable = epics(type=epic ∧ open ∧ labels⊇{epic-audited} ∧ all children closed)
4. current = queue ∪ closable
   last = read prior "human-decision digest" issue body   # DEDUP STORE = the digest issue itself
   new  = current − last
   if new ≠ ∅:
     upsert the digest issue with `current`               # Dolt-durable, cross-machine
     PushNotification summarizing `new`
     bd dolt push
5. report one line: queue depth, N new, M closable
```

## DECIDED (from debate)
- Dedup state lives IN the digest issue (Dolt-durable, travels cross-machine). A
  scratchpad state file re-notifies the whole queue from a second machine — REJECTED.
- This collapses "is it even a skill?" — the digest upsert + derived close-ready query
  justify a small skill; the state has a home (the issue), not a scratchpad file.

## Cadence
`/loop 30m /sweep` — escalations are exceptions, epics complete rarely; slow tick is fine.

## Dependency note (soft, not a hard blocker)
Without child #2 (`land-escalated` resolution transition) the surfaced queue never
DRAINS — `/sweep` still works (surfaces + dedups) but shows a growing list. Build order
preference: #2 before or with this, but this does not hard-block on it.
acceptance_criteria: Empty queue + no closable epics => clean no-op (no write, no notify). A new land-escalated/human item notifies exactly once; same queue next pass notifies nothing; resolved item drops out. A close-ready epic (epic-audited+open+all children closed) surfaced exactly once. Dedup survives across machines (state in the digest issue). Never writes trunk, dispatches no builder/lander/auditor, never touches .beads/issues.jsonl. A failing sub-step reports and the loop survives.
notes:
EMBEDDED DRAFT SPEC (verbatim, source of record — replaces scratchpad/sweep-spec.md):

# `/sweep` — human-decision surfacer (SPEC, pre-debate, v2)

**Status:** proposal, not built. Written to be stress-tested by `/debate`.
**v2 change:** verified against `.claude/skills/land/SKILL.md` and
`.claude/skills/epic-audit/SKILL.md`. The audit-dispatch leg is **dropped**
(already covered by `/loop /epic-audit`); escalation markers confirmed to exist;
scope narrowed to a near-read-only surfacer.

## One-liner

The third `/loop` leg. It scans `bd` for work that has **stopped waiting on a
human** and nothing else consumes — land/audit escalations, and epics ready for
a human close-decision — dedups them, and **actively surfaces** them
(PushNotification + a running digest). It writes no `trunk`, makes no decisions,
and dispatches no builders. It is the observability layer that makes running
`/code` + `/land` + `/epic-audit` unattended safe.

## Why it exists (verified gap)

`/code` sweeps `needs-rebase`; `/land` bounces re-enter `bd ready`; `/epic-audit`
runs itself as `/loop /epic-audit`. The only pipeline outputs with **no
downstream consumer** are the ones parked for a human:

| Human-parked signal | Set by | Queryable via | Consumed today |
|---|---|---|---|
| `land-escalated` label | `/land` escalate (incl. rebase-conflict) | `bd list --label land-escalated` | **nothing** ✗ |
| `human`-labeled `decision` ticket | `/epic-audit` escalate | `bd human list` | only a human manually ✗ |
| epic `epic-audited` + open + all children closed | `/epic-audit` (never closes epics) | derived query | **nothing** ✗ |

All three sit silent until a human happens to look. `/sweep` turns them into an
active ping.

## What changed after reading the skills (do NOT re-litigate in debate)

- **Audit dispatch dropped.** Bare `/epic-audit` is already a sweep (prefers
  `epic-ready-to-audit`, no-ops when none). Use `/loop 30m /epic-audit`; `/sweep`
  does not audit.
- **Audit regeneration loop does not exist.** `epic-audited` is terminal and
  excluded from both `/epic-audit`'s filter and `/land`'s re-flag guard. Auditing
  is once-per-epic. No cap needed.
- **Escalation markers confirmed present** — `land-escalated` and the `human`
  label. Leg B has real inputs; the earlier "no queryable marker" blocker is void.

## Responsibilities (in scope)

1. **Surface the human-decision queue.** Collect `bd list --label land-escalated`
   + `bd human list`. Notify on **new** items only; keep a single running digest
   of the full current queue.
2. **Surface epics ready for a human close-decision.** Epics that are
   `epic-audited`, still `open`, with every `parent-child` child closed —
   `/epic-audit` leaves these for the human and nothing else flags them.

## Non-goals (invariants — hold the line in debate)

- **Never writes `trunk`** (that is `/land` alone).
- **Never builds, lands, or audits** — not `/code`, `/land`, or `/epic-audit`.
- **Never makes or auto-defaults the human's decision** — surface only. Honors
  the escalation-autonomy / wait-when-away norms.
- **Does not own the livelock caps.** The bounce-lineage cap belongs in `/land`,
  the rebase-attempt cap in `/code`. `/sweep` only makes their escalations visible.
- **Does not touch `.beads/issues.jsonl`** (no add/commit/import — `import.auto:
  false` invariant, lode-6ra).

## Per-pass algorithm

```
1. bd dolt pull                              # fresh state (Dolt authoritative)
2. queue = bd list --label land-escalated  ∪  bd human list
3. closable_epics = epics where type=epic ∧ status=open
                    ∧ labels ⊇ {epic-audited}
                    ∧ all parent-child children closed
4. current = queue ∪ closable_epics
   new = current − last_surfaced          # dedup on stable IDs
   if new ≠ ∅:
     upsert ONE "human-decision digest" issue with `current` (full queue)
     PushNotification summarizing `new`
     persist last_surfaced := current      # durable store (see open Q)
5. report one line: queue depth, N new surfaced, M epics closable
```

No `bd dolt push` is required if `/sweep` writes no bd state (see dedup-store
question). If it upserts a digest issue, push after.

## Outputs / side effects

- **Near read-only.** Optional single digest issue (upserted in place) + a
  PushNotification on the delta. No trunk write, no merge, no GC, no builder
  dispatch. This is deliberately the lowest-privilege leg of the three.

## Termination & convergence (the reason `/sweep` earns its place)

Verified state of the 3-loop system:

- **Provably convergent:** the land/close path (monotone `bd close`) and the
  audit leg (`epic-audited` terminal, excluded from re-flag + sweep). No revert
  flip-flop exists — the one true revert hazard (jsonl auto-import reverting a
  close) is mutexed off in `/land` (`import.auto:false`, `restore
  --staged --worktree`, push-then-close-then-dolt-push ordering).
- **Residual non-terminating edges** (both route to a human-escape valve, both
  currently silent — which is `/sweep`'s justification):
  1. **Bounce rebuild chain** — `/land` bounce → supersede + rebuild ticket →
     `/code` rebuild → bounce again for the same reason → unbounded supersede
     chain. No lineage cap today. *Fix lives in `/land`* (cap lineage depth →
     escalate `land-escalated`); `/sweep` surfaces the escalation.
  2. **needs-rebase starvation** — only under *perpetual* trunk churn; a finite
     backlog quiesces, and a real rebase conflict escapes to `land-escalated`.
     Low priority; optional attempt-cap in `/code`.

So `/sweep` does not make the system converge — the caps do — but it makes the
non-convergent cases **visible** the moment they escalate, which is what lets you
run all three loops unattended.

## Cadence

`/loop 30m /sweep`. Escalations are exceptions and epics complete rarely; a slow
tick is fine and keeps cache-warmth irrelevant.

## Open design questions (FOR DEBATE)

1. **Surface channel.** PushNotification + digest issue vs. transcript-only vs.
   `bd`-native report. Which actually reaches a non-watching human, and is a
   digest *issue* worth the one bd write (and the `bd dolt push` it forces)?
2. **Dedup store.** Scratchpad state file (ephemeral, per-machine) vs. a durable
   `bd` marker. If `/sweep` may run on a different machine than last time, the
   `last_surfaced` set must be durable, else it re-notifies the whole queue.
3. **Should `/sweep` exist as its own skill at all,** or is it thin enough to be
   a `/loop`-able one-liner query + notify? Counter-argument for a skill: the
   dedup state and the digest-issue upsert want a stable home.
4. **Do the livelock caps get built alongside `/sweep`** (in `/land` and
   `/code`), or is surfacing-only acceptable for v1 on the bet that bounce-chains
   are rare? `/sweep` makes them survivable-but-visible; the caps make them
   impossible. Sequencing call.

## Acceptance criteria

- `/sweep` with an empty human-decision queue and no closable epics is a clean
  no-op — no write, no notification.
- A new `land-escalated` / `human` item triggers exactly one notification; a
  subsequent pass with the same queue notifies nothing; a resolved item drops out.
- An `epic-audited` + open + all-children-closed epic is surfaced as
  "ready to close" exactly once.
- `/sweep` never writes `trunk`, never dispatches a builder/lander/auditor, and
  never touches `.beads/issues.jsonl`.
- A failing sub-step reports and the `/loop` survives to the next tick.
CRITICISM (/debate 2026-07-08):
1. DIGEST-ISSUE IDENTITY UNDEFINED (blocker). The dedup design rests on upsert 'THE' digest issue + read 'the prior' digest body, but nothing specifies how /sweep FINDS that same issue next pass, esp. cross-machine. bd create mints a random ID; remembering it in scratchpad is the per-machine state the debate REJECTED. So it must be found by a durable query (reserved label e.g. sweep-digest, or title match) — unspecified in spec + acceptance. First-run bootstrap (no digest -> create) vs steady-state (find -> update) also unspecified. Two builders will guess differently. RESOLVE: name a reserved locator label + specify find-or-create bootstrap in acceptance. [DECISION PENDING - surfaced to human]
2. 'if new != empty' GUARD LEAVES RESOLVED ITEMS STALE (contradicts acceptance). Algorithm only upserts digest when new != empty. A pass whose ONLY change is a removal (item resolved, nothing added) has new = empty, so digest is NOT rewritten and shows the zombie until the next ADD triggers a rewrite. But acceptance says 'a resolved item drops out' — it doesn't, promptly. FIX: rewrite digest whenever current != last (add OR remove); only NOTIFY when new != empty. Separate the two triggers.
3. SOFT-DEP NOTE CONTRADICTS HARD DEP EDGE. Description calls the dep on .2 'soft, not a hard blocker', but the bd graph has .2 BLOCKING .1 (hard) — /code won't schedule .1 until .2 closes. Text and graph disagree; graph wins at dispatch. RESOLVE: drop the hard dep (keep as preferred-order note) OR delete the 'soft' language. [DECISION PENDING - surfaced to human]
4. SURFACE-CHANNEL DELIVERY UNVERIFIED (see also .4). Spec open Q#1 (which channel reaches a NON-WATCHING human) was listed FOR DEBATE but only the dedup-store half got resolved. Whether PushNotification from an unattended /loop /sweep actually reaches an away human is never confirmed, yet scope+acceptance hardcode it. If it only renders in an unwatched transcript, /sweep degrades to 'writes a bd issue nobody sees'. RESOLVE: verify PushNotification delivery semantics BEFORE build; make acceptance assert delivery-to-away-human, not just 'a notification was emitted.'
DECISION (human, 2026-07-08) — Finding #1 RESOLVED: digest locator = a RESERVED LABEL (e.g. sweep-digest). /sweep queries bd list --label sweep-digest; 0 rows -> create + add-label (bootstrap); 1 row -> update; >1 -> surface duplicate + stop. Rationale: it is another label but its purpose is clear w.r.t. the label/state diagram. DOC IMPACT: the new sweep-digest label must be added to the label/state diagram + label glossary in docs/agents-workflow.md (record in .4).
DECISION (human, 2026-07-08) — Finding #3 RESOLVED: the dep on .2 is HARD (keep the graph edge; .2 blocks .1). /sweep ships only once the queue can drain. The 'Dependency note (soft, not a hard blocker)' paragraph in this ticket's DESCRIPTION is VOID/superseded — treat .2 as a hard blocker. (Kept as a superseding note rather than rewriting the long embedded description; builder should honor this note over the description prose.)

metadata.land_summary: /sweep surface-only human-decision surfacer; review restored the specified PushNotification channel, reverted a false docs/decisions.md fact, and fixed bootstrap-never-notifies + partial-failure digest truncation.

title: Stop mirroring httpx 200-OK lines to the console (work/ask); errors only
description: specs/03-tui-features.md item 4. The anthropic SDK's httpx transport logs 'HTTP Request: POST ... 200 OK' at INFO on the 'httpx' logger, which the root console handler mirrors to stderr during 'work'/'ask'. The end user doesn't need to see 200s. In src/lode/logconfig.configure_logging, raise the 'httpx' logger to WARNING for console output (keep lode's own INFO), so successful requests are silent and only httpx WARNING+/errors surface. Apply globally (every command benefits), not just work/ask. Confirm the file handler still records what's useful for debugging.
acceptance_criteria: 'lode ask'/'lode work' no longer print httpx 2xx lines to stderr; the file handler (lode.log) STILL records httpx 200 lines; an httpx WARNING+/error still surfaces on the console; lode's own INFO console lines are unaffected.
notes: MECHANISM (decided 2026-07-06): do NOT bump the 'httpx' logger level — that would strip 200s from the file handler too. Instead attach a logging.Filter to the CONSOLE/stream handler only that drops httpx INFO records (name.startswith('httpx') and levelno < WARNING), leaving the file handler (tagged _lode_file in logconfig) untouched so lode.log keeps the 200s for debugging. In logconfig.configure_logging: the stream handler is the one basicConfig installs on root; add the filter there (and note the TUI's console=False path removes stream handlers entirely, so the filter is a console-only concern). httpx WARNING+/errors still reach the console.

title: work: --wait option that blocks until submitted jobs are processed (bounded)
description: specs/03-tui-features.md item 3. Add a 'lode work --wait' (a.k.a. --until-done) option that polls — reconcile + drain + batch-collect — until no pending/running jobs remain, so the user doesn't have to re-run 'work' to see async (Batches API) enrich jobs land. Bound it with a timeout ('up to some reasonable time') so it can't hang forever on a stuck batch; on timeout, exit non-zero with a clear message naming the still-in-flight jobs. Reuse the existing --loop/--interval machinery and WorkerLock in cli.work; the difference from --loop is the exit-when-drained condition + timeout. Default timeout should be configurable via Settings (docs/configuration.md) with a sensible default.
acceptance_criteria: 'lode work --wait' returns only once the queue is fully drained (incl. batch enrich results collected) or the timeout fires; on timeout it exits non-zero and names the outstanding jobs; without --wait behaviour is unchanged (one-shot).
notes: DESIGN DECISION (async latency, 2026-07-06): --wait is bounded and MAY legitimately time out on slow enrich batches (Batches API can take minutes-to-hours) — this is accepted, not a bug. On timeout with jobs in-flight, exit non-zero and NAME the outstanding jobs (as specified). Document in help text / docs that --wait suits embed-heavy or small-batch cases, and that large async enrich loads may need a re-run. Do NOT switch enrich to the synchronous _enrich_handler fallback under --wait. ---- TERMINATION INVARIANT (verified against worker.py): batch-submitted enrich jobs stay status='running' with batch_handle set and are EXCLUDED from _reclaim_stale_running; they only flip running->done when a later drain's _batch_collect_enrich pre-step polls the ended batch. So the 'no pending/running jobs remain' condition is correct ONLY because _batch_collect_enrich (top of every drain) eventually completes them. Do NOT dead-letter or reclaim in-flight batch jobs in the wait loop.

metadata.land_summary: Add 'lode work --wait' (--until-done): polls reconcile+drain until the queue drains or Settings.work_wait_timeout_s (default 1800s) elapses, then exits non-zero naming outstanding jobs; rejects --wait+--loop; adds work_wait_timeout_s knob (config.py + docs/configuration.md).

title: work: print a per-job outcome summary of what enrichment/embedding produced
description: specs/03-tui-features.md item 2 (chosen surface: in-flow work summary). Today 'lode work' only prints 'drained N job(s)' — the user can't tell what enrichment did. Have work report, per processed job, what happened: e.g. 'enriched <short-id>: 4 tags, 2 entities, 3 edges, summary set' and 'embedded <short-id>: 3 passages'. enrich_version already logs these counts (src/lode/enrich.py: 'enrich_version: version=.. tags=.. entities=.. edges=.. summary=..'); the async/batch path lands via lode.worker.drain + collect_enrich_batch. acceptance_criteria: A drain pass that COLLECTS a completed enrich batch prints a human-readable per-note line (tags/entities/edges/summary); a drain pass that runs embed jobs prints a per-note passage-count line; a no-op drain still prints the existing 'drained 0 job(s)'. notes: SEAM CORRECTION (verified against worker.py): enrichment is async-batch. drain() returns int (main claim-run loop only) and its docstring notes batch pre-step activity is NOT in the return count. So there are TWO channels, not one 'drain return path': (a) EMBED counts land synchronously via run_one in the main loop; (b) ENRICH counts land on a LATER drain via the _batch_collect_enrich pre-step (batch results). The function is _batch_collect_enrich (private), NOT 'collect_enrich_batch'. Emit the enrich summary from the collect pass, not the submit pass. Depends on lode-1gr.6 (--wait) because that is what makes enrich outcomes observable within one command; a bare one-shot work only SUBMITS the batch and prints 'drained 0 job(s)'.

title: purge: accept an unambiguous note-id prefix, not just the full 36-char id
description: specs/03-tui-features.md item 1 (ergonomics). With Browse/notes showing short ids, requiring the full UUID for 'lode purge' is hostile. Let 'lode purge <prefix>' resolve an unambiguous note_id prefix to the full id before delegating to Repository.purge (src/lode/cli.py purge + src/lode/repository.py). A prefix matching zero notes -> clear 'no such note' error (exit 1, as today); a prefix matching >1 note -> 'ambiguous' error listing the candidates (exit 1); exactly one match -> purge it. Full ids must still work unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: 'lode purge <unique-prefix>' purges the right note; ambiguous prefix errors and lists candidates without deleting; unknown prefix errors; full-id purge behaviour is unchanged.
notes: SCOPE (decided 2026-07-06): add a REUSABLE, unit-tested resolver in repository.py — e.g. Repository.resolve_note_prefix(prefix) -> full note_id — do NOT inline it in cli.purge. lode-1gr.5 ('lode show') shares this exact resolver (it depends on this ticket). CANDIDATE SET = LIVE notes only (same v.op != 'delete' filter list_notes/Browse use): a prefix resolves only what the user can see via 'lode notes'/Browse; a tombstoned note is NOT reachable by prefix. A FULL 36-char id must still purge regardless of state (unchanged from today). Zero live matches -> 'no such note' (exit 1); >1 -> 'ambiguous', list candidates (exit 1); exactly one -> purge.

metadata.land_summary: purge (and future 'lode show') accept an unambiguous live-note-id prefix via reusable Repository.resolve_note_prefix + AmbiguousNoteIdError; full-id bypass preserved; empty/zero/ambiguous prefixes error clearly (exit 1)

title: TUI Browse: 8-char id column + full note id on the note-view screen
description: specs/03-tui-features.md item 1 (TUI part). Browse (src/lode/tui/screens/browse.py) shows Date|Version|Summary but never the note id, so a user can't purge what they see. Add a short (8-char prefix) 'Id' column to BrowseScreen's table, and show the FULL note_id on NoteViewScreen (e.g. in its header/subtitle) so it can be selected/copied. Respect the existing width budget in _reload_rows (the Id column must be accounted for alongside Date/Version so Summary still wraps rather than horizontal-scrolls, per lode-5qp). NoteRow already carries note_id.
acceptance_criteria: Browse shows a short id per row; opening a note shows its full 36-char id; the Summary column still wraps (no horizontal scroll) at narrow widths.
notes: SHORT-ID STANDARD (decided 2026-07-06): 8 chars is THE short note-id length across the epic (Browse Id column here, 'lode show' short refs in .5). Add/reuse ONE note-id short helper at 8 chars; cli.py's existing _short() (12) stays for VERSION-id digests only, don't conflate. An 8-char Browse prefix must be long enough to feed 'lode purge <prefix>' (lode-1gr.3) unambiguously in practice. Depends on lode-1gr.1: build against the relocated neutral read module, not lode.tui.browse.

metadata.land_summary: TUI Browse gains a leading 8-char Id column (shared notes_read.short_note_id helper) + NoteViewScreen shows the full 36-char note_id in its header sub_title; Summary column width budget recomputed for the 4th column so it still wraps. Tests added.

title: CLI: 'lode notes' — list live notes with id, date, summary
description: specs/03-tui-features.md item 1 (CLI part). There is currently NO way to get a note id from the CLI, so 'lode purge <id>' is unusable without one. Add a 'lode notes' command that lists every live note with its full note_id, a short human-readable date, and its summary (head kind='summary' annotation, falling back to the note's first line — same rule as lode.tui.browse._head_summary). Reuse lode.tui.browse.list_notes (already returns note_id/created/version/summary, live-notes-only) rather than re-querying; move/rename it if 'tui.browse' is the wrong home for a CLI reader. Keep the Typer/echo style of the existing cli.py read-outs (status/jobs/egress).
acceptance_criteria: Running 'lode notes' prints one row per live note with the full note_id visible and copy-pasteable into 'lode purge'; empty DB prints a 'no notes' line; tombstoned notes are excluded.
notes: HOME (decided 2026-07-06): MOVE the read functions out of lode.tui.browse into a neutral, non-UI module (e.g. lode/notes_read.py) — list_notes/NoteRow/note_body/list_versions/VersionRow/version_body + _head_summary/_first_line. They are already pure I/O (no Textual imports), so this is a relocation, not a rewrite. cli.py imports from the neutral module (fixes the cli->tui direction); keep the TUI screens working by re-exporting from lode.tui.browse OR updating their imports. This is why lode-1gr.2 now depends on this ticket (both touch the same read module). SHORT-ID: 'lode notes' lists the FULL note_id (copy-paste into purge); the 8-char abbreviation is only for column/inline displays (see lode-1gr.2/.5).

metadata.land_summary: Add 'lode notes' CLI (full id/date/summary, live-only) + relocate read-side list_notes/note_body/list_versions/version_body from tui.browse to neutral lode.notes_read, fixing cli->tui direction

title: Save-on-exit confirm should be a popup over the editor, not a blank full screen
description:
specs/02-feedback.md item 4: when the user presses Esc (or Ctrl+Q) over a dirty capture buffer, the Save/Discard/Cancel prompt appears on an otherwise blank screen. It should instead be a popup window centered over the still-visible editor, dismissed (returning to the editor unchanged) on Cancel — less jarring and closer to normal UI conventions.

Root cause: src/lode/tui/screens/capture.py DiscardConfirmScreen is a bare ModalScreen with NO styling, and the repo has no TUI CSS at all (no .tcss anywhere). Without CSS the dialog isn't sized/centered and the backdrop isn't styled, so it reads as a blank screen with a prompt.

## Design (confirmed with user 2026-07-04)
Ship an external Textual .tcss stylesheet (NOT DEFAULT_CSS) — this establishes the repo's TUI stylesheet pattern. That means three coordinated pieces:
1. A .tcss file (e.g. src/lode/tui/screens/capture.tcss, or an app-level src/lode/tui/lode.tcss) styling DiscardConfirmScreen: a centered, bounded, bordered dialog box floating over the capture editor, with the editor visible/dimmed behind it.
2. Wire it: set CSS_PATH on LodeApp (src/lode/tui/app.py) — or the screen's CSS_PATH — to load the file.
3. PACKAGE it: add the .tcss to [tool.setuptools.package-data] in pyproject.toml. Today that section only has: lode = ["*.sql"]. package-data keys are per-package and non-recursive, so add an entry that actually covers the .tcss's location (e.g. "lode.tui.screens" = ["*.tcss"], or a recursive lode = ["**/*.sql", "**/*.tcss"] if using recursive globs). MISS THIS and it works from a source checkout but the INSTALLED WHEEL ships without the stylesheet — a bug nox will not catch.

Before styling, verify the pinned Textual version's ModalScreen default background: if it already dims/shows the screen below, the only fix needed is sizing+centering the dialog box; if it does not, ALSO set a translucent backdrop so the editor is visible behind the box rather than a black void.

## Acceptance Criteria
- DiscardConfirmScreen renders as a centered, bounded, bordered dialog floating over the capture editor, with the editor visible (dimmed) behind it — not a full blank screen.
- The stylesheet is an external .tcss loaded via CSS_PATH, and pyproject [tool.setuptools.package-data] is updated to ship it; verify the built wheel/sdist actually contains the .tcss (e.g. inspect 'python -m build' output or the installed tree), not just a source run.
- Cancel (c / Escape) dismisses the dialog and returns to the editor with the buffer untouched (existing _on_discard_confirm behavior preserved); Save (s) and Discard (d) keep current semantics.
- Existing tests (tests/test_tui_capture_confirm.py) still pass; add coverage that the confirm is an overlay — the CaptureScreen below stays mounted on the screen stack while the dialog is up.
- nox -t fix and nox -s tests pass.

## Notes
Refines lode-0wj.1 (Escape guard) / lode-0wj.8 (Ctrl+Q guard) from epic lode-0wj. Touches src/lode/tui/screens/capture.py, a new .tcss, src/lode/tui/app.py (CSS_PATH), and pyproject.toml (package-data) — independent of the logging children (.1/.2/.3).

metadata.land_summary: Save-on-exit DiscardConfirmScreen is now a centered, bordered popup over the still-visible (dimmed) editor via the repo's first external Textual stylesheet (src/lode/tui/lode.tcss, loaded through LodeApp.CSS_PATH and shipped via pyproject package-data 'lode.tui'=['*.tcss']).

title: Add top-level 'lode --debug' flag to enable diagnostic instrumentation
description:
specs/02-feedback.md item 2: there should be a --debug flag for the CLI that enables debugging features (e.g. the event-loop-lag probe). Today those features are only reachable via LODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG; there is no CLI flag.

## Design (confirmed with user 2026-07-04)
TOP-LEVEL flag on the root Typer callback (src/lode/cli.py main()): 'lode --debug <subcommand>' sets the log level to DEBUG and thereby enables the diagnostic instrumentation already gated on DEBUG (e.g. lode.tui.latency_probe via CaptureScreen, gated on log.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG)). Applies to every subcommand (tui/ask/add/...), not just tui. Wiring is sound: configure_logging sets the ROOT logger to DEBUG, and child loggers (lode.tui.screens.capture, etc.) inherit that effective level, so the probe gate turns on.

Known, accepted coupling: --debug == 'set log level to DEBUG'. This ties log VERBOSITY to feature ENABLEMENT (the probe). Consistent with the existing latency_probe design decision to reuse the DEBUG toggle every lode module already logs behind (see latency_probe.py docstring), so we accept it now. If a future debug feature must be enabled WITHOUT DEBUG-level log spam (or vice-versa), split the two concepts then.

## Acceptance Criteria
- 'lode --debug tui' (and other subcommands) runs at DEBUG log level, turning on the event-loop-lag probe and other DEBUG-gated instrumentation.
- Without --debug, behavior is unchanged; LODE_LOG_LEVEL is still honored as the env fallback, and --debug takes precedence when passed.
- Interplay with TUI-only file logging (lode-1i8.2): in the TUI, --debug raises verbosity in the log FILE only — console stays suppressed (the TUI never echoes to the terminal, debug or not). For plain CLI commands, --debug raises verbosity on the existing stderr + file handlers (console stays available for the CLI).
- The flag is documented as the switch for diagnostic instrumentation. NOTE: to avoid colliding with lode-1i8.1 on docs/configuration.md, this ticket depends on .1; document --debug by ADDING to the logging section .1 creates (or in CLI --help), not by racing the same file.
- Tests cover the callback wiring (DEBUG level applied when --debug set; env fallback otherwise).
- nox -t fix and nox -s tests pass.

## Notes
Touches src/lode/cli.py main() callback and the configure_logging call. Depends on lode-1i8.2 (shared logconfig/cli files) AND lode-1i8.1 (shared docs/configuration.md) — build after both land.

metadata.land_summary: Add top-level 'lode --debug' flag on the root Typer callback: resolves to an explicit DEBUG log level (precedence over the LODE_LOG_LEVEL env fallback), enabling every DEBUG-gated diagnostic (e.g. the TUI latency_probe) across all subcommands; threaded through ctx.obj so tui's file-only reconfigure (lode-1i8.2) re-applies DEBUG without reattaching the console handler. Docs row + 5 tests. Technical review: no fixes needed, gates green.

title: TUI-only file logging: suppress console log output while the TUI runs (keep file handler)
description:
specs/02-feedback.md item 3: debug logging correctly writes to the log file, but ALSO dumps to the console, which corrupts the Textual TUI. This blocks the current exercise of collecting latency telemetry from the TUI.

Root cause: src/lode/logconfig.py configure_logging() calls logging.basicConfig(level, format), which attaches a stderr StreamHandler in addition to the file handler from _attach_file_handler. Both are live, so every log record echoes to the terminal. configure_logging() is called once, in the top-level Typer callback (cli.py:73), for ALL commands.

## Design (confirmed with user 2026-07-04, re-scoped after debate)
TUI-ONLY console suppression. Do NOT drop stderr logging globally: plain CLI commands (ask/add/...) legitimately use stderr — notably 'lode ask' deliberately relies on the root logger mirroring to stderr to surface an AuthError's cause (see cli.py ~260-269 and its comment). That path must keep working unchanged.

Instead, only the TUI runs file-only:
- When 'lode tui' launches, suppress console/stderr log output for the TUI session (remove the stderr StreamHandler basicConfig added from the root logger), keeping ONLY the file handler.
- MUST guarantee a file handler is attached for the TUI session so that, with no stream handler present, Python's last-resort handler (logging.lastResort, WARNING+ to stderr) can never fire and re-corrupt the display. The callback already attaches the file handler via log_dir(); the TUI path must ensure it remains/attaches, not merely remove the stream handler.

Suggested shape (builder's discretion): either the 'tui' command calls a small helper (e.g. in logconfig) that detaches root stream handlers and asserts the file handler, or configure_logging grows a console: bool flag the tui command passes as False. Keep it simple.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Running 'lode tui' emits ZERO log output to the terminal at any level (INFO or DEBUG) — verified by observation; this is a manual/observational check, NOT an automatable assertion (a live TUI owns the alternate screen).
- The AUTOMATABLE acceptance is structural: after the TUI configures logging, assert the root logger has no stream/console handler AND has the lode file handler (so records land in the file, not lastResort→stderr). Cover in tests/test_logconfig.py (or a tui logging test).
- Plain CLI behavior is UNCHANGED: 'lode ask'/'lode add' still mirror logs to stderr; the cli.py AuthError stderr-mirroring path and its comment remain valid (do not edit that comment).
- Log records still land in $LODE_HOME/logs/lode.log (format unchanged) so latency telemetry is collectible via the file.
- nox -t fix and nox -s tests pass.

## Notes
Touches src/lode/logconfig.py (+ the 'tui' command in cli.py, or tui/app.py). BLOCKS lode-1i8.3 (--debug) since both edit logconfig/cli — build .2 first. Telemetry collection is unblocked by THIS ticket alone (set LODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG + file-only TUI); the --debug flag (.3) is a convenience on top.

metadata.land_summary: TUI-only file logging: configure_logging grows a keyword-only console flag; the tui command calls it with console=False to strip the stderr stream handler while keeping the file handler (never handler-less, so lastResort can't fire). Plain CLI stderr logging unchanged.

title: init_db missing next_attempt_at migration: pre-2f2379d jobs tables crash lode work
description: A jobs table created before commit 2f2379d (schema hardening) lacks the next_attempt_at column. schema.sql's CREATE TABLE has it for fresh DBs, but storage.py _apply_migrations never added a matching ALTER, so existing DBs are never upgraded. Result: 'lode work' -> _batch_submit_enrich -> OperationalError: no such column: next_attempt_at. Fix: add nullable ADD COLUMN (SQLite rejects an expression default) + backfill next_attempt_at=created for NULL rows so pre-existing jobs become due.

metadata.land_summary: migrate jobs.next_attempt_at onto pre-existing DBs (nullable add + backfill)

title: Add kind='summary' AI enrichment — Haiku one-line note summary
description: Browse (lode-0wj.5) shows a Summary column, but no summary exists today: enrich (src/lode/enrich.py) produces only kind=tag/entity/edge. Add a new WHOLE-NOTE AI annotation kind='summary' — a one-line Haiku-derived summary of the note's head version — by EXTENDING the existing extract_enrichment tool (not a new job type): add a 'summary' field to the tool schema + prompt, bump ENRICH_PROMPT_VER, and write it to the annotations table (source='ai', kind='summary', target=note_id, source_version=head) with the same full provenance (model, prompt_ver, created) and idempotent source_version-keyed replace as tag/entity. Honor user-pin suppression like other kinds; the reconcile enrich_gap scan re-enqueues a head missing a live summary on prompt/model change. docs/storage.md §'Whole-note annotations' already lists 'summary' as a valid whole-note kind. Blocks lode-0wj.5's Summary column.
acceptance_criteria: enrich_version writes exactly one kind='summary' annotation (source='ai') for the head version, with provenance; re-enrichment replaces it idempotently; ENRICH_PROMPT_VER bumped; user-pinned summary suppression honored; reconcile re-enqueues a head missing a live summary. Tests cover write + idempotent replace + provenance + pin-suppression.

metadata.land_summary: Add kind='summary' whole-note AI annotation (Haiku one-line summary) with full provenance, idempotent source_version replace, user-pin suppression, and prompt-ver reconcile re-enqueue; code-review folded the summary write into the tag/entity kind-loop.

title: App-level Ctrl+Q: confirm-if-dirty before quitting from any screen
description: Split out of lode-0wj.1. Ctrl+Q is a GLOBAL App binding (priority=True, src/lode/tui/app.py) that quits from ANY screen, so a confirm-if-unsaved guard must live at the App level, not the capture screen: override App.action_quit (or relax the binding) so quitting first asks the CURRENT screen whether it has unsaved state. Only the capture screen (and later lode-0wj.6's edit flow) has unsaved state; ask/config/reconcile quit immediately. Reuses the Save/Discard/Cancel dialog lode-0wj.1 builds. Secondary to Escape (the actual muscle-memory footgun), hence P1.
acceptance_criteria: Ctrl+Q from the capture screen with a dirty buffer confirms (Save/Discard/Cancel) before quitting; from a clean capture buffer or any non-capture screen it quits immediately. Reuses lode-0wj.1's confirm dialog. Tests cover dirty-capture / clean-capture / other-screen.

metadata.land_summary: App-level Ctrl+Q confirm-if-dirty: LodeApp.action_quit asks the current screen via duck-typed confirm_quit() before exiting; capture's dirty-check pulled out of action_cancel into confirm_quit and reused, so Ctrl+Q on a dirty capture buffer pops the Save/Discard/Cancel dialog, a clean buffer or any non-capture screen quits immediately. 6 new pilot tests.

title: Browse screen: list notes (Date | Version | Summary), F3 from capture, select opens read-only, Escape returns
description: Columns: Date | Version | Summary. VERSION = the note's edit count / chain length (walk parent_version_id from the head) rendered as e.g. 'v3', NOT the content-hash version_id. SUMMARY = the head version's kind='summary' AI annotation (lode-0wj.9), FALLING BACK to the note's first line when no summary annotation exists yet (fresh/un-enriched notes — enrichment is async). Requires a NEW read function (this is NOT UI-only): list LIVE notes (EXCLUDE tombstoned/deleted, versions op=delete) -> notes.created, chain length, and head summary-or-first-line, ordered newest-first, with its own test. New screen module under src/lode/tui/screens/ + one SCREENS entry per the app.py registration convention. F3 global keybinding from capture; select opens read-only; Escape steps back note->list->capture. App still opens straight to capture. DEPENDS ON lode-0wj.9 (the summary annotation kind must exist for the column to be meaningful/testable).
acceptance_criteria: F3 from capture opens a browse list with Date | Version | Summary columns, newest-first, excluding deleted/tombstoned notes. VERSION shows the edit count (chain length). SUMMARY shows the head kind='summary' annotation, or the note's first line when no summary annotation exists yet. A tested read function returns (note_id, created, chain-length, summary-or-first-line) for live notes only. Selecting a row opens a read-only view. Escape steps back note->list->capture. Default startup still opens capture. Tests cover navigation, contents + ordering, deleted-note exclusion, edit-count, and the summary/first-line fallback.
notes: Debate + user resolution (lode-0wj): Summary column KEPT, backed by a NEW kind='summary' enrichment (lode-0wj.9) with first-line fallback for un-enriched notes. Version column KEPT as edit-count (chain length), not the content-hash id. Still needs a new list-notes read fn (not UI-only). Deleted/tombstoned notes (op=delete) EXCLUDED from the list.

metadata.land_summary: Browse screen (F3 from capture): DataTable of live notes Date | Version(v{n} chain-length) | Summary(head kind='summary' AI annotation, first-non-blank-line fallback), newest-first, op!='delete' excluded; row-select opens read-only NoteViewScreen; Escape pops note->list->capture via the Textual screen stack. New tested read fn lode.tui.browse.list_notes/note_body. Technical review: no correctness or simplification fixes needed; code correct, clean, convention-matching.

title: Optimise TUI input latency based on instrumentation findings
description: Follow-up to the instrumentation spike: apply the measured optimisation(s) so typing no longer feels blocked. Candidate directions the user raised: better async isolation, deferring background tasks, or manual-instead-of-auto task runs for the async work queue. Scope firms up once the spike reports where the input path actually blocks. Depends on the diagnosis ticket.
acceptance_criteria: At least one measured optimisation lands; keystroke->render latency measurably improved vs the spike's baseline; typing no longer blocks on background work.
notes:
SPIKE VERDICT (lode-0wj.2, ready-for-land): the passive related-notes worker is NOT the felt-lag source — fastembed/ONNX releases the GIL, asyncio.to_thread is relieving input as designed, event-loop lag stayed single-digit ms vs the 100ms target. So the optimisation should look ELSEWHERE than the related-notes/embedder path (that path is already non-blocking). Re-scope against the other candidate directions before building; the spike's instrumentation (LODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG heartbeat + capture.py debug logs) is the tool to localise the real blocker.
BUILD (lode-0wj.4): re-scoped per the lode-0wj.2 verdict -- looked elsewhere
than embedder inference, which the spike already cleared. Live-diagnosed the
REAL CaptureScreen (driven through Textual's pilot against the lode-5y8.4 seed
corpus, real embedder -- not an isolated find_related_notes() call) and found
capture.py never passed an embedder into find_related_notes, so every
debounce-fired pass built a *fresh* FastEmbedEmbedder and reloaded the ONNX
model from scratch. Measured: ~1.5s of event-loop stall per pause in typing,
every pause, for the whole session -- ONNX model *construction* (unlike
inference) does not release the GIL.

FIX: CaptureScreen._ensure_embedder constructs one embedder and reuses it for
the screen's lifetime (src/lode/tui/screens/capture.py); FastEmbedEmbedder._load
gets a lock (src/lode/lode/embedding.py) since reuse makes concurrent-thread
access to one instance real for the first time. MEASURED RESULT: pass #1 in a
session still pays ~1.3s (unavoidable first load), pass #2+ measures ~90ms with
zero event-loop-starvation warnings -- matching the spike's single-digit-ms
inference verdict. ~14x improvement on the repeat case, which is the common
case in any real typing session longer than one pause.

Tried and reverted: eagerly warming the embedder at screen mount (so even pass
#1 would be fast). Reverted because it made every CaptureScreen mount pay a
real ONNX load unconditionally -- broke tests/test_tui_quit.py's
Ctrl+Q-discard test by giving the debounce timer enough real wall-clock time to
fire mid-test. Scoped back to lazy reuse-on-first-use only (docstring on
_ensure_embedder records why).

Tests: tests/test_tui_app.py::test_embedder_is_constructed_once_and_reused_across_multiple_passes
pins the fix (construction count == 1 across 3 debounce-fired passes with a
stub embedder). Full suite green (702 passed, 7 skipped).

metadata.land_summary: Reuse one query embedder per capture screen (CaptureScreen._ensure_embedder) instead of one per debounce pass; FastEmbedEmbedder._load gains a lock for the now-real concurrent-thread access. ~14x faster on the repeat-pass common case (~1.5s stall -> ~90ms). Review: corrected the _load lock's docstring rationale (phantom mount-time warmup). Gates green (702 passed).

title: Make passive related-notes surfacing opt-in / disable-able (quick lag mitigation)
description: Hypothesis-driven lag relief, now GATED on lode-0wj.2's GIL/event-loop-yield verdict. The passive related-notes pass already runs off the UI thread (asyncio.to_thread + @work(exclusive=True), src/lode/tui/screens/capture.py), so it only blocks input IF the fastembed/ONNX embed holds the GIL. lode-0wj.2 answers that. If it DOES hold the GIL: add a setting (docs/configuration.md knob) to disable the passive related-notes pass and/or gate the embedder off the keystroke path — genuine relief. If it does NOT: rework/close this (the cause is elsewhere). Either way, a user-facing disable toggle is defensible; the dependency just stops us shipping a knob we believe is a fix before confirming it is.
acceptance_criteria: A config knob disables passive related-notes surfacing; with it off, no embedder/LanceDB work runs on the input path. Documented in docs/configuration.md. Default preserved.
notes: SPIKE VERDICT (lode-0wj.2, ready-for-land): fastembed/ONNX DOES release the GIL; the passive related-notes pass runs off the UI thread as designed and event-loop lag stayed single-digit ms (p95 ~5-8ms full pass) vs the 100ms target. So the 'does it hold the GIL' branch resolves to NO — disabling related-notes is a RED HERRING as a lag fix, not genuine relief. This ticket should REWORK/CLOSE the fix framing: a user-facing disable toggle is still defensible as a preference knob, but do NOT ship it as the lag remedy. The felt-lag cause is elsewhere (see lode-0wj.4).

metadata.land_summary: Add related_notes_enabled preference knob (default on): master switch that short-circuits find_related_notes before any FTS5/embedder/LanceDB work. Framed as a user preference, NOT a lag fix (per lode-0wj.2's GIL-release verdict). Doc row + config field + 2 tests.

title: Eval harness: capture a live baseline and set pass-bar thresholds (resolve metric-weighting open question)
description: Spun out of the E9 (lode-5y8) debate on completeness/closure. The eval harness ships as a runnable scaffold with NO quality floor: tests/test_eval_live.py asserts only that each metric is in [0,1], so every run is 'green' regardless of retrieval/answer quality (0% recall passes). E9's stated purpose — 'so rerank / entailment-threshold / chunk-size knobs have a target' — is therefore unmet: there is no target. This also resolves the open sub-question left in docs/decisions.md (the eval-harness entry): the exact metric weighting and how the golden set is curated. WORK: (1) run 'nox -s eval' with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY against the deterministic golden fixture and record the three metrics (recall@k / faithfulness / abstention) as the baseline; (2) set minimum-metric floors in test_eval_live.py so a regression below the baseline fails the CI-style check (replace the [0,1] bounds-only asserts); (3) settle + record the metric weighting (do the three metrics combine, or are they judged independently against per-metric floors?) in docs/decisions.md, closing that open sub-question; (4) note the golden-set curation policy (how it grows / is maintained). Depends on nothing new — the harness, corpus, and golden set already landed under E9.
acceptance_criteria: 'nox -s eval' with credentials records a documented baseline for recall@k/faithfulness/abstention on the golden fixture; the live test fails when any metric drops below its set floor (no longer bounds-only); docs/decisions.md's open metric-weighting/curation sub-question is resolved and the floors + weighting are recorded there; bare 'nox' and 'nox -s tests' stay offline/keyless/green.
notes:
ESCALATION: No live ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is available in this producer worktree (checked shell env and repo for .env files — none found). Acceptance criteria step 1 requires running 'nox -s eval' against the deterministic golden fixture with real credentials to record a baseline (recall@k / faithfulness / abstention); tests/test_eval_live.py and the noxfile's eval session both gate strictly on os.environ.get('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') being set (this is the existing, intentional design per docs/decisions.md's eval-harness entry — nox -s eval is the only key-gated session, and it must stay that way). title: Restore synchronous FTS5 on the capture path (regression from x6r.5)
description:
E3's core invariant is violated on trunk after lode-x6r.5: the FTS5 lexical index must be written SYNCHRONOUSLY on save so a just-captured note is keyword-findable BEFORE any async work runs (x6r.4 AC; docs/retrieval.md 'sync, always fresh'; the vector leg is allowed to lag precisely BECAUSE the lexical leg is fresh). On trunk neither leg is synchronous.

ROOT CAUSE: x6r.5 (move EMBEDDING off the capture path) deleted cli._embed_inline, which bundled BOTH the model-bearing vector leg AND the model-FREE FTS lexical leg. Moving embedding async was correct; moving FTS async was over-reach — FTS being model-free is the whole reason the design keeps it synchronous (instant keyword-findability, no model wait). Now the only FTS write is in worker._embed_handler (worker.py:304-330), reached only when 'lode work' drains the embed job. Compounding it: cli.py add (cli.py:138) builds Repository(conn) with NO cache => NullCache() (repository.py:137), so Repository.save's post-commit self.cache.index() is a no-op. The CompositeCache + FTS CacheBackend machinery built by lode-1f9 was never injected into the capture path — pre-x6r.5 the sync FTS was carried only by the _embed_inline skeleton stand-in, which x6r.5 removed.

EFFECT: 'lode add' then immediately 'lode ask' finds nothing by keyword until 'lode work' runs. The design's retrieval-correctness argument no longer holds.

MISSED BECAUSE: x6r.5 rewired the skeleton-gate tests from add->ask to add->work->ask, masking the regression; there is no test for x6r.4's actual AC (FTS-findable before any async work).

FIX (Option A, ratified by bildzeitung 2026-06-29 debate of lode-x6r):
- Inject the real CompositeCache — with the FTS lexical CacheBackend (lode-1f9) — into the Repository that cli.py add uses, so Repository.save writes passages + FTS5 rows SYNCHRONOUSLY after the version commit (chunking and FTS are model-free; safe in the capture path).
- Keep EMBEDDING async: the worker stays the sole embedder; do NOT re-introduce synchronous embedding (preserve x6r.5's capture-latency win).
- Make worker._embed_handler vector-only (drop its FTS leg) OR keep FTS idempotent so the worker never double-indexes; the capture-path sync write is the source of the invariant.
- KEY COUPLING to resolve: i05.4's reconciliation embed-gap query keys off 'head version with no passages row'. If passages are now written synchronously on save, that signal no longer detects a missing VECTOR. Re-key the embed-gap signal to 'head version with no vectors' (or equivalent) so reconciliation still re-enqueues embeds correctly. Verify the i05.1 atomic save+enqueue and i05.4 reconcile still behave.
- Record the settled capture-path composition (CompositeCache injected; passages+FTS synchronous, embedding async) in docs/ (storage.md / retrieval.md), in a worktree.
design: Inject CompositeCache (FTS CacheBackend from lode-1f9, + the LanceDB vector backend) into Repository in cli.py add. Repository.save already drives self.cache.index() post-commit (repository.py:170) — wiring a real composite there gives synchronous passages+FTS. Embedding stays in worker._embed_handler. Split the legs: model-free (chunk + passages + FTS) = synchronous on save via the cache seam; model-bearing (embed -> LanceDB vectors) = async via the worker. Then fix the i05.4 reconcile gap query to key off missing vectors, not missing passages.
acceptance_criteria: A note saved via 'lode add' is keyword-findable via FTS5 BEFORE 'lode work' runs — 'lode ask' on a keyword in the note returns it with no intervening 'lode work'. Embedding remains async (the vector leg still requires the worker). A regression test asserts add -> ask (no work) finds the note by keyword (this is x6r.4's real AC, currently untested). The worker does not double-index FTS. The reconciliation embed-gap signal (i05.4) still correctly detects a missing vector now that passages are written synchronously. The capture-path cache composition is recorded in docs/.

metadata.land_summary: Restore synchronous FTS5 on capture: cli.py add injects CompositeCache([LexicalCacheBackend]) so Repository.save writes passages+passages_fts synchronously post-commit (keyword-findable before any async work); worker._embed_handler is now vector-only (no double-index); i05.4 reconcile embed-gap signal re-keyed from 'no passages row' to 'no non-dead embed job' (passages now exist on save). New Gate 4 (add->ask, no work, FTS finds + cites) and Gate 5 (worker doesn't double-index FTS) regression tests; reconcile tests cover passages-alone-not-a-gap + dead-job re-enqueue. Docs updated (storage.md/retrieval.md). Code review: clean, no changes needed. Gates green: 448 passed, 4 skipped.

title: Wire vector store as a CacheBackend + cache-engine composition (Repository)
description:
Route cache access THROUGH the Repository interface (lode-s2f.5) and resolve how multiple regenerable-cache engines coexist in the Repository's single cache slot. Deferred out of lode-x6r.3 (LanceDB vector store), which built the standalone VectorStore engine but did NOT wire it as a CacheBackend because doing so forces this composition decision before the FTS leg exists.

Scope:
- Make the vector store reachable via the Repository CacheBackend Protocol (index/evict -> chunk+embed+VectorStore.replace_vectors / drop), so callers reach vectors through Repository, not lode.embedding directly. This satisfies the 'access is through the repository interface' criterion that x6r.3 deferred.
- Decide + implement the COMPOSITION: the Repository takes one 'cache' slot, but the cache has multiple engines — passage vectors (LanceDB, x6r.3), the FTS5 lexical index (x6r.4), and later the networkx knowledge graph. Likely a composite CacheBackend that fans index/evict out to each engine. Settle this so x6r.4 (FTS sync-on-save) plugs into the same mechanism rather than inventing its own.
- Keep it the simplest thing that works (docs/stack.md 'keep the cache behind a repository interface'); record any settled composition decision in docs/ (stack.md/storage.md), not only code.
acceptance_criteria: Vector (and the FTS) cache engine is driven through the Repository CacheBackend; a composite/multiplexing backend fans head-change index/evict to each engine; callers reach the cache only through Repository, not the engine modules directly.
notes: NEXT-SESSION SEQUENCING (handoff 2026-06-23): build this SOLO and FIRST. It is the E3 lynchpin — it settles the composite CacheBackend that BOTH x6r.4 (FTS sync-on-save, now dep-gated on this) and the eventual E4 retrieval wiring plug into. Touches the repository.py seam + embedding.py/vectorstore.py, so it does not parallelize cleanly with other E3 work. The only safe sibling to fan out alongside it is lode-5y8.3 (golden Q&A set — disjoint files, but carries its own open metric-weighting question). After 1f9 lands, x6r.4 becomes ready and plugs FTS into the settled composite. Record the composition decision in docs/ (stack.md/storage.md), not only code.

metadata.land_summary: Composite cache multiplexer (one Repository slot fans index/evict to N engines) + LanceDB vector store wired through the seam as EmbeddingCacheBackend; vectors now reached through Repository. Composition decision recorded in docs/storage.md.

title: Harden bd↔git sync: jsonl post-checkout hook reverts bd writes on rebase
description: REPRODUCIBLE: a bd close/label change made in a session is silently reverted when a later 'git pull --rebase' runs. Root cause: core.hooksPath=.beads/hooks; the post-checkout/post-merge hooks call 'bd hooks run', which reconciles Dolt FROM the working-tree .beads/issues.jsonl. 'git pull --rebase' checks out intermediate commits whose exported jsonl still shows the pre-close state (in_progress + ready-for-land), so post-checkout re-imports that and reverts the Dolt close. Hit 3x (lode-8bh, lode-wvf, lode-bxz). Contradicts the stated model (Dolt authoritative, jsonl passive). WORKAROUND that holds: after bd writes, 'bd dolt push' first, then export+commit jsonl once, then PLAIN 'git push' (no --rebase). Proper fix: make the flow Dolt-authoritative end-to-end — bake ordering into the producer/lander/coding agent defs + CLAUDE.md session-close (which currently mandates 'git pull --rebase'); consider ff-only pulls and/or disabling the jsonl→Dolt import on checkout. Blocks reliable landing — the whole landing loop rests on 'ready-for-land lives in beads'.
acceptance_criteria: A bd close survives a normal sync (no silent revert); the producer/lander/coding flows + CLAUDE.md encode a Dolt-authoritative ordering that doesn't lose bd writes; documented.
close_reason: import.auto disabled in committed config.yaml + CLAUDE.md rule; Dolt authoritative, jsonl export-only

title: Deterministic seed-corpus fixture for the eval harness (reproducible version_ids)
description: The golden Q&A set pins known-good citations to content-hash version_ids + verbatim spans (faithfulness schema). Those ids do not exist until notes are saved, and re-save/re-chunk changes them. So commit a FIXED set of input note bodies the harness loads deterministically, yielding reproducible version_ids the golden citations can reference. Unblocks lode-5y8.3 (the golden set is unauthorable without this).
design:
Re-sequenced by the lode-5y8.4 land escalation resolution (2026-06-23, option b): the STORAGE CORE owns the content-hash encoding; the seed fixture CONSUMES it. Now depends on lode-s2f.2 (hashing.py).
REBUILD BRIEF: Keep the committed corpus (markdown bodies under src/lode/eval/corpus/), the importlib.resources sorted-filename loader, the SeedNote shape, and the golden pinned-id snapshot test — all correct and reusable from the prior attempt @ git 9dcb6a4. CHANGE: import content_version_id from lode-s2f.2's hashing module (the single source of truth) instead of reimplementing the framing in seed.py; do NOT edit docs/storage.md (the encoding decision and its doc pin are lode-s2f.2's). The golden snapshot ids are whatever hashing.py produces — if they differ from the prior attempt's pinned hex, update the snapshot to match the storage core.
acceptance_criteria: A committed set of input note bodies loads deterministically into a fresh store, yielding stable version_ids the golden citations reference.
notes:
ESCALATION (/land semantic review, 2026-06-22T18:07:46Z): The fixture is correct and green, but to get reproducible golden version_ids it PINS lode's canonical content-hash encoding in docs/storage.md — choosing the length-prefixed form (8-byte big-endian length prefix; field order note_id,parent,body; root parent = empty string) over the OTHER form docs/storage.md §135-139 had presented as 'equivalent' (the two hash to different values). It binds the future storage-core ticket lode-s2f.2 (hashing.py) to match, and leaves the encoding implemented in TWO places (eval/seed.py now, hashing.py later) kept in sync only by doc prose. The ticket sanctioned a deterministic fixture, NOT the canonical hash-framing decision for all of storage; the producer itself flagged this.

DECISION NEEDED — who owns lode's canonical content-hash encoding, and does this branch land as-is?
(a) Accept the pin: eval fixture defines the canonical encoding in docs/storage.md; lode-s2f.2 must implement THIS framing. Lands now, unblocks lode-5y8.3 immediately. Cost: a build-constant invariant lives in two implementations bound only by doc prose; a fixture ticket made a storage-core decision.
(b) Storage core owns it: build hashing.py::content_version_id first, have the fixture IMPORT it (single source of truth), make lode-5y8.4 depend on lode-s2f.2; rebuild the branch to drop its own hash impl. Cost: lode-5y8.3 waits on the storage core.
Some decision is forced (docs offered two non-equal 'equivalent' forms, no pinned length-prefix width/endianness or root-parent encoding), but which form is canonical and which ticket owns it is a real architectural/sequencing choice the ticket didn't authorize. Branch origin/land/lode-5y8.4 @ 9dcb6a4 is KEPT for the human.
RESOLVED 2026-06-23 -> option (b). Storage core (lode-s2f.2) owns the encoding; this ticket now depends on it and imports the hash rather than defining it. Escalated branch origin/land/lode-5y8.4 @ 9dcb6a4 dropped (corpus + loader + test salvageable from that SHA). Stale land_head/land_summary metadata point at the dropped branch — a rebuild will overwrite them.

title: lode add (capture + save)
description: Capture a note from CLI and persist via versions.save(); enqueue derive jobs. Instant, no AI in the path.
design: lode add = capture/create. Mint a fresh uuid4 note_id (logical id, no aliasing), read body from positional TEXT arg or stdin (verbatim; reject empty/whitespace-only). Open DB via init_db at --db (envvar LODE_DB, default ~/.local/share/lode/lode.db). Call versions.save() (always a create) — NO AI in path. On HeadConflictError write the rejected buffer to a unique draft file beside the DB, print 'note changed since opened' + draft path, exit 1 (never clobber/auto-merge). On success enqueue derive jobs (pending embed+enrich rows) via new thin lode.jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs in its own txn; reconciliation scan (docs/storage.md) is the self-healing net for the save/enqueue gap since the lane fence forbids editing versions.py to make it one txn. Lane: cli.py + test_cli.py + new jobs.py + test_jobs.py only.
acceptance_criteria: lode add captures a note and persists via save() with no AI call in the path, enqueues derive jobs, and on CAS reject writes a draft + prints the diff path.
notes: CAS-reject UX (CLI-first phase, since the interactive reconciliation UI is E11/TUI): on a CAS rejection, 'lode add' writes the rejected buffer to a draft file and prints the diff path + 'note changed since opened'; full interactive re-apply/discard waits for E11. Never auto-merge, never clobber.

title: versions.save() — CAS head, no-op dedup, op tombstone
description: save(): write immutable version row + move head via compare-and-swap (reject if head moved); no-op dedup vs head body; op = create/update/delete (tombstone); soft-delete recovery = repoint head.
design: versions.save() over the s2f.1 schema + s2f.2 hashing. Single primitive save(conn,note_id,body,*,parent,settings) that creates (note absent -> op=create, parent=NO_PARENT, atomic note+root-version insert via DEFERRABLE FK) or updates (note present -> CAS: parent must==current head). No-op dedup: body==head body returns the head, writes no row. delete(conn,note_id,*,parent) tombstones (op=delete, carries head body forward, CAS-moves head). recover(conn,note_id,*,target_version) repoints head to a prior version (no new row). CAS reject raises HeadConflictError(note_id,expected_parent,actual_head) — the clean seam s2f.4 extends into the diff/buffer-preserve conflict surface; NOT implementing that surface here. import content_version_id from lode.hashing (single source of truth).
acceptance_criteria: save() rejects a write whose parent != current head (CAS); a save with body identical to head returns the head and writes NO new row (no-op dedup); delete writes a tombstone op preserving lineage; head can be repointed to recover a soft-deleted note.

metadata.land_summary: lode.versions: save() (create/update with head CAS + no-op dedup), delete() (op=delete tombstone, body carried forward), recover() (repoint head); HeadConflictError seam left for s2f.4. Imports content_version_id from hashing. 11 tests, gates green.

title: CAS-reject structured conflict (buffer preserved)
description: On CAS rejection return a structured 'changed since opened' conflict carrying the rejected buffer + new head for diff; never auto-merge, never clobber. Consumed by the TUI reconciliation UI (E11).
acceptance_criteria: A CAS-rejected save returns the structured conflict (rejected buffer + new head) and persists the buffer as a draft; nothing is clobbered or auto-merged.
notes:
ESCALATION (/land semantic review, 2026-06-23): AC clause 2 'persists the buffer as a draft' is deferred by the branch to the consumer layer ('the durable draft store is the consumer's job'), recorded only in a versions.py docstring. The structured conflict (rejected_buffer + actual_head + actual_head_body) and never-clobber/auto-merge are fully implemented. docs/storage.md says the buffer is 'preserved as a draft' without naming the owning layer; there is no drafts table in the landed schema (s2f.1); and y42.1's 'lode add' already writes the rejected buffer to a *.draft file — so the no-lost-work guarantee is met system-wide.

DECISION NEEDED — who owns draft persistence, and does this branch satisfy the AC as-is?
(a) Ratify consumer-owned persistence: land s2f.4 as-is (storage returns the preserved buffer; CLI/E11 persist the draft) and add a docs/storage.md line pinning the layer split so it isn't code-only. (Reviewer leans here.)
(b) Storage owns it: bounce/rebuild s2f.4 to durably persist the draft in the storage layer (a drafts table in schema.sql), independent of the CLI. Cost: new schema surface not in s2f.1, likely duplicating the CLI *.draft, arguably wrong layer.
Branch origin/land/lode-s2f.4 @ 5062f4f is KEPT for the human.
RESOLVED 2026-06-23 -> option (a). Human ratified CONSUMER-OWNED draft persistence: the storage layer's contract is the honest CAS reject + the buffer-preserving structured conflict it hands back (rejected_buffer + actual_head/body); persisting the buffer as a durable draft is the consumer's job (lode add already writes a *.draft beside the DB; the TUI/E11 owns the interactive re-apply/discard store). A dedicated 'drafts' table/mechanism is DEFERRED until the system is exercised in production. ACTION: the s2f.4 branch lands as-is, plus a docs/storage.md line pinning this layer split (so the decision lives in docs/, not only the versions.py docstring). The design decision is recorded in docs/storage.md, not here — this note is just the audit trail.
close_reason: Landed on trunk via /land (merge cae8248); escalation resolved option (a), layer split pinned in docs/storage.md

metadata.land_summary: versions.py: HeadConflictError enriched into structured CAS-reject conflict (rejected_buffer + actual_head/actual_head_body for diff; delete buffer=None). Plus docs/storage.md pins the layer split: storage hands back the buffer-preserving conflict, consumer (lode add *.draft / TUI E11) persists the draft; drafts table deferred.

title: hashing.py — framed xxh3-128 content-address hash
description: Length-prefixed framed H (xxh3-128, blake2b-128 stdlib fallback) for version_id=H(framed:note_id,parent,body) and snapshot_id. Unit-test the framing-ambiguity cases (H('a','bc') != H('ab','c')) per docs/storage.md.
design:
OWNS lode's canonical content-hash encoding — this is a STORAGE decision, ratified here, NOT by the eval seed fixture (see lode-5y8.4 escalation resolved 2026-06-23 -> option b). Beyond the hash code, two deliverables:
(1) Record the canonical framing in docs/storage.md, resolving the current §135-139 ambiguity: it presents the length-prefixed form and the hash-of-sub-hashes form as 'equivalent', but they hash to DIFFERENT values, so exactly one must be frozen.
(2) Expose content_version_id(note_id, parent, body) as the SINGLE source of truth that eval/seed.py (lode-5y8.4) and the version-save path both import — no second implementation anywhere.
RECOMMENDED encoding (worked out and validated green in the bounced lode-5y8.4 attempt @ git 9dcb6a4 — ratify or revise): length-prefixed form; each field = its UTF-8 bytes prefixed by an 8-byte big-endian unsigned length; concatenate framed(note_id) || framed(parent) || framed(body) in that order; a root 'create' has parent = empty string (8-byte zero length, then no bytes); H = xxh3-128 (config.content_hash), lowercase hex digest; the blake2b-128 stdlib fallback must frame identically so it produces the same ids.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests prove framing is unambiguous: H('a','bc') != H('ab','c'); version_id = H(framed:note_id,parent,body) is reproducible for identical inputs; blake2b-128 fallback path exercised.
notes: Scope note (2026-06-23): per the lode-5y8.4 land escalation resolution (option b), this ticket — not the eval fixture — owns the content-hash encoding decision and its docs/storage.md pin. lode-5y8.4 now depends on this ticket and will import content_version_id rather than reimplement it.

metadata.land_summary: lode.hashing: framed xxh3-128 content-address ids (content_version_id/content_snapshot_id, blake2b-128 fallback); canonical length-prefixed encoding pinned in docs/storage.md
