title: EditScreen lacks the passive related-notes panel CaptureScreen has
description:
Editing an existing note (BrowseScreen 'e' -> EditScreen in src/lode/tui/screens/browse.py) shows no related past notes, unlike composing a new note. EditScreen.compose() yields only Header + TextArea + Footer — none of CaptureScreen's related-notes machinery (debounced find_related_notes pass, RELATED_ID panel, shared query embedder, pass-seq instrumentation from lode-0wj.2/lode-mkc.3) is wired in. User expectation: parity — the same passive 'you wrote about this before' surfacing while editing.

Implementation notes:
- The pass itself is screen-agnostic (lode.tui.related.find_related_notes takes a draft string + settings), so the work is wiring, likely by extracting capture's debounce/panel plumbing into something shareable rather than copy-pasting ~100 lines.
- Edit-specific wrinkle: the note being edited will trivially match itself; the pass must exclude self.note_id from results (find_related_notes may need an exclude parameter).
- Honor the same knobs (related_notes_enabled / debounce_ms / limit / min_chars) and the lazy-embedder + in-flight-pass-cancel behavior capture has (see capture.py docstrings re lode-0wj.2 lag findings).
design:
Decided (2026-07-09, with user): achieve parity via COMPOSITION, not inheritance — extract capture's related-notes machinery (debounce timer, on_text_area_changed handling, the @work exclusive search pass, lazy shared embedder, cancel-in-flight logic, _render_related, pass-seq DEBUG instrumentation) into a self-contained RelatedNotesPanel widget that owns its own timer/worker/embedder/rendering. Surface: update_draft(text) + reset(), plus an exclude_note_id constructor param so EditScreen's pass never matches the note being edited (find_related_notes likely grows an exclude parameter to support this). Both CaptureScreen and EditScreen compose the panel and forward their TextArea.Changed text to it; any future screen gets the feature the same way.

Explicitly REJECTED: a common NoteEditorScreen superclass. The screens' lifecycle plumbing (dirty check, DiscardConfirm dance, reconcile resolution) is deliberately divergent — capture ends every path in app.exit(), edit in pop_screen(); their dirty semantics differ ('non-empty' vs 'changed since load'); EditScreen.action_cancel's docstring already documents why such methods can't be shared. A base class would need ~5 template-method hooks landing exactly on those divergences, obscuring the delicate parts to share the part composition shares for free.

Keep capture's existing behavior contracts intact when extracting: lazy embedder (no eager ONNX load at mount), cancel scheduled+in-flight pass on clear/reset, empty-buffer clears the panel immediately without a pass, markup=False on the Static (bracket-heavy note text, lode-mkc.3).
acceptance_criteria: Editing a note surfaces related past notes in a panel with the same debounce/knob behavior as capture; the edited note itself never appears in its own related list; existing capture behavior unchanged; tests cover the edit-screen pass incl. self-exclusion.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run the lode TUI and open the browse screen with at least two live notes on a related topic.
2. Highlight a note and press 'e' to open EditScreen.
3. Type/extend the body past related_notes_min_chars and pause past the debounce interval.
4. Observe: no related-notes panel appears. Doing the same in the new-note capture screen surfaces related past notes.

title: docs/decisions.md: '/code-review has no path/base argument' is false and self-contradicted; record which /code-review resolves in a subagent
description:
Two documentation corrections found by /land's semantic review of lode-k5e (accepted and landed; these did not block it).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Read docs/decisions.md:248 (as landed by lode-k5e): it says '/code-review'/'/simplify' are 'both cwd-relative, no path/base argument'.
2. Read ~20 lines later in the SAME entry: it explains that the explicit 'trunk...HEAD' BASE matters because '/code-review''s fallback base is 'main...HEAD'.
3. Observe .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md passes 'trunk...HEAD' as a base argument 4 times.

The claim is self-contradicted and factually wrong. /code-review's argument spec is [low|medium|high|max|ultra] [--fix] [--comment] [<target>], and its own prompt text says 'If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument, review that target instead.' What it lacks is a PATH/DIRECTORY argument (it cannot be pointed at another working tree); it very much has a base/target argument, which is exactly why the fix works.

## Second correction
lode-k5e's acceptance criteria required: 'Confirmed which /code-review resolves inside a subagent (built-in vs the marketplace PR-review plugin).' This WAS confirmed empirically — the lode-k5e code-reviewer's '/code-review high --fix trunk...HEAD' applied a fix to its working tree, which the marketplace plugin (~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/claude-plugins-official/plugins/code-review) cannot do: it reviews a GitHub PR via gh and comments on it. But the confirmation was never written down — grep for 'marketplace' or 'plugin' across docs/decisions.md, .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md, and .claude/skills/code/SKILL.md returns nothing.

This matters because a land/<id> branch has no PR. If the marketplace command ever shadows the built-in in some environment, the review silently breaks again in a new way.
design: Two edits to docs/decisions.md's lode-k5e entry: (1) change 'no path/base argument' to 'no path/directory argument (a base/target rev-range IS accepted, which is why the explicit trunk...HEAD works)'. (2) Add a sentence recording that the built-in /code-review is what resolves inside a subagent, evidenced by --fix writing the working tree, and that the marketplace plugin of the same name is PR-based and would be wrong here.
acceptance_criteria: docs/decisions.md no longer claims /code-review has no base argument, and no longer contradicts itself within the same entry. The built-in-vs-marketplace /code-review question is recorded in docs/ with the evidence.
notes: Filed 2026-07-09 by /land semantic review of lode-k5e (verdict: accept). discovered-from lode-k5e. Both are one-sentence prose fixes to the rationale; the instruction docs (code-reviewer.md, coding.md) are already correct, so no agent behaves wrongly today.

title: Reconsider whether builders still need to keep their worktree, and whether /land's worktree GC should change
description:
lode-k5e retired the 'code-reviewer drives the builder's worktree via git -C' architecture: the reviewer now fetches origin/land/<id> and checks it out into its own launch worktree, and coding.md's rebase-pickup cycle does the same. Neither ever opens the builder's original worktree anymore.

The builder still keeps its worktree on disk and still records metadata.review_worktree, because /land's worktree GC (docs/agents-workflow.md #mechanics-decided) keys off that path to reclaim the local worktree after a clean land. That GC mechanic is unchanged by lode-k5e -- explicitly out of scope for it (see docs/decisions.md, the 'Review architecture' entry).

Open question for a follow-up: now that nothing reads the builder's worktree except /land's own GC at the very end, does the builder still need to keep it around for the whole build->review->land lifecycle, or could /land (or even the builder itself, post-push) reclaim it sooner? This touches /land's mechanics directly and deserves its own design pass rather than folding into lode-k5e.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A decision (keep as-is, or change the builder/land worktree-retention contract) is recorded in docs/agents-workflow.md and/or docs/decisions.md.
- If changed: /land's worktree GC and the builder's hand-off step are updated consistently, and no in-flight ready-for-code-review / ready-for-land ticket's hand-off contract is broken.
- If kept as-is: docs/decisions.md records why, with a revisit trigger.

title: /code step-0 rebase pickup can never resolve a conflict: Edit is guard-pinned off $WT and coding.md forbids the bash route code-reviewer.md mandates
description:
`/code`'s step-0 rebase pickup claims to self-heal `needs-rebase` kick-backs — code/SKILL.md's frontmatter says it "dispatches a `coding` producer to rebase, re-gate, force-push, and swap each straight back to ready-for-land — **no manual nudge needed**." In practice a rebase pickup escalates to a human on *any* conflict git cannot auto-resolve, including a trivially obvious one.

## Root cause
Two things compose badly:
1. `Edit`/`Write` are guard-pinned to the agent's own launch worktree and cannot reach the build worktree `$WT` (upstream behavior; same guard as lode-k5e).
2. `.claude/agents/coding.md:337-340` treats hitting that guard as "the signal to escalate (below), not to fight the guard", and `:350-351` says on any rebase conflict, `rebase --abort` and escalate "rather than guess a resolution that could silently change reviewed content".

So the rebase-pickup cycle has **no mechanism at all** for writing a conflict resolution, even when the resolution is mechanical.

## The inconsistency
`.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md:124-132` hits the identical guard and resolves it the opposite way: "Don't fight it: apply every `/code-review --fix` / `/simplify` change with `bash` instead — a precise, single-match replacement against an absolute path under `$WT`." Two agent docs, same guard, contradictory policy. Either bash-into-`$WT` is an acceptable, auditable mechanism (then the rebase pickup may use it for a mechanical conflict) or it is fighting the guard (then code-reviewer.md is instructing a violation and every review commit today was produced that way).

Note the two cases are not identical — resolving a rebase conflict is a judgment call in a way that applying a review fix is not, so "escalate on conflict" may well be the right *policy*. But then the frontmatter's "no manual nudge needed" is false and should be corrected, and coding.md should say the escalation is a deliberate judgment boundary rather than a consequence of the tool guard, which is how it currently reads.

## Observed
2026-07-09, lode-ay5.2. `/land` kicked it back (`docs/storage.md` conflict). The dispatched rebase pickup rebased onto trunk, hit the conflict, and reported: the two sides do not disagree (trunk carries the ay5.3 CLI-parity section; the branch adds the ay5.2 TUI-modal section at the same insertion point), it could see the correct ordering from an existing cross-reference in the file — and it still aborted and escalated, because `Edit` refused the write and its doc forbids the bash route. Branch left untouched at `0a9db4f`, label swapped `needs-rebase` → `land-escalated`.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Get any `land/<id>` branch kicked back by `/land`'s precheck with a real textual conflict (not one git auto-resolves on replay).
2. Run `/code`; its step-0 sweep dispatches a `coding` rebase pickup.
3. The pickup runs `git -C $WT rebase origin/trunk`, hits the conflict, and has no way to write the resolution: `Edit` is guard-pinned away from `$WT`, and coding.md forbids the bash workaround.
4. It aborts and applies `land-escalated`. A human must finish it. Step 0's "no manual nudge needed" did not hold.

## Scope note
Because `/land` issues `needs-rebase` precisely when a branch stopped merging cleanly, the conflicting case is the common one. Self-healing only actually works when `git rebase`'s replay auto-merges where `/land`'s `git merge-tree` precheck did not — a real but narrower window than the frontmatter implies.
design:
Decide the guard policy ONCE and make both agent docs agree.
(a) Permit a bash single-match write into $WT for a MECHANICAL rebase conflict (both sides add independent, non-overlapping content), with the same single-match assertion discipline code-reviewer.md already requires; keep escalation for any conflict where the sides genuinely disagree. Preserves step-0 self-healing for the common 'two branches appended prose at the same anchor' case.
(b) Keep 'always escalate on conflict' as a deliberate judgment boundary, and FIX code/SKILL.md's frontmatter, which currently promises 'no manual nudge needed'. Also restate coding.md:337-340 so escalation reads as a policy choice, not a tool-guard consequence.
(c) The structural fix from lode-k5e option (a): launch the agent cwd'd AT $WT, so Edit/Write work normally and the whole guard question evaporates for both agents.
Blocked-ish on lode-k5e: (c) resolves both tickets at once, so settle k5e's investigation first.
acceptance_criteria: coding.md and code-reviewer.md state the SAME policy for writing into a build worktree they did not launch in, with the difference (if any) justified explicitly rather than left as an unremarked contradiction. code/SKILL.md no longer claims step-0 needs 'no manual nudge' if conflicts still escalate. If option (a) is taken, a mechanical two-sided-append conflict rebases and force-pushes without human involvement, demonstrated on a real kick-back.
notes:
Filed 2026-07-09. Discovered when the lode-ay5.2 rebase pickup escalated on a conflict it had correctly diagnosed as mechanical. Sibling of lode-k5e (same Edit guard, different victim). lode-ay5.2 is currently sitting at land-escalated and needs a human to finish the rebase; the escalation note on that ticket already records the exact proposed resolution and ordering rationale.
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-07-09 (docs, not speculation). The EnterWorktree tool description states: 'Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched...) and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session.'

This DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md:98 ('I do not call EnterWorktree with path = $WT') and .claude/skills/code/SKILL.md ('the isolation guard refuses EnterWorktree for commands resolved into a path-entered worktree'). The builder worktree IS under .claude/worktrees/ of the same repo, so a code-reviewer launched with isolation:'worktree' MAY EnterWorktree(path=$WT).

Consequence: cwd becomes $WT, so (1) Edit/Write work normally — the bash single-match workaround becomes unnecessary; (2) /code-review and /simplify analyze the REAL branch diff instead of an empty one — this bug's root cause; (3) nox/gates run in cwd with no -f flag. This is option (c), and it resolves lode-k5e and lode-8k3 with a single change.

Constraint from the same doc: 'After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with path to return to one.' So only one worktree is active at a time; that is fine for a reviewer that only ever touches $WT.

Secondary finding (from the shipped skill's own prompt text): /code-review DOES accept a target argument — 'If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument, review that target instead' — and its arg spec is [low|medium|high|max|ultra] [--fix] [--comment] [<target>]. This is a FALLBACK if EnterWorktree(path) turns out not to work: aiming it at 'trunk...land/<id>' would at least give the finders the right diff. But note --fix applies to the CWD working tree, so --fix would still write the wrong tree; the fallback requires dropping --fix and applying by hand.

CONFIDENCE: [Likely], not [Certain]. Our agent docs may encode a real failure observed on an older CLI (current: 2.1.205). VERIFY EMPIRICALLY BEFORE REWRITING THE DOCS.
lode-k5e's dispatched producer empirically tested this ticket's shared 'ROOT CAUSE FOUND' theory (EnterWorktree(path=$WT) from an isolation:'worktree'-pinned subagent) on 2026-07-09 and it FAILED: EnterWorktree(path=<other worktree>) reports success but a separate isolation guard still refuses both Bash and Write against the target path, with explicit errors naming the agent's original launch worktree as the only writable one. Full probe transcript is on lode-k5e's notes.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS TICKET: option (c) ('the structural fix from lode-k5e option (a): launch the agent cwd'd AT $WT... the whole guard question evaporates') is NOT AVAILABLE. This ticket is no longer blocked-ish on lode-k5e's investigation in the sense of possibly being solved for free by it — lode-k5e did NOT rewrite the docs (it escalated, land-escalated, no code change). This ticket still needs its own decision between design options (a) (permit a bash single-match write into $WT for MECHANICAL rebase conflicts only, keep escalation for genuine disagreements) and (b) (keep 'always escalate on conflict' as policy, fix code/SKILL.md's 'no manual nudge needed' claim, and restate coding.md so escalation reads as a deliberate judgment boundary rather than a guard consequence). Both remain live; this note only closes off (c).

land/lode-k5e carries no fix for this ticket (contrary to what the dispatching task assumed it would say) — the probe result changed the plan. Do not close lode-8k3 on the assumption lode-k5e resolved it structurally.
DECISION (human, 2026-07-09): adopt the 'review in the reviewer's OWN launch worktree' architecture.

The probe (see prior note) FALSIFIED the EnterWorktree premise: EnterWorktree(path=...) reports success, but a separate isolation guard still hard-pins Bash/Write to the agent's original launch worktree. So 'git -C' was never a workaround for a nonexistent constraint — the constraint is real.

But the constraint does not require driving the BUILDER's worktree. Verified 2026-07-09: no land/<id> branch is checked out in any worktree — builders work on 'worktree-agent-<hash>' branches and merely PUSH to land/<id> as a remote ref. Therefore the reviewer can fetch origin/land/<id> and check it out INTO ITS OWN launch worktree, where Bash/Edit/Write/nox all work natively and cwd's HEAD *is* the branch. /code-review --fix and /simplify then analyze the real diff and write the correct tree.

This resolves lode-k5e (empty-diff review) AND lode-8k3 (rebase pickup cannot write a conflict resolution) with one architecture, and retires the 'git -C $WT' contortion plus the bash single-match workaround.

Shape:
  git fetch origin land/<id> trunk
  git checkout -B land/<id> FETCH_HEAD     # or --detach if it is checked out elsewhere
  /code-review high --fix trunk...HEAD ; /simplify
  ./scripts/python-init.sh && nox -t fix && nox -s tests
  git commit -a && git push origin HEAD:land/<id>

Known costs, accepted: (1) the launch worktree has no venv, so python-init.sh rebuilds it per review; (2) metadata.review_worktree becomes vestigial — /code SKILL.md step-1's stranded-review guard must key on review_head instead; (3) uncommitted work in the builder's worktree is invisible, which is fine because the builder's hand-off contract already requires a clean tree.

Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this fix (file a follow-up): changing whether builders keep their worktrees, and /land's worktree GC.
land/lode-k5e carries this ticket's fix too: coding.md's rebase-pickup cycle now fetches land/<id> and checks it out into its own launch worktree (option (c) from this ticket's own design), so Edit/Write work natively there. A rebase conflict is now classified before touching anything -- MECHANICAL (independent, non-overlapping additions) is resolved directly with Edit and the rebase continues; a GENUINE disagreement still aborts and escalates, per this ticket's design option (a)/(b): that stays a deliberate judgment boundary, not a tool-guard consequence. code/SKILL.md's frontmatter and the 'no manual nudge needed' claim are corrected to say so explicitly. title: Make external snapshots directly retrievable (rebuild after land bounce)
description:
Rebuild of lode-w0h.8, bounced by /land semantic review (2026-07-09).

The bounced branch (land/lode-w0h.8 @ 53caca8) was CORRECT on acceptance, scope, and approach, but violated the redact-before-index invariant (lode-n60) on the very FTS leg it introduced. Rebuild from a clean brief.

## Original scope (unchanged, all still required)
- Union external heads into the retrieval allow-list: live_head_versions UNIONs externals.head_snapshot_id (non-tombstone) so lexical_search and vector_search admit CURRENT snapshots as direct candidates. Stale (non-head) snapshots stay excluded from the direct legs; trust_rank still tiers current-vs-stale for graph-reached ones.
- Polymorphic embed-body resolution: embedding._version_body resolves versions-then-snapshots (mirror cited_answer._resolve_target) so an enqueued embed job for a snapshot_id succeeds.
- Synchronous FTS-on-ingest: the externals ingest drives the FTS leg for a snapshot synchronously itself.

## THE BOUNCE — what went wrong (blocker)
_index_snapshot_fts (externals.py) chunked the snapshot's RAW body:
    passages = chunk(body, snapshot_id, settings=settings)   # NOT redacted
For an owned note, redaction happens AT THE CALLER: Repository.save calls
    self.cache.index(note_id, version_id, redact_before_index(body, settings))
Nothing in lexical.py or chunking.py redacts on its own, and nothing upstream of ingest_snapshot redacts either (ingest_fetch_result passes result.clean_text verbatim). So the branch created a split-brain on the SAME content:
- Vector leg REDACTED: embedding.embed calls redact_before_index(_version_body(...)); the branch's own embed docstring says 'the body read from versions/snapshots is redacted'.
- FTS leg NOT REDACTED: raw text lands in passages_fts.text and passages.text.

embed NEVER writes passages_fts, so the unredacted text is never overwritten -- it persists. And because this ticket's own live_head_versions union is what admits snapshots to lexical_search, a secret in a fetched page becomes DIRECTLY keyword-retrievable. That is exactly what docs/externals.md forbids: 'Redact-before-index -- a pasted .env / API key does not become locally retrievable (vector + FTS).' The config knob is self-describing: redact_before_index_patterns = 'High-precision secret regexes kept out of the local vector/FTS index.'

Secondary consequence: passage_id is positional (f'{target_version}:{ord}'), and LexicalCacheBackend.index documents the assumption that 'the embed worker re-writes the same rows later (same deterministic passage_ids)'. That holds only if both legs chunk IDENTICAL text. Here FTS chunks raw and embed chunks redacted; if redaction shortens the body enough to drop a chunk, embed's INSERT OR REPLACE overwrites ords 0..n-1 and leaves a trailing raw-text passages row orphaned. expand_parents builds Q&A context from passages.

Why the green gate missed it: no test feeds a secret-bearing snapshot body. With ordinary text redact_before_index is the identity function, so all 895 tests passed while the invariant was broken -- the same 'N tests passed proves nothing' shape lode-w0h.1's review already taught this epic.

## REBUILD BRIEF -- must satisfy everything the bounced branch did, PLUS:
1. REDACT BEFORE CHUNKING ON THE FTS LEG. In _index_snapshot_fts, chunk redact_before_index(body, settings), not body. This restores the invariant AND makes both legs chunk identical text, re-establishing the deterministic-passage_id assumption. snapshots.body itself stays untouched (only purge clears the durable copy), exactly as versions.body does.
2. TEST IT WITH A REAL SECRET. Ingest a snapshot whose body contains a value matching a default redact_before_index_patterns entry, then assert: (a) passages_fts contains the REDACTED form and not the secret; (b) passages.text likewise; (c) a lexical_search for the secret returns no hit; (d) snapshots.body still holds the original.
3. ASSERT LEG PARITY. After ingest AND after the embed worker drains, passages rows for the snapshot must match the redacted chunking in count and text -- no orphaned trailing raw-text row.

## PRESERVE from the bounced branch (these were right)
- Commit 53caca8's ordering fix: _index_snapshot_fts runs AFTER ingest_snapshot's write txn commits, mirroring Repository.save's cache-after-commit. A nested 'with conn:' commits, which would prematurely flush the half-done irreplaceable write. Keep the embed enqueue atomic with the snapshot row.
- live_head_versions UNION with _LIVE_SNAPSHOT_PREDICATE (s.status != 'tombstone'); stale snapshots excluded by construction (only head pointers read); trust_rank untouched.
- Polymorphic _version_body (versions first, snapshots second, KeyError on neither).
- Tombstone fail-closed on BOTH legs (no FTS write, no embed enqueue) plus the read-side status guard for a source whose only-ever snapshot is a tombstone.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A freshly ingested snapshot is a DIRECT keyword hit (FTS, synchronous) and a DIRECT vector hit (after the embed worker drains), without a citing note being retrieved.
- An embed job enqueued for a snapshot_id runs to completion (no KeyError).
- Stale snapshots are not admitted to the direct legs; trust_rank ordering (current>stale) still holds for graph-reached snapshots.
- A secret-bearing snapshot body is redacted on BOTH the FTS and vector legs before indexing; snapshots.body retains the original; a lexical_search for the secret returns no hit.
- nox -t fix + nox -s tests green.
notes:
PARKED 2026-07-09 pending lode-k5e. This branch's Phase 2 technical review ran /code-review + /simplify from the reviewer's own launch worktree, which sits at trunk HEAD with an empty diff — so the mandated review tooling analyzed nothing and its 'no issues found' is not evidence of a clean branch (lode-k5e). The Opus reviewer's hand review still happened and its findings stand; what is missing is the skill's independent 5-agent coverage (CLAUDE.md adherence, shallow bug scan, git-history context, prior-PR comments, code-comment compliance). Label ready-for-land was REMOVED so /land cannot land it. Deliberately NOT set to ready-for-code-review: that would let /code's step-1 sweep re-review it with the same broken tooling. Once lode-k5e is fixed, swap needs-rereview -> ready-for-code-review to re-enter Phase 2 for a real review.
RE-REVIEW 2026-07-09: promoted needs-rereview -> ready-for-code-review after lode-k5e landed (merge bad00ea) fixing the empty-diff review bug. metadata.review_head refreshed to the branch's CURRENT origin tip, which includes the FIRST technical review's refinement commits — those are legitimately part of the branch and are what must now be re-reviewed. This is not builder drift. The prior Phase 2 ran /code-review + /simplify against an empty diff, so its 'no issues found' carried no information; the reviewer's hand findings from that pass stand, but the skill's independent coverage never ran. Re-review from scratch under the new architecture (fetch land/<id>, check out into own launch worktree, /code-review high --fix trunk...HEAD).

title: reconcile._embed_gap_step has no snapshot arm: a dead snapshot embed job is never re-enqueued
description:
Surfaced by the lode-w0h.8 technical review (2026-07-08), which deliberately did NOT fix it (not in w0h.8's acceptance criteria; adding it would be scope creep). The lode-w0h.2 review note had already anticipated filing exactly this against w0h.8.

reconcile._embed_gap_step is the self-healing net for embeddings: it finds content whose embed job never produced a vector and re-enqueues it. Its query joins 'notes JOIN versions' ONLY. Snapshots are not covered.

lode-w0h.8 made external snapshots directly retrievable by unioning externals.head_snapshot_id into live_head_versions, so a snapshot is now a first-class retrieval candidate with both a lexical leg (FTS, synchronous) and a vector leg (embed, async). The lexical leg self-heals trivially -- it is written synchronously on ingest. The VECTOR leg does not: if a snapshot's embed job exhausts its retries and reaches 'dead', nothing ever re-enqueues it, because the gap sweep cannot see snapshots.

CONSEQUENCE: a snapshot permanently present in lexical_search and permanently absent from vector_search. The hybrid retrieval pipeline (docs/retrieval.md) silently degrades to lexical-only for that source, forever, with no signal. A note's version in the same state WOULD be healed.

Note this is NOT the crash-orphan window w0h.8's reviewer closed. That fix made the embed enqueue atomic with the snapshot write (previously a nested 'with conn:' committed early, so a crash between the FTS write and enqueue_derive_jobs could leave a committed 'ok' snapshot with no embed job at all). This ticket is the case where the job WAS enqueued, ran, and died.
design:
Extend reconcile._embed_gap_step with a snapshots arm, mirroring its notes arm.

CONSTRAINT already recorded by the lode-w0h.2 review: the embed-gap reconciliation query must EXCLUDE tombstone snapshots. A tombstone has no body to embed; sweeping it would enqueue a job that can only fail, converting a silent gap into a retry loop.

Care is needed on what 'gap' means for a snapshot. For a note it is 'head version with no vector'. For an external the analogue is 'externals.head_snapshot_id with no vector, where the snapshot status != tombstone'. A SUPERSEDED snapshot must not be swept -- only the current head, matching what live_head_versions admits (verified by w0h.8's reviewer: superseded snapshots are excluded from the union).

Cross-check against lode-at8 before building: at8 covers the 'refresh job went dead, no tombstone written' case. Both tickets are about dead-letter terminals being unobserved. If at8 introduces a worker terminal-transition hook, that hook may be the better home for this too -- a dead embed job could re-enqueue or record itself directly, rather than being discovered later by a sweep. Decide which mechanism owns dead-letter recovery before implementing both.
acceptance_criteria: A snapshot whose embed job reached 'dead' is re-enqueued by reconcile's embed-gap sweep, exactly as a note's version would be. The sweep excludes tombstone snapshots (no body to embed) and superseded snapshots (only the current head_snapshot_id is swept), consistent with what live_head_versions admits. A test drives a snapshot's embed job to 'dead', runs reconcile, and asserts a fresh embed job exists; a companion test asserts a tombstoned snapshot is NOT enqueued. The relationship to lode-at8's dead-letter mechanism is settled (one owner, recorded in docs/decisions.md), not implemented twice.
notes:
Filed 2026-07-08 so the finding does not die with the lode-w0h.8 review transcript.

RELATED:
- lode-w0h.8 made snapshots retrievable (the union), which is what gives this gap user-visible consequences.
- lode-w0h.2's review note anticipated this and specified the tombstone-exclusion constraint.
- lode-at8 (dead refresh job leaves no tombstone) is the same class of defect one layer up: a dead-letter terminal that nothing observes. Consider a single owner for dead-letter recovery.
- lode-bvg (needs-decision) conflates transient 'failed' with terminal 'dead' in the enrichment_state predicate -- the same 'dead is under-observed' theme.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Ingest an external snapshot (status='ok'), which enqueues an 'embed' job for its snapshot_id.
2. Force that embed job to fail repeatedly until the worker's retry/backoff chain reaches the 'dead' terminal.
3. Run reconcile. Its _embed_gap_step queries 'notes JOIN versions' and never sees the snapshot.
4. The snapshot remains a lexical_search hit (FTS was written synchronously on ingest) but is permanently absent from vector_search.
5. Perform the same sequence for a NOTE's version: reconcile re-enqueues it. The two content types heal differently.

title: canonicalize_url preserves userinfo, so a pasted URL's credentials become part of the stored external_id
description:
Surfaced by the lode-w0h.3 technical review (2026-07-08) as a non-blocking observation, then escalated to its own ticket by the human because it is a PRIVACY surface, not a dedup nit.

lode-w0h.3's 'canonicalize_url' implements exactly the rules pinned by the debate-round-3 decision (lowercase scheme+host, strip default ports, drop fragment, strip tracking params, sort query, normalize trailing slash) and no more. userinfo is therefore PRESERVED, password included: a pasted 'https://user:hunter2@example.com/page' canonicalizes with the credentials intact.

That canonical form is not incidental -- the pinned decision makes it 'the external_id dedup key AND the w0h.6 refresh join key'. So the credential is written into external_id: a PRIMARY KEY, replicated into edges.to_id on every citing note, and (per lode-w0h.8) unioned into live_head_versions and thus reachable from the retrieval candidate set.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN AN UGLY STRING:
1. external_id is a durable identifier, not a payload field. It propagates: edges.to_id, the knowledge graph, citation surfaces, and any introspection UI (lode-8d2 would render the source URL in the browse modal and 'lode show' -- i.e. print the password on screen).
2. docs/externals.md commits to link-rot immunity, privacy, and HARD DELETE. Hard-deleting the snapshot BODY does not scrub an identifier that has been copied into edges and indexes. The credential outlives the content it guarded.
3. w0h.7 ('mark a web source no_egress') controls whether we TALK to a source. It does not help here: the secret is already at rest, in a key, before any egress decision is reached.
4. A refresh job (w0h.3's handler, reused by w0h.6) will happily re-fetch using the stored credential indefinitely, long after the user forgot it was in the URL.

Note the asymmetry that makes this look like an oversight rather than a decision: w0h.3 DOES normalize query values (parse_qsl -> urlencode round-trip) but not userinfo, and it DOES strip tracking params (utm_*, fbclid, gclid) on privacy grounds. The rule set already encodes 'strip things the user did not mean to persist' -- userinfo is the strongest instance of that class and was simply not enumerated.

This is NOT a defect in lode-w0h.3, which correctly refused to widen the pinned rules unilaterally. It is a gap in the pinned rules.
design:
The narrow question is what canonicalize_url does with userinfo. The options are not symmetric.

(a) STRIP userinfo entirely (recommended). 'https://user:pass@example.com/p' -> 'https://example.com/p'. Rationale: userinfo is transport credentials, not source identity -- two notes pasting the same page with different credentials cite the SAME source and must dedup to one node. This is the same reasoning that strips utm_*. Cost: we lose the ability to fetch a source that genuinely requires basic-auth in the URL. That is acceptable -- such a fetch should be a configured credential, never an identifier.

(b) Strip the PASSWORD, keep the username. Half-measure: still leaks the identity, still forks the node per-user, still writes a personal identifier into a primary key. Reject.

(c) Keep userinfo but redact it at display time. Rejects the actual problem -- the secret is still at rest in a primary key, in edges, and in indexes; only the UI lies about it. Reject.

MIGRATION IS THE REAL WORK, and it is why this should be decided NOW. Changing canonicalize_url changes external_id for already-stored externals. Today that set is empty or near-empty (w0h.3 has not landed a real draw-down against a live store). After w0h.6/w0h.8 land and real snapshots accumulate, this needs a re-key + edge-repoint migration -- machinery that w0h.3 ALREADY has in _repoint_edges for the redirect wrinkle, but which would have to be run as a one-shot over existing rows. Do it before there is anything to migrate.

Also decide the adjacent, already-identified gaps in the same pass, since they are the same class ('what is source identity?'): path percent-encoding is not normalized ('%7E' != '~') while query values are; IDN hosts are not punycoded. See lode-w0h.6's inherited-constraint note. Settle all three in docs/externals.md as the canonicalization contract, so w0h.6 inherits a decision rather than an accident.
acceptance_criteria: canonicalize_url strips userinfo (both username and password) from the canonical form, so credentials never enter external_id, edges.to_id, or any index. A test asserts that 'https://user:pass@example.com/p', 'https://user@example.com/p', and 'https://example.com/p' all canonicalize to one identical external_id. The canonicalization contract -- including the settled disposition of path percent-encoding and IDN hosts -- is recorded in docs/externals.md as the definition of source identity, and docs/configuration.md notes it is the w0h.6 refresh join key. If any external rows already exist with userinfo in their external_id, a one-shot re-key + edge repoint is applied (reusing w0h.3's _repoint_edges shape); if none exist, the ticket states that and skips the migration.
notes:
Filed at the human's direction (2026-07-08) after the lode-w0h.3 reviewer flagged it as a non-blocker.

RELATED:
- lode-w0h.3 introduced canonicalize_url. Not its bug -- it implemented the pinned rules faithfully.
- lode-w0h.6 carries an inherited-constraint note covering this plus percent-encoding and IDN. Resolve together; w0h.6 should not have to decide it.
- lode-w0h.7 (no_egress) does NOT mitigate this -- the secret is at rest before any egress gate.
- lode-w0h.8 unions externals.head_snapshot_id into live_head_versions, widening where the identifier is reachable.
- lode-8d2 would render an external's source URL in the browse modal and 'lode show' -- i.e. display the credential.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Capture a note whose body contains 'https://user:hunter2@example.com/page'.
2. lode-w0h.3's detect_and_enqueue_drawdown extracts the URL and calls canonicalize_url.
3. Inspect the resulting external_id (and the source='user' edge's to_id): the credential 'user:hunter2@' is present verbatim.
4. Paste the same page with different credentials in a second note: a SECOND external node is created for what is one source.
5. Hard-delete the snapshot body per docs/externals.md. The credential survives in external_id and in every edges.to_id that referenced it.
BUILD SUMMARY (lode-0as): canonicalize_url now drops userinfo (user[:pass]@) entirely -- 'https://user:pass@host/p', 'https://user@host/p', and 'https://host/p' all canonicalize to one external_id. Migration check: queried the local ~/.lode/lode.db (4 notes, real dev store) before making the change -- 0 rows in externals, 0 edges.to_id containing '@'. No existing rows to re-key, so no migration script was written; documented that check in docs/externals.md so a future revisit re-checks rather than assumes. Also settled (out of scope for a code change) the two adjacent gaps -- path percent-encoding and IDN hosts -- as a deliberate 'left unnormalized for now' decision with reasoning, recorded in docs/externals.md alongside the userinfo rule; docs/configuration.md's URL tracking-param blocklist row now also notes the w0h.6 refresh-join-key relationship and the userinfo fix. Gates green: nox -t fix (no changes), nox -s tests (924 passed, 6 skipped). Pushed origin/land/lode-0as @ 996614d5c32058f8b610715106f1878d5a0dd4c5.

The Opus reviewer's hand review still happened and its findings stand; what is missing is the skill's independent 5-agent coverage (CLAUDE.md adherence, shallow bug scan, git-history context, prior-PR comments, code-comment compliance). Label ready-for-land was REMOVED so /land cannot land it. Deliberately NOT set to ready-for-code-review: that would let /code's step-1 sweep re-review it with the same broken tooling. Once lode-k5e is fixed, swap needs-rereview -> ready-for-code-review to re-enter Phase 2 for a real review.

This is not builder drift. The prior Phase 2 ran /code-review + /simplify against an empty diff, so its 'no issues found' carried no information; the reviewer's hand findings from that pass stand, but the skill's independent coverage never ran. Re-review from scratch under the new architecture (fetch land/<id>, check out into own launch worktree, /code-review high --fix trunk...HEAD).

title: land/SKILL.md: escalate exit (a) snippet edits --description, but land-review reads --acceptance
description:

title: webfetch User-Agent advertises a fabricated repo URL to every third-party server
description:
src/lode/webfetch.py:120 sets

    _USER_AGENT = "lode-webfetch/1 (+https://github.com/anthropics/lode)"

That URL does not exist. The repo is git@github.com:bildzeitung/lode.git. The convention for the `+<url>` token in a bot User-Agent is a page a server operator can visit to find out who is fetching them and how to contact/block them — so this is not cosmetic: every site lode draws down receives a dead link claiming Anthropic ownership of this crawler.

Surfaced as a non-blocking nit by /land semantic review of lode-w0h.1 (landed on trunk @ 795732a); it is outward-facing, so it is filed rather than dropped.
acceptance_criteria: _USER_AGENT points at a real, reachable URL for this project (or the +<url> token is dropped entirely rather than faked). No test asserts the fabricated anthropics/lode string.
notes: CODE REVIEW (Opus, lode-yzv): The build took AC branch one (repoint the +<url> at github.com/bildzeitung/lode). That URL is real, public and anonymously reachable (verified HTTP 200), so branch one is literally satisfied — but branch two is better and the AC pre-authorizes it, so the reviewer took it. Reasons: (1) branch one presumes a project-owned URL; none exists — the only real URL is a maintainer's PERSONAL GitHub account. Self-hosted tools that legitimately ship +<url> point at a project identity (Miniflux -> miniflux.app, FreshRSS -> freshrss.org), not a person. (2) Per the ticket's own definition the +<url> tells an operator 'who is fetching them and how to contact/block them'; for a locally-run personal KB that party is the END USER, never the repo owner — so the fix made the link live while the MISATTRIBUTION SURVIVED (an individual swapped in for Anthropic), and the operator still cannot contact or block the actual fetcher. (3) docs/externals.md frames lode as explicitly NOT a crawler ('Recursion = unbounded web crawler, not a notes app'); +<url> is a crawler/centrally-operated-bot convention. (4) The constant's own comment already justified only the product token ('identifiable, non-empty UA rather than a bare httpx default') — the URL did no work. PRIVACY, stated precisely: docs/externals.md's privacy section is scoped to CONTENT egress to Anthropic and does NOT legislate on UA metadata, so this is NOT a documented-policy violation — but its ethic ('Single-user does not mean low-stakes... a concentrated high-value target', plus its refusal to overclaim what leaves the box) cuts the same way: broadcasting a named individual's account to every third-party host drawn down from buys the user nothing, and for the repo owner running his own tool it correlates IP <-> identity at every host. Result: _USER_AGENT = 'lode-webfetch/1' — still greppable and blockable, the one affordance an operator can act on. Restore (+<url>) if lode ever gains a project-owned URL. Gates green on the working tree: nox -t fix clean, nox -s tests 867 passed / 6 skipped. No docs/ change -> mermaid gate N/A. Not escalated because the AC explicitly pre-authorizes BOTH branches — no clarifying decision is owed to a human. If the human disagrees, /land's semantic review is the natural second non-author check and this is a one-line revert.

title: enrichment_state 'failed' buckets a TRANSIENT job with the dead-letter terminal
description:
Found during the technical review of lode-ay5.1 (not introduced by it -- the predicate was pinned by the epic's debate note and implemented faithfully).

enrichment_view._enrichment_state() reports 'failed' when the head has an enrich job with status in ('failed','dead') and zero source='ai' rows. But schema.sql says 'failed' is the TRANSIENT state, not a terminal: worker._reset_backoff_ready_failed flips 'failed AND next_attempt_at <= now' back to 'pending'. Only 'dead' is the dead-letter terminal.

Consequence: a note whose enrich job hit a transient 429 reads 'failed' to the user for the length of its backoff window, then 'pending', then 'ready'. The TUI modal (lode-ay5.2) and 'lode show' (lode-ay5.3) will both present a retrying job as a dead-letter failure. The epic's debate note that pinned this predicate called 'failed'/'dead' both 'terminals' -- the schema contradicts that.

The reviewer deliberately did NOT change it: under a THREE-value constraint, including 'failed' is strictly better than excluding it (excluding would make a transiently-failed job read 'ready' or enriched-empty -- the exact misread the epic exists to kill). There is nowhere to put it without a fourth state.
design:
DECIDED 2026-07-08 (human): option (3) -- map transient 'failed' -> 'pending'; reserve the user-facing 'failed' state for job status='dead' only.

RATIONALE. worker.py writes status='failed' ONLY in the else-branch of the max-attempts gate (worker.py:245 for the reclaim path, worker.py:401 for the run_one path); the >= retry_max_attempts branch writes 'dead'. Therefore a job in 'failed' ALWAYS has a retry coming -- there is no non-retrying 'failed' job. 'failed' job status is, definitionally, pending work. The mapping is not a compromise; it is what the data means.

NOT A CONTRADICTION OF THE PIN. The ay5 epic DESIGN says 'a dead-lettered enrich job reads failed'. That is exactly option (3). The three-value pin {pending, ready, failed} is preserved as-is; what changes is that ay5.1's implementation over-broadened the terminal bucket to ('failed','dead'), and docs/storage.md then recorded that over-broadening as an accepted caveat. This restores the epic's stated intent. No decision needs re-pinning.

ACCEPTED COST: a job deep in backoff is indistinguishable from a freshly-enqueued one until it dead-letters. Acceptable -- the epic exists to stop enrichment failure from masquerading as enriched-empty, and 'pending' does not do that; jobs.last_error retains the diagnostic; cli.py:717 already lists dead rows.

IMPLEMENTATION (all in one worktree):
1. src/lode/enrichment_view.py:57,63 -- _LIVE_JOB_STATUSES = ('pending','running','failed'); _DEAD_JOB_STATUSES = ('dead',). The live check at :269 runs first, so ordering already yields the correct result; no restructuring of _enrichment_state needed.
2. src/lode/enrichment_view.py module docstring (~lines 30-36) -- restate the 'failed' bullet as job status='dead' only, and the comments on the two constants at :56-63.
3. docs/storage.md:256-260 -- rewrite the predicate bullets to match.
4. docs/storage.md:275-279 -- DELETE the 'Known caveat ... awaiting a human decision' paragraph; it documents the bug being fixed.
5. Test: a job forced to status='failed' with next_attempt_at in the future must read enrichment_state == 'pending'; a job at status='dead' with zero source='ai' rows must read 'failed'. tests/test_cli.py:1013 (wording-distinct test) should still pass.

lode-ay5.2 (TUI modal, in_progress) renders the three states and needs NO change; it should be built against the corrected predicate.
acceptance_criteria: enrichment_state distinguishes a job that will retry from a dead-lettered one, or the epic explicitly accepts that it does not and says so in docs/storage.md. lode-ay5.2 and lode-ay5.3 render whatever is decided consistently.
notes:
Surfaced by the technical review of lode-ay5.1, 2026-07-08. Blocks nothing today (ay5.1's seam ships the pinned predicate); becomes user-visible the moment ay5.2 or ay5.3 renders it.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Seed a note; enqueue its enrich job; force the job to status='failed' with next_attempt_at in the future (a transient 429 does this).
2. Call enrichment_view(db_path, note_id).
3. enrichment_state reads 'failed' -- indistinguishable from a dead-lettered job.
4. Wait past next_attempt_at, run the worker: the job flips to 'pending' and the same note now reads 'pending'.
PARKED 2026-07-09 pending lode-k5e. This branch's Phase 2 technical review ran /code-review + /simplify from the reviewer's own launch worktree, which sits at trunk HEAD with an empty diff — so the mandated review tooling analyzed nothing and its 'no issues found' is not evidence of a clean branch (lode-k5e). The Opus reviewer's hand review still happened and its findings stand; what is missing is the skill's independent 5-agent coverage (CLAUDE.md adherence, shallow bug scan, git-history context, prior-PR comments, code-comment compliance). Label ready-for-land was REMOVED so /land cannot land it. Deliberately NOT set to ready-for-code-review: that would let /code's step-1 sweep re-review it with the same broken tooling. Once lode-k5e is fixed, swap needs-rereview -> ready-for-code-review to re-enter Phase 2 for a real review.
RE-REVIEW 2026-07-09: promoted needs-rereview -> ready-for-code-review after lode-k5e landed (merge bad00ea) fixing the empty-diff review bug. metadata.review_head refreshed to the branch's CURRENT origin tip, which includes the FIRST technical review's refinement commits — those are legitimately part of the branch and are what must now be re-reviewed. This is not builder drift. The prior Phase 2 ran /code-review + /simplify against an empty diff, so its 'no issues found' carried no information; the reviewer's hand findings from that pass stand, but the skill's independent coverage never ran. Re-review from scratch under the new architecture (fetch land/<id>, check out into own launch worktree, /code-review high --fix trunk...HEAD).

metadata.land_summary: Map transient enrich job status='failed' -> enrichment_state 'pending'; reserve 'failed' for 'dead' only. Predicate live-check ordering already correct; docs/storage.md + enrichment_view + cli.py docstrings + tests updated; stale lode-bvg caveat removed from cli.py.

The identical stale instruction survives in Step 0 (the needs-rebase sweep), which tells the coding producer to 'EnterWorktree (path form) into the recorded build worktree' and repeats it in the dispatch prompt ('read metadata.review_worktree from bd, EnterWorktree into it'). .claude/agents/coding.md's own Rebase pickup cycle says the opposite: it drives $WT purely via git -C / nox -f and notes Edit/Write stay guard-pinned to its launch worktree. title: code/SKILL.md still tells reviewers to EnterWorktree (path form); isolation guard refuses it
description:

In practice the isolation guard REFUSES commands resolved into a path-entered worktree, so the reviewer cannot do this.

Observed 2026-07-08: the code-reviewer dispatched at lode-nps.3 declined EnterWorktree deliberately and drove the builder worktree via 'git -C' instead, per its own agent doc (.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md), completing the review normally.

So .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md is CORRECT (git -C) and .claude/skills/code/SKILL.md is STALE — it predates the git -C reviewer mechanics that landed in commit 957e759 (which aligned docs/agents-workflow.md but not this skill). The main session's dispatch prompts inherit the stale wording and tell every reviewer to do the wrong thing; each reviewer then has to notice and route around it.

Fix: update code/SKILL.md Phase 2 + Step 0 to say 'drive the recorded worktree via git -C' rather than EnterWorktree, and correct the stated rationale for isolation: "worktree" (it gives a legal cwd off the repo root, not a license to path-enter).

notes:
Discovered during Phase 2 review of lode-nps.3. Blocked-ish on lode-95o, which is concurrently editing code/SKILL.md — sequence after it lands to avoid a merge collision.

## Steps to Reproduce

title: code-reviewer.md: forbid backgrounding nox gates during re-gate (same hazard as lode-95o)
description: lode-95o hardened .claude/agents/coding.md to forbid run_in_background/Monitor for nox gates and stop-on-pending-wait, because a subagent with no live background children is stopped by the harness and can never receive the notification it armed. .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md's step 5 (re-gate: nox -f "$WT/noxfile.py" -t fix / -s tests) runs the identical gate pattern and has the identical latent hazard — nothing in that file currently forbids backgrounding it. Apply the same fix: add a non-negotiable forbidding run_in_background/Monitor for its nox invocations, and reinforce it inline at step 5 where the gate actually runs, mirroring the coding.md edit from lode-95o.
acceptance_criteria: .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md explicitly forbids run_in_background/Monitor for its nox gate invocations (step 5, re-gate) and requires foreground execution with output read in the same turn, mirroring the non-negotiable added to .claude/agents/coding.md in lode-95o.
notes:
SCOPE EXTENSION (main /code session, 2026-07-08): add a SECOND non-negotiable to code-reviewer.md while you are
in this file — a clean-worktree assertion. This is the DETECTION half of lode-tpt (which owns the PREVENTION half
in coding.md). They are deliberately split because they live in different files and would otherwise collide.

WHY BOTH. lode-tpt fixes the builder so it cannot hand off a dirty tree. But the reviewer is the last gate before
a branch is landable, and on 2026-07-08 the reviewer was the ONLY thing that caught a builder handing off a
36-line uncommitted delta (lode-nps.2) — it noticed only because it happened to diff the working tree rather than
trusting `review_head`. Nothing in code-reviewer.md requires that. A reviewer that checks out review_head and
reviews it faithfully would silently drop the builder's final work, with every signal green.

WHAT TO ADD
1. On ENTRY, before reviewing: assert `git -C "$WT" status --short` is empty. If it is NOT, the builder violated
   its hand-off contract (lode-tpt). Do not silently fold the delta in and do not silently discard it — surface
   it: report the delta, fold it into the review commit, and say so explicitly in the hand-off summary. (Folding
   it in is what the nps.2 reviewer did, and it was right; the defect is that it was discretionary.)
2. On EXIT, before swapping the ticket to ready-for-land: assert `git -C "$WT" status --short` is empty again, so
   the reviewer cannot commit the same sin it is checking for.
3. Same ordering caveat as lode-tpt: a dirty tree at RE-GATE time invalidates the gate, because nox reads the
   working tree, not HEAD. Assert clean before the re-gate, not only before the push.

This is not belt-and-braces for its own sake. The failure mode is SILENT — every existing signal (label present,
origin ref resolves, review_head matches, gates green) reads correct while the branch is missing content. A
one-line `git status --short` is the cheapest possible detector for a defect with no other symptom.

PRIORITY: consider raising this from P2 to P1 when you pick it up — its original scope (the nox backgrounding
hazard, mirroring lode-95o) is genuine but latent; this added scope catches an actively silent data-loss path.

metadata.land_summary: code-reviewer.md: forbid backgrounding the re-gate nox invocations (lode-95o, mirrors coding.md) + clean-worktree assertions at entry/pre-re-gate/exit (sanctioned lode-tpt detection half). Review fixed a self-nullifying pre-gate assertion (commit-before-gate), an open-loop exit recovery that could record an unpushed land_head, and two wording inaccuracies.

title: Harden bd dolt push against concurrent-writer rejection + embedded-mode lock contention under /code fan-out
description:
Discovered while validating lode-nps.3 (concurrent bd dolt push under /code N-producer fan-out).

Determination: bd dolt push to refs/dolt/data never silently loses a write under concurrent
producers -- Dolt's push is fast-forward-only + atomically CAS-protected on the branch ref, same
guarantee as git push (documented at https://www.dolthub.com/docs/concepts/dolt/git/remotes), and
lode's remote is itself a plain git remote so a git server's own atomic ref-update is a second
enforcement layer underneath it. A losing push is REJECTED, not corrupted or dropped. That part is
recorded as an explicit invariant in docs/agents-workflow.md (see "Concurrent bd dolt push under
fan-out" subsection, under "The producers").

But two real gaps sit on top of that safe-but-not-self-healing primitive:

1. NO RETRY-ON-REJECT. Every `bd dolt push` call site in the skills (.claude/agents/coding.md,
   .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md, .claude/skills/land/SKILL.md) is a bare call with no
   exit-status check. Under concurrent producers a rejected (non-fast-forward) push is an EXPECTED
   outcome, not an edge case -- today it just fails silently, so the "durable, cross-machine"
   hand-off the comments assume may not have actually reached origin's refs/dolt/data.

2. EMBEDDED MODE IS THE WRONG MODE FOR THIS, BY BEADS' OWN DOCS. lode runs bd in embedded
   (in-process Dolt engine) mode (`bd dolt show` -> `Mode: embedded`). Every git worktree of this
   repo -- confirmed via `bd where` run from inside a linked .claude/worktrees/ checkout, no
   .beads/redirect needed -- resolves to ONE shared physical Dolt store on a machine
   (.beads/embeddeddolt at the main checkout). Beads' own docs (docs/DOLT.md, docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md)
   are explicit: "Embedded mode is single-writer (enforced via file lock). If you need concurrent
   access, switch to server mode" and "For high-concurrency scenarios (multiple agents), use Dolt
   server mode ... which handles concurrent access natively." /code's bare fan-out -- N producer
   worktrees on one machine, all writing bd state -- is precisely that scenario. The documented
   failure mode is a hard "database is locked" error with no built-in retry (troubleshooting's fix
   is "find and kill hanging processes").

Both gaps were live during this investigation: 9 producer worktrees were concurrently active on
this machine while validating this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) add a retry-on-reject (pull, merge, push again) loop to every bd dolt push call site in the skills, or (b) evaluate and decide whether lode should switch local bd config to Dolt server mode (bd dolt set mode server) for /code fan-out safety, or (c) both. Record the decision + rationale in docs/decisions.md or docs/agents-workflow.md. This ticket builds the fix; lode-nps.3 only validated and documented the gap.
notes:
CORRECTION (code-review of lode-nps.3, 2026-07-08): this ticket's description enumerates THREE bd dolt push call sites. There are FOUR -- .claude/skills/epic-audit/SKILL.md:151 (`rtk bd dolt push  # publish gap tickets + escalations + label changes`) was omitted. epic-audit is one of the landing-side loops declared to run unattended, so the retry-on-reject fix MUST cover it too. docs/agents-workflow.md has been corrected to say 'all four'. Verified via: grep -rl 'rtk bd dolt push' .claude/
CODE REVIEW (Opus, 2026-07-08): Found and fixed one real bug — the retry loop's exit paths were both inside the loop body, so a zero/negative/non-numeric BD_DOLT_PUSH_MAX_ATTEMPTS skipped the body entirely and fell off the end of the script with exit 0, reporting a bd dolt push that never ran (the exact silent-strand the wrapper exists to prevent). Added a terminal 'exit 1' after the loop. Verified against a fake bd binary across 8 paths, all asserting exit codes: immediate success (0), retry-then-succeed (0), exhaust-and-fail (propagates the real code, 7), MAX_ATTEMPTS=0 (now 1, was 0), MAX_ATTEMPTS=abc (now 1, was 0), failing intermediate 'bd dolt pull' (swallowed by design, push still retries), BASE_DELAY=0 (non-zero, no silent success), flag forwarding via "$@". Confirmed the builder's reported $?-after-if bug is genuinely fixed and no sibling instance survives ($? is captured directly after 'bd dolt push'). Shebang is '#!/bin/bash -u' (no -e) — correct, since -e would kill the script on the intentionally-failing push. Wrapper does not 'bd import' and never touches .beads/*.jsonl (CLAUDE.md invariant honored). Blanket retry-on-any-nonzero was judged CORRECT rather than discriminating on error text: bd/Dolt error strings are not a stable contract, the schedule is bounded (~35s worst case), the real exit code always propagates, and 'bd dolt pull' is itself the sanctioned wire (import.auto:false, so no jsonl hook can fire) — a permanent error (bad auth, missing remote) costs ~35s of noisy stderr and then exits non-zero, never silently. Merge surface: doc edits are localized to call sites + adjacent explanatory prose, no unrelated reformatting.

RESIDUAL (deliberately not fixed here, to keep the merge surface narrow): a FIFTH directive 'bd dolt push' call site exists at .claude/skills/debate/SKILL.md:104 ('...then `bd dolt push` so the writes reach the wire'). It was missed by the ticket's own 'grep -rl "rtk bd dolt push"' correction because that line has no 'rtk' prefix. /debate is human-invoked and interactive (the operator sees a failed push), unlike the four unattended loops this branch rewired, so the risk is materially lower. Worth a one-line follow-up.

metadata.land_summary: Adds scripts/bd-dolt-push.sh (backoff+jitter retry wrapper around bd dolt push, re-pulling between attempts) and rewires all four unattended-loop call sites to it; decision + why-not-server-mode recorded in docs/decisions.md. Review fixed a silent-exit-0 path where a degenerate BD_DOLT_PUSH_MAX_ATTEMPTS skipped the loop and reported a push that never ran.

title: Define exit (a) re-entry for producer-side land-escalated escalations
description:
lode-nps.2 defined the three resolution exits for `land-escalated` as /land's semantic
review sets it. But `/code`'s producers set the SAME label from three other places:

- `coding` build-time clarifying decision (.claude/agents/coding.md) — branch green-but-possibly-
  incomplete, ticket never reached `ready-for-code-review`
- `code-reviewer` technical-review escalation (.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md) — `ready-for-code-review`
  removed, branch green + pushed
- `coding` rebase-pickup conflict (.claude/agents/coding.md) — `needs-rebase` removed

Exits (b) rebuild and (c) drop apply to all of these unchanged (they only close + GC). Exit (a)
'land as-is' does NOT: it prescribes `--add-label ready-for-land`, which for a build-time escalation
would skip the technical review entirely, and for a rebase-conflict escalation hands /land a branch
that still does not merge onto trunk (it gets kicked straight back to needs-rebase).

## What 'done' looks like
Define, in .claude/skills/land/SKILL.md (and mirror into docs/agents-workflow.md), the exit-(a)
re-entry label per escalation source. Proposed principle, needs a human call: re-enter at the GATE
THAT ESCALATED, so that gate re-runs against the now-unambiguous ticket — /land -> ready-for-land,
code-reviewer -> ready-for-code-review, rebase-pickup -> needs-rebase. The build-time case is the
genuinely arguable one (the build may be incomplete, so re-entering at ready-for-code-review would
review a half-built branch; a rebuild via exit (b) may be the right answer instead).

Surfaced by the technical review of lode-nps.2.
notes:
## Acceptance Criteria
- land/SKILL.md 'Resolving a land-escalated branch' states the exit-(a) re-entry label for each of the four setters of land-escalated (/land semantic review, coding build-time, code-reviewer, coding rebase-pickup).
- The build-time case is explicitly decided (re-enter at ready-for-code-review, or rebuild via exit (b)) rather than left implicit.
- docs/agents-workflow.md mirrors the decision in one clause; it does not restate the mechanics.
- Exits (b) and (c) are confirmed source-agnostic (no change needed).
- bd list --label land-escalated can still reach empty from every setter.

DECISION (human, 2026-07-08): RE-ENTER AT THE GATE THAT ESCALATED. The ticket's proposed principle is ACCEPTED
as written, including the arguable build-time case.

  escalated by                     -> exit (a) re-entry label
  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  /land semantic review            -> ready-for-land
  code-reviewer technical review   -> ready-for-code-review
  coding rebase-pickup conflict    -> needs-rebase
  coding build-time clarification  -> ready-for-code-review

Rationale: one uniform rule, no special cases. Every gate re-runs against the now-unambiguous ticket, so the
gate that could not decide is the gate that decides.

ACCEPTED TRADE-OFF (stated, not hidden): a build-time escalation means the builder stopped mid-build, so its
branch is green-but-possibly-INCOMPLETE and never reached ready-for-code-review. Re-entering it at
ready-for-code-review therefore hands the code-reviewer a branch that may not implement the whole ticket. The
human accepted this rather than forcing exit (b) rebuild, because a trivially-answerable build question should
not cost a full rebuild when the branch is in fact complete.

MITIGATIONS the implementation MUST carry (these are what make the accepted trade-off safe):
1. The human resolving a build-time escalation writes the answer into the ticket (--append-notes) BEFORE applying
   ready-for-code-review, so the reviewer reads the resolved ambiguity rather than rediscovering it.
2. The code-reviewer already owns "bounce" and "escalate" verdicts. A half-built branch is exactly what those
   exist for -- the reviewer is not obliged to pass an incomplete branch, and should escalate again (or the
   lander's later semantic review, land-review, catches it against the ticket's acceptance criteria). The
   re-entry is not an assertion that the branch is complete; it is an assertion that the AMBIGUITY is resolved.
3. Document in land/SKILL.md that exit (a) at the build-time source means "the decision is made, re-run the
   pipeline from technical review", NOT "this branch is finished".

IMPLEMENTATION
- Define the per-source exit-(a) re-entry label in .claude/skills/land/SKILL.md (the exits section lode-nps.2
  landed), and MIRROR it into docs/agents-workflow.md -- design facts live in docs/ per CLAUDE.md.
- Exits (b) rebuild and (c) drop apply to ALL FOUR sources unchanged (they only close + GC).
- lode-nps.2 landed the three exits for /land's own escalations and explicitly carved out the producer-side
  sources, deferring them to THIS ticket. Do not re-litigate nps.2's definitions; extend them.
- NOTE: land/SKILL.md is also touched by lode-83d. Sequence to avoid a merge collision.

metadata.land_summary: Defines exit-(a) re-entry label per land-escalated source (re-enter at the gate that escalated) in land/SKILL.md + one-clause mirror in docs/agents-workflow.md; review corrected a false 'code-reviewer owns bounce' claim (it owns escalate only; bounce is land-review's) and aligned the per-source table. Downstream gaps filed as lode-t83.

title: /debate: persist findings + surface decisions one-at-a-time by default
description: Change the debate skill (.claude/skills/debate/SKILL.md) so its two closing behaviors become DEFAULTS instead of opt-in. Currently SKILL.md section 4 says 'By default I just tell you' and only persists 'if you ask', and the skill stops after the readout. User preference (2026-07-08): (1) ALWAYS persist the analysis to the relevant beads tickets (bd update --notes per item) as the default final step of a debate; (2) AFTER persisting, the default NEXT step is to surface the identified decisions to the user ONE AT A TIME (one AskUserQuestion per decision, not a batch), driving each to resolution before the next. Keep an explicit opt-out (user can say 'just tell me, don't persist'). Do NOT auto-edit docs/ or tickets' design fields as a side effect — persistence is to --notes; design/doc edits stay a separate explicit step, as today.

title: Record the debate decisions in docs/ (reject auto-close; defer caps; concurrency assumption; land-escalated gap)
description:

facts live in docs/, never only in tickets or memory — a fact that lives only in a
ticket forks the record). Touches docs/agents-workflow.md and docs/decisions.md. MUST be

## Decisions to record
1. The loop family (`/code` + `/land` + `/epic-audit` + `/sweep`) is intended to run
   UNATTENDED; `/sweep` is the exception-surfacing leg that makes that safe.
2. The load-bearing concurrency assumption is that concurrent `bd dolt push` from the
   N-producer fan-out is safe — NOT any lock. "single-lander lock" guards `trunk` only.
   (Cross-reference the validation ticket / its outcome.)

   human-decision queue can drain.

title: Validate concurrent bd dolt push under /code N-producer fan-out
description:
Validate that concurrent `bd dolt push` to `refs/dolt/data` is SAFE under the existing
`/code` N-producer fan-out. This is the real (and PRE-EXISTING) load-bearing assumption
behind running the loops unattended — reframed out of the debate's "does /sweep need a
bd-write lock" (a category error: the single-lander lock guards `trunk`, not Dolt).

## Why this matters
Bare `/code` fans out N parallel producers, each doing its own `bd dolt push`
(code/SKILL.md), plus reviewers, plus `/land`. So the system is ALREADY many-writer to
Dolt. If concurrent pushes to `refs/dolt/data` can be rejected (non-fast-forward, like a
git push race) or silently lose a write, that is a bug in the CURRENT loop — independent
of `/sweep`. If it is safe (as the shipped fan-out implies), then adding `/sweep` (one
self-owned digest row) is trivially safe.

## What "done" looks like
- A determination, with evidence, of what `bd dolt push` does under concurrent writers:
  does Dolt serialize / merge disjoint-row writes server-side, does a loser get rejected
  and need retry, or is there a real lost-write window?
- If safe: record the assumption explicitly in docs/ so it is a stated invariant, not a
  lucky accident.
- If NOT safe: file a follow-up bug against the loop (retry-on-reject, or a real
  serialization mechanism) — this ticket only VALIDATES; it does not build the fix.

## Notes
- Producers write DISJOINT rows (each owns its ticket); same-row contention is the only
  thing that truly races. `/sweep`'s digest row is written by nothing else, so `/sweep`
  cannot contend regardless of the answer.
- Distributed `refs/locks/land` is a separately-deferred item (docs/decisions.md) and is
  about TRUNK landing, not this Dolt question — do not conflate.
design:
DETERMINATION (evidence-backed, grounded in Dolt's documented push/merge semantics, not a stress
test): bd dolt push to refs/dolt/data is fast-forward-only + atomic-CAS-protected on the branch
ref, exactly like git push (https://www.dolthub.com/docs/concepts/dolt/git/remotes). A racing
loser is REJECTED outright, never silently lost -- confirmed further by beads#2466 (a real
multi-machine push/pull conflict, fixed in beads v0.60.0). Recorded as an explicit invariant in
docs/agents-workflow.md ("Concurrent bd dolt push under fan-out", under "The producers").

BUT two real gaps surfaced on top of that safe-but-not-self-healing primitive, filed as a
follow-up bug (lode-83d, discovered-from this ticket) since this ticket validates only:
1. No retry-on-reject in any bd dolt push call site across the skills (coding.md,
   code-reviewer.md, land/SKILL.md) -- a rejected push fails silently today.
2. lode runs bd in EMBEDDED mode (bd dolt show -> Mode: embedded), and every git worktree on this
   machine shares ONE physical Dolt store (.beads/embeddeddolt at the main checkout, confirmed via
   `bd where`). Beads' own docs say embedded mode is single-writer (file lock) and recommend
   SERVER mode for "high-concurrency scenarios (multiple agents)" -- precisely /code's fan-out.
   Failure mode: hard "database is locked" error, no built-in retry.
acceptance_criteria: A written, evidence-backed determination of bd dolt push behavior under concurrent writers. If safe: the assumption is recorded as an explicit invariant in docs/. If unsafe: a follow-up bug is filed against the loop (this ticket validates only, does not build the fix).
notes:
CRITICISM (/debate 2026-07-08):
1. 'VALIDATE' METHOD UNDER-SPECIFIED. Acceptance 'an evidence-backed determination' is satisfiable two very different ways: (a) reading Dolt's documented refs/dolt/data push semantics (does it fast-forward-check and reject the loser like a git push race, or server-side-merge disjoint rows?), or (b) a stress test firing N concurrent pushes. Different confidence — and (b) is a TRAP: a green stress run cannot PROVE absence of a rare lost-write race, only its non-occurrence in that run. FIX: require the determination to rest on Dolt's push/merge semantics (docs or source), with any stress test as corroboration, not proof. (Ticket already gestures at the right question — this just mandates the grounding.)

metadata.land_summary: Records concurrent bd dolt push under /code fan-out as a validated invariant in docs/agents-workflow.md (fast-forward-only + atomic CAS: a racing push is rejected, never silently lost); two gaps filed as lode-83d.

title: /land Section 3 batch-merge aborts on a STAGED .beads/issues.jsonl (git diff reads clean, git merge refuses)
description:
/land's batch-merge (Section 3) assumes a clean index. In practice bd dolt pull (Section 1) can leave .beads/issues.jsonl STAGED in the index — the working tree matches the staged blob, so 'git diff' / 'git diff --quiet' report CLEAN, but 'git merge --no-ff' aborts with 'error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge: .beads/issues.jsonl / Merge with strategy ort failed.' This bit a real land pass (lode-ccv/lode-81e/lode-5g4, 2026-07-07): all three merges failed repeatedly even though none of the branches carried a committed jsonl diff and no bd daemon was running.

Root cause: the churn is a STAGED index change (index blob != HEAD blob, worktree == index), not an unstaged worktree change. 'git checkout -- .beads/issues.jsonl' does NOT clear it (it only touches the worktree, leaving the index entry staged), so a naive reset loops. The fix that worked: 'git restore --staged --worktree .beads/issues.jsonl' (equivalently 'git reset -q HEAD -- .beads/issues.jsonl && git checkout -- .beads/issues.jsonl') to unstage back to HEAD before merging.

This is a sharper variant of the known 'never commit the passive jsonl' footgun (CLAUDE.md / lode-6ra): the existing guidance covers not COMMITTING it, but Section 3 has no step to reset a STAGED jsonl before the merge, and 'git diff' clean is misleading. It bites repeatedly (every pass where bd left jsonl staged).
design:
Fix in .claude/skills/land/SKILL.md Section 1 (or a pre-merge step in Section 3): before the batch merge, hard-reset the passive export out of the index+worktree so a staged jsonl can't abort 'git merge'. Recommend adding, right before the Section 3 merge loop:

  rtk git restore --staged --worktree .beads/issues.jsonl 2>/dev/null || true   # unstage the passive export; a STAGED jsonl aborts merge even though 'git diff' reads clean

Note in the SKILL text WHY 'git diff' being clean is not sufficient (staged != unstaged) and why 'git checkout --' alone doesn't fix it. Cross-check the 'What I never do' / bd-sync-discipline section so the reset is framed as 'never let the passive export block or enter a merge', consistent with import.auto:false. Keep it a docs-only SKILL change.
acceptance_criteria: land/SKILL.md has an explicit pre-merge step that unstages/discards .beads/issues.jsonl (staged OR unstaged) before the Section 3 batch merge, with a one-line note that 'git diff' clean is misleading because the churn is staged; the recommended command uses 'git restore --staged --worktree' (not a bare 'git checkout --'). No behavior change beyond the SKILL doc.

metadata.land_summary: land/SKILL.md: unstage passive .beads/issues.jsonl (git restore --staged --worktree) before Section 3 batch merge — a STAGED jsonl aborts git merge though git diff reads clean

title: Make external snapshots directly retrievable
description:
E12 read-enablement child, split out of w0h.2 after the debate (2026-07-07). DECISION A: externals must be DIRECTLY retrievable (a snapshot is a first-class lexical/vector hit on its own content), not only reachable via graph-expansion from a citing note.

## Scope
- Union external heads into the retrieval allow-list: live_head_versions (retrieval.py:87) today selects only notes JOIN versions; add externals.head_snapshot_id so lexical_search (retrieval.py:94) and vector_search (retrieval.py:110) admit current snapshots as direct candidates. Stale (non-head) snapshots stay excluded from the direct legs (trust_rank still tiers current-vs-stale for graph-reached ones).
- Polymorphic embed-body resolution: embedding.embed -> _version_body (embedding.py:139-145) does SELECT body FROM versions and raises KeyError for a snapshot_id. Teach it to resolve versions|snapshots (mirror cited_answer._resolve_target) so an enqueued embed job for a snapshot succeeds.
- Synchronous FTS-on-ingest: FTS is the synchronous model-free leg (docs/retrieval.md 'FTS5 is the synchronous index'), driven note-side via Repository.save -> CacheBackend.index (repository.py:224). The externals ingest (w0h.2) must drive the FTS leg for a snapshot synchronously itself; LexicalCacheBackend.replace_passages (lexical.py) is already target_version-generic and reusable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A freshly ingested snapshot is a DIRECT keyword hit (FTS, synchronous) and a DIRECT vector hit (after the embed worker drains), without a citing note being retrieved.
- An embed job enqueued for a snapshot_id runs to completion (no KeyError).
- Stale snapshots are not admitted to the direct legs; trust_rank ordering (current>stale) still holds for graph-reached snapshots.
- nox -t fix + nox -s tests green.

metadata.land_summary: External snapshots directly retrievable: live_head_versions UNIONs each external's non-tombstone head_snapshot_id (stale/superseded + tombstone snapshots excluded, proven absent by tests); embedding._version_body resolves versions-then-snapshots (raises on neither); ingest_snapshot drives the synchronous FTS leg. Review fix (53caca8): moved FTS out of ingest_snapshot's write txn to AFTER commit (nested with-conn was prematurely committing, breaking atomicity + risking a committed ok snapshot with no embed job since _embed_gap_step is notes-only), mirroring Repository.save's cache-after-commit; embed enqueue kept atomic with the irreplaceable write. Gates: nox -t fix clean, nox -s tests 895 passed/6 skipped.
