title: Detect pasted URLs in a note, create explicit edge, trigger draw-down
description:
E12 web draw-down connector — the trigger that turns note capture into connector activity.

## Scope
- On note save, extract URLs from the body. For each, create a user-asserted edge (edges.source='user', high confidence) from the note version to the external_id (docs/externals.md 'Edges: explicit vs inferred' — explicit = user-asserted, never a gated suggestion).
- Trigger the draw-down: fetch (w0h.1) + ingest (w0h.2) the URL. Follow the explicit link ONE HOP, then stop — do NOT follow the fetched page's own outbound links (externals.md 'Draw-down rules'; recursion = web crawler).
- Normalize the URL to a stable external_id (canonical form) so the same link from two notes dedups to one external node with two edges.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A note pasting a URL yields a source='user' edge note->external and a fetched, ingested snapshot.
- The same URL in two notes = one external node, two edges (dedup on normalized external_id).
- Only one hop is followed; the fetched page's links are not crawled.
- nox -t fix + nox -s tests green.
notes:
CRITICISM (debate): (1) Sync-vs-async unspecified. Repository.save is a single atomic 'with conn:' txn; fetch+ingest inline puts network I/O inside the save txn (wrong). Must be a queued async job (jobs.py:32 notes 'refresh arrives with connectors'). The job type is UNNAMED and is SHARED with w0h.6 refresh (same fetch->ingest path) -- w0h.3 must introduce the async draw-down job type that w0h.6 rides, else they are built independently and will not share. (2) URL normalization 'canonical form' is hand-waved: the concrete rules (trailing slash, query-param order, utm stripping, fragment, case, scheme) ARE the dedup correctness the AC depends on, and are the same external_id join key w0h.6 refresh uses. Specify them.
DECISION-NEEDED (debate round 3, 2026-07-08): two round-1 criticisms logged but never resolved. (1) URL canonicalization 'canonical form' is still hand-waved. The concrete rules (trailing slash, query-param order, utm_* stripping, fragment, case, scheme) ARE the dedup correctness this AC asserts AND the external_id join key w0h.6 refresh reuses. Specify them or 'same URL in two notes = one node' is unverifiable. (2) The shared async draw-down JOB TYPE is only an ordering edge (w0h.6->w0h.3), not a named deliverable. Neither ticket's SCOPE names the job type, so two builders can still write two independent fetch->ingest paths. Name the job type in w0h.3 scope as the artifact w0h.6 reuses.
DECISION (debate round 3, 2026-07-08, user): (1) URL canonicalization = RFC-3986 syntax norm + tracking blocklist + query-sort: lowercase scheme+host, strip default ports (:80/:443), drop fragment, strip tracking params (utm_*, fbclid, gclid; blocklist a config knob), sort remaining query params, normalize trailing slash. This canonical form IS the external_id dedup key AND the w0h.6 refresh join key. (2) Shared async job type = REUSE the reserved 'refresh' enum value (jobs.type already IN embed/enrich/refresh) -- NO schema migration. w0h.3 introduces the fetch->ingest HANDLER for 'refresh'; the paste-triggered initial draw-down is just the first 'refresh', so it rides the SAME retry/backoff machinery (failed->pending->dead) as w0h.6 re-fetches. w0h.6 reuses the handler and adds only the staleness/scheduling policy. (3) Redirect wrinkle to resolve at build: w0h.1 follows 3xx to a cap and the FINAL URL is canonicalized into external_id, so a note edge created pre-fetch on the pasted-canonical may need aliasing/re-point to the final-canonical external_id.

INHERITED LESSON from lode-w0h.1's technical review (2026-07-08) — read before you design your test seam.

THE TRAP: w0h.1 made its HTTP client an injectable `Fetcher` Protocol so the gate never hits the network. Good.
But the stub Fetcher BYPASSES `HttpxFetcher` entirely, so the default implementation's status-classification
branch — the precise taxonomy boundary the whole ticket existed to get right — had ZERO test coverage. Every
"taxonomy test" was exercising `fetch_and_extract`'s dispatch, never the code that decides transient-vs-permanent
from a status code. That is exactly how a real bug (408 Request Timeout classified as permanent, contra
RFC 9110 §15.5.9) survived the builder's 13 green tests all the way to review.

GENERAL FORM: an injectable seam that makes tests offline also makes the DEFAULT implementation untested unless
you deliberately reach past the seam. Watch for this shape in your own work.

WHAT TO DO: cover the default implementation offline too (w0h.1 used a fake `httpx.Client` injected into
`HttpxFetcher` — no new production seam added, just a test-only reach-past). If you add an injectable seam, add
a test that exercises the real implementation behind it.

VERIFY OFFLINE-NESS WITH A NEGATIVE CONTROL. "N tests passed" proves nothing about network isolation. w0h.1's
reviewer ran the suite under a pytest plugin that hard-fails on any DNS lookup or non-loopback connect(), then
NEGATIVE-CONTROLLED it (a deliberate `GET http://example.com/` must trip the guard). Do the same.

ALSO INHERITED, factual, from the same review:
- Transient HTTP set is {408, 429} + 5xx + network/timeout. NOT "any non-429 4xx is permanent" — that was the
  builder's original (wrong) rule. 425 Too Early is deliberately EXCLUDED as unreachable (httpx sends no TLS
  early data); do not add it speculatively.
- `httpx.InvalidURL` is NOT an `httpx.HTTPError` subclass. If you catch `HTTPError` expecting to cover httpx's
  typed exceptions, InvalidURL escapes unclassified and crashes your job handler instead of reaching the retry
  machinery. Probe the hierarchy; do not trust the docstring.
- A 429's `Retry-After` header is deliberately DISCARDED by w0h.1 — plumbing a delay out to the worker is the
  QUEUE's concern, i.e. YOURS (w0h.2/w0h.3), not the fetch unit's. If you want backoff to honor Retry-After you
  must plumb it yourself.
- `fetch_max_redirects` (HTTP redirect cap, default 5) is DISTINCT from `drawdown_hop_limit` (graph draw-down
  hops). Do not conflate them.

metadata.land_summary: URL detect + canonicalize (pinned RFC-3986 rules: lowercase scheme/host, strip default port, drop fragment, blocklist utm_*/fbclid/gclid, sort query, normalize trailing slash) -> source='user' edge + reused 'refresh' job type (no migration); refresh_external is the shared fetch->ingest handler w0h.6 rides; redirect wrinkle re-points pre-fetch edges to final-canonical id. Technical review found no bugs, no over-design; 918 passed/6 skipped.

title: Ingest a fetched page as a mirrored snapshot
description:
E12 web draw-down connector — the write path that turns a fetched page (w0h.1 output) into a mirrored content node on the already-built externals/snapshots substrate.

- Write externals + snapshots rows: dedup on external_id; create a NEW snapshot only when snapshot_id (= hashing.py H(external_id ‖ body)) differs from the current head — an identical refetch is free (docs/externals.md 'Snapshot churn'). Update externals.head_snapshot_id.
- body = clean_text; raw_payload = raw_html. On a fetch failure, write a tombstone snapshot (status) rather than garbage.
- Enqueue the EMBED job on the async queue so the snapshot becomes retrievable — re-embed on ANY change (cheap, local). Do NOT gate embedding on materiality (that gate is enrich-only, w0h.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- A fetched page becomes one externals row + one snapshots row; identical refetch adds no row; changed body adds a new snapshot and moves head_snapshot_id.
- Fetch failure writes a tombstone snapshot, not scaffolding.
- Embed job enqueued on save; the snapshot is keyword- and vector-retrievable after the worker drains.
- nox -t fix + nox -s tests green.

RFC 9110 §15.5.9) survived the builder's 13 green tests all the way to review.

GENERAL FORM: an injectable seam that makes tests offline also makes the DEFAULT implementation untested unless
you deliberately reach past the seam. Watch for this shape in your own work.

WHAT TO DO: cover the default implementation offline too (w0h.1 used a fake `httpx.Client` injected into
`HttpxFetcher` — no new production seam added, just a test-only reach-past). If you add an injectable seam, add
a test that exercises the real implementation behind it.

VERIFY OFFLINE-NESS WITH A NEGATIVE CONTROL. "N tests passed" proves nothing about network isolation. w0h.1's
reviewer ran the suite under a pytest plugin that hard-fails on any DNS lookup or non-loopback connect(), then
NEGATIVE-CONTROLLED it (a deliberate `GET http://example.com/` must trip the guard). Do the same.

ALSO INHERITED, factual, from the same review:
- Transient HTTP set is {408, 429} + 5xx + network/timeout. NOT "any non-429 4xx is permanent" — that was the
  builder's original (wrong) rule. 425 Too Early is deliberately EXCLUDED as unreachable (httpx sends no TLS
  early data); do not add it speculatively.
- `httpx.InvalidURL` is NOT an `httpx.HTTPError` subclass. If you catch `HTTPError` expecting to cover httpx's
  typed exceptions, InvalidURL escapes unclassified and crashes your job handler instead of reaching the retry
  machinery. Probe the hierarchy; do not trust the docstring.
- A 429's `Retry-After` header is deliberately DISCARDED by w0h.1 — plumbing a delay out to the worker is the
  QUEUE's concern, i.e. YOURS (w0h.2/w0h.3), not the fetch unit's. If you want backoff to honor Retry-After you
  must plumb it yourself.
- `fetch_max_redirects` (HTTP redirect cap, default 5) is DISTINCT from `drawdown_hop_limit` (graph draw-down
  hops). Do not conflate them.
ESCALATION (code-reviewer, Opus, 2026-07-08): tombstone snapshots enqueue an `embed` job exactly like `ok` snapshots. Branch is GREEN (880 passed) and technically clean; this is the ONE decision that must be made before it lands, because the answer determines whether w0h.2 needs a change or is fine as-is.

DECISION NEEDED: should a `status='tombstone'` snapshot (placeholder body `"[tombstone: <reason>]"`) be embedded — i.e. become a retrievable/citable passage once w0h.8 wires snapshot retrieval — or be silent like an owned-note delete tombstone?

Today this is INERT (embedding._version_body reads only `versions`; a snapshot_id raises KeyError until w0h.8's polymorphic resolution lands). The harm, if any, only bites once w0h.8 makes snapshot embeds resolve.

The docs do not conclusively settle it; both readings have support:
- SKIP (do not embed tombstones): the module frames itself as "the mirrored analogue of Repository.save", and the owned-note tombstone path (Repository.delete) does NOT enqueue embed and is filtered from retrieval by live_head_versions' `op != 'delete'` guard. The faithfulness bet (retrieval.md / design.md §2: "a hallucination wearing the uniform of a verified fact" is the worst outcome) argues against injecting a synthetic placeholder vector that can pass the verbatim-span faithfulness check (the body IS the quoted span) and surface as a citation — there is no absolute score floor in vector_search, so top-k always returns k. Fail-closed direction.
- EMBED (keep as-is): externals.md literally says "Re-embed on any change"; and a plausible product behavior is citing a dead/blocked source honestly ("this source was 403 as of fetched_at"), consistent with w0h.4's "as of fetched_at" citation honesty. On this reading the tombstone SHOULD be retrievable.

The tie-break is a product choice — should dead/blocked sources be citable as "unavailable", or silent like deleted notes? — with cross-ticket ramifications: whichever way it goes, w0h.8 must special-case tombstones (exclude from the retrieval live-head union if EMBED; exclude from the embed-gap reconciliation query if SKIP, else a tombstoned external re-enqueues embed forever). It should be decided coherently WITH w0h.8, not guessed by a reviewer editing w0h.2 in isolation.

REVIEWER RECOMMENDATION: SKIP embed on tombstones (with a test), on faithfulness + owned-note-precedent grounds — it is the fail-closed default and does not build a speculative dead-link-citation feature nobody asked for. If accepted, the fix is a ~1-line conditional in ingest_snapshot (skip enqueue when status == "tombstone") + a test asserting a tombstone enqueues no embed job; it belongs in THIS ticket (w0h.2 owns the enqueue).

REST OF REVIEW IS CLEAN (no other blocker): (2) content-addressing correct — snapshot_id=H(framed:external_id,body) folds in external_id+body ONLY, never URL-beyond-id/fetch-timestamp/HTTP-status; matches the storage.md §8 pin exactly; identical refetch is a no-op, revert re-heads onto the prior row (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). Parent is deliberately NOT folded (unlike versions), doc-backed and justified in the docstring — not a quiet divergence. (3) embed-only-never-enrich confirmed AND doc-backed (externals.md + epic decision C: enrich gate is post-embed, w0h.5). (4) tombstone_body honors link-rot immunity (snapshot row exists so the note edge resolves); NOTE (out of w0h.2 scope): no code path anywhere purges a `snapshots` row — hard delete cannot currently reach mirrored content; snapshots.body is as durable as versions.body but the "Hard delete" design covers only versions. Possible follow-up, not a w0h.2 defect. (5) scope clean — externals.py imports only jobs/config/hashing/webfetch; nothing in retrieval/embedding/lexical/vectorstore imports externals; no retrieval path touched. Atomic `with conn:` txn + DEFERRABLE FK ordering verified.
DECISION (human, 2026-07-08): SKIP embed on tombstone snapshots. A failed fetch must NOT produce a retrievable/citable vector. Rationale: vector_search has no score floor (top-k always returns k), and a tombstone's body IS its own quoted span, so an embedded placeholder would pass the verbatim-span faithfulness check and could surface as a citation -- 'a hallucination wearing the uniform of a verified fact' (design.md §2). Matches the owned-note delete path (no embed, filtered from retrieval by op != 'delete'). Fail closed.

Implementation (in this ticket, w0h.2 owns the enqueue): in ingest_snapshot, skip the embed enqueue when status == 'tombstone'; add a test asserting a tombstone enqueues NO embed job (and that an ok snapshot still does). Items 2-5 of the technical review were already clean; only item 1 changes.

Follow-on constraint for w0h.8 (record so it isn't lost): the embed-gap reconciliation query must EXCLUDE tombstone snapshots, else a tombstoned external re-enqueues embed forever. File that against w0h.8 when it's picked up.
RESOLVED (escalation-resolution pickup, 2026-07-08): applied the human's SKIP-embed-on-tombstone decision. ingest_snapshot now gates the embed enqueue on status != 'tombstone'. Updated module + function docstrings and docs/externals.md's write-path note; swapped the stale test asserting tombstone-enqueues-embed for one asserting no job, plus an explicit regression test (test_tombstone_ingest_enqueues_no_embed_job). Gates green: nox -t fix clean, nox -s tests 881 passed / 6 skipped (baseline 880+1 new test), validate-mermaid.sh clean (docs/externals.md touched). Force-pushed land/lode-w0h.2 @ db64543 (was 7dc675f). Back to ready-for-code-review for a fresh technical review of the new code (not straight to ready-for-land, since this is new code, not a rebase replay).

title: Revert Claude Code OAuth fallback in auth.build_client (keep graceful AuthError handling)
description:
Remove the Claude Code OAuth credential fallback added by lode-tcq. Decision (bildzeitung, 2026-07-07): it was a secondary, never-fully-verified add (a subscription OAuth token was never proven to complete a messages.parse structured-output call — only a 429), and carrying an unverified auth path is unwise. Rather than verify it (lode-eyp, now closed), remove it.

## Scope
Revert ONLY the OAuth fallback. lode reverts to the SDK credential chain alone (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN env, ant auth login profile, WIF).
- src/lode/auth.py: drop _oauth_client(), _OAUTH_BETA_HEADER, CLAUDE_CODE_CREDENTIALS, the OAuth fallback branch in build_client(), and remove the Claude Code login language from MISSING_CREDENTIALS_MESSAGE + the module docstring.
- tests/test_auth.py: remove the ~13 OAuth-path assertions; keep/adjust the SDK-chain + AuthError coverage.
- docs/stack.md:108-109: remove the 'fall back to the Claude Code login' paragraph.

## KEEP (do NOT revert)
The graceful AuthError handling in cli.py ask (clean actionable message, no traceback, details to log) was also added by lode-tcq but is orthogonal and desirable — keep it. After removal it should fire whenever the SDK chain resolves nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No OAuth/Claude-Code-login code, message text, or docs remain (grep for oauth/claudeAiOauth/CLAUDE_CODE_CREDENTIALS/'Claude Code login' is clean outside history).
- build_client() resolves via the SDK chain only, else raises AuthError with a message that no longer names the Claude Code login.
- lode ask still fails gracefully (no traceback) on missing credentials.
- nox -t fix + nox -s tests green.

title: coding.md & code-reviewer.md assume EnterWorktree moves git cwd into the entered worktree; needs git -C workaround
description: Both .claude/agents/coding.md (the new needs-rebase rebase-pickup cycle) and .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md assume that EnterWorktree (path form) moves a worktree-isolated agent's bash/git cwd into the entered worktree, then run git/nox commands (rev-parse, fetch/rebase, nox, push --force-with-lease) with cwd inside that tree. In practice, for an isolation: worktree agent the bash isolation guard refuses to run any command resolved into the path-entered worktree ('commands from a worktree-isolated agent must run inside its worktree'): the reviewer of lode-wfl had to keep cwd in its launch worktree and drive the builder worktree via 'git -C <path>'. A dispatched coding producer is launched the same way and would hit the same wall. Fix: update coding.md steps 2-5 and the parallel code-reviewer.md steps to use 'git -C <worktree>' / nox with an explicit dir instead of assuming cwd moved. Pre-existing (the claim already ships in the landed code-reviewer.md) and cross-cutting, so it spans BOTH docs to keep them from diverging. Sibling to lode-5g4.
design: Root cause: EnterWorktree(path) does not exempt subsequent bash/git commands from the worktree-isolation guard for an isolation:worktree agent -- the guard refuses any command resolved into the path-entered worktree ('commands from a worktree-isolated agent must run inside its worktree'), discovered empirically while code-reviewing lode-wfl. Fix: coding.md's rebase-pickup cycle and all of code-reviewer.md stop calling EnterWorktree(path) entirely and instead stay in the agent's own launch worktree, driving the target worktree ($WT = metadata.review_worktree) via path-scoped commands: git -C "$WT" for every git op, nox -f "$WT/noxfile.py" for gates (verified against nox/tasks.py: -f os.chdir()s into the noxfile's own dir before running sessions -- nox's own git -C equivalent), venv activated via absolute path in the SAME bash call as the nox invocation (shell state/PATH doesn't persist across separate bash calls per this harness), a one-time subshell cd for the cwd-relative python-init.sh bootstrap (no -C equivalent; a plain subshell cd inside one bash call isn't gated the way EnterWorktree's harness-tracked path-entry is), and validate-mermaid.sh called by absolute path (self-locating via dirname $0, needs no cd). code-reviewer.md's existing Edit/Write-guard-pinned workaround (apply /code-review fixes via bash sed/python -c single-match replacements) stays, just retargeted at $WT absolute paths instead of an assumed post-EnterWorktree cwd. docs/agents-workflow.md has the same wrong EnterWorktree(path) claim in prose + 2 mermaid diagrams but is out of this ticket's named scope -- filing a discovered-from follow-up rather than expanding scope silently.
notes: ESCALATION (build-time, before any commit): the fix this ticket requires is editing .claude/agents/coding.md and .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md to document that EnterWorktree(path) does NOT actually move a worktree-isolated agent's bash/git cwd (the isolation guard refuses commands resolved into the entered worktree), and that the workaround is driving the target worktree via 'git -C <path>' (and a subshell cd for nox, which has no -C flag) instead. Claude Code's auto-mode permission classifier repeatedly blocked these specific edits with escalating reasons: first a generic denial, then '[Self-Modification] Editing the agent's own .claude/agents/coding.md config ... not the requested ticket implementation and was not user-authorized', then finally an explicit '[Self-Modification] ... adds instructions for bypassing the worktree isolation guard ... also implicating Auto-Mode Bypass ... and Instruction Poisoning (writing guard-bypass content into an instruction file); run outside auto mode so the user can review the permission prompt directly.' One small edit to coding.md step 2/3/4-intro succeeded before the classifier hardened its block on subsequent near-identical edits; I reverted all working-tree changes (git checkout -- .claude/agents/coding.md) so the worktree is back to pristine trunk state with nothing committed. code-reviewer.md was never touched. DECISION NEEDED: a human must either (a) run this producer task outside auto mode so the edit permission prompts can be approved directly, (b) make the coding.md/code-reviewer.md edits by hand per the ticket's design, or (c) add an explicit permission allowance for editing .claude/agents/*.md so a producer can complete self-referential agent-doc tickets like this one under auto mode. Worktree kept at /home/dmklein/PROJECTS/lode/.claude/worktrees/agent-a338ad55520ef4f1d on branch worktree-agent-a338ad55520ef4f1d, nothing pushed (no commits exist to strand).

title: land/SKILL.md 2a drift precheck reads metadata.head_sha but code-reviewer writes land_head
description: land/SKILL.md's 2a drift precheck (the cheap re-validation before the semantic review) reads metadata.head_sha and metadata.summary (see 'rtk bd show <id> --json # read metadata.head_sha and metadata.summary' and the drift check that compares origin/land/<id>'s tip SHA to metadata.head_sha). But code-reviewer.md step 8, which is what actually swaps a ticket to ready-for-land, writes metadata.land_head and metadata.land_summary — not head_sha/summary. So on a real ready-for-land ticket, 2a's read of metadata.head_sha is likely always empty, meaning the drift check as literally written can't detect a real re-push after marking ready. Reconcile the two: either land/SKILL.md's 2a should read land_head/land_summary (matching what code-reviewer actually sets), or code-reviewer.md should write head_sha/summary (matching what land/SKILL.md actually reads) — pick one field-name convention and update the other side plus any callers. Found while implementing lode-wfl (producer-side needs-rebase pickup): the rebase-pickup cycle in coding.md now defensively refreshes both key pairs to stay correct regardless of which side wins, but that's a workaround, not a fix.
design: Root cause: land/SKILL.md 2a precheck was written expecting metadata keys head_sha/summary, but code-reviewer.md step 8 (the actual writer, added later) uses land_head/land_summary instead — the two were never reconciled. Fix: pick one field-name convention (recommend land_head/land_summary since code-reviewer.md is the sole writer today) and update land/SKILL.md's 2a to read it; grep the whole .claude/ tree for the other name and update every reader/writer to match.
acceptance_criteria: land/SKILL.md's 2a precheck and code-reviewer.md's ready-for-land write use the same bd metadata key names for the landing-context SHA + summary; the drift check in 2a actually fires on a real post-mark push.

title: Producer/-code must pick up needs-rebase kick-backs from /land
description: /land's conflict precheck (lode-bg3) kicks a stale-conflicting branch back by removing ready-for-land, adding a needs-rebase label, and keeping the same land/<id> branch + build worktree (ticket stays in_progress). But an in_progress ticket does NOT appear in 'bd ready', so nothing currently consumes needs-rebase — it would strand. Add producer-side handling: /code (or a sweep) scans for needs-rebase, re-enters the recorded build worktree, rebases land/<id> onto current trunk, re-runs the quality gates, force-pushes the branch, refreshes metadata.head_sha, then swaps needs-rebase back to ready-for-land. Acceptance: a branch kicked back with needs-rebase is picked up automatically, rebased+re-gated+re-pushed, and re-marked ready-for-land without manual intervention.

title: /land: cheap conflict precheck before land-review; kick back needs-rebase
description: When a ready-for-land branch conflicts with current trunk, /land currently discovers it late (Section 3, at merge time) after land-review already spent Opus tokens semantically verifying content that gets thrown back. Add a cheap merge-cleanliness precheck in Section 2 BEFORE dispatching land-review. On conflict: short-circuit — remove ready-for-land, add needs-rebase label, keep the same land/<id> branch + worktree, surface it. Producer rebases in its own worktree, re-gates, re-marks ready-for-land. A clean-but-stale branch does NOT need a rebase (git merge --no-ff handles non-linear history; Section 3 re-gate retests the combined result) — only textual conflicts trigger the kick-back.

title: Flaky test: test_notes_lists_the_full_id_date_and_summary races the async enrichment worker
description:
tests/test_cli.py::test_notes_lists_the_full_id_date_and_summary is non-deterministic and intermittently fails the nox -s tests landing gate (observed 2026-07-07 during /land of the lode-0ru release epic; reproduced 2 fail / 1 pass in three back-to-back runs).

ROOT CAUSE: the test does 'lode add "the first line of the note"' then 'lode notes' and asserts the raw first line appears in the notes-list summary column. But 'add' enqueues async enrichment; when the worker completes fast enough, it replaces the summary column with an LLM-generated summary (observed: 'The note contains only a single generic line with no meaningful content.'), so the raw substring 'the first line of the note' is no longer present and the assertion fails. When 'notes' is read before enrichment lands, the raw line shows and it passes — hence the flake. Captured log at failure: 'lode.enrich enrich_version ... summary=True' + 'worker job N (enrich ...) done'.

IMPACT: makes the full-suite landing gate non-deterministic — a red run here is NOT attributable to the branch under test (it flaked while landing docs-only + shell-script branches that touch no Python).

FIX DIRECTION: make the test deterministic wrt enrichment — e.g. disable/stub the async worker for this test (assert against pre-enrichment state), or assert on a column the enrichment does not overwrite, or wait for a known enrichment state before asserting. Pick whichever matches how the other notes-list tests isolate the worker.
acceptance_criteria: test_notes_lists_the_full_id_date_and_summary passes deterministically across repeated runs regardless of async enrichment timing; the full nox -s tests suite is stable (no intermittent failure on this test).

metadata.land_summary: Stub lode.enrich.enrich_version to a no-op in test_notes_lists_the_full_id_date_and_summary so the notes-list assertion no longer races the immediate-enrich fast path (test-only, matches sibling stub pattern).

title: docs/release.md: first-release ordering runbook + explicit no-PyPI non-goal
description:
Two additions to the existing docs/release.md (created in 0ru.1), surfaced by the 0ru debate:
1. First-release runbook line: GitHub Actions runs the workflow file AS IT EXISTS in the tagged commit, so .github/workflows/release.yml (0ru.3) MUST be merged to trunk BEFORE the first vX.Y.Z tag is cut by scripts/release.sh (0ru.2) — otherwise the tag push triggers nothing (no error). State this ordering in the release flow section.
2. Explicit non-goal: lode publishes a GitHub release with wheel+sdist attached ONLY — there are NO PyPI releases (confirmed by owner 2026-07-07). Record so a reader does not assume 'pip install lode' works.
Doc-only change; must be done in a worktree per CLAUDE.md.
design: Edit-only, no new files. Fold the ordering note into the existing 'Release flow (high level)' section and add a short 'Non-goals' or 'Scope' note for the PyPI point. Keep the prose style of the existing doc.
acceptance_criteria: docs/release.md states the release.yml-before-first-tag ordering constraint in its release-flow section, and carries an explicit 'no PyPI releases' non-goal. Mermaid/link checks (if any) stay green; no code change.
notes: ALSO fold in lode-3v5 (superseded into this ticket): docs/release.md currently says the kickoff gate is 'nox -t fix + nox -s tests', but scripts/release.sh (0ru.2) correctly runs ONLY 'nox -s tests' (nox -t fix mutates the tree and would violate the clean-tree guard at tag time). Reword the kickoff-gate description in docs/release.md to drop 'nox -t fix' (say 'nox -s tests' / 'verify green', check-only). This makes docs/release.md the single file all three edits (ordering runbook + no-PyPI non-goal + gate wording) land through, avoiding a parallel-branch conflict.

title: .github/workflows/release.yml: tag-triggered clean-room build + GitHub release
description: Net-new CI (no .github/ exists yet). Trigger: push tags 'v*'. Steps: checkout with fetch-depth:0 (setuptools-scm needs full history/tags), setup Python 3.14, pip install build, python -m build, then gh release create ${GITHUB_REF_NAME} dist/* --title "lode ${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --generate-notes. Uses GITHUB_TOKEN. This owns the reproducible artifacts so releases never depend on a laptop.
design: DECISION (2026-07-07): (a) Workflow MUST set 'permissions: contents: write' (default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only -> gh release create 403). (b) Verification = throwaway pre-release tag, NOT a real release. Builder: git tag v0.0.0-rc1 && git push origin v0.0.0-rc1; confirm the workflow runs green and the GitHub release has wheel+sdist attached and the wheel version derives from the tag; then 'gh release delete v0.0.0-rc1 --cleanup-tag' to remove both release and tag. (c) First real v0.1.0 requires this workflow already merged to trunk BEFORE the tag is cut (Actions runs the workflow as it exists in the tagged commit) — see docs/release.md runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Pushing a throwaway v0.0.0-rc1 tag runs the workflow green and creates a GitHub release with wheel+sdist attached whose wheel Version derives from the tag; the rc tag+release are then deleted (gh release delete --cleanup-tag). Workflow declares permissions: contents: write. No real vX.Y.Z release is cut to satisfy this ticket.
notes:
CRITICISM (debate 2026-07-07):
1. [Certain] Missing 'permissions: contents: write'. gh release create uses GITHUB_TOKEN, whose default is READ-ONLY on modern-default repos -> 403, first release silently fails. Add permissions: contents: write at job/workflow level.
2. [Certain] Acceptance is only verifiable by an irreversible side effect: pushing a real vX.Y.Z tag cuts a real public release and burns a version name. No dry-run path stated. Decide verification story: throwaway v0.0.0-rc1 tag (then delete), act, or 'human verifies on first real release'. Otherwise unclosable without side effects.
3. [Certain] First-release ordering trap not in dep graph: Actions runs the workflow file AS IT EXISTS in the tagged commit. If release.sh (0ru.2) tags a trunk HEAD predating this ticket landing, the workflow does NOT trigger (no error). First v0.1.0 requires this merged to trunk BEFORE the tag is cut. Capture in docs/release.md runbook.
Minor [Likely]: --generate-notes on first release (no prior tag) diffs all history, fine; tag-push already checks out the tag so fetch-depth:0 suffices for setuptools-scm, no fetch-tags needed.
SECOND PASS (2026-07-07): re-verified against updated acceptance (debate 2026-07-07). permissions: contents: write already present (lines 12-13) from first build. Trigger/checkout/python/build/gh-release steps match updated spec exactly. No in-file wording referenced the verification procedure, so nothing needed alignment. File is BYTE-IDENTICAL to first build (25bbe26) -- no functional change made. Did NOT execute the live throwaway-tag verification (git tag v0.0.0-rc1 && push && confirm workflow run && gh release delete --cleanup-tag) in this producer session -- that pushes a real tag to origin and triggers a real Actions run/GitHub release with side effects beyond a normal build-and-gate cycle, which this task's instructions scoped to file-correctness + gates, not live execution. Flagging for reviewer/lander/human: someone should run that verification before or as part of landing to close acceptance criterion 1 for real. Gates green: nox -t fix (no changes), nox -s tests (803 passed, 7 skipped).
ESCALATION (/land semantic review 2026-07-07): release.yml is correct by inspection and matches the ticket spec byte-for-byte (v* trigger, permissions: contents: write, checkout fetch-depth:0, Python 3.14, python -m build, gh release create --generate-notes). BUT acceptance criterion 1 requires a LIVE runtime verification — push throwaway v0.0.0-rc1, confirm the workflow runs green with wheel+sdist attached whose version derives from the tag, then gh release delete v0.0.0-rc1 --cleanup-tag — which the producer explicitly did NOT perform and flagged for lander/human. The lander will not run it: it is a live GitHub Actions run + public release create/delete (outside the nox re-gate remit), AND it can only run once the workflow is on trunk (Actions runs the workflow from the tagged commit), so it is structurally a POST-land verification, not a pre-land gate.

DECISION NEEDED: (A) Accept landing on inspection now, then run the throwaway v0.0.0-rc1 verification against trunk as an immediate post-land step BEFORE cutting any real vX.Y.Z tag (recommended — the file is correct and the verification is inherently post-land); or (B) hold until a human runs the verification some other way. Branch origin/land/lode-0ru.3 @ 25bbe26 is KEPT (not deleted). Sibling branches 0ru.5 (docs) + 0ru.2 (script) landed this pass; no tag was cut, so first-release ordering is unaffected.
close_reason: Landed on trunk via /land (merge 0128d01785f875ebce3ec506a35da83505022d0b). Escalation resolved: human ran throwaway v0.0.0-rc1 verification 2026-07-07 — workflow green, release had lode-0.0.0rc1 wheel+sdist, version derived from tag; rc release+tag cleaned up. Acceptance criterion 1 satisfied for real.

Technical review (code-review+simplify) found no bugs/simplifications; file byte-identical to build. Gates green (nox -t fix clean, 803 passed), actionlint exit 0, YAML parses. NOTE: live throwaway-tag verification (v0.0.0-rc1 push -> confirm green Actions run + release with wheel+sdist -> gh release delete --cleanup-tag) NOT executed here (side-effecting) -- lander/human must run it to close acceptance criterion 1.

title: scripts/release.sh: gate + annotated tag + push (kickoff)
description: Local kickoff script. scripts/release.sh <version>: guard on trunk + clean tree + tag not already existing + 'nox -s tests' green; git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m 'lode vX.Y.Z' on HEAD; git push origin vX.Y.Z. Build+publish is owned by the CI workflow (triggered by the tag push), so the script stops after pushing the tag. Typer is the repo CLI convention but a release-kickoff shell script is fine here (matches existing scripts/*.sh); keep it POSIX-ish and match scripts/python-init.sh style.
acceptance_criteria: running scripts/release.sh 0.1.0 on a clean trunk creates+pushes an annotated v0.1.0 tag and refuses (nonzero exit) on a dirty tree, wrong branch, existing tag, or failing gates.
notes:
CRITICISM (debate 2026-07-07):
1. [Certain] Gate ambiguity that mutates the tree: this ticket says gate = 'nox -s tests'; docs/release.md step 1 says 'nox -t fix + nox -s tests'. nox -t fix REWRITES files (ruff format/fix), so running it after the clean-tree guard leaves the tree dirty at tag time or tags un-committed reformatting. Release gate must be CHECK-ONLY (lint check, not fix). Reconcile ticket vs doc before building.
2. [Likely] No 'HEAD up-to-date with origin' guard. Guards are clean-tree + on-trunk + tag-absent + gates. If local trunk is ahead of origin/trunk you tag an unpushed commit; git push origin vX.Y.Z pushes a dangling tag or drags unreviewed commits. Add git fetch + ancestry/@{u} check.
3. [Minor] No SemVer well-formedness / monotonicity check on the arg. Only guards 'tag doesn't already exist' — nothing stops release.sh 0.0.9 after v0.1.0, or a typo'd double-v. Validate arg shape and that it exceeds the latest tag.
Second build (2026-07-07): addressed debate criticism 1-3 — gate stays check-only (nox -s tests, reconciled docs/release.md which wrongly said nox -t fix); added git fetch + HEAD==origin/trunk freshness guard; added SemVer monotonicity guard (version_gt scan of existing v* tags). Verified all guard paths end-to-end against a scratch git remote/work pair. land/lode-0ru.2 force-pushed to c2046a7 (was dbf74f9).
Made land/lode-0ru.2 script-only per coordinator direction: reverted docs/release.md to trunk state (owned exclusively by sibling lode-0ru.5, ready-for-land, to avoid a land-time conflict on the gate wording). scripts/release.sh guards (origin-freshness, semver monotonicity, check-only gate) unchanged. Re-gated (nox -t fix clean, nox -s tests 803 passed/7 skipped). land/lode-0ru.2 force-pushed to 1adc51f (was c2046a7). git diff trunk --name-only now shows only scripts/release.sh.

metadata.land_summary: scripts/release.sh (script-only; docs/release.md owned by sibling 0ru.5): release kickoff guarding on-trunk + clean tree + local HEAD==origin/trunk (git fetch freshness) + well-formed SemVer strictly > latest tag (numeric version_gt) + tag absent local & origin, then check-only nox -s tests, annotated vX.Y.Z tag + push. Technical review clean (no fixes). Gates green (803 passed/7 skipped). All 6 guard paths verified nonzero end-to-end; first-release + monotonic bumps succeed; version_gt numeric (0.1.10>0.1.9).

title: Wire setuptools-scm: dynamic version + metadata-resolved __version__ + docs/release.md
description:
Make the version tag-driven. Changes:
1. pyproject.toml: build-system.requires += 'setuptools-scm>=8'; [project] replace version="0.0.0" with dynamic=["version"]; add [tool.setuptools_scm] version_file="src/lode/_version.py".
2. src/lode/__init__.py: resolve __version__ via importlib.metadata.version("lode") with try/except PackageNotFoundError -> "0.0.0+unknown".
3. .gitignore: add src/lode/_version.py (build-generated, never committed).
4. Add docs/release.md (version source, tag format vX.Y.Z, SemVer policy, the release flow) and a one-line pointer in docs/stack.md.
Foundation for the script/CI/skill — they all depend on scm producing the version.
acceptance_criteria: python -m build produces a wheel whose metadata Version comes from git-describe; in the editable dev install 'lode version' prints a real scm version (not 0.0.0); tests/test_cli.py still green (unchanged); docs/release.md exists and stack.md links it; nox -t fix + nox -s tests pass.

metadata.land_summary: Wire setuptools-scm: dynamic version + metadata-resolved __version__ (PackageNotFoundError fallback), _version.py gitignored, docs/release.md + stack.md pointer. Gates green (803 passed), lode version reports real scm version.

title: [epic] Release process: tag-driven versioning + automated GitHub releases
description:
Stand up a repeatable release process. Today the version is a hardcoded literal (__version__="0.0.0" in src/lode/__init__.py, version="0.0.0" in pyproject.toml), there are no git tags, no GitHub releases, and no CI at all. Goal: a single kickoff cuts a SemVer release — tags a commit, builds wheel+sdist, makes 'lode version' report the real version, and publishes a GitHub release with artifacts attached.

Decided (2026-07-07):
- Version source of truth = setuptools-scm. The git tag IS the version; no literal to hand-edit. Between releases 'lode version' reports a real dev version (e.g. 0.1.dev4+g<sha>) because requirements.txt is '-e .[dev]' so every dev has an editable install.
- Automation = local release script + tag-triggered GitHub Actions workflow (clean-room build+publish) + a /release Claude skill that computes the next semver bump and drives the flow.
- Tag format vX.Y.Z (annotated), SemVer, first release v0.1.0 (pre-1.0 while core loop stabilizes).
design: setuptools-scm wiring: build-system.requires += setuptools-scm>=8; [project] version='0.0.0' -> dynamic=['version']; add [tool.setuptools_scm] version_file='src/lode/_version.py'; src/lode/_version.py gitignored. __init__.py resolves __version__ via importlib.metadata.version('lode') with PackageNotFoundError -> '0.0.0+unknown' fallback. 'lode version' command and tests/test_cli.py:63 (asserts __version__ in stdout) need NO change. CI owns the reproducible build so scripts/release.sh = gate+tag+push; workflow does python -m build + gh release create on tag push. Design doc: docs/release.md + a line in docs/stack.md.
acceptance_criteria: A single documented kickoff produces: an annotated vX.Y.Z tag on the release commit; a GitHub release with wheel+sdist attached; 'lode version' on a clean install of that artifact prints X.Y.Z (not 0.0.0); nox gates stay green; docs/release.md describes the process.
notes:
CRITICISM (debate 2026-07-07), epic-level:
1. [Certain] First-release ordering constraint spans 0ru.2 and 0ru.3 but isn't captured: Actions runs the workflow as it exists in the TAGGED commit, so 0ru.3 (release.yml) must land on trunk BEFORE the first tag is cut by 0ru.2's script, or the workflow never triggers. Add this to the docs/release.md first-release runbook.
2. [Likely] Unstated non-goal: epic publishes a GitHub release only, never PyPI. Almost certainly intentional pre-1.0, but nothing records it — a later reader may assume 'pip install lode' works. Add one line to docs/release.md.
Per-child detail in the notes on 0ru.2 / 0ru.3 / 0ru.4.
close_reason: Epic complete: all 5 children (0ru.1–.5) landed on trunk; /epic-audit clean bill 2026-07-07 (release path verified live via v0.0.0-rc1). Tag-driven versioning + automated GitHub releases stood up.

title: ruff format auto-adopts PEP 758 unparenthesized-except on lock.py once floor is >=3.14
description:
Bumping pyproject.toml requires-python to >=3.14 (lode-93o) makes ruff infer target-version=py314 (no explicit [tool.ruff] target-version override exists). Its formatter then auto-rewrites src/lode/lock.py's bare 'except (ValueError, OSError):' into the unparenthesized PEP 758 form 'except ValueError, OSError:' on any repo-wide 'ruff format .' / 'nox -t fix' run. This is exactly the collateral edit that got the original lode-8am branch bounced by land-review, and lode-93o's rebuild deliberately reverted it after each gate run rather than fix it durably.

grep -rn 'except (' src/ shows only src/lode/lock.py and src/lode/auth.py have parenthesized multi-exception except clauses; auth.py's (which binds 'as err') was NOT auto-rewritten by ruff, only lock.py's bare form was.

Need a human/team decision: (a) add a durable '# fmt: skip' pragma to lock.py's except line so it survives every future gate run without manual reverting, or (b) adopt PEP 758 unparenthesized-except deliberately tree-wide (a project style decision, not a bugfix), or (c) pin an explicit older '[tool.ruff] target-version' so ruff's formatter target lags behind requires-python. Whatever is chosen should also be recorded in docs/ per repo convention.
design: Decide and implement one of: (a) '# fmt: skip' pragma on lock.py's except line, (b) tree-wide PEP 758 adoption as a deliberate style decision, or (c) pin an explicit older [tool.ruff] target-version. Record the decision in docs/ (configuration.md or a style note) per repo convention.
acceptance_criteria: A subsequent repo-wide 'ruff format .' / 'nox -t fix' run leaves src/lode/lock.py's exception-handling syntax unchanged (no silent PEP 758 flip), and the chosen approach (fmt:skip pragma, explicit target-version pin, or deliberate tree-wide PEP 758 adoption) is recorded in docs/.
notes: DECIDED (human, 2026-07-06): approach (b) — adopt PEP 758 unparenthesized-except tree-wide as a deliberate 3.14-only style decision. NOT fmt:skip, NOT a target-version pin. Convert parenthesized multi-exception except clauses to unparenthesized form across src/ (lock.py AND auth.py's 'except (...) as err' — verify ruff handles the 'as' bind), let ruff own the formatting, and RECORD the decision in docs/ (configuration.md or a style note) per repo convention. Acceptance: a repo-wide 'nox -t fix' leaves the tree stable (no further flips) and the decision is documented. SEQUENCING: blocked on lode-93o landing first (raises floor to >=3.14) so the flip is reproducible/verifiable.

metadata.land_summary: Adopt PEP 758 unparenthesized-except tree-wide (3.14-only style): ruff owns the flip on lock.py; auth.py's 'except (...) as err:' stays parenthesized (as-bind is a SyntaxError unparenthesized on 3.14). Decision recorded in docs/configuration.md. Review: nox -t fix idempotent (104 files unchanged), 803 tests pass; no refinements needed.

title: related.py fromisoformat(Z) fix + Python floor >=3.14 (rebuild after land bounce)
description:
Rebuild of lode-8am, bounced by /land semantic review for silent scope creep.

The bounced branch (land/lode-8am @ 782653d) correctly delivered the intended fix but ALSO smuggled in an unrelated edit to src/lode/lock.py.

REBUILD BRIEF (from land-review):
Land ONLY these three changes (all correct on the bounced branch, per the recorded human decision to raise the floor to >=3.14 matching .python-version 3.14.5):
  1. src/lode/tui/related.py: humanize_age parses via datetime.strptime(created, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ').replace(tzinfo=UTC), matching dates.py (the ticket's actual fix).
  2. pyproject.toml: requires-python = '>=3.14'.
  3. docs/onboarding.md: Python floor reconciled to >=3.14.

DO NOT touch src/lode/lock.py. The bounced branch changed its exception handler from 'except (ValueError, OSError):' to 'except ValueError, OSError:' (PEP 758 unparenthesized-except, new in 3.14). It is functionally equivalent (verified on 3.14.5: catches both, OSError not rebound) so it is NOT a bug, but it is out of scope, unmentioned in the ticket/summary, and introduces a bleeding-edge 3.14-only syntax form in one random spot for zero benefit. Leave lock.py as 'except (ValueError, OSError):'.

If adopting PEP 758 unparenthesized-except tree-wide is actually desired, that is a SEPARATE discovered-from task, not part of this fix.

metadata.land_summary: related.py humanize_age fromisoformat(Z)->strptime matching dates.py; Python floor >=3.14 (pyproject + docs/onboarding.md). Review: corrected stale humanize_age docstring. lock.py untouched (zero diff); ruff PEP 758 auto-flip reverted per lode-mkm.

title: related.py fromisoformat(Z) breaks under declared py3.10 floor
description: src/lode/tui/related.py:201 calls datetime.fromisoformat(created) on a 'Z'-suffixed UTC timestamp. datetime.fromisoformat only accepts the trailing 'Z' on Python 3.11+, but pyproject.toml declares requires-python = '>=3.10', so this line is latently broken on the declared floor. Flagged during code review of lode-1gr.8 (whose new tui/dates.py correctly uses strptime instead). Fix: either parse via strptime like dates.py, or raise the python floor to >=3.11 and reconcile the declaration. Reconcile which is intended.
notes: ESCALATION: Ticket asks to 'reconcile which is intended' between patching related.py's fromisoformat(Z) call (strptime, preserving the declared >=3.10 floor) vs raising requires-python to >=3.11. Found concrete evidence this is genuinely ambiguous per the ticket's own escalation criterion: 'from datetime import UTC' (datetime.UTC is a Python 3.11-only addition, absent in 3.10) is ALREADY used in src/lode/worker.py:86 and src/lode/enrich.py:53 -- two already-landed, unrelated modules -- not just related.py. So the package already silently requires 3.11+ in practice, independent of this ticket. Patching only related.py's fromisoformat call to strptime (the ticket's suggested low-risk default) would NOT actually restore genuine 3.10 compatibility for the package as a whole, since worker.py/enrich.py still break under 3.10. Conversely, raising requires-python to >=3.11 is a project-wide packaging decision (classifiers, docs/stack.md, any CI matrix) beyond this ticket's stated scope, and I should not make that call unilaterally. Need a human decision: (a) raise the floor to >=3.11 and reconcile docs/classifiers/CI (in which case related.py's fromisoformat call is arguably fine as-is, though strptime is still slightly more explicit/consistent with dates.py), or (b) actually commit to 3.10 support, in which case this ticket's fix must also cover worker.py and enrich.py's UTC imports (broader than the ticket describes) -- probably worth its own ticket(s). No code changes made; worktree left clean.

metadata.land_summary: Raise Python floor to >=3.14 (per human decision, matching .python-version 3.14.5); related.py humanize_age fromisoformat(Z)->strptime matching dates.py; review reconciled docs/onboarding.md floor to >=3.14.

title: TUI Browse: adaptive human-readable dates instead of full ISO-8601
description: specs/03-tui-features.md item 5. Browse's Date column (and the version-history Date column) shows a full ISO-8601 timestamp. Replace with an adaptive absolute format: time-of-day for today (14:30), weekday+time this week (Mon 09:12), month+day this year (Jul 3), ISO date for older/last-year (2025-11-20). notes.created / versions.created are ISO-8601 strings; add a small formatter (its own function, unit-testable) and apply it in lode.tui.browse where NoteRow.created / VersionRow.created are built (or at render in screens/browse.py). Note _reload_rows sizes the Date column off len(row.created); a shorter date frees width for Summary — recompute accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: Browse and version-history show short adaptive dates (today=time, this week=weekday+time, this year=mon+day, older=ISO date); the Summary column gains the freed width; a formatter unit test covers each bucket.

metadata.land_summary: TUI Browse + version-history Date column now renders lode.tui.dates.format_adaptive_date (today=time, this week=weekday+time, this year=mon+day, older=ISO) instead of full ISO-8601; _reload_rows recomputes date_width off the shorter adaptive cells so Summary gains the freed width. New dates.py formatter + bucket/boundary unit tests and two TUI render-site tests.

title: Browse screen: wrap Summary column instead of horizontal-scrolling the table
description: The TUI browse DataTable (src/lode/tui/screens/browse.py) grows to the widest cell, so a long Summary forces inconvenient horizontal scrolling. Bound the Summary column to the remaining terminal width and add rows with height=None so the summary wraps and the row grows vertically. Recompute on resize. Date/Version keep their natural widths (Date is a full ISO-8601 string ~32 chars, left as-is).

metadata.land_summary: Wrap the browse Summary column instead of horizontal-scrolling the table (lode-5qp): cap Summary to the room left after natural-width Date/Version columns and add rows height=None (auto height) so a long summary wraps down over multiple lines; recompute on resize. Date keeps its full ISO-8601 timestamp. Regression test asserts wrap (row height>1), no h-scroll (virtual_width<=widget_width), untruncated cell. Gates green: ruff clean, 25 browse + 125 tui/app tests pass.

title: Split test suite into fast unit tests vs slow pre-merge/landing tests
description:
The full nox -s tests suite (~731 tests) is slow enough that running it on every code-time change is friction. Investigate splitting tests into two tiers: (1) TRUE UNIT TESTS — fast, isolated, high signal, run constantly during development; and (2) LONGER-RUNNING TESTS — integration/model-download/TUI-pilot/end-to-end tests that are more appropriate to gate at pre-merge / landing time. Goal: a fast inner-loop feedback set at code time, with the heavier set still enforced before a branch lands.

Investigate: which tests actually dominate wall-clock (profile with pytest --durations), a mechanism to tag/mark the split (pytest markers, nox session split, or directory convention), and how it wires into the existing gates — the fast set on the coding producer's inner loop, the full set still required at land. Confirm the /land re-gate keeps running the FULL suite so nothing slow is skipped before trunk.
acceptance_criteria: Tests are partitioned into a fast unit tier and a slow/pre-merge tier via an explicit, documented mechanism (marker/session/dir). A fast command exists for code-time inner loop; the full suite still runs as the landing gate. Slowest tests are identified (pytest --durations evidence) and correctly assigned. No test is dropped — every test runs in at least one tier, and /land still runs everything.

metadata.land_summary: Split test suite into fast unit tier (nox -s unit, pytest -m 'not slow') vs unchanged full landing gate (nox -s tests); 8 real-reranker/live-Q&A tests tagged @pytest.mark.slow, registered with --strict-markers. No test dropped (8 slow + 711 not-slow = 719).

title: App-level Ctrl+Q confirm-if-dirty guard doesn't cover EditScreen
description: lode-0wj.8 wired LodeApp.action_quit's confirm_quit() hook for CaptureScreen only. lode-0wj.6's new EditScreen (edit-existing-note-from-browse) has its own real unsaved state but deliberately does NOT define confirm_quit() -- Ctrl+Q from EditScreen today just quits the whole app immediately, discarding any in-progress edit with no confirm (same as every other non-capture screen, but now a screen with genuine unsaved state falls into that gap). Wiring it would need EditScreen's confirm_quit() to end in self.app.exit() (matching Ctrl+Q's global 'quit' contract) rather than self.app.pop_screen() (Escape's 'back to browse' contract) -- see lode-0wj.6's --design notes for why the two can't share one method.
design: EditScreen (lode.tui.screens.browse) should define confirm_quit() that: exits immediately if the buffer equals the loaded body (same 'unchanged, not empty' check as action_cancel), otherwise pushes DiscardConfirmScreen and on resolution calls self.app.exit()/self.app.exit(note_id) (not pop_screen), mirroring CaptureScreen.confirm_quit()'s contract exactly.
acceptance_criteria: Ctrl+Q from EditScreen with an unchanged buffer quits immediately (no confirm). Ctrl+Q with a changed buffer pops Save/Discard/Cancel (DiscardConfirmScreen); Save writes the version then quits the app, Discard quits without saving, Cancel returns to editing. Escape's existing pop-to-browse behavior (lode-0wj.6) is unaffected.

metadata.land_summary: EditScreen.confirm_quit() wires app-level Ctrl+Q to the confirm-if-dirty guard: unchanged buffer quits immediately (dirty check vs loaded body, not emptiness), dirty buffer pops DiscardConfirmScreen -> Save appends a new version then app.exit(note_id), Discard app.exit(), Cancel resumes editing; CAS conflict on the quit-save pushes ReconcileScreen with the default (no on_resolved) so it exits the app rather than popping to browse. Save logic shared with Ctrl+S via extracted _attempt_save; Escape's pop-to-browse contract unchanged. Technical review (/code-review + /simplify): no correctness or simplification fixes needed. Gates green: 737 passed, 6 skipped.

title: Add 'build' to the dev extra for a canonical wheel/sdist packaging path
description:
The repo has no packaging/build tool in its dev deps, so there is no canonical way to produce or verify a wheel/sdist. 'python -m build' (PyPA's standard front-end for setuptools.build_meta, which is already the [build-system] backend) is the obvious tool and is exactly what lode-1i8.4's acceptance criterion assumed: 'verify the built wheel/sdist actually contains the .tcss (e.g. inspect python -m build output)'. But 'build' is not installed.

CONTEXT: hit during /epic-audit of lode-1i8 — I went to run 'python -m build --wheel' to confirm the TUI stylesheet actually ships in the wheel (the package-data footgun lode-1i8.4 flagged) and it failed with 'No module named build'; I fell back to 'pip wheel . --no-deps' (works, but is not the standard/reproducible packaging path and doesn't exercise the sdist).

## Design
Add 'build' to [project.optional-dependencies].dev in pyproject.toml (alongside pytest/nox/ruff), unpinned per the repo's current 'unpinned until the build starts' convention. That makes 'python -m build' available in ./venv so packaging (wheel + sdist) is a first-class, reproducible operation and package-data regressions (like the .tcss shipping) can be verified the way the tickets already assume.

Optional (builder's discretion, keep it simple): a small nox session (e.g. 'nox -s build' or a package-data smoke check) that builds the wheel and asserts expected data files (*.sql, *.tcss) are present — turning the lode-1i8.4-class footgun into an automated gate instead of a manual inspection. Only add this if it stays lightweight; the dep itself is the core ask.

## Acceptance Criteria
- 'build' is listed in the dev extra in pyproject.toml (unpinned, consistent with pytest/nox/ruff).
- After ./scripts/python-init.sh + activate, 'python -m build' produces a wheel AND an sdist with no missing-module error.
- The built wheel contains the shipped package-data (src/lode/schema.sql -> lode/schema.sql and src/lode/tui/lode.tcss -> lode/tui/lode.tcss).
- nox -t fix passes; if a build/smoke nox session is added, it passes too.

## Notes
Touches pyproject.toml (dev extra). Docs/deps-only; no runtime code. Independent of lode-1i8.* (that epic is audited); this is standalone dev-tooling.
acceptance_criteria: 'build' is in the pyproject dev extra; 'python -m build' yields a wheel+sdist post python-init; the wheel contains lode/schema.sql and lode/tui/lode.tcss; nox -t fix passes.

metadata.land_summary: Add 'build' to dev extra + opt-in 'nox -s build' that builds wheel+sdist and asserts lode/schema.sql & lode/tui/lode.tcss ship in the wheel

title: Record the --debug↔DEBUG coupling deferral in docs/decisions.md (epic-audit gap on lode-1i8)
description:
Found by /epic-audit closing-side review of lode-1i8 (E15).

GAP: E15 settled a deferred design decision — the top-level 'lode --debug' flag is deliberately COUPLED to log level (--debug == set root logger to DEBUG), tying log VERBOSITY to feature ENABLEMENT (the DEBUG-gated diagnostics, e.g. the latency_probe). The decision explicitly defers the alternative: 'if a future debug feature must be enabled WITHOUT DEBUG-level log spam (or vice-versa), split the two concepts then.' This is a textbook 'deferred, not forgotten' decision, but it lives ONLY in the lode-1i8 epic description and the lode-1i8.3 ticket description — not in docs/, the source of truth.

EVIDENCE: lode's routing rule (CLAUDE.md): 'Design facts and decisions -> docs/, never memory/ticket ... open questions in docs/decisions.md ... A design fact that lives only in memory/ticket forks the record.' docs/decisions.md is titled 'Open decisions (deferred, not forgotten)' and is exactly where this belongs. grep of docs/decisions.md finds no debug/coupling/verbosity/enablement entry. The OBSERVABLE behavior is already documented (docs/configuration.md 'lode --debug' row) — only the deferred DECISION + its split-trigger is missing from the record. Once these closed tickets age out of easy view, the 'why coupled, when to split' rationale is undiscoverable in docs/.

DONE WHEN: docs/decisions.md carries a bullet capturing the --debug↔DEBUG-level coupling as a deferred decision: what was decided (couple verbosity to feature-enablement for the diagnostics), the accepted tradeoff, and the split trigger (a debug feature needing enablement without DEBUG log spam, or vice-versa). Link it to the configuration.md '--debug' row and the latency_probe design. Docs-only change; no code touched.
acceptance_criteria: docs/decisions.md contains a deferred-decision bullet for the --debug==DEBUG-level coupling, stating the decision, tradeoff, and split trigger, cross-linked to configuration.md's --debug row; no code changed.

metadata.land_summary: docs(decisions): record --debug↔DEBUG-level coupling as a deferred decision (tradeoff + split trigger, cross-linked to configuration.md --debug row); docs-only, no code.

title: Document LODE_LOG_LEVEL (and ANTHROPIC_LOG) in docs/configuration.md

Doc-only edit under a worktree per CLAUDE.md. Independent of the other children (touches only docs/). Deliberately does NOT document the new --debug flag — that flag documents itself as part of its own ticket (the --debug child).

title: Instrument the capture screen: lag diagnosis spike (rebuild after land bounce)

title: Enrich gap: empty-summary heads thrash reconcile (stamp job prompt_ver in worker)
description: Surfaced during lode-0wj.9 review. The enrich-gap query (src/lode/reconcile.py, _enrich_gap_step) keys 'enrichment is current' on the presence of a kind='summary' annotation stamped with the current ENRICH_PROMPT_VER. A head whose enrichment ran under the current prompt but where Haiku returned an empty summary writes NO summary row, so it is re-flagged as a gap on every reconcile tick and re-enqueued indefinitely — a fresh Haiku call each cycle for a content-free/summary-less note. Untested and real. Root cause: the design (docs/storage.md ~L354) keys enrich jobs by (type, target_version, prompt_ver), but the worker never actually stamps prompt_ver on the job (worker.py ~L338 sets only status='done'; prompt_ver appears nowhere in worker.py, contradicting the enqueue_derive_jobs docstring). Fix: implement the design's job-prompt_ver stamping in the worker and switch the enrich-gap signal to the job's own prompt_ver instead of annotation presence — fixes the empty-summary thrash and aligns reconcile with the documented job-identity model. Touches worker.py, hence out of scope for lode-0wj.9.
notes: Not a land-blocker for lode-0wj.9 — that branch correctly implements its AC and strictly improves on prior behavior (which didn't re-enqueue on prompt bumps at all).

metadata.land_summary: Stamp jobs.prompt_ver on enrich completion in both the immediate (worker.run_one) and Batches API (collect_enrich_batch) paths; re-key reconcile enrich-gap off the done job's own prompt_ver instead of summary-annotation presence, fixing empty-summary head thrash.

title: /land bounce: re-parent the rebuild ticket to the bounced child's epic
description: When /land bounces a ready-for-land child of an epic, it creates a NEW rebuild ticket and supersede-closes the original — but the rebuild is currently unlinked, so the epic loses a child and can read 'complete' while real work is still open. Re-parent NEW to the original's epic (parent-child) so the epic's completion accounting stays honest and /epic-audit sees the real work. Also soften the now-resolved caveat in the /epic-audit skill.
acceptance_criteria: /land Bounce section captures the bounced ticket's parent epic and links the rebuild ticket to it as parent-child before supersede; /epic-audit §3 caveat updated to reflect that /land re-parents.

title: Epic-completion audit: /land labels completed epics, /epic-audit reviews + files gap tickets
description:
Closing-side gate for epics, mirroring how /debate gates them going in. When an epic's children are ALL closed, it should be reviewed for gaps/consistency against the epic goals, and any actionable gaps filed as tickets (ambiguous ones escalated to a human).

Two pieces (user-approved split trigger):
1. /land Section 4: after closing a landed ticket, walk to its parent epic (dependencies[] parent-child); if the parent is an open epic whose parent-child dependents are now all closed and it is not already labeled, add label 'epic-ready-to-audit'. Cheap, event-exact detection in the single-writer.
2. New /epic-audit skill: consume epics labeled 'epic-ready-to-audit' (or an explicit id), run a debate-style completion review (acceptance met? dropped scope? tickets closed inconsistent with epic intent?). Disposition per finding: actionable gap -> bd create child ticket labeled 'epic-audit-gap' (flows to /code); needs-human-judgment -> bd human escalate. On clean/done, relabel epic 'epic-audited'.
acceptance_criteria: 1) /land labels an epic 'epic-ready-to-audit' exactly when its last parent-child dependent closes (idempotent, epics only). 2) /epic-audit skill exists, reads labeled epics or an explicit id, files actionable gaps as epic-audit-gap child tickets and escalates ambiguous ones via bd human, and relabels the epic epic-audited when reviewed. 3) Both usable via /loop.

title: Wire redact-before-index into the actual save/index path
description:
lode-fk8.2 built redact_before_index() (src/lode/redact.py) as a pure, unit-tested function, but it has zero callers outside its own test file. docs/externals.md's "Two redactions, aimed at the right legs" is explicit that a pasted .env/API key must not become locally retrievable via vector or FTS search -- but today it does:

- cli.py `add` -> Repository.save(note_id, body) stores the raw body, no redaction call.
- embedding.py:embed() reads the raw body via _version_body() and calls chunk() directly -- no redact_before_index() call before chunking/embedding into LanceDB.
- lexical.py:LexicalIndex.replace_passages() also chunks the raw body directly into passages_fts -- no redaction there either.

redact-before-egress (the enrich/Q&A leg) is correctly wired via lode.egress.gate_qa_egress and enrich.py -- only the before-index leg was left unconnected. Found during a /debate completeness pass on lode-fk8 prior to closing the epic.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. `lode add "key: TOPSECRET-42 done"` (or any text matching a redact_before_index_patterns seed).
2. Vector- or keyword-search (`lode ask` context retrieval, or a direct FTS/LanceDB query) for `TOPSECRET-42`.
3. Observe the secret is retrievable -- it was never stripped before chunking/embedding/FTS indexing.
acceptance_criteria: A pasted secret matching redact_before_index_patterns is stripped before it reaches the vector index (LanceDB) and the FTS index (passages_fts) -- e.g. saving a note containing a seeded secret pattern, then vector- and keyword-searching for the raw secret string, returns no hits. Most natural fix point: apply redact_before_index() to the body once in Repository.save (or equivalent shared point) before it is handed to embedding.embed() and LexicalIndex.replace_passages(), so both indexing legs see the same redacted text. Existing redact_before_egress wiring (enrich.py, egress.py) is untouched.
notes: Surfaced by /debate lode-fk8 (completeness pass) -- see lode-fk8 for full epic context.

metadata.land_summary: Wire redact_before_index() into both index legs: embedding.embed() (async vector leg, re-reads versions.body) and Repository.save() cache.index call (sync FTS leg); versions.body stays raw, egress path untouched; +3 regression tests.

title: immediate Haiku on save + Batches API for bulk (rebuild after land bounce)
description:
Rebuild of lode-npx.2, bounced by /land semantic review.

ORIGINAL: Fresh note enriches via one immediate Haiku call; bulk/backfill/re-enrich via
the 50%-off Batches API (uses E2 batch-resume). embed always lands fast regardless.

REBUILD BRIEF (from land-review):

Acceptance: The ticket's contract is "A fresh note enriches via one immediate Haiku
call" — the note just saved, specifically. cli.py::_enrich_immediately(conn, db_path,
version_id) takes a version_id parameter and its docstring claims it "opportunistically
claim[s] + run[s] the enrich job just enqueued for version_id" — but the body never uses
version_id; it calls worker.claim_and_run_one(conn, db_path, Settings(),
types=("enrich",)), which claims via _claim_one: oldest pending job of type enrich,
FIFO, no filter by version/target at all (src/lode/worker.py _claim_one).

If any other enrich job is already pending at the moment of `add` — a backlog from a
burst of prior adds, an idle/offline worker, jobs not yet swept by
_batch_submit_enrich's flush-size-limited pass — the freshly saved note's own job stays
pending and an unrelated, older note gets the immediate Haiku call instead. The new note
is silently NOT enriched immediately, contradicting the acceptance criterion as written.
This isn't hypothetical: the bounced branch's own commit 10b1d36 ("fix(enrich): close
batch-submit vs immediate-enrich double-spend TOCTOU") describes exactly this —
"an interactive `lode add` immediate-enrich (claim_and_run_one, which runs without the
worker lock) can flip a job pending->running between the batch step's SELECT and its
UPDATE" — the branch's own author relied on claim_and_run_one grabbing an arbitrary
pending job to explain the TOCTOU it then had to fix.

Test coverage masked this: every test in test_cli.py starts from an empty DB, so the
job just enqueued is always the only pending enrich job and happens to be the one
claimed — the tests can't distinguish "claims the job for this note" from "claims
whatever's oldest." No test exercised a backlog at time of `add`.

docs/storage.md's "How the immediate path stays a fast path" section states the capture
path "claims and runs that specific job inline" — documents the same false invariant as
the code; needs correcting too.

WHAT THE REBUILD MUST SATISFY:
1. _enrich_immediately must claim the SPECIFIC job it just enqueued for version_id, not
   an arbitrary oldest-pending enrich job. Options: (a) have save()/
   enqueue_derive_jobs return the enrich job's row id and add a claim-by-id primitive
   (CAS UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND status='pending', mirroring _claim_one but keyed on id
   instead of type-priority scan), or (b) filter claim_and_run_one's candidate query by
   target_version.
2. Correct docs/storage.md's "that specific job" claim to match reality (or make it true).
3. Add a regression test that seeds an unrelated pending enrich job before calling `add`
   and asserts the NEW note's job — not the backlog one — ends up 'done'.
4. Carry over what was sound in the bounced branch: the atomic embed+enrich enqueue in
   Repository.save, the double-spend CAS fix for batch-submit vs immediate-enrich
   (commit 10b1d36's mechanism), and the Batches API bulk path — all reviewed clean and
   should not be redone from scratch.

Bounced branch for reference: land/lode-npx.2 @ 10b1d369a3b9afa7a03a3cb19ca3f5d9eb7a9b9f
(dropped from origin as part of this bounce).
acceptance_criteria: A fresh note's enrich job (not an arbitrary pending backlog job) is the one claimed and run inline by lode add's immediate-enrich path, verified by a regression test that seeds an unrelated pending enrich job first; docs/storage.md's description of the immediate-claim mechanism matches the implementation; the atomic embed+enrich enqueue, the batch-submit/immediate-enrich double-spend CAS fix, and the Batches API bulk path from the bounced branch are preserved.

metadata.land_summary: Rebuild of lode-npx.2: immediate-enrich now claims the just-saved note's OWN enrich job, not an arbitrary oldest-pending one. Threads keyword-only target_version through worker._claim_one (adds 'AND target_version = ?' to the candidate SELECT) and worker.claim_and_run_one; cli._enrich_immediately passes result.version_id. Carried over clean: atomic embed+enrich enqueue, batch-vs-immediate double-spend per-row CAS, Batches API bulk path. docs/storage.md immediate-claim invariant corrected. Regression tests (test_cli backlog scenario + 3 worker tests) genuinely exercise the bug. Technical review found no defects; gates green: 581 passed/4 skipped.

title: Wire rerank + graph_expand into the live retrieve() pipeline (cli._retrieve)
description:
Context: found during /land semantic review of lode-72m.5 (graph_expand + trust_rank).

E4's own epic-level acceptance criteria (lode-72m) reads: "hybrid retrieval runs
FTS5 + vector -> RRF -> rerank -> expand_parents -> graph_expand -> trust_rank
over passages, heads only." With lode-72m.5 landed, all 5 subtasks are closed
and the epic reads 5/5 -- but the live `lode ask` path (cli.py's private
`_retrieve`) only calls: lexical_search + vector_search -> reciprocal_rank_fusion
-> expand_parents -> trust_rank. Two of the six documented stages are never
invoked from the live path:

- `rerank()` (lode-72m.3, closed) -- built, unit-tested, config-gated via
  `Settings.rerank_enabled` (default on) -- but `_retrieve` never imports or
  calls it.
- `graph_expand()` (lode-72m.5, closed) -- same story: built, unit-tested,
  no-ops safely with no edges -- but `_retrieve` never calls it either.

Neither subtask's own (narrower) acceptance criteria mentioned wiring into
cli.py, so neither branch was bounced for it -- but the epic's acceptance is
not actually met, and nothing currently tracks closing that gap now that all
named subtasks are closed.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `lode ask <question>` against a DB with edges and multiple candidate
   passages.
2. Read `src/lode/cli.py`'s `_retrieve` function.
3. Observe it imports only `build_match_query, expand_parents, lexical_search,
   reciprocal_rank_fusion, trust_rank, vector_search` from `lode.retrieval` --
   `rerank` and `graph_expand` are absent, so results are never reranked and
   the knowledge graph is never traversed, regardless of `Settings.rerank_enabled`
   or edge data present.
design: Depends on lode-72m (parent epic, for context) but is independent of any single closed subtask -- this closes the wiring gap left across lode-72m.3 and lode-72m.5.
acceptance_criteria: cli._retrieve calls rerank(...) (respecting Settings.rerank_enabled) between reciprocal_rank_fusion and expand_parents, and graph_expand(...) between expand_parents and trust_rank -- matching the full pipeline order in lode-72m's epic description and docs/retrieval.md. An integration test against the live 'lode ask' path (not just the individual retrieval.py unit tests) demonstrates both stages actually fire.

metadata.land_summary: Wire rerank + graph_expand into cli._retrieve (RRF→rerank→expand_parents→graph_expand→trust_rank); review restored the retrieval_top_k cap at the fusion→rerank boundary so the rerank-off path stays bounded. +3 integration tests.

title: structural staleness + re-anchor rules (rebuild after land bounce)
description:
Rebuild of lode-npx.3, bounced by /land semantic review.

REBUILD BRIEF (from land-review):
Wire reanchor_annotations(conn, note_id, new_version_id, new_body) and reanchor_edges(conn, note_id, new_version_id, new_body) into the real note-update path so the acceptance criteria's "on update" behavior actually occurs. The natural call site is Repository.save (repository.py) alongside its existing versions._save_core + jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs call — inside the same 'with conn:' transaction, guarded to run only on SaveResult.kind == "update" (not "create", where there's no prior AI annotation/edge layer to re-anchor yet) and skipped when deduped=True (no-op save). Add an integration test exercising this through Repository.save / the public save path (not just direct staleness.py calls) proving that updating a note's body actually flips a previously-fresh AI annotation to stale/orphaned per the documented rules. Keep the existing staleness.py unit tests and schema migration as-is — they are correct and can carry forward into the rebuild (the bounced branch land/lode-npx.3 @ a121cb77 has the classifier + migration + 541 lines of unit tests already, just no caller).

WHAT WAS WRONG: staleness.py's reanchor_annotations/reanchor_edges were implemented and unit-tested but never called anywhere in src/ outside their own definitions — a real note update via Repository.save never re-anchors any AI annotation or edge, so the ticket's literal acceptance criteria ("on update an unchanged quote stays fresh, a changed quote is stale, a missing quote is orphaned") does not happen in the live system.
acceptance_criteria: When the head moves past source_version the annotation reads stale; on update an unchanged quote stays fresh, a changed quote is stale, a missing quote is orphaned — verified through Repository.save (the real update path), not only direct staleness.py unit calls.
