metadata.land_summary: Wire staleness reanchor into Repository.save: update-only, non-dedup save re-anchors AI annotations/edges inside the version-write transaction; removed staleness.py's inner 'with conn:' so it composes atomically. Verified fresh/stale/orphaned via public save path.

title: worker loop: claim → run → retry/backoff → dead-letter (rebuild after land bounce)
description:
Rebuild of lode-i05.3, bounced by /land during a batch merge with lode-i05.1.

BOUNCE CAUSE (combined-merge breakage; each branch was green in isolation):
lode-i05.3 was built off a trunk that did NOT yet contain lode-i05.1. lode-i05.1 (now LANDED on trunk, merge c14a6a3) removed the internal 'with conn:' from lode.jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs — after i05.1, enqueue runs as a plain INSERT on the CALLER'S open transaction and no longer commits on its own. i05.3's test tests/test_cli.py::test_work_leaves_enrich_pending calls 'enqueue_derive_jobs(conn, "ver-1")' WITHOUT a surrounding 'with conn:' and then closes the connection, so post-i05.1 the inserts roll back on conn.close() → no enrich row → 'TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType object' at test_cli.py:851. Combined re-gate: 1 failed, 426 passed.

REBUILD BRIEF:
- Re-implement i05.3's accepted scope UNCHANGED on top of current trunk (which now includes i05.1): src/lode/worker.py (handler registry with only 'embed'; atomic CAS _claim_one; run_one done/failed+backoff/dead; _reset_retryable; drain one-shot/--loop) + the 'lode work' Typer command under the i05.2 WorkerLock + the _iso() helper. The worker IMPLEMENTATION itself was semantically ACCEPTED and is correct against i05.1's contract — only one test made a now-invalid assumption.
- FIX the stale test: in tests/test_cli.py::test_work_leaves_enrich_pending, wrap the enqueue_derive_jobs(conn, ...) call in a 'with conn:' block (or otherwise commit) before closing the connection, since after i05.1 enqueue_derive_jobs does not open/commit its own transaction. Audit the other worker/cli tests for the same assumption (test_work_drains_pending_embed_jobs already wraps its inserts in 'with conn:', so it is fine).
- Re-verify ALL i05.3 acceptance criteria green via nox against the post-i05.1 enqueue contract before handing off.
- Scope fence still holds: do NOT remove capture's inline embed (that is x6r.5) and do NOT add enrich/refresh handlers.

metadata.land_summary: Worker loop rebuild (lode.worker) + 'lode work' Typer command on top of landed i05.1: handler registry (embed only), atomic CAS _claim_one, run_one state machine (done | failed+backoff | dead at max-attempts), durable next_attempt_at backoff, _reset_retryable + drain one-shot/--loop under the i05.2 WorkerLock (second invocation exits 1). Stale-test fix: test_work_leaves_enrich_pending now wraps enqueue_derive_jobs in 'with conn:' to commit before close (post-i05.1 enqueue no longer opens its own txn). Scope fence held: capture inline embed untouched, no enrich/refresh handlers. Reviewer refactor: re-extracted _iso() for the schema ISO-8601 timestamp (DRY).

title: jobs schema hardening: idempotency key + backoff/dead-letter columns
description: The landed E1 jobs table (src/lode/schema.sql) cannot support the E2 acceptance criteria ('idempotent by key', 'backoff-retry -> dead-letter') as written. Harden the schema BEFORE the jobs-table/enqueue and worker-loop work so those tickets build on a sound table. Surfaced by the 2026-06-28 debate of E1 as the E2 foundation (see lode-i05 notes, findings 1/2/6).
design:
Three schema changes to src/lode/schema.sql + a docs/storage.md pin. Decisions PINNED 2026-06-28 (lode-i05 breakdown) — this supersedes the earlier "decide and pin" forks.

(1) IDEMPOTENCY KEY — a partial UNIQUE index over an expression.
Add a key expressing job identity so enqueue (i05.1) AND reconciliation re-enqueue (i05.4) is a no-op against an existing LIVE job, not a duplicate row. Identity is (type, target_version) for embed and (type, target_version, prompt_ver) for enrich. prompt_ver is NULL on embed and SQLite treats NULLs as DISTINCT in UNIQUE, so a naive UNIQUE(type,target_version,prompt_ver) will NOT dedupe embed jobs. Use a partial unique index over a COALESCE expression, scoped to live jobs:
    CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_jobs_live ON jobs(type, target_version, COALESCE(prompt_ver, ''))
        WHERE status IN ('pending', 'running');
Scoping to pending/running is load-bearing: it dedupes in-flight work, but STILL ALLOWS a re-enqueue after the prior job reached 'done'/'dead' — a prompt_ver bump or a re-derive must be able to enqueue again (the reconciliation scan depends on this). Enqueue switches to INSERT .. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Also fix docs/storage.md:264, which omits `type` from the key formula.

(2) BACKOFF SCHEDULING — next_attempt_at.
Add `next_attempt_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime(...'now'))` (ISO-8601 UTC) so the worker (i05.3) durably schedules a retry: a claim selects WHERE status='pending' AND next_attempt_at <= now. Without it a restart mid-backoff retries immediately.

(3) DEAD-LETTER TERMINAL — distinct 'dead' status (DECISION: distinct 'dead', NOT "'failed' is terminal").
Add 'dead' to the status CHECK so the enum is ('pending','running','done','failed','dead'). 'dead' is the poison terminal reached at the max-attempts gate; 'failed' is the transient last-error state a retry resets to 'pending' from. Update src/lode/cli.py (the `status` read-out, ~line 411, which today labels 'failed' as the dead-letter) to surface 'dead' as the dead-letter terminal. Record the status lifecycle pending -> running -> {done | failed -> pending | dead} in docs/storage.md, and update the §8 jobs status enum in the data-shape sketch (storage.md:342, currently pending|running|done|failed).

SCOPE FENCE: schema + docs + the cli.py status-label fix only. Does NOT fold enqueue into the save txn (i05.1), does NOT move enqueue ownership (i05.1), does NOT write the worker loop (i05.3). Update tests/ for the new constraints.
acceptance_criteria: A duplicate enqueue of the same LIVE (type,target_version[,prompt_ver]) is a no-op for BOTH embed (NULL prompt_ver) and enrich; a re-enqueue after the prior job is 'done'/'dead' IS allowed; jobs has next_attempt_at and 'dead' in the status CHECK; cli.py status read-out surfaces 'dead' as the dead-letter; docs/storage.md §8 + the async-queue section record the corrected (type-inclusive) idempotency key, next_attempt_at, and the pending->running->{done|failed->pending|dead} lifecycle.

metadata.land_summary: jobs schema hardening: live-job partial unique index (COALESCE prompt_ver) for idempotent enqueue (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), next_attempt_at backoff column, distinct 'dead' terminal + cli status surfaces dead-letters; docs/storage.md key formula/lifecycle pinned

title: code-reviewer: apply /code-review --fix edits via bash in path-entered builder worktree
description: The code-reviewer subagent is launched with isolation: worktree and EnterWorktree(path=…) into the builder's worktree. Claude Code's built-in Edit/Write isolation guard stays pinned to the reviewer's OWN launch worktree and rejects Edit/Write against the path-entered builder worktree, even though bash/git cwd moved correctly. Upstream Claude Code behavior (EnterWorktree path-form does not re-pin the Edit/Write guard) — not patchable from this repo. Fix on the lode side: encode the proven workaround in .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md so reviewers apply /code-review --fix + /simplify edits via bash (precise single-match replacements) instead of Edit/Write, rather than rediscovering it each run. Discovered during lode-5y8.5 technical review.
acceptance_criteria: code-reviewer.md step 4 (and/or step 6) tells the reviewer that in a path-entered builder worktree the Edit/Write isolation guard is pinned to the launch worktree and rejects those paths, so /code-review --fix + /simplify edits must be applied via bash (precise single-match replacements, assert one match per edit); the guidance is consistent with the existing 'work in the builder's worktree' steps and does not contradict CLAUDE.md.
close_reason: Encoded the bash-workaround in .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md (steps 2, 4, quick-card): reviewer applies /code-review --fix + /simplify via bash single-match replacements in the path-entered builder worktree, since Claude Code's isolation guard pins Edit/Write to the launch worktree. Merged to trunk via worktree-lode-ddv.

title: Verify end-to-end lode ask under Claude Code OAuth (messages.parse + structured outputs)
description:
## Context
lode-tcq added a Claude Code OAuth fallback in auth.build_client (auth_token bearer + anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20). Auth was proven to succeed (429 rate-limit, not 401), but a full successful messages.parse / structured-output call under the OAuth token was NOT verified — the test session was rate-limited by a concurrent Claude Code session. Subscription-scoped OAuth tokens may behave differently from API keys on some endpoints (e.g. may expect a Claude-Code-style system prompt, or reject structured outputs / certain betas).

## Steps to Reproduce
On a box whose only credential is the Claude Code login (~/.claude/.credentials.json), with no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and no ant profile, run a real `lode ask` against a populated DB and observe whether it returns cited claims or errors (403/identity/beta-conflict).

## Acceptance Criteria
- A real `lode ask` returns synthesized cited claims (or an honest abstention) under OAuth-only auth, OR
- if it fails, the failure mode is documented and the OAuth path is adjusted (e.g. required system prompt / beta headers) or the fallback is scoped accordingly.
notes:
VERIFICATION CHECKLIST (added 2026-07-07). What's under test: ask calls client.messages.parse(output_format=_ClaimsEnvelope) — structured outputs (qa.py:190) — while the OAuth client pins anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20 (auth.py:137). Open Q: does a subscription OAuth token accept structured outputs + that beta? Prior attempt only got 429 (auth proven, parse not).

TRAPS: (1) enrichment != ask — lode add runs inline enrich via messages.create WITH A TOOL (enrich.py:168), a different API surface, and itself hits the API. Pre-populate on a KEYED box so the only OAuth call judged is messages.parse. (2) repo ./.env holds a key; don't source it and unset key env vars or you silently test the SDK key path, not OAuth.

Phase 0 (on a KEYED box): export LODE_HOME=/tmp/eyp-verify; lode add a specific keyword-answerable fact + 2-3 more notes; lode work (drain embeds so dense retrieval, not just lexical, is exercised — check lode jobs); confirm keyed baseline: lode ask returns a cited claim (isolates corpus from auth).

Phase 1 (OAuth-only condition): ensure ~/.claude/.credentials.json exists w/ non-expired claudeAiOauth.expiresAt (run claude to refresh; auth.py:126 rejects expired); unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN ANTHROPIC_PROFILE; ensure no ant profile selected; do NOT source ./.env (move it aside). Don't run from inside an active Claude Code session on the same subscription (avoids the 429 that blocked last time).

Phase 2: same LODE_HOME; run: lode --debug ask "<question>". CONFIRM OAuth actually used: --debug log must contain "Resolved Anthropic credentials from the Claude Code login" (auth.py:132) — else a credential leaked in; fix Phase 1. Optionally repeat with --think-harder (Opus, qa.py:155) to test beta/structured-output combo on a 2nd model.

Phase 3 outcome: PASS = returns cited claims (version/snapshot + verbatim span) OR the honest abstention line — either is a successful messages.parse round-trip = acceptance met. FAIL = capture exact error, match anticipated mode & act: beta/header conflict -> structured outputs may need its own beta comma-joined into default_headers (auth.py:138); 403/identity/"system prompt required" -> OAuth may need a Claude-Code-style system prompt, adjust system=_SYSTEM_PROMPT (qa.py:193); structured outputs rejected for subscription tokens -> scope the OAuth fallback (ok for enrich tool-call, not ask structured output) and document. Record verbatim cmd + resolved-credential log line + result into this ticket (acceptance requires documenting the failure mode if it fails).

Phase 4 close: PASS -> bd close lode-eyp --reason with cmd/output, then bd dolt push. If a code fix was needed, make it IN A WORKTREE (never trunk), land via /code -> /land, then close referencing the fix; file discovered-from tickets for anything deferred. title: Wire a configured Settings into the interactive 'lode ask' CLI command
description:
cli.ask (src/lode/cli.py:145) constructs no Settings and passes none into cited_answer.ask, so the chain uses Settings() defaults end-to-end. With lode-u51 the gate now honors a threaded Settings (the eval path at cli.py:502 already passes one), but the interactive ask command still does not load/construct a user-configured Settings, so gate-tuning knobs like entailment_threshold remain inert from the interactive entry point. Harmless in v1 (threshold ships untuned) but the user-facing path can't honor config.

## Acceptance Criteria
- cli.ask resolves/constructs a Settings and passes settings= into cited_answer.ask so a configured entailment_threshold (and other gate knobs) is honored from the interactive 'lode ask' path.
- A test proves a configured Settings reaches the gate via the CLI ask command (mirroring the offline ask-path test added in lode-u51).
- Depends on whatever CLI config-loading mechanism is decided (no config-file/env loader is wired into the ask command today).

metadata.land_summary: Construct a Settings() in cli.ask and thread it into _retrieve and cited_answer.ask (mirroring the eval path) so configured gate knobs like entailment_threshold are honored from the interactive 'lode ask' path; CLI test proves a strict threshold abstains and a lax one survives via the real ask command.

title: Migrate existing ~/.local/share/lode data to $LODE_HOME (~/.lode)

Existing users with data at ~/.local/share/lode/lode.db are NOT yet migrated. Decide + implement the migration mechanism (see docs/decisions.md '$LODE_HOME migration'): (a) one-time move-if-present on startup (zero-touch, but the CLI relocates an irreplaceable DB — data-safety care: move lode.db, lode.db.lock, lancedb/ atomically, never clobber an existing ~/.lode, leave a marker) vs (b) document a manual move (release note / 'lode doctor' hint). Product/UX + data-safety decision deliberately deferred out of lode-qd9. Acceptance: an existing ~/.local/share/lode install keeps working after upgrade with its notes intact; no silent data loss; chosen mechanism documented.
acceptance_criteria: An existing ~/.local/share/lode install keeps working after upgrade with its notes intact (DB, lock, lancedb vectors reachable under the chosen scheme); no silent data loss or clobber of an existing ~/.lode; the chosen migration mechanism (auto move-if-present vs documented manual move) is decided in docs/decisions.md and implemented/documented accordingly.

title: Thread Settings into gate_cited_answer so entailment_threshold is honored on the ask path
description: cited_answer.gate_cited_answer calls gate.apply_gate(result.answer, bodies) without passing through ask()'s Settings, so the step-3 NLI entailment_threshold (and any future gate-tuning knob) falls back to the Settings() default regardless of a user's configured value. Harmless in v1 (the threshold ships untuned/conservative and is not meant to be tuned yet), but it means the knob is inert end-to-end. Fix: thread settings (and optionally an EntailmentScorer) from ask() -> gate_cited_answer -> apply_gate. Out of lode-1k3.4's declared file scope (gate/faithfulness/config only).

metadata.land_summary: Thread Settings (+optional EntailmentScorer seam) from cited_answer.ask through gate_cited_answer into apply_gate so the configured entailment_threshold is honored on the ask path; offline ask-path test proves a non-default threshold flips the gate decision.

title: Eval harness: embed the dense-leg query with search_query prefix (asymmetric nomic)
description: lode.eval.harness._retrieve embeds the question via Embedder.embed_passages, which the production FastEmbedEmbedder prefixes with 'search_document: '. nomic-embed-text-v1.5 is asymmetric and expects 'search_query: ' for queries. Using the document prefix symmetrically biases the dense (cosine ANN) retrieval leg, softening recall@k quality when the harness is wired with the real embedder. The Embedder protocol (lode.embedding) currently exposes only embed_passages — fixing this means adding a query-embedding method to the seam (embedding.py), then using it in the harness query path. Lexical leg carries recall meanwhile, so impact is bounded.

metadata.land_summary: Point eval harness _retrieve at Embedder.embed_query (search_query prefix) for the dense-leg query vector, removing the asymmetric-nomic bias; mirror embed_query on the harness test stub.

title: lode ask: wire the dense (vector) retrieval leg
description: The 'lode ask' command (lode-y42.2) currently retrieves on the synchronous lexical leg alone; RRF scores a single-leg passage fine, so this is a valid subset. The dense (LanceDB cosine ANN) leg is deferred because it needs two pieces not yet landed: (1) the on-disk LanceDB location the capture-side indexing wiring establishes (lode-1f9 cache composition wires EmbeddingCacheBackend into the add path and owns where vectors live), and (2) a query-side embedding helper (the landed FastEmbedEmbedder.embed_passages uses the 'search_document:' prefix; nomic wants 'search_query:' for queries, so a query embed path must land). Once both exist, wire vector_search(store, conn, query_vector, k) into lode.cli._retrieve alongside the lexical leg. Acceptance: lode ask fuses lexical + dense legs via RRF over a populated store.
acceptance_criteria: lode ask fuses the lexical + dense legs via app-side RRF over a populated LanceDB store: a question's query vector is embedded (search_query prefix) and vector_search is wired into lode.cli._retrieve alongside lexical_search; a passage matched only by the dense leg still reaches the Q&A context.

metadata.land_summary: Wire the dense (LanceDB cosine ANN) leg into lode ask via a shared Embedder.embed_query (asymmetric search_query: prefix); _retrieve fuses lexical+dense over the documented $LODE_HOME/lancedb store. Tests offline.

title: Wire `lode purge` to the hard-delete mechanism (E8)
description: lode-y42.3 shipped `lode purge` as a deliberate refusing stub (exits non-zero, names the missing mechanism) because the E8 hard delete — chain sweep + cache cascade — is lode-fk8.4, which is not built and itself touches off-limits subsystems (LanceDB vectors, FTS). Once fk8.4 exists, replace the refusing stub body in src/lode/cli.py with a real delegation to it. Acceptance: `lode purge <target>` invokes the fk8.4 hard delete (overwrites body with [purged YYYY-MM-DD], sets purged_at, sweeps the chain, cascade-drops the derived cache, keeps source=user annotations).
design: Acceptance: 'lode purge <note_id>' performs the hard delete via Repository.purge(note_id) and reports what it swept (no longer refuses, exits 0 on success). Replace the refusing-stub body in src/lode/cli.py: add a TARGET note_id argument + reuse _DB_OPTION/_open_db; construct Repository(conn) (default NullCache — cache composition wiring lands in lode-1f9, and 'add' likewise does not yet route through Repository, so NullCache is the simplest correct thing today); call repo.purge(target); KeyError -> 'no such note' on stderr, exit 1; on success echo the swept version count + the [purged YYYY-MM-DD] marker. Localized to cli.py.

metadata.land_summary: lode purge <note_id> now hard-deletes via Repository.purge (chain sweep + cache cascade, reports the sweep); replaces the refusing stub in cli.py

Both the lode-x6r.1 (chunking.py) and lode-y42.1 (jobs.py) producers hit this in the same /code run and each lost a test cycle building a worktree-local venv (scripts/python-init.sh) to recover. Editing an EXISTING module doesn't need this (the file already resolves under the main-checkout package). Keep it to a couple of sentences in the right place; do not redesign the venv strategy — just document the gotcha and the one-line fix. Verify the doc edit doesn't break any mermaid (scripts/validate-mermaid.sh if a diagram changed; prose-only otherwise).

title: Web fetch + readability extraction unit (draw-down)
description:
First real child of E12 (web draw-down connector). A pure fetch/extract unit with NO storage coupling — the raw material every other connector child consumes.

## Scope
Given a URL, return (clean_text, raw_html, status): fetch the page, run readability extraction (strip nav/ads/chrome), and on failure (403/paywall/JS-scaffold/network) return a tombstone status instead of garbage (docs/externals.md 'Draw-down rules'). This unit fetches ONE page only; one-hop-then-stop is enforced by the edge/trigger layer (w0h.3), not here.
- Add the HTTP client + readability dependency to pyproject.toml (decide which; keep it lean, stdlib-friendly if practical).
- Injectable fetcher seam (like the embedding/entailment seams) so tests run fully offline — no live network in nox.
- Output feeds w0h.2's snapshot body (clean_text) and raw_payload (raw_html).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pure function/unit: url -> (clean_text, raw_html, status); no DB writes.
- Readability strips navigation/ads; a JS-scaffold/403/paywall page yields a tombstone status, not scaffolding text.
- Fetcher is injectable; offline tests cover success, empty/garbage, and failure->tombstone. nox -t fix + nox -s tests green.
- New dep recorded in pyproject.toml (single source of truth per CLAUDE.md).
acceptance_criteria: Placeholder — not actionable until the core loop ships end-to-end (design.md §7). No implementation criteria until decomposed.
notes:
CRITICISM (debate): AC 'JS-scaffold/403/paywall yields tombstone not scaffolding' depends on an UNSPECIFIED detection heuristic -- readability extraction alone does not tell you a 200-OK page is a JS shell. Name the heuristic (extracted-text length threshold, known-scaffold marker) or the AC is not testable. Also the HTTP-client + readability dep choice is still undecided, baked into this leaf.
DECISION-NEEDED (debate round 3, 2026-07-08): the round-1 CRITICISM was logged but never resolved, and this is the READY frontier. (1) Tombstone-detection heuristic is still UNNAMED: AC 'JS-scaffold/403/paywall yields tombstone not scaffolding' is untestable until you name it (extracted-text-length threshold? known-scaffold marker? status-code + empty-readability?). Readability alone won't flag a 200-OK JS shell. (2) HTTP-client + readability LIBRARY still undecided and baked into this leaf; 'stdlib-friendly' won't hold for the readability half (a real dep is coming). Library can defer to the builder; the heuristic cannot — decide it before build.
DECISION (debate round 3, 2026-07-08, user): Fetch-outcome taxonomy replaces the vague 'yields tombstone'. (a) 2xx + extractable -> job done, 'ok' snapshot. (b) PERMANENT failure (403/401/paywall; 2xx JS-shell or empty-extract) -> job done, 'tombstone' snapshot (retry won't help). (c) TRANSIENT failure (429/5xx/network/timeout) -> RAISE so the existing queue machinery re-tries: attempts + next_attempt_at backoff, failed->pending retry, ->dead at max-attempts (PINNED lode-i05.6); on 'dead' write a 'tombstone' snapshot so the note edge still resolves. (d) 3xx -> follow to a hop cap, then the FINAL resolved URL is what w0h.3 canonicalizes into external_id. Testable detection signal = extractor None/empty (trafilatura-style) combined with HTTP status; text-length floor is a config knob. LIBRARY: this is a SPIKE -- deliverable MUST include a documented evaluation + basis for the HTTP-client/readability choice (or an explicit flag that more exploration is needed), not a silent pick. JS-rendered pages = PERMANENT tombstone here; headless-render retrieval is a filed follow-on (lode-follow), NOT first-connector scope.
(the JS headless-render follow-on referenced above is lode-oni.)

title: durable batch-handle persistence + resume-on-restart
description:
Persist submitted Claude Batch handles + their member jobs and resume on restart — re-poll the handle, ingest results, mark done; NEVER resubmit. This is the one thing reconciliation can't reconstruct: once a Batch is POSTed it's money in flight, and a reconcile scan would see "not yet enriched" and double-spend (docs/storage.md "The one thing reconciliation can't reconstruct: a submitted Batch"). It is the requirement that rules out an in-memory queue.

DEFERRED out of the core E2 embed pass — DECISION 2026-06-28: a batch_handle only exists once enrich-via-Batches (E7 / lode-npx.2) is built, so this is untestable until then and should land alongside it. The jobs.batch_handle column already exists in schema.sql; the resume hook is the worker's (i05.3) startup step. Blocked on lode-npx.2 (the Batches submit path that produces handles) and lode-i05.3 (the worker startup where resume runs).
design: On batch submit (E7): persist the batch_handle on the member enrich jobs and mark them in-flight ('running' with the handle set). On worker startup (i05.3), as a step alongside reconciliation: find jobs with a non-null batch_handle in a non-terminal state and re-poll the Batch — ingest completed results (write the enrichment, mark member jobs 'done'); leave a still-running handle for the next poll; NEVER re-submit. Because the in-flight rows are 'running' with a handle (not 'pending'), the reconciliation scan's "not yet enriched" gap query must skip them, so it can't double-spend.
acceptance_criteria: A persisted batch handle is re-polled and ingested on restart without resubmission; completed handles mark their member jobs 'done'; an in-flight handle survives restart and is not resubmitted; the reconciliation scan skips in-flight ('running' + handle) jobs so it cannot double-spend.

Tests: test_enrich_gap_skips_in_flight_batch_job + 3 worker tests incl. end-to-end restart-resume asserting batches.create never called and no duplicate enqueue. Plus a worker.py docstring tightening. Mechanism was pre-built (lode-npx.2/i05.3/i05.4); this ticket certifies it via tests. Review found nothing to fix. Gates green: 585 passed/4 skipped, lint clean.

title: worker loop: claim -> run -> retry/backoff -> dead-letter
description: The single-owner worker that drains the durable jobs queue. Exposed as a Typer command `lode work` (worker model PINNED 2026-06-28): a ONE-SHOT DRAIN by default — acquire the advisory lock (i05.2), run the reconciliation scan (i05.4) on startup, then claim -> run ready jobs until none remain, release the lock, exit. One-shot is testable and serves the eval harness + scripted use now (Phase A has no long-running host process). A `--loop` / `--watch` flag runs the SAME loop polling on an interval as the long-running single owner. Once this lands, x6r.5 flips capture's skeleton inline-embed onto this queue.
design:
HANDLER REGISTRY: the worker dispatches on jobs.type via a registry. `embed` has a handler NOW (runs the existing chunk+embed+FTS path: lode.embedding.embed + lode.lexical). `enrich` and `refresh` handlers are registered later by E7 (npx) and the connectors step. A job whose type has NO registered handler is LEFT pending (never claimed, never dead-lettered) — so the enrich rows i05.1 enqueues per capture accumulate harmlessly until E7's handler arrives. The claim query therefore filters to types the worker can actually run.

CLAIM: select one ready, runnable job — status='pending' AND next_attempt_at <= now AND type IN (<registered handler types>) — ORDER BY priority (embed > enrich, docs/storage.md:274) then created. Atomically flip to 'running' with UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND status='pending' and assert rowcount=1, so a stray second claimer can't double-take (belt-and-suspenders behind the single-owner lock).

RUN: invoke the type's handler.
  - ok -> status='done'.
  - transient error -> attempts += 1, last_error set, status back to 'pending' with next_attempt_at = now + exponential backoff (base/factor from lode.config); a restart mid-backoff does NOT retry early (the reason i05.6 added next_attempt_at). Mark 'failed' as the transient last-error state per i05.6's lifecycle.
  - max-attempts gate reached (config knob) -> status='dead' (i05.6's poison terminal), preserving attempts + last_error for the `lode status` read-out.

SINGLE OWNER: the whole loop runs under the i05.2 advisory lock; a second `lode work` refuses.

SCOPE FENCE: the worker loop + `lode work` command + the embed handler wiring. Does NOT remove capture's inline embed (that flip is x6r.5). Does NOT implement enrich/refresh handlers (E7 / connectors).
acceptance_criteria: A claimed embed job runs once and lands its passages/vectors/FTS; a transient failure retries with growing next_attempt_at backoff (not before next_attempt_at); a poison job reaches status='dead' with attempts + last_error recorded; 'lode work' drains all runnable jobs then exits and '--loop' keeps polling; an enrich job with no registered handler is left pending, never dead-lettered; the loop runs under the advisory lock (a second 'lode work' refuses).

metadata.land_summary: Async work queue worker (lode.worker) + 'lode work' Typer command: handler registry (embed only), atomic CAS claim, run_one state machine (done | failed+backoff | dead at max-attempts), durable next_attempt_at backoff, _reset_retryable + drain one-shot/--loop under the i05.2 WorkerLock (second invocation exits 1). Scope fence held: capture inline embed untouched, no enrich/refresh handlers (enrich left pending, never dead-lettered). Reviewer refactor: extracted _iso() for the schema-coupled ISO-8601 format.

title: reconciliation scan (startup + periodic)
description:
The self-healing net (docs/storage.md "Reconciliation scan on startup + periodically"). Scans head versions and re-enqueues any missing fresh derived work, so crashes, dropped jobs, the save/enqueue gap, and prompt_ver bumps all self-correct. Runs on worker startup (i05.3) and periodically in `--loop` mode. Idempotent by i05.6's key: re-enqueue is INSERT .. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING against the live-job partial unique index, so running it repeatedly enqueues no duplicates.

Phase-A scope is the EMBED gap: a live head version (notes.head_version_id, excluding delete tombstones and purged notes) with no passages row for that version_id -> enqueue an embed job. The ENRICH gap (no fresh source='ai' enrichment for the head, or a prompt_ver bump made it stale -> re-enqueue the corpus) is a registered scan step filled by E7 — it needs the enrichment tables and prompt_ver semantics that don't exist yet. Mirror i05.3's handler-registry shape: scan steps for types that exist now run now; E7 appends the enrich step.
design:
EMBED GAP QUERY: head versions missing passages — e.g. notes joined to their head version, where the head op is not 'delete' and the note is not purged, and no passages row exists for head_version_id -> enqueue embed(head_version_id).

IDEMPOTENCY: the scan does NOT pre-check for an existing job; it relies entirely on i05.6's live-job partial unique index + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING to dedupe. This is why i05.6 scopes the unique index to pending/running: a head whose embed is already 'done' but later goes stale (new head) enqueues against the NEW version_id, which has no live job, so it is correctly re-enqueued.

ONE ENQUEUE PATH: reuse the i05.1 Repository/jobs enqueue, not a second hand-rolled INSERT, so there is a single enqueue site.

SCOPE: embed-gap reconciliation + the periodic hook for `--loop`. Enrich-gap step is left as a seam for E7.
acceptance_criteria: A live head version with no fresh embed is re-enqueued by the scan; running the scan repeatedly enqueues no duplicate jobs (idempotent against i05.6's live-job unique index); a soft-deleted/purged head is not enqueued; enqueue reuses the single i05.1 enqueue path. (Enrich-gap reconciliation is a registered step filled by E7.)

metadata.land_summary: Reconciliation scan (src/lode/reconcile.py): step-registry mirrors worker's handler-registry; Phase-A embed_gap step re-enqueues live head versions (notes.head_version_id, op!='delete', purged_at IS NULL) missing a passages row via jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs(types=('embed',)) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING against idx_jobs_live (in-flight=no-op, re-enqueue after done/dead allowed). Wired into 'lode work' before each drain pass (startup + every --loop tick). jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs gains a backward-compatible keyword-only types= param. Enrich-gap seam left open for E7 (register_step) with no dead code. Review: removed one redundant/misleading test; gates green (443 passed).

title: single-instance advisory lock
description:
Startup advisory lock (lockfile + PID, beside the DB under $LODE_HOME) so the async worker has a single owner (docs/storage.md "Single-instance = a startup advisory lock"). This lock is NOT a data-integrity guard — CAS + SQLite serialization cover correctness; it exists solely so two workers don't run duplicate / racing embed+enrich loops and double-spend Claude Batches (docs/storage.md:100-104). It is what lets the one-claimer SQLite queue (i05.3) stay correct with no distributed locking (docs/storage.md:280).

Behaviour: acquire on worker start (i05.3 `lode work`); if held by a LIVE pid, refuse to start and name the holding pid; release on clean exit. A lock left by a NO-LONGER-RUNNING pid is reclaimable (stale), not a permanent wedge — a crashed worker must not block the queue forever.
design:
Lockfile path under $LODE_HOME (lode.config paths). On acquire, write the current pid. On start:
  - file present AND pid alive  -> refuse: print "another lode worker is running (pid N)", non-zero exit.
  - file present AND pid dead   -> stale: reclaim (overwrite) and proceed.
  - file absent                 -> acquire.
Release = remove the file on clean exit (context manager / finally), so a normal exit frees it immediately.

SCOPE: the lock primitive + acquire/refuse/reclaim/release, with a direct test. Wiring it into the `lode work` loop is i05.3's job. Liveness check is best-effort (os.kill(pid, 0) / equivalent) — single-machine, single-user, so a pid-reuse false "alive" is acceptable; we are not building a distributed lock.
acceptance_criteria: A second acquisition refuses while the lock is held by a live pid and names that pid; the lock releases on clean exit; a lock left by a no-longer-running pid is reclaimed, not treated as held.

metadata.land_summary: Single-instance advisory lockfile primitive (lode.lock.WorkerLock): acquire writes PID beside the DB, refuse+name a live holder, reclaim a stale/corrupt lock, release on clean exit (context manager). Path derived from caller-supplied db_path (lode.config default_db_path), not re-derived; not wired into 'lode work' (that is i05.3). Reviewer reuse fix: 'lode config' now reads the lock path from lock.lock_path instead of re-deriving it.

title: jobs table + atomic enqueue in save txn
description: Durable jobs (type embed|enrich|refresh, target_version, prompt_ver?, status, attempts, last_error?, batch_handle?). Enqueue derive jobs in the SAME txn as the version write (single-file SQLite atomicity, docs/stack.md).
design:
ENQUEUE OWNERSHIP / ATOMICITY — DECISION PINNED 2026-06-28 (lode-i05 breakdown), supersedes the earlier "decide consciously" fork in this ticket.

OWNERSHIP: the Repository owns enqueue. It already owns the save+cache seam (irreplaceable version write, then cache index/evict); enqueueing a head version's derive jobs is the third thing that must happen on a head change, and jobs are operational/irreplaceable rows — so enqueue belongs at the Repository seam, NOT in the CLI and NOT buried in versions.py.

ATOMICITY / SEAM: refactor lode.versions.save (and delete/recover as the enqueue path needs) so the version-write runs inside a CALLER-MANAGED transaction instead of opening + committing its own `with conn:`. Repository.save then wraps the version-write AND the enqueue in ONE `with conn:`, so "write version row + enqueue its derive jobs" commits atomically (docs/storage.md:269 "enqueued in the same transaction as the save"). Job-type knowledge (jobs.DERIVE_JOB_TYPES) stays in jobs.py / the Repository — it never enters versions.py.

RETIRE the standalone path (kills the "two enqueue sites = hazard" the debate flagged):
  - jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs stops opening its own txn — it becomes a plain INSERT .. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (against i05.6's live-job partial unique index) on the caller's conn, run inside Repository's transaction.
  - the direct caller in `lode add` (src/lode/cli.py:177) is removed; capture goes through Repository.save, now the SINGLE enqueue site.

BUILD ON i05.6: enqueue is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING against the live-job unique index, so a duplicate / reconcile re-enqueue is a no-op. Do not re-add the key here.

CONSTRAINTS: keep versions.save's CAS + no-op-dedup contract intact — only the transaction OWNERSHIP changes (save must not commit independently when Repository drives it). On a deduped no-op save, Repository enqueues NOTHING (same skip as the cache index). Editing versions.py is now permitted: the y42.1 lane fence that originally forbade it is gone. Record the pinned ownership/atomicity/layering choice in docs/storage.md (the async-queue section) so the decision lives in the design, not only in code.
acceptance_criteria: Writing a version and enqueuing its derive jobs commit in one transaction; an injected failure between the version-write and the enqueue (or in the enqueue) rolls back BOTH — no version without its jobs, no jobs without the version. A deduped no-op save enqueues nothing. lode add no longer calls jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs directly; Repository.save is the sole enqueue site. The pinned ownership/atomicity choice is recorded in docs/storage.md.

metadata.land_summary: Atomic save+enqueue: Repository.save wraps versions._save_core (CAS write, no own txn) + jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs (plain ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING insert) in one 'with conn:' so version-write + derive-job enqueue commit/rollback together; dedup no-op enqueues nothing; lode add + eval harness route through Repository.save as the sole enqueue site (cli no longer calls jobs directly); ownership/atomicity/layering pinned in docs/storage.md

title: E12 — First external connector: web-link draw-down
description:
Step 2 of the build sequence (docs/design.md §7): the first external connector, decomposed 2026-07-07 after the core loop (E0–E11) shipped. Connector chosen = WEB-LINK DRAW-DOWN (a note pastes a URL -> fetch, extract, snapshot) — it exercises the novel external machinery (refresh, material-change gating, 'as of fetched_at' citation) while avoiding the §7 rot sources (auth, pagination, alien API models).

Scope note: the storage + read substrate for externals was ALREADY built during the core loop and marked 'UNUSED until the connectors step' — externals/snapshots/edges tables, snapshot_id hashing (hashing.py), trust_rank (retrieval.py), external-aware Q&A + egress (cited_answer.py/qa.py). E12 is a WRITE-SIDE spike on that substrate, normalized to (external_id, snapshot, fetched_at, source_type, raw_payload) — which is already the physical schema.

Children — skeleton first (prove end-to-end), then hardening:
- w0h.1 fetch+readability unit -> w0h.2 ingest mirrored snapshot -> w0h.3 URL-detect + explicit edge + one-hop draw-down -> w0h.4 cite 'as of fetched_at' + trust-rank verify   (SKELETON: pasted URL -> snapshot -> retrievable -> honestly cited)
- w0h.5 material-change re-enrich gating; w0h.6 refresh policy (TTL/on-access); w0h.7 no_egress on a source   (HARDENING)

OUT OF SCOPE (fan-out, not first connector): inferred note<->external edges — enrichment already writes gated source='ai' edges generically (lode-npx.3); promoting those belongs to E13 (lode-kke).

No dependency on lode-ccv (OAuth revert): connector credential resolution goes through auth.build_client but there is no code coupling (confirmed 2026-07-07).
design: Connector = web-link draw-down (user decision 2026-07-07). Rationale: exercises refresh/materiality/fetched_at — the genuinely novel external machinery — with the least connector-specific rot; there is no corpus-usage signal yet to prefer tickets vs repo, and repo-at-commit is too static to exercise refresh. Build skeleton (w0h.1-4) to prove end-to-end before hardening (w0h.5-7). Fan out to more connectors only after this loop genuinely works (design.md §7 step 3 = E13/lode-kke).
acceptance_criteria: The web draw-down connector works end-to-end: a note pasting a URL yields a fetched, readability-extracted, snapshotted, embedded, locally-retrievable external node, cited in answers 'as of fetched_at', with re-embed-on-any-change but re-enrich-only-on-material-change gating, a working refresh policy, and no_egress honored (withheld from cloud, cited as such). All EIGHT children closed (w0h.1-w0h.8; w0h.8 = read-enablement, added by decision B). Link-rot immune (snapshot, never a bare URL).
notes:
CRITICISM (debate 2026-07-07): The 'read substrate already built, E12 is write-side-only' framing is FALSE on one axis. live_head_versions (retrieval.py:87) is built purely from notes JOIN versions; both direct legs lexical_search (retrieval.py:94) and vector_search (retrieval.py:110) scope to it, so a snapshot_id is never a direct hit. trust_rank tiers snapshots (retrieval.py:626-630) only AFTER candidate selection. Externals currently reach Q&A ONLY via graph-expansion from a citing note, not by their own content.

DECISIONS (2026-07-07, escalated+resolved): (A) Externals ARE directly retrievable -> union externals.head_snapshot_id into live_head_versions. (B) Read-enablement is a NEW child lode-w0h.8 (depends on w0h.2; w0h.4 now depends on w0h.8). (C) w0h.5 materiality signal = embedding similarity, so the enrich gate runs POST-embed. (D) w0h.7 now depends on w0h.4.
CORRECTION (debate round 3, 2026-07-08): child count is EIGHT, not seven. The DESCRIPTION 'Children —' narrative predates the w0h.8 split (decision B) and lists only .1-.7; w0h.8 (direct-retrievability read-enablement) belongs in the skeleton group: it blocks w0h.4 and is depended on by w0h.5. AC count corrected seven->eight.

title: E8 — Privacy, egress & purge
description: Per docs/externals.md privacy: no_egress on notes (captured/indexed/locally-retrievable, never sent to Claude, cited 'withheld'); redact-before-index + redact-before-egress pattern sets (high-precision seeds in config); egress_log read surface; purge hard delete = version/note granularity, sweep whole chain incl tombstones, overwrite body with [purged YYYY-MM-DD] + set purged_at, cascade cache drop + local re-derive, flag purged (hash no longer recomputable).
acceptance_criteria: All E8 tasks closed: no_egress is honored everywhere, redact-before-index/egress are active, the egress log is queryable, and purge hard-deletes with cache cascade.
close_reason: E8 complete: all 6 children landed. no_egress honored at both send legs, redact-before-index wired at every body-writing index caller (save/recover; purge marker n/a) + redact-before-egress on enrich/Q&A, egress_log queryable, purge hard-deletes with cache cascade. Final gap (recover leg, lode-ibv) surfaced by /debate completeness pass and landed.

title: E2 — Async work queue & single-owner
description: Durable jobs table per docs/storage.md: atomic enqueue in the same txn as save (single-file SQLite); single-instance advisory lock (lockfile/PID); worker loop claim->run->backoff-retry->dead-letter; reconciliation scan (startup+periodic) re-enqueues head versions missing fresh embed/enrich, idempotent by key; durable batch-handle persistence + resume-on-restart (the one thing reconcile cannot reconstruct without double-spend).
acceptance_criteria: All E2 tasks closed: derive jobs enqueue atomically with the save, a single owner runs the claim/retry/dead-letter loop, the reconciliation scan self-heals idempotently, and batch handles resume without double-spend.
notes:
CRITICISM (debate 2026-06-28, E1->E2 handoff): landed jobs table + enqueue do NOT support the E2 ACs as written.
1. jobs table has NO idempotency key (INTEGER PK + non-unique idx_jobs_status only); enqueue_derive_jobs plain-INSERTs, so double-enqueue / reconcile re-enqueue = duplicate pending rows. 'Idempotent by key' (E2 AC, docs/storage.md:264) has nothing to be idempotent against.
2. Key formula in docs/storage.md:264 (version_id | version_id+prompt_ver) OMITS type, so embed+enrich for one version collide. Real key is (type,target_version[,prompt_ver]); prompt_ver is NULL on embed rows and SQLite treats NULLs as distinct in UNIQUE, so naive UNIQUE won't dedupe embed. Must coalesce/partial-key.
3. 'Atomic enqueue in same txn as save' (docs/storage.md:269) is ALREADY VIOLATED: jobs.py enqueues in a SEPARATE txn (y42.1 lane fence forbade editing versions.py). E2.1 is a refactor+migration: fold enqueue into versions.save txn AND retire standalone enqueue_derive_jobs + its CLI caller. Two enqueue sites = hazard.
4. versions.save() has no seam for same-txn enqueue (opens+commits own 'with conn:'). Folding in forces a layering decision: push job-type knowledge into versions.py (the coupling jobs.py avoided) vs restructure save to expose its open txn. Decide consciously; record in docs/storage.md.
5. Enqueue ownership unsettled across 3 layers: CLI calls jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs; Repository.save indexes cache but never enqueues; versions.save knows nothing of jobs. Collides with E2 'single owner'. Pin one home, reconcile with the Repository irreplaceable-vs-cache seam.
6. jobs schema lacks worker-loop columns: status CHECK is pending/running/done/failed (no dead-letter terminal distinct from transient failed); no next_attempt_at/not-before for durable backoff (restart mid-backoff retries immediately). E2.3 backoff+dead-letter not implementable without schema change or a pinned max-attempts policy.
RESOLUTION: leading schema-hardening ticket (idempotency key, next_attempt_at, dead-letter terminal) blocks the jobs-table/enqueue work; record the enqueue-ownership/layering decision in docs/storage.md.
BREAKDOWN PINNED 2026-06-28 (4 decisions resolved with bildzeitung):
1. Worker model: one-shot 'lode work' drain by default + '--loop' polling mode (no daemon/TUI host in Phase A); not an in-process thread. -> i05.3.
2. Batch resume (i05.5) DEFERRED to land with E7: a batch_handle only exists once enrich-via-Batches (npx.2) is built, so it is untestable now. i05.5 dep-linked to npx.2 + i05.3.
3. Enqueue seam: Repository OWNS enqueue; refactor versions.save to run inside a caller-managed txn so Repository.save commits version-write + enqueue atomically; retire jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs's standalone txn and the lode-add caller (one enqueue site). -> i05.1.
4. Dead-letter terminal: distinct 'dead' status (not 'failed'-is-terminal); 'failed' is the transient last-error state retries reset from. -> i05.6.
Build order this pass: i05.6 -> i05.1 -> {i05.2 -> i05.3} -> i05.4. i05.5 lands with E7. Each design-doc decision (idempotency key fix, 'dead' lifecycle, enqueue ownership) is recorded in docs/storage.md by its owning ticket, in a worktree.
close_reason: E2 (async work queue & single-owner) complete: i05.1/i05.2/i05.3/i05.4/i05.6 all landed on trunk; i05.5 (batch-handle resume) re-parented under E7/npx to land with enrichment.

title: canonicalize_url corrupts IPv6 literal hosts: netloc rebuilt from bracketless parts.hostname yields invalid external_id
description:
canonicalize_url (src/lode/drawdown.py) rebuilds netloc from parts.hostname + parts.port. For an IPv6 literal host, urlsplit strips the brackets from parts.hostname ("[::1]:8080" -> hostname "::1"), so the rebuilt netloc becomes "::1:8080" and the canonical form is "http://::1:8080/p" -- a corrupt, non-reparseable authority (re-parsing raises ValueError: port could not be cast, since the host colons are read as a port delimiter). external_id for any IPv6-literal source with a non-default port is therefore malformed; even with a default port the bracketless host is ambiguous.

PRE-EXISTING: introduced by lode-w0h.3's canonicalize_url (the hostname+port reconstruction predates lode-0as). lode-0as (userinfo strip) did NOT introduce it -- and the userinfo/privacy strip itself works correctly for IPv6 (credentials are dropped even for bracketed hosts). This is orthogonal: a dedup-correctness / identifier-validity defect, not a privacy one.

SAME CLASS as the two gaps lode-0as deliberately deferred and documented in docs/externals.md "URL canonicalization" (path percent-encoding %7E vs ~; IDN unicode vs punycode) -- "left for a future ticket if a real corpus ever shows it matters." IPv6 bracket handling is a third sibling, but arguably slightly worse: percent-encoding/IDN yield DISTINCT-but-valid external_ids (a dedup miss = two nodes), whereas IPv6 yields a CORRUPT/invalid external_id.

Discovered by the lode-0as technical review (code-reviewer, 2026-07-09) while scrutinizing the userinfo-strip parsing. Not folded into lode-0as: that branch is a tightly-scoped privacy fix, and expanding it to fix one of three documented-as-deferred dedup gaps (while leaving the other two) would be arbitrary scope creep.
design: Bracket the host when it is an IPv6 literal before appending the port: if the host contains ":", wrap it as "[host]". Standard approach. Add tests for "http://[::1]:8080/p", "http://[2001:db8::1]/p" (default-port), and "https://user:pass@[::1]:8080/p" (userinfo + IPv6 both handled). Consider settling all three deferred normalization gaps (percent-encoding, IDN, IPv6) together, since docs/externals.md already groups them and lode-w0h.6 inherits the same constraint.
acceptance_criteria: canonicalize_url preserves IPv6 literal host brackets: "http://[::1]:8080/p" canonicalizes to a re-parseable "http://[::1]:8080/p" (host "::1", port 8080), not "http://::1:8080/p". Tests cover IPv6 with non-default port, IPv6 with default port, and IPv6 + userinfo (userinfo still stripped). nox -t fix + nox -s tests green.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. python -c: from lode.drawdown import canonicalize_url; print(canonicalize_url("http://[::1]:8080/p"))
2. Observe output "http://::1:8080/p" (brackets lost).
3. Re-parse it: from urllib.parse import urlsplit; urlsplit("http://::1:8080/p").port -> raises ValueError (host colons read as port delimiter).
4. Expected: "http://[::1]:8080/p" (host "::1", port 8080), a valid re-parseable authority usable as external_id.

title: A 'refresh' job that exhausts retries and goes dead leaves no tombstone snapshot for that URL
description:
Surfaced by the lode-w0h.3 builder (2026-07-08), which deliberately left it out of scope: it is not covered by w0h.3's acceptance criteria, and the fix is real work, not a one-liner.

lode-w0h.3 introduced the fetch->ingest HANDLER for the reserved 'refresh' job type. A pasted URL's initial draw-down IS the first 'refresh' job, riding the same retry/backoff machinery as w0h.6's later re-fetches (failed -> pending -> dead).

THE GAP: when a refresh job exhausts its retries and reaches the 'dead' terminal, nothing records that outcome against the external. No tombstone snapshot is written for the URL. lode.webfetch's own docstring assigns tombstone-writing to 'the caller', but the caller in the dead-letter path is the worker's retry machinery, which has no external-specific knowledge.

CONSEQUENCE: a note citing a URL that permanently fails to fetch has an explicit source='user' edge to an external node that never acquires a head_snapshot_id. Downstream this is indistinguishable from a draw-down still in flight. Note lode-w0h.8 makes snapshots directly retrievable by unioning externals.head_snapshot_id into live_head_versions -- a never-fetched external is silently absent there, which is correct but silent. Nothing surfaces 'this link is dead' to the user.

RELATED: lode-bvg is the same shape one layer up -- 'failed' (transient, in backoff) vs 'dead' (terminal) are conflated in the enrichment_state predicate. Both tickets are about the dead-letter terminal being under-observed. Resolve them with a consistent notion of 'permanently failed' if possible.
design:
Implementing this needs a hook the worker does not currently have. Two shapes:

(a) A worker.py terminal-transition callback: when a job moves to 'dead', invoke a per-job-type handler (e.g. refresh -> write a tombstone snapshot recording the failure + last error). Generalizes to other job types (embed/enrich dead-letters are equally unobserved today).

(b) A reconcile.py step that sweeps dead 'refresh' jobs and writes the tombstones out of band. Cheaper, no worker change, but introduces a lag and a second place that knows about externals.

Prefer (a) if the terminal-transition hook is wanted for embed/enrich too (likely -- see lode-bvg). Prefer (b) if the worker must stay dumb.

Decide alongside lode-bvg (needs-decision): both hinge on how the system represents 'permanently failed' vs 'still retrying' to a reader. A fourth enrichment_state value, or a tombstone with a reason, may serve both.
acceptance_criteria: A 'refresh' job that exhausts its retries and reaches 'dead' leaves a durable, readable record against the external -- a tombstone snapshot (or equivalent) carrying the failure and its last error -- so a dead link is distinguishable from a draw-down still in flight. The chosen mechanism (worker terminal-transition hook vs reconcile sweep) is recorded in docs/decisions.md with rationale. A test drives a refresh job to 'dead' and asserts the record exists.
notes:
Discovered during the lode-w0h.3 build. The builder flagged it in its hand-off rather than filing, so it is filed here to keep it from dying with the transcript.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Save a note containing a URL that cannot be fetched (unresolvable host, or a fetcher stubbed to always raise).
2. lode-w0h.3's detect_and_enqueue_drawdown creates the source='user' edge and enqueues a 'refresh' job.
3. Let the worker exhaust the retry/backoff chain: pending -> running -> failed -> ... -> dead.
4. Inspect the external node: it has no head_snapshot_id, and no tombstone snapshot records the permanent failure.
5. Nothing distinguishes this from an external whose first refresh job is still queued.
PARKED 2026-07-09 pending lode-k5e. This branch's Phase 2 technical review ran /code-review + /simplify from the reviewer's own launch worktree, which sits at trunk HEAD with an empty diff — so the mandated review tooling analyzed nothing and its 'no issues found' is not evidence of a clean branch (lode-k5e). The Opus reviewer's hand review still happened and its findings stand; what is missing is the skill's independent 5-agent coverage (CLAUDE.md adherence, shallow bug scan, git-history context, prior-PR comments, code-comment compliance). Label ready-for-land was REMOVED so /land cannot land it. Deliberately NOT set to ready-for-code-review: that would let /code's step-1 sweep re-review it with the same broken tooling. Once lode-k5e is fixed, swap needs-rereview -> ready-for-code-review to re-enter Phase 2 for a real review.
RE-REVIEW 2026-07-09: promoted needs-rereview -> ready-for-code-review after lode-k5e landed (merge bad00ea) fixing the empty-diff review bug. metadata.review_head refreshed to the branch's CURRENT origin tip, which includes the FIRST technical review's refinement commits — those are legitimately part of the branch and are what must now be re-reviewed. This is not builder drift. The prior Phase 2 ran /code-review + /simplify against an empty diff, so its 'no issues found' carried no information; the reviewer's hand findings from that pass stand, but the skill's independent coverage never ran. Re-review from scratch under the new architecture (fetch land/<id>, check out into own launch worktree, /code-review high --fix trunk...HEAD).

metadata.land_summary: Dead-letter hook: a 'refresh' job reaching terminal 'dead' (from both gates -- run_one max-attempts + _reclaim_stale_running crash-reclaim) tombstones its external via ingest_snapshot(status='tombstone', body carries last_error), in its own txn after the dead-status commit. Only on terminal dead, never on retry. Technical review added best-effort try/except so a raising hook can't wedge the drain loop / interactive lode add; degrades to the documented accepted 'tombstone-not-written-yet' gap. 926 passed/6 skipped.

title: Concurrent /code invocations can double-dispatch a reviewer onto the same worktree (step-0 and step-1 sweeps)
description:
Surfaced by the lode-t83 technical reviewer (2026-07-08), which deliberately did NOT fix it: not a regression t83 introduces, and it does not meet 'making it worse'.

WITHIN a single /code invocation the sweeps are safe by construction: step 0 (needs-rebase) and the new step 1 (stranded ready-for-code-review, added by lode-t83) both run BEFORE that invocation's Phase 1/2, so neither can select a ticket its own reviewer is mid-reviewing.

ACROSS two concurrent /code invocations it is not safe. A ticket stays labeled ready-for-code-review until its reviewer swaps it at the very END of review. So invocation B's step-1 sweep can select a ticket whose reviewer from invocation A is still live, and dispatch a SECOND code-reviewer onto the same builder worktree. The step-0 needs-rebase sweep has the structurally identical exposure (a needs-rebase ticket keeps its label until the rebase pickup completes) -- t83's step 1 mirrors it deliberately.

Failure is currently benign, which is why it was not escalated: reviewers never write trunk; the second reviewer's 'push HEAD:land/<id>' non-fast-forward-rejects or no-ops; clean-tree assertions guard the worktree. But two agents driving one worktree via 'git -C' concurrently is a race, and 'benign' is an observation about today's code paths, not an invariant.

Note /land has a local lockfile guard precisely so two landers cannot overlap. /code has no such guard, and concurrent /code is not a documented mode -- so the real question may be whether to document it as unsupported rather than to build a lock.
design:
Decide first WHETHER concurrent /code is a supported mode.

(a) If NOT supported: document it (code/SKILL.md + docs/agents-workflow.md) as unsupported, mirroring how /land states its one-machine topology invariant. Cheapest; no mechanism. This is likely correct -- /code fan-out already parallelizes within one invocation, so a second concurrent invocation buys little.

(b) If supported: the sweeps need a claim step, not a lock. A ticket selected by a sweep should be marked (e.g. label swap to in-review, or a metadata claim stamp) BEFORE the reviewer is dispatched, so a concurrent sweep's label predicate no longer matches it. Both step 0 and step 1 need it, not just step 1.

Do NOT reach for /land's lockfile: it guards writes to trunk (a single shared resource). The resource contended here is a per-ticket worktree, so a per-ticket claim is the right granularity.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) concurrent /code is documented as an unsupported mode in code/SKILL.md and docs/agents-workflow.md, consistent with how /land documents its one-machine invariant; OR (b) both the step-0 needs-rebase sweep and the step-1 stranded-review sweep claim a ticket (label or metadata) before dispatching an agent at it, such that a concurrent sweep's predicate cannot select the same ticket. The chosen option is recorded in docs/decisions.md with its rationale.
notes:
Discovered during the lode-t83 technical review. Related: lode-t83 (added the step-1 sweep), lode-83d (needs-rebase sweep hardening). /land's lockfile guard is the contrast case -- different resource, different granularity.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Dispatch a /code invocation that leaves a ticket at ready-for-code-review with its Phase 2 reviewer still running (any nontrivial branch; the reviewer swaps the label only at the END of review).
2. While that reviewer is still live, start a SECOND /code invocation on the same machine.
3. Invocation B's step-1 sweep runs 'bd list --label ready-for-code-review --status in_progress' and matches the ticket, because invocation A's reviewer has not swapped the label yet.
4. Invocation B dispatches a second code-reviewer at the same metadata.review_worktree.
5. Two code-reviewer agents now drive the same worktree concurrently via 'git -C <path>'.

Same recipe reproduces on the step-0 needs-rebase sweep by substituting a needs-rebase ticket with a live rebase-pickup producer.

Observed consequence today is benign (the loser's push non-fast-forward-rejects), so this reproduces as a race, not a visible failure -- which is the reason to fix or document it before the failure mode changes.
PARKED 2026-07-09 pending lode-k5e. This branch's Phase 2 technical review ran /code-review + /simplify from the reviewer's own launch worktree, which sits at trunk HEAD with an empty diff — so the mandated review tooling analyzed nothing and its 'no issues found' is not evidence of a clean branch (lode-k5e). The Opus reviewer's hand review still happened and its findings stand; what is missing is the skill's independent 5-agent coverage (CLAUDE.md adherence, shallow bug scan, git-history context, prior-PR comments, code-comment compliance). Label ready-for-land was REMOVED so /land cannot land it. Deliberately NOT set to ready-for-code-review: that would let /code's step-1 sweep re-review it with the same broken tooling. Once lode-k5e is fixed, swap needs-rereview -> ready-for-code-review to re-enter Phase 2 for a real review.
RE-REVIEW 2026-07-09: promoted needs-rereview -> ready-for-code-review after lode-k5e landed (merge bad00ea) fixing the empty-diff review bug. metadata.review_head refreshed to the branch's CURRENT origin tip, which includes the FIRST technical review's refinement commits — those are legitimately part of the branch and are what must now be re-reviewed. This is not builder drift. The prior Phase 2 ran /code-review + /simplify against an empty diff, so its 'no issues found' carried no information; the reviewer's hand findings from that pass stand, but the skill's independent coverage never ran. Re-review from scratch under the new architecture (fetch land/<id>, check out into own launch worktree, /code-review high --fix trunk...HEAD).

title: retrieval.graph_expand: 'AND n.head_version_id IS NOT NULL' is redundant against its own JOIN
description:
In src/lode/retrieval.py, graph_expand's query carries 'AND n.head_version_id IS NOT NULL' alongside 'JOIN versions v ON v.version_id = n.head_version_id'. The JOIN already excludes NULL heads (NULL never equals anything), so the predicate can never change the result set.

Harmless but misleading: it implies a NULL head is reachable through this query, which invites a reader to preserve it during a future refactor.

Spotted by the lode-n3t technical reviewer, which deliberately did NOT fix it -- pre-existing, untouched by that branch, and removing it there would have been scope creep. Correct call; filed so it isn't lost.
design: Delete the redundant conjunct. Verify the four retrieval regression tests still pass untouched (test_live_head_versions_are_current_non_deleted_heads, test_lexical_search_excludes_soft_deleted_note, test_vector_search_excludes_soft_deleted_note, test_graph_expand_skips_deleted_linked_notes). No new test needed -- this is a no-op by construction; a test would be asserting SQLite's JOIN semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
- The redundant 'AND n.head_version_id IS NOT NULL' is gone from graph_expand.
- nox -s tests green, the four named regression tests pass without modification.
notes:
Depends on lode-n3t landing (it touches the same query). 

SEPARATE, LARGER OBSERVATION from the same review, recorded here rather than filed -- decide whether it deserves its own ticket:

_LIVE_HEAD_PREDICATE is module-private, but SIX other queries restate 'v.op != \'delete\'' outside retrieval.py: reconcile.py (x2), notes_read.py (x2), repository.py, tui/edit.py. They cannot reuse it. Worse, reconcile.py additionally guards 'AND v.purged_at IS NULL' -- so 'live' is NOT one notion repo-wide, and the reviewer judged that divergence CORRECT and explicitly warned against unifying it (retrieval deliberately does not filter purged rows; purge cascades the FTS/LanceDB caches, so a purged head returns no passages anyway).

Any future 'de-duplicate the live predicate repo-wide' ticket must start by deciding whether retrieval-live and reconcile-live are the same predicate. The reviewer's answer is no. Do not paper over it with a shared constant.

metadata.land_summary: retrieval.py graph_expand: deleted the redundant 'AND n.head_version_id IS NOT NULL' conjunct. Verified no-op by construction — the INNER JOIN 'versions v ON v.version_id = n.head_version_id' already excludes NULL heads (NULL never equals anything); WHERE is a pure AND-chain (no LEFT/OUTER, UNION, CTE, or OR reintroducing NULL heads). Assembled query spacing verified clean. Review found no other refinements; the _LIVE_HEAD_PREDICATE cross-file de-dup was left intentionally divergent per lode-n3t. 883 passed / 6 skipped; four named regression tests pass, tests/ untouched. 1 file, 1 deletion.

title: bd dolt push call sites were enumerated with a grep that misses unprefixed invocations
description:
lode-83d routed 'all four' bd dolt push call sites through scripts/bd-dolt-push.sh. The enumeration used 'grep -rl "rtk bd dolt push" .claude/', which cannot see a call site written WITHOUT the rtk prefix.

Confirmed on trunk (2026-07-08), at least two survive unwrapped:
  .claude/skills/debate/SKILL.md:104  -- '...then `bd dolt push` so the writes reach the wire.'
  .beads/README.md:30                 -- bare 'bd dolt push' in a usage block

Found by the lode-83d technical reviewer, which deliberately did NOT fold the fix in: /debate is human-invoked and interactive (a failed push is observed, unlike the four unattended loops lode-83d hardens), and touching a fifth file would have widened the merge-conflict surface against four branches concurrently editing that set. Correct call -- but the note would have died with the ticket, hence this issue.

The defect is the ENUMERATION METHOD, not just the two sites. Any future audit of 'where do we call X' across .claude/ that greps for the rtk-prefixed form has the same blind spot. Note CLAUDE.md's golden rule says to always prefix with rtk, so unprefixed sites are themselves a (minor, separate) convention drift.
design:
Two parts, both cheap:

1. Route the surviving unwrapped call sites through scripts/bd-dolt-push.sh (or, for .beads/README.md, decide it is illustrative prose and leave it -- but decide, do not skip). Enumerate with a prefix-agnostic pattern, e.g. grep -rnE '(rtk +)?bd +dolt +push' over .claude/ and docs/ and scripts/, excluding .claude/worktrees/.

2. Judge whether /debate genuinely needs the wrapper. The reviewer argued it does not (human-invoked, failure observed). If that holds, record it as a deliberate exemption in the skill or docs/agents-workflow.md rather than leaving it looking like an oversight -- otherwise the next audit re-files this ticket.

Do NOT add a lint/CI check for this unless the two-site fix proves insufficient; simplest thing that works (CLAUDE.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- Every bd dolt push call site under .claude/, scripts/, and docs/ is enumerated with a prefix-agnostic grep (worktrees excluded), and each is either routed through scripts/bd-dolt-push.sh or documented as a deliberate exemption with the reason.
- .claude/skills/debate/SKILL.md:104 is resolved either way (wrapped, or explicitly exempted in-line).
- docs/agents-workflow.md's claim about the number of call sites, if any survives, matches reality.
notes:
Depends on lode-83d landing first -- that branch creates scripts/bd-dolt-push.sh and rewrites the four prefixed call sites. Doing this before it lands guarantees a conflict.

Surfaced by the lode-83d technical review, 2026-07-08.
