title: retrieval: the live-head predicate is defined twice (graph_expand re-states 'op != delete' inline)
description:
The "a live head is a head whose version op != 'delete'" predicate -- the single thing that keeps soft-deleted content out of every retrieval result -- is currently written in TWO places:

1. `live_head_versions()` (retrieval.py:76-90), the documented single source of truth. Called by `lexical_search` (:103) and `vector_search` (:126).
2. Hand-rolled inline inside `graph_expand` (retrieval.py:485-491): `... JOIN versions v ON v.version_id = n.head_version_id WHERE n.note_id IN (...) AND n.head_version_id IS NOT NULL AND v.op != 'delete'`.

(2) does not reuse (1) because it needs a per-note lookup keyed on `note_id IN (...)`, not the full live-head list `live_head_versions()` returns. So the duplication is understandable -- but it means "what counts as live" now has two definitions that must be changed together.

THIS IS NOT A LEAK, AND NOT A BUG TODAY. Three things are already true and were verified:
  - The lingering cache rows are INTENTIONAL and documented: docs/storage.md:294-300 states that a normal update/delete only indexes the new head, "so each superseded version's cache rows linger (retrieval filters to the live head) -- purge is the only op that clears them all." `LexicalCacheBackend.evict()` (lexical.py:196) is passed the TOMBSTONE's version_id, which never had passages, so it is a no-op in practice -- its own comment says so. The deleted note's content head keeps its rows in `passages`, `passages_fts`, and LanceDB. By design.
  - Every leg that exists today IS covered by a soft-delete exclusion test: test_lexical_search_excludes_soft_deleted_note (test_retrieval.py:144), test_vector_search_excludes_soft_deleted_note (:179), test_graph_expand_skips_deleted_linked_notes (:802). Plus test_live_head_versions_are_current_non_deleted_heads (:110).
  - Hard deletion of the content itself is `lode.versions.purge`, which cascades the caches. That is the correct and documented remedy.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH FIXING. The privacy guarantee ("a soft-deleted note is not keyword-findable") is enforced by convention -- each leg remembering -- rather than by construction. Two concrete failure modes:
  (a) A FOURTH retrieval leg is added and simply forgets to scope. Nothing structural stops it; the reviewer would have to know the invariant exists.
  (b) Delete semantics grow (e.g. a second tombstone op, or an `op IN ('delete','expunge')` predicate). One of the two sites gets updated, the other silently keeps the old definition, and the two legs disagree about what is live.

Surfaced by the /code technical review of lode-n8q (2026-07-08) as an out-of-scope observation; downgraded from the reviewer's original framing ("deleted content becomes keyword-findable") after checking the docs and the test suite -- the leak is already guarded and documented. What remains is the duplicated predicate.
acceptance_criteria:
The live-head predicate ("head whose version op is not a delete tombstone") is defined exactly ONCE in src/lode/retrieval.py, and graph_expand consumes that definition rather than re-stating `v.op != 'delete'` inline. A change to what counts as a delete requires editing one place. Existing behavior is unchanged: the four existing tests (test_live_head_versions_are_current_non_deleted_heads, test_lexical_search_excludes_soft_deleted_note, test_vector_search_excludes_soft_deleted_note, test_graph_expand_skips_deleted_linked_notes) still pass untouched.

Keep it simple: a shared SQL fragment constant, or a small helper taking an optional note_id filter, is enough. Do NOT introduce a query-builder abstraction. No docs/ change is owed -- docs/storage.md:294-300 and docs/retrieval.md already describe the intended semantics correctly; this only makes the code match the record in one place instead of two.

metadata.land_summary: retrieval.py: the live-head tombstone guard is defined once as module-private _LIVE_HEAD_PREDICATE; live_head_versions() and graph_expand() both interpolate it. Comment-only review fix corrected two false claims in the constant's contract (it is NOT repo-wide -- six other queries restate it, and reconcile also guards purged_at) and added the missing join-on-head_version_id precondition. All nine execute() SQL strings in retrieval.py verified byte-identical to trunk by AST constant-folding; zero behavior change. Four named regression tests pass, tests/ untouched.

title: Surface external-snapshot enrichment in the introspection UI (browse modal + lode show)
description: FOLLOW-ON bridging the enrichment-introspection epic (lode-ay5) and the web draw-down connector (lode-w0h). Once externals exist as fetched, readability-extracted, snapshotted nodes (w0h), the introspection surfaces built in ay5 should also render them: an external node's source URL, fetched_at ('as of'), source_type, current snapshot id, and — when present — its refresh/re-enrich state (last refreshed, whether the last change was material enough to re-enrich vs carried forward, no_egress 'withheld'). This is ADDITIVE to w0h's committed surfacing channel (citation 'as of fetched_at', w0h.4): that's the answer-time channel; this is the browse-time introspection channel, the external analogue of seeing a note's tags/entities/edges. Belongs to neither epic's completion gate on purpose — ay5 closes without externals, w0h closes on its core loop; this lands when both seams are ready.
design: Extend the ay5.1 EnrichmentView (or add a sibling ExternalView on the same seam) to carry external-snapshot fields, and teach the ay5.2 browse modal + the ay5.3 'lode show' path to render them for a note that draws down an external (or for the external node itself, if it becomes directly selectable per w0h.8). Reuse the shared reader/renderer — do NOT add a third copy of the display logic. Exact fields to surface follow whatever w0h's snapshot schema settles (external_id, snapshot, fetched_at, source_type, raw_payload; refresh/materiality state from w0h.5/.6/.7). Revisit scope once w0h.2 lands and the physical shape is concrete.
acceptance_criteria: A note that drew down a web link (or an external node) shows its snapshot introspection — source URL, fetched_at, source_type, snapshot id, and available refresh/re-enrich/no_egress state — through the SAME ay5 browse modal and 'lode show' path (no third display copy); un-refreshed vs stale vs withheld states are distinguishable. Depends on ay5.1 + w0h.2 being landed.

title: Mark a web source no_egress (control + enforcement)
description:
E12 web draw-down connector — let a sensitive source stay local (externals.md 'No-egress tier').

## Scope
- A control surface (CLI) to set externals.no_egress=1 for a source (domain / external_id).
- Confirm the enforcement path: a no_egress external snapshot is still captured, embedded, and locally retrievable, but is NEVER sent to Claude — excluded from enrichment AND from cloud Q&A context, and cited as 'present, withheld from cloud synthesis' rather than silently dropped. Confirm egress_log records external sends (and non-sends where relevant).
- The gate already handles is_external redaction/egress generically (qa.py); net-new is the control surface + confirming external coverage end-to-end.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Marking a source no_egress keeps it locally retrievable but excludes it from all cloud egress (enrich + Q&A); answers cite it as withheld.
- egress_log reflects external egress decisions.
- nox -t fix + nox -s tests green.
notes:
CRITICISM (debate): AC 'answers cite it as withheld' depends on the external citation-rendering surface built in w0h.4, but w0h.7 depended only on w0h.2.

DECISION (2026-07-07): dep w0h.7->w0h.4 ADDED, so the cite-as-withheld surface exists before no_egress is verified.

title: Refresh policy (TTL / on-access revalidation) for web sources
description:
E12 web draw-down connector — resolves the per-connector refresh decision (open in docs/decisions.md; externals.md 'external staleness is NOT topological').

## Scope
- Decide and implement how a mirrored URL gets re-fetched (decisions.md leans on-access revalidation + optional TTL — settle it for THIS connector). Re-run fetch (w0h.1) -> ingest (w0h.2) and ride the material-change gate (w0h.5) so a refresh that finds no material change costs no enrichment.
- Record the resolution in docs/decisions.md (move the 'External refresh' item from open to decided-for-web).

## Acceptance Criteria
- A stale external is revalidated per the chosen policy; an unchanged refetch is free (no new snapshot); a changed one snapshots + re-embeds and re-enriches only if material.
- decisions.md records the web-connector refresh decision.
- nox -t fix + nox -s tests green.
notes:
CRITICISM (debate): Missing dependency on w0h.3 -- w0h.6 reuses w0h.3's fetch->ingest trigger path (shared async draw-down job type) but DEPENDS ON listed only w0h.2 and w0h.5. Edge w0h.6->w0h.3 added 2026-07-07.
DECISION (debate round 3, 2026-07-08): rides the 'refresh' job type + fetch->ingest handler introduced by w0h.3 (dep already present); w0h.6 adds only staleness detection + scheduling policy, not a second fetch path.

INHERITED CONSTRAINT from lode-w0h.3's technical review (2026-07-08) — read before you build the refresh policy.

w0h.3's canonicalize_url IS your refresh join key (per the pinned debate-round-3 decision: 'This canonical form IS the external_id dedup key AND the w0h.6 refresh join key'). It implements exactly the pinned rules and no more. Three normalizations are therefore ABSENT, deliberately — they were not in the decision:

  1. PATH percent-encoding is NOT normalized ('%7E' != '~'). Query VALUES are normalized (parse_qsl -> urlencode round-trip), so the two halves of a URL are treated inconsistently.
  2. IDN hosts are NOT punycoded.
  3. userinfo ('user:pass@host') is PRESERVED, password included.

CONSEQUENCE FOR YOU: two URLs that are 'the same page' but differ only in those respects canonicalize to DISTINCT external_ids -- so they are two nodes, and your refresh policy will schedule and re-fetch them independently, never recognizing them as one source. This is consistent with the pinned rules (w0h.3 was right not to widen them unilaterally), but it is inherited, not chosen, and you are the ticket that has to live with it.

DECIDE EXPLICITLY, do not silently inherit: either (a) confirm the narrow canonical is correct and record why in docs/externals.md, or (b) widen canonicalize_url as part of your ticket -- but note that widening it CHANGES external_id for already-stored externals, so it needs a migration/re-key story, not just a code change. Option (b) is much cheaper before real snapshots exist than after.

Also note the userinfo case is a PRIVACY surface: a pasted URL carrying credentials currently becomes part of a stored external_id. Cross-reference docs/externals.md's privacy + hard-delete sections.

title: Material-change re-enrich gating for chatty sources
description:
E12 web draw-down connector — cost control for noisy externals (externals.md 'Snapshot churn: decouple new snapshot from re-enrich').

## Scope
- On a NEW snapshot of an EXISTING external: re-embed always (cheap, local — already true from w0h.2), but re-enrich ONLY when the local delta between the new snapshot and its predecessor (size / similarity) exceeds a materiality threshold.
- Below the bar, do NOT pay for Claude enrichment: carry the PRIOR enrichment forward, re-anchored to the new snapshot (a one-comment PR/page update re-embeds but does not re-enrich).
- Add the materiality threshold as a tunable knob in configuration.py + docs/configuration.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A material change enqueues an enrich job; an immaterial change does not, and the prior enrichment is carried forward re-anchored to the new snapshot.
- Threshold is a documented config knob.
- nox -t fix + nox -s tests green.
notes:
CRITICISM (debate): 'similarity' had a hidden ordering dependency vs the async embed job.

DECISION (2026-07-07): materiality signal = EMBEDDING SIMILARITY (cosine, new-vs-predecessor snapshot vectors). Consequence: the enrich gate must run AFTER the new snapshot's embed job completes (its vector must exist) -- materiality is decided POST-embed, NOT at ingest. Sequence the enrich decision downstream of embed accordingly.
DEP ADDED (debate round 3, 2026-07-08): w0h.5 -> w0h.8. Decision C made materiality = embedding cosine similarity on new-vs-predecessor SNAPSHOT vectors, but snapshot embedding raises KeyError until w0h.8 (embedding.py:139 _version_body SELECTs body FROM versions only). No snapshot vectors exist for w0h.5 to compare until w0h.8 lands. The earlier rounds added the post-embed ORDERING note but never the dep edge; now added.

title: /release Claude skill: compute next semver bump + drive the release
description: A .claude skill that: reads the latest vX.Y.Z tag, offers patch/minor/major next-version (or accepts an explicit version), confirms, runs the gates, and invokes scripts/release.sh. Thin wrapper over the script — no build logic of its own. Model it on the repo's existing skill/SKILL.md conventions.
design: DECISION (2026-07-07): History-derived bump. /release parses conventional-commit prefixes on commits since the latest vX.Y.Z tag (feat -> minor, fix -> patch, '!' or BREAKING CHANGE -> major; pre-1.0 per docs/release.md a breaking change bumps MINOR not MAJOR) to PROPOSE the next version, always confirmable, with an explicit-version override (/release patch|minor|major or /release X.Y.Z). Matches the epic + docs/release.md wording ('from commit history') — no doc reconciliation needed. ASSUMPTION now load-bearing: the repo uses conventional-commit subjects (recent history does: feat(release)/fix(land)/style:). Fallback: if no commit since the last tag carries a recognized prefix, default the proposal to a PATCH bump and make the user confirm/override rather than guessing. Thin wrapper — no build logic; invokes scripts/release.sh (0ru.2).
acceptance_criteria: /release proposes the correct next SemVer from the latest tag, and on confirm invokes scripts/release.sh which cuts the release; /release patch|minor|major honored.
notes:
CRITICISM (debate 2026-07-07):
1. [Certain] Two descriptions disagree on what the skill does. This ticket says it 'offers patch/minor/major next-version' (a menu). The epic + docs/release.md say it 'computes the next semver bump FROM COMMIT HISTORY since the last tag'. History-derived means parsing conventional commits (feat->minor, fix->patch, !->major), which assumes commit-message hygiene the repo hasn't committed to. Decide: dumb menu (safe, matches this ticket) vs history-derived (needs a stated commit convention). Pin it or a builder can satisfy one description while violating the other.

metadata.land_summary: /release Claude skill (.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md): thin wrapper over scripts/release.sh that proposes the next SemVer from conventional-commit history since the latest vX.Y.Z tag (feat->MINOR, fix->PATCH, breaking->MINOR pre-1.0 else MAJOR, none->PATCH fallback), confirms, then invokes the script (which owns all gating/tag/push). Tag-selection mirrors release.sh's version_gt byte-for-byte; no gate/build logic duplicated. Technical review clean (no fixes). Docs-only: no nox/mermaid gate applies.

title: Unify note-id abbreviation: use short_note_id() for all note_id[:N] log literals

title: Extract shared short_version_id() helper; de-duplicate [:12] version-id literals
description:
Follow-up from the /land pass that landed lode-1gr.4 (per-job 'lode work' outcome summary).

WHY
lode-1gr.2 gave NOTE-ids a shared abbreviation helper — notes_read.short_note_id() + SHORT_NOTE_ID_LENGTH (8). VERSION-ids never got the same treatment: the 12-char version-id abbreviation is a bare ':12' slice literal duplicated across the codebase, including two now-USER-FACING sites added by lode-1gr.4:
  - src/lode/worker.py:740  _embed_handler -> f"embedded {target_version[:12]}: {count} passages"
  - src/lode/enrich.py:285  format_enrich_outcome -> f"enriched {version_id[:12]}: ..."
plus cli._short (cli.py:603, the existing 12-char version-id abbreviator) and many enrich.py log-line literals (version_id[:12], e.g. lines 329/335/363/472/...).
12 chars is CORRECT here (these are version-ids, matching cli._short) — this is NOT a length mismatch with short_note_id. It is a missing shared helper + duplicated literal.

WHAT
- Add a shared short_version_id() helper + a named length constant (mirroring notes_read.short_note_id / SHORT_NOTE_ID_LENGTH). Put it in a NEUTRAL module, not cli.py — worker.py and enrich.py must be able to import it without a cli dependency (cli depends on them, not vice-versa). notes_read.py is a candidate but is note-centric; a small shared ids/util module may be cleaner — producer's call.
- Replace the version-id ':12' literals with it. Required: the two user-facing lode work output sites (worker.py:740, enrich.py:285) and cli._short (delegates to the helper). The enrich.py log-line literals are nice-to-have — sweep them if cheap, but don't let scope balloon.

ACCEPTANCE
- One shared short_version_id() helper + named length constant; no bare ':12' version-id literal remains in the user-facing 'lode work' output paths; cli._short delegates to the helper (behavior unchanged, still 12 chars).
- No behavior change to output wording. nox -t fix + nox -s tests green.

title: Edit an existing note from the browse screen (append new version to its chain)
description: Deferred follow-up to the browse screen (lode-0wj.5). Let the user open a note from browse and edit it, saving as a NEW version appended to the note's version chain via the CAS head path (docs/storage.md event-sourced chains). Bigger scope than read-only browse because the capture screen currently only creates brand-new notes — this needs loading an existing version into an editable buffer and saving against the existing note id. File now, build after read-only browse lands and the exit-safety/lag work is done.
design:
Entry point: BrowseScreen gets a new 'e' binding (on the highlighted row) that pushes EditScreen(note_id) directly -- reading "edit an existing note from the browse screen" literally, rather than requiring a detour through the read-only NoteViewScreen first. NoteViewScreen is untouched.

Save path: lode/tui/edit.py's save_edit() mirrors capture.py's save_capture() but never mints a uuid -- it reparents the buffer onto the caller-supplied `parent` (the loaded head) via Repository.save, so a non-dedup save is always an 'update' op appended to the existing chain. An unchanged buffer relies on Repository.save's existing dedup (no new row) rather than a special case here -- that's what makes "unchanged vs empty" a real, correct distinction: dirty is compared against the loaded buffer (EditScreen._loaded_body), never against emptiness.

CAS conflict handling: reused ReconcileScreen, but gave it a new optional `on_resolved` constructor callback (default None preserves capture's existing app.exit() behavior byte for byte -- all pre-existing reconcile tests still pass unmodified). EditScreen passes on_resolved=self._on_reconcile_resolved, which pops both ReconcileScreen and itself, landing back on BrowseScreen instead of exiting the whole app.

Empty-body save: refused (EmptyEditError), mirroring capture's refusal -- editing to blank is not wired as an implicit delete; Repository.delete is a separate, unbuilt path here.

Scope decision -- Ctrl+Q: NOT wired to EditScreen. The acceptance criteria cites lode-0wj.1 (Escape-only guard) specifically, not lode-0wj.8 (the app-level Ctrl+Q confirm_quit() hook). Reusing the confirm_quit() name for Escape's "pop back to browse" would have silently changed Ctrl+Q's meaning too (LodeApp.action_quit calls confirm_quit() for its own "quit the whole app" contract), so Escape's guard lives in action_cancel instead, under a different name. Net effect: Ctrl+Q from EditScreen still quits immediately with no confirm today (same as every other non-capture screen). Filed as a follow-up: lode-0wj.6 discovered-from ticket to extend lode-0wj.8's guard to EditScreen if that's wanted.
acceptance_criteria: From browse, a note can be opened editable; saving appends a new version to that note's chain (CAS), not a new note. Escape returns to the list. Confirm-on-unsaved guard (lode-0wj.1) applies here too.
notes: Debate (lode-0wj): 'confirm-on-unsaved guard applies here too' inherits whatever lode-0wj.1 actually builds. If lode-0wj.1 is narrowed to Escape-only (app-level Ctrl+Q split into its own ticket), this edit-existing-note flow uses that same Escape guard. Also note: THIS is the first flow where 'unchanged vs empty' becomes a real distinction (a loaded existing version can be unchanged) — until then capture dirty == non-empty.

metadata.land_summary: Edit-existing-note flow from browse: 'e' on a highlighted browse row pushes EditScreen, which loads the note's live head into an editable buffer (lode.tui.edit.load_head) and on Ctrl+S saves via save_edit -> Repository.save with parent=loaded head, appending a NEW version to the chain via the CAS head path (never mints a note id); unchanged buffer dedups to a no-op, empty body refused (EmptyEditError). Escape's dirty check compares against the loaded buffer (not emptiness) and reuses lode-0wj.1 DiscardConfirmScreen; CAS reject reuses ReconcileScreen via a new optional on_resolved callback that pops back to browse instead of exiting. Technical review (/code-review + /simplify): no correctness or simplification fixes needed; code correct, clean, mirrors capture-path conventions. Gates green: 731 passed, 6 skipped.

title: Repository.recover() feeds cache.index() an unredacted body (redact-before-index gap)
description:
lode-n60 wired redact_before_index() into Repository.save() (the body handed to CacheBackend.index()) and into embedding.embed() (the vector leg's own re-read of versions.body). Repository.recover() has the identical shape — it reads the target version's raw body via self._body(target_version) and hands it straight to self.cache.index(note_id, result.version_id, body) with no redaction — so recovering a version whose body matches a redact_before_index_patterns seed would push the raw secret into the FTS leg (LexicalCacheBackend.index() uses the body param verbatim). embed()'s own internal redaction protects the vector leg regardless of caller, so only the FTS/lexical leg is actually exposed today. recover() is not yet CLI-wired (no 'lode recover' command exists), so this is currently latent, not reachable in production — but should be fixed before any CLI wiring lands.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. repo.save("note-1", "key: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE done")
2. repo.delete("note-1", parent=<that version>)
3. repo.recover("note-1", target_version=<the secret-bearing version>)
4. LexicalIndex(conn).search("AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE", k=5) returns a hit — the secret is keyword-findable again post-recover.

## Acceptance Criteria
Repository.recover() applies lode.redact.redact_before_index() to the body before calling self.cache.index(), same pattern as save() (lode-n60). recover() gains a settings: Settings | None = None parameter (it currently has none) so the patterns can be resolved. A regression test proves a recovered secret-bearing version is not keyword-findable via LexicalIndex.search().

metadata.land_summary: Wire redact_before_index() into Repository.recover()'s cache seam: recover() gains settings param; recovered head's raw body (_body) is redacted before cache.index() so a recovered secret-bearing version is not FTS-findable; versions.body stays raw; +2 regression tests. Technical review: no bug/simplify changes — faithful mirror of lode-n60 save() path.

title: Batch-submit enrich jobs don't stamp claimed_at before batch_handle persist (early-reclaim risk)
description:
Context: surfaced during lode-aor's technical review (crash-recovery for stuck 'running' jobs).

lode-aor added _reclaim_stale_running(), which reclaims any job in status='running'
with batch_handle IS NULL past a staleness timeout, on the assumption that claimed_at
is stamped on every path that flips a job to 'running' (true for _claim_one).

_batch_submit_enrich (worker.py, ~L526-530) flips enrich jobs to 'running' WITHOUT
stamping claimed_at. If a crash lands in the narrow window between
submit_enrich_batch's batches.create() returning and the batch_handle persist
(enrich.py:465-474), the row is left running + batch_handle NULL + claimed_at NULL.
_reclaim_stale_running treats claimed_at IS NULL as immediately stale, so it will
reclaim (and eventually resubmit) that job -- risking a duplicate Batches API
submission if the original batch_handle write was actually about to succeed.

This is pre-existing batch-path non-atomicity, not introduced by lode-aor. lode-aor's
new behavior is still a net improvement (trades "stuck forever + orphaned batch" for
"eventual resubmit"), so it was not blocking and did not need to land with a fix.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Kick off a bulk enrich batch submission (_batch_submit_enrich).
2. Kill the process between batches.create() returning in submit_enrich_batch and the
   batch_handle UPDATE persisting (enrich.py:465-474).
3. Restart and let drain() run past the staleness timeout.
4. Observe: the row (running, batch_handle NULL, claimed_at NULL) is reclaimed and
   resubmitted even though the original batch may have gone through -- possible
   duplicate Batches API spend.

## Acceptance Criteria
Either (a) stamp claimed_at when _batch_submit_enrich flips a job to 'running' (so it
gets a real staleness window instead of being treated as immediately stale), or (b)
make the batch_handle persist atomic/two-phase with the running-flip, so this window
cannot exist. Scope belongs with the batch path (lode-i05.5's owner), not with
lode-aor's staleness-reclaim mechanism.

metadata.land_summary: Stamp claimed_at in _batch_submit_enrich's pre-claim CAS (worker.py) so a crash between batches.create() and the batch_handle persist (enrich.py) leaves batch-path rows a real 900s staleness window instead of being treated as immediately stale by _reclaim_stale_running (lode-aor). +2 regression tests. Gates green: 601 passed/4 skipped.

title: Reclaim stuck 'running' jobs after a crash (no TTL/timeout reclaim exists)
description:
Context: found while designing the fix for lode-npx.2's double-enrichment bug.

worker.py's claim/run state machine has no mechanism to reclaim a job left in
status='running' by a crash. _reset_retryable (worker.py) only resets
status='failed' jobs whose next_attempt_at is due back to 'pending' -- it never
touches 'running' rows. _claim_one only ever selects status='pending'. So a
worker (or, once lode-npx.2's fix lands, the CLI's inline immediate-enrich
claim) that crashes or is killed between claiming a job (UPDATE ... SET
status='running') and completing it leaves that row permanently stuck: no
reconciliation step, no gap query, and no claim query will ever pick it up
again.

This is NOT specific to enrich -- it applies identically to embed jobs claimed
by the normal `lode work` worker loop. worker.py's own module docstring
half-acknowledges this ("Regular embed jobs left running by a crash are
covered by the embed-gap reconciliation query if the embed result is also
missing") but that claim doesn't hold: reconcile.py's embed_gap / enrich_gap
queries both exclude any job with status != 'dead' (which includes 'running')
from being treated as a gap, so a genuinely stuck 'running' row is invisible
to reconciliation too.

Pre-existing gap, not introduced by any one ticket -- surfacing it now because
lode-npx.2's fix (CLI opportunistically claims+runs the enrich job it just
enqueued, same primitives as the worker) adds a new trigger for it: a crash or
Ctrl-C during `lode add` mid-Haiku-call, in addition to the existing
worker-crash trigger.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run \`lode work\` (or, after lode-npx.2 lands, \`lode add\`) and kill the
   process (SIGKILL) after it flips a job row to status='running' but before
   the handler completes.
2. Run \`lode work\` again (fresh process).
3. Observe: the killed job's row stays status='running' forever -- it is never
   re-claimed, never appears in \`lode jobs\` as a gap, and reconcile's
   embed_gap/enrich_gap steps do not re-enqueue it (both queries treat any
   status != 'dead' row, including 'running', as \"not a gap\").
design: Root cause: no signal exists for 'how long has this job been running', so nothing can distinguish a legitimately in-flight job from one abandoned by a crash. _claim_one only selects status='pending'; reconcile's embed_gap/enrich_gap queries exclude any status != 'dead' (including 'running'). Fix: add jobs.claimed_at (ISO-8601 UTC, set by _claim_one's claim UPDATE); a new lode.worker._reclaim_stale_running(conn, settings), run at the top of every drain() pass before _reset_retryable, selects status='running' AND batch_handle IS NULL AND (claimed_at IS NULL OR claimed_at <= now - settings.stale_running_timeout_s new Settings knob, default 900s) and puts each through the identical attempts/backoff/dead-letter accounting run_one uses for a transient handler failure (reuse, no parallel retry policy). Batch-backed enrich jobs are excluded via batch_handle IS NOT NULL (lode-i05.5 owns their long-lived running + resume-on-restart semantics). Once reclaimed to dead or pending, reconcile's existing gap queries see the job correctly with no changes of their own.
acceptance_criteria: A job stuck in status='running' past some staleness threshold (e.g. no update to the row for N minutes, or a dead process' pid) is detected and reclaimed -- either reset to 'pending' for retry, or dead-lettered if attempts are exhausted -- without manual DB surgery. Applies uniformly to embed, enrich, and refresh job types. Batches-backed enrich jobs (batch_handle set) are explicitly excluded (lode-i05.5 already owns their long-lived 'running' + resume-on-restart semantics).
notes: Reviewer (technical review pass) surfaced a related but out-of-scope gap: _batch_submit_enrich flips enrich jobs to 'running' without stamping claimed_at before the batch_handle persist completes, so a crash in that window could trigger an early reclaim -> possible duplicate batch resubmission. Filed as lode-uhu (belongs to the batch path / lode-i05.5's owner, not this ticket's staleness-reclaim scope).

metadata.land_summary: Reclaim stuck status='running' jobs after a crash: adds jobs.claimed_at (schema+migration), Settings.stale_running_timeout_s (900s), and worker._reclaim_stale_running run atop every drain() pass; reuses run_one's attempts/backoff/dead-letter accounting, excludes batch-backed enrich jobs. Review verified correctness + hoisted a loop-invariant. 12 tests, all gates green.
